<margin>7th Observation.</margin>
Seventhly, it does not say: those people are rather blessed who hear *my* words, as it says in some other places; but here it says: those who hear *God’s Word*. For if Christ had said, "yes, they are blessed who hear *my* words," the people might have thought that Christ attributed salvation only to his own preaching and to those who heard him in person. Therefore Christ says, "yes, blessed are those who hear God’s Word," by whomever it may be preached, be it Peter, or Paul, or Apollos, be it any disciple now living, or any <term>Minister of the Gospel</term> <note>original: "Dienaer des Euangeliums"</note> who shall live hereafter until the end of the world. Anyone who hears God's Word (as contained in the scriptures of the Old and New Testament) and keeps it, is "rather blessed" <note>The author uses "eer saligh" to mean "more blessed" or "blessed indeed."</note> than my Mother was, in so far as she is regarded as an instrument through whom I was brought into the world. And in this manner of speaking, Christ places a hidden honor and glory upon the Ministers of the Gospel, since he does not restrict the blessing only to his own preaching, but extends it to all the Ministers who preach God's Word. And this is the reason (as many
<margin>John 14:12.</margin>
believe) why the Scripture says: *He who believes shall do greater things than Christ himself.* This is not understood as the work of redemption, but as the work of ministry; namely, that a faithful Minister shall convert more souls than Christ himself converted through his own ministry. Certainly, Christ could have converted all his listeners; but he did not do so, so that men should not think that they must hear no one but Christ. We do not read of many who were converted by Christ's preaching; more were converted by Peter and the other Apostles than by Christ himself. Christ did this so that the people would not despise any of his ordinary Ministers. If Christ
had converted more than all the disciples, then the people might have held the disciples in low esteem and followed only Christ. This weed began to grow in the days
<margin>1 Corinthians 1:12.</margin>
of the Apostles. *This I say,* says Paul, *that every one of you says, I am of Paul, and I of Apollos, and I of Cephas, and I of Christ.* The Apostle rebukes those who said, "I am of Christ." This does not mean that they were to be blamed for following and acknowledging Christ—far from it. But there were some in the Church of Corinth who easily said: "I do not care for the preaching of Paul or Apollos, but I will hear Christ alone." This was an irregular and sinful way of exalting Christ. No, Christ does not want himself and his preaching to be so exalted that, in the meantime, one despises the service of his Ministers; such preaching is evil in his eyes, for he says: *blessed are those who hear God's Word and keep it,* regardless of who has preached it, provided he is a faithful Minister.

<margin>8th Observation.</margin>
Lastly, it does not say: they are blessed *because* of the hearing and *because* of the keeping; but blessed are those who hear and who keep it. The Lord God would not bless you for the hearing, even if you heard as many sermons as there are days in the year: but he blesses those who hear, obeying his command and doing what they hear. Thus you have here eight considerations regarding the manner of speaking that Christ uses here.

<margin>What it is</margin>
Now I shall proceed to show you what is understood

<column-break/>

by keeping the heard Word of God; this keeping happens in two ways.

<margin>To keep God's word.</margin>
<margin>1. Keeping it in the memory.</margin>
First, that you keep it in your memory. *Mary,* it is written, *kept all these words together, pondering them in her heart.* She kept them in her memory. Our memory must be like the Ark in which the Manna was preserved: the Manna is the Divine Truth; the same must be kept very closely in our memory. But this is not the "keeping" spoken of here, for many people have a good memory to keep what they hear, but they do not have good hearts, they do not live well; therefore they are not blessed through their "keeping."

<margin>2. Putting it into practice and observing it.</margin>
Secondly, one also keeps the Word when one puts it into practice; that is, when we take watchful care to make our life and conduct correspond with what we hear and know. Truly blessed are you who hear God’s Word and keep it in this way. And thus all the difficulties of the text are explained.

<margin>Doctrine.</margin>
The Doctrine shall be this: That those are "rather blessed" who hear God’s Word and observe it, than the Mother of Jesus Christ was for having brought him into the world. Truly this is a matter that deserves careful attention, and if it had not stood in the Bible, it would have been almost unbelievable; that Christ would say that you, Man or Woman, in whatever age of the world you live, shall be "rather blessed" if you shall hear the Word of God and keep it.

It is noteworthy that this woman in the text uses a completely different way of speaking
<margin>Luke 11:28.</margin>
than Elizabeth, who was the cousin of the Virgin Mary. This woman said: *blessed is the womb that bore you, and the breasts which you sucked.* But Eliza-
<margin>Luke 1:45.</margin>
beth cried out: *blessed is she who has believed.* On these words a learned writer has a very good observation; "If the Virgin Mary," he says, "had not birthed Christ in her heart through faith as well as through her body, she would not have been blessed"; for Elizabeth explains here wherein the blessedness of the Virgin Mary and of all the elect consisted.

Well, this serves then as a refutation of the
<margin>Usefulness for refutation.</margin>
folly of the Roman Church, which exalts the Virgin Mary so excessively. I have looked into some Popish <note>The original Dutch uses "Paepsche" (Papist), a common 17th-century Protestant term for Roman Catholics.</note> authors a little, and I have found that they attribute much more dignity and glory to the Virgin Mary than to Christ. They recount strange histories and follies regarding her, the likes of which were never heard of in
<margin>The Idolatry of the Papists uncovered.</margin>
former times, in order to idolatrously exalt her name; such as, that she was free from <term>original sin</term> <note>The doctrine that all humans inherit a sinful nature from Adam.</note>, though the Scripture expressly says that all those who descend from Adam are stained with original damnation, including therefore the Virgin Mary, being a daughter of Adam. The Papists speak with more reverence of the Virginity, dignity, and holiness of the Virgin Mary, the Mother, than they do of the righteousness, grace, and merits of Christ the Son. And therefore they uphold justification through works, and not through faith in the righteousness of Christ; yes, they are so obsessed with the Virgin Mary that they make her into a great <term>Intercessor</term> <note>A go-between or advocate who prays to God on behalf of others.</note> with God.

# True Blessedness.

the Father. Someone might think that it is unnecessary to argue against <term>Catholic doctrine</term> <note>original: "Paepsche Leere"; literally "Popish teachings." At this time in the Dutch Republic, there was significant tension between the Reformed Church and the Catholic Church.</note>, but the Ministers have never had more reason for it than now: for never has <term>Popery</term> spread more craftily than in these days, in which—through a cursed tolerance—the Priests and Jesuits so spread their blasphemous and idolatrous views, and carry out their Jesuitical tricks and schemes; God also knows how quickly you, who do not want to bow your neck under the yoke of Christ, shall be brought under the Catholic yoke. This I can say from my own experience, that I have never found more people leaning towards the Papacy than recently. Those who have confessed the <term>Reformed religion</term> <note>The official state-sanctioned Protestantism of the Dutch Republic.</note> shamefully deviate from their first confession and solemn covenants; and God knows how quickly they shall place the Virgin Mary above Christ. But I hope for better things from you, therefore I shall pass over this and come to the Reasons for this Doctrine, which are these:

<margin>1st Reason. They are so close to Christ.</margin>
Firstly, those who hear God’s Word and keep it are "more blessed" than the Virgin Mary was by bringing Christ into the world, because Christ considers them to be more closely related to Him than His own natural friends.
> Luke 8:21. But he answered and said to them, my Mother and my brothers are these, who hear God’s Word and do the same.
See, here is a straight path to enter into a new covenant of friendship with Christ, to become a blood-relative of Christ, and to be regarded as the brother, sister, and mother of Jesus Christ; namely, by obeying the will of Christ.

<margin>2nd Reason. A perseverance.</margin>
Secondly, your salvation is proven by this: because if you hear and do the Word, you shall persevere until the very end; while others shall fall away from the Faith and suffer shipwreck; just as Christ says in Matthew 7, from verse 24 to 28 exclusive:
> Therefore whosoever hears these sayings of mine, and does them, I will liken him unto a wise man, which built his house upon a rock; and the rain descended, and the floods came, and the winds blew, and beat upon that house; and it fell not, for it was founded upon a rock. And every one that hears these sayings of mine, and does them not, shall be likened unto a foolish man, which built his house upon the sand; and the rain descended, and the floods came, and the winds blew, and beat upon that house; and it fell, and great was the fall of it.
Only those who hear God’s Word and keep it persevere; they alone have built their souls upon a rock, and they stand immovable in times of persecution. Certainly, they can fall, and even fall uglily (as seen in David, Peter, and many other dear Saints) through the violence of Satan’s temptations and the remnant of corruption which is in them; but they shall never fall away entirely and to the end, because they are built on an immovable Rock, and that Rock is Christ, who—
<margin>Matt. 12:2. Hebr. 12:32.</margin>
is the author and the finisher of their faith. He has also prayed for them, that their faith might not fail. And this He has also obtained, and therefore, though storm-winds and 

<column-break/>

fearful waves arise, yet they shall never fall away completely. Others fall and perish when the winds and storms arise.

<margin>3rd Reason. God makes glorious promises to them.</margin>
Thirdly, God makes very glorious promises to those who hear the Word of God and keep it.
> Revelation 1:3. Blessed is he that reads, and they that hear the words of this prophecy, and keep those things which are written therein; for the time is at hand.
Here you see that all those become blessed who hear and keep God’s Word; that is, who lay the same up in their hearts and express the power of it in their lives.

<margin>4th Reason. They can be instruments to bring others to salvation.</margin>
Fourthly, you can bring others to salvation by working out what you hear in God’s Word; and blessed are those who are instruments to bring others into Heaven. 1 Peter 3:1. *Likewise, you wives, be in subjection to your own husbands; that, if any obey not the word, they also may without the word be won by the conversation of the wives.* So also 1 Peter 2:12. *And keep your conduct honest among the Gentiles: that, whereas they speak against you as evildoers, they may by your good works, which they shall behold, glorify God in the day of visitation.* Their godly conduct can be a means to bring others to salvation.

<margin>5th Reason. They shall undoubtedly be saved.</margin>
Fifthly, if you take narrow care to do what you hear (even if you do not bring others to salvation), you shall nevertheless certainly come into Heaven and inherit salvation.
> Revelation 14:12, 13. Here is the patience of the saints: here are they that keep the commandments of God, and the faith of Jesus. And I heard a voice from heaven saying unto me, Write, Blessed are the dead which die in the Lord from henceforth: Yea, says the Spirit, that they may rest from their labors; and their works do follow them.
O you who earnestly strive to keep God’s Commandments and the Faith of Jesus, you shall certainly come into Heaven, even though you bring no one but yourself with you.

<margin>Utility, regarding complaint.</margin>
Now I pass over to the application; and that shall be a sorrowful complaint.
If it is so, that those who hear and keep God’s Word are "more blessed" than the Virgin Mary was in the respect that she brought Christ into the world; then this must serve as a sorrowful complaint, that men do not want to seek salvation where they can obtain it with so little trouble. If God had said, "I will make you blessed if you move mountains; if you fulfill my Law to the smallest jot and tittle"; this would have been impossible for us. But God says: "Blessed are you, if you hear the Word of God and keep it." Therefore, if you do not want to put into practice what you hear, you reject the offered grace.
<margin>The will stands in place of reason. <note>original: "Stat pro ratione voluntas." This Latin legal/philosophical maxim suggests that for some, their desire or will is their only justification, rather than logic.</note></margin>
The Devil could not bring you to damnation if you did not want to do it yourself. O man, you have a stiff-necked heart, you who want to do everything that pleases you (let the Preacher say what he will), who makes little conscience of hearing God’s Word, and even less of doing what you hear; you are without excuse.

First consideration. You shall increase your damnation. <note>original: "Minor erat culpa ubi erat culpae ignorantia."</note> <note>Latin: "The fault was less where there was ignorance of the fault."</note>

Firstly, if you do not put the heard Word into practice, then that hearing will one day increase your damnation. John 15:22 <note>The text mistakenly cites John 5:22.</note>: *If I had not come and spoken to them, they would have no sin; but now they have no excuse for their sins.* Sin can be somewhat diminished where there is no knowledge of the sin; it is a far greater sin to despise the known Law of God than to not know it at all. Those who sin against their knowledge have no pretext or excuse for their sins. *That servant who knew the will of his Lord, and did not prepare himself, nor did according to his will, shall be beaten with many stripes.* In Isaiah 13, one reads of many nations and peoples against whom God commands the Prophet to announce a heavy prophecy; but in Isaiah 22, one reads of the burden of the "Valley of Vision," that is, of Jerusalem, and it is noted there that this burden was the heaviest of all; no burden was as heavy as that of the Valley of Vision. It was a place where there was much knowledge and where many sermons were given; therefore, that burden was heavier than those against Babylon, Tyre, Damascus, and all the others. Although the people who live in parts of **America** shall go to Hell for their disobedience, nevertheless, consider that you who live in **England**, where the Gospel is confessed and preached, shall go to Hell with a heavier burden on your conscience than those who have not had the Gospel. You shall be damned with a <unclear>shaking</unclear> <note>original: "gerupte"</note>, you who hear the Word of God there and take no care to perform what you have heard. Someone might stand amazed and terrified who reads what is written in Jeremiah 10:25: *Pour out your fury upon the heathens who do not know you.* If then God's fury shall be poured out over the poor, ignorant heathens who do not know God, who do not have the means of salvation, and who do not hear the Gospel of Christ—well, what kind of wrath shall then be poured out over the Christians who do not know God? But especially, what unspeakable fury and vengeance shall be poured out over those Christians who sin against the knowledge of God, against the light shining clearly in their eyes, and against an awakened and convicted conscience? If there is one place in Hell hotter than another, it shall be for them; for it is a far greater sin to despise the known Law of God than to be ignorant of God’s Law; those who sin against their conscience have no pretext or excuse for their sin.

<margin>
Second consideration: you have no love for God.
</margin>
Secondly, you do not have the love of God in you if you do not put into practice that which you hear. 1 John 2:5 <note>The text mistakenly cites John 5:25.</note>: *Whoever keeps His Word, in him truly is the love of God perfected.*

<margin>
Third consideration: your confession is worth nothing.
</margin>
Thirdly, God considers your confession worth nothing unless you maintain what you hear. No matter how many zeros <note>original: "ootjens"; literally "little o's" or zeros.</note> one places together in arithmetic, they still do not make a sum; but place one significant figure <note>original: "cijfertjen"</note> with them, and then it will make a large sum. Likewise, though you pray ever so often, and though you hear ever so many sermons, they shall be nothing other than zeros, unless you add to them a conscientious walk that corresponds with what you hear and pray. Consider within yourself (you who have been a **Confessor** <note>In this context, a "Confessor" or "Belijder" is someone who publicly professes the Christian faith.</note> for so long)

<column-break/>

whether you would want God to look upon you as if you had been a godless person all your life. Well, so it is: God reckons you as such if you do not put what you hear or know into practice. 1 Samuel 2:12: *But the children of Eli were children of Belial; they did not know the Lord.* They knew the Lord well in terms of theory; for they had a theoretical knowledge of God and the Law through their upbringing, since they were Priests of the Lord; and God would not choose ignorant men to be His Priests. But they did not have an active, powerful, and saving knowledge of God, and therefore God regarded their knowledge as no knowledge, and their confession as no confession. Remember, God will regard your hearing as no hearing, your praying as no praying, your receiving of the Sacraments as no receiving, if you do not strive to obediently do what you hear.

<margin>
Fourth consideration: you can have no assurance of God's love toward you.
</margin>
Fourthly, you can have no assurance or proof of God’s love toward your soul unless you attempt to keep what you hear. *If you love me, keep my commandments,* it says in John 14:15 <note>The text cites 14:16.</note>. Therefore, one finds in Scripture that the love of God is often joined with the keeping of God's commandments. Exodus 20:6: *I show mercy unto thousands of those who love me and keep my commandments.* Those two are placed together to show that where the love of God is, there is also a keeping of His commandments.

<margin>
Fifth consideration: God will take the Word from us.
</margin>
Fifthly, if we do not earnestly strive to work out what we hear, then God will be moved to take the Gospel from us. Amos 8:9: *And it shall come to pass in that day, says the Lord GOD, that I will make the sun go down at noon, and I will darken the earth in broad daylight.* Verse 11: *I will send a famine in the land; not a famine of bread, nor a thirst for water, but of hearing the words of the Lord.* Remember this: God will take the Word away because you do not do any good with it. Matthew 21:43: *Therefore I say to you, the Kingdom of God shall be taken from you, and given to a nation bringing forth the fruits thereof.* By the "Kingdom of God," one must understand the Gospel, God’s Word, and the ministry thereof; this shall be taken from you and given to others if you bring forth no fruit. And from this, we can clearly read our sin and our heavy judgment: for if any people in the world are guilty of unfruitfulness under the <term>means of grace</term> <note>A theological term referring to the tools God uses to bring people to faith, such as preaching and sacraments.</note>, it is our nation; we have been lifted up to Heaven, and therefore we may rightly fear and expect that we shall be cast down to Hell.

But to awaken your consciences, I shall first present some proofs that we are indeed highly guilty of unfruitfulness under the means of grace; and secondly, I shall show you that we are then in great danger that the Gospel [will be taken] from us...

# True Blessedness.

...shall be taken away from us / and given to a people / that brings forth the fruits thereof. <note>A reference to Matthew 21:43.</note>

It is evident that we are guilty of fruitlessness / despite the Gospel-ordained means of worship:

<margin>1. Proof of our fruitlessness under the aforementioned means.</margin>
First / from the sorrowful complaint / which even the most fruitful plants in God's vineyard make; they complain with distress and the sighing of their hearts over their fruitlessness / under the means of grace: well, if the trees of righteousness / which God has planted in His vineyard / complain / that they bear no fruit / then certainly the wild trees are unfruitful; if the trees of God’s Garden bring forth no fruit; what then shall the trees of the wilderness do? If God’s people sit down and weep / because no sufficient fruit is found in them: how great a cause for complaining then have the godless of the world / whose hearts are as hard as a millstone / even though the Heavenly dew falls upon them from time to time.

<margin>Proof.</margin>
Secondly / it is evident from the sorrowful complaints of God’s Ambassadors / the Ministers of Jesus Christ; who observe / that only small fruit comes from all their labor; that their Gospel ministry has little progress / therefore they lie with sadness upon their beds / and complain with dismay of spirit / just as Peter did / that they have fished all night / but have caught nothing; that they are as if sowing upon rocks / and that they break their tools to pieces / but that they cannot break the hearts of men; that they wear out their own lives / and consume their lungs / but that they cannot consume the corruptions of the people. And thus they complain with the Prophet (in the person of Christ) *I have labored in vain.* <note>Isaiah 49:4.</note>

<margin>Proof.</margin>
Thirdly / it is evident from the comparison of our times with the time / in which the Gospel was first planted; *Christ* says in *Matthew 11:12:* *From the days of John the Baptist until now, the Kingdom of Heaven suffers violence, and the violent take it by force.* In those days people used a holy violence in the ways of religion; but where is that violence to be found now? When the seventy Disciples received the command from Christ <margin>Luke 10:17.</margin> / to preach the Gospel / it was said of them / that they went out to preach the word, and God was with them, so that many were converted, and the devil fell like lightning from Heaven. Their service had a very glorious progress. And it says in *Isaiah 54:2* (which is a prophecy of the first times of the preaching of the Gospel) *Enlarge the place of your tent, and let them stretch forth the curtains of your habitations.* As if there were not enough room for the converts; make then your Tents wider / which refers to the Apostle in *Galatians 4:27:* *Rejoice, you barren, who do not bear; break forth and shout, you who have no birth pains: for the children of the desolate are many more than those of her who has a husband.* So it also says in *Acts 11 verse 21:* *The Hand of the Lord was with them, and a great number believed and turned to the Lord.* Yes, three thousand were converted by one sermon of *Peter’s*; whereas now one might preach three thousand sermons / and hardly convert one soul to Christ; and the Heavenly Prophet says in *Psalm 110 verse 3:*

<column-break/>

*Your people shall be very willing in the day of your power, in holy attire, from the womb of the morning you shall have the dew of your youth;* The meaning of these words / *from the womb of the morning you shall have the dew of your youth,* is this / namely that / at the first preaching of the Gospel / the converts would be in so great a number / as the drops of dew on the grass in the morning. But now at this time the converting of souls / and the bringing over of men to Christ / is not as numerous as the drops of dew / but as rare as Pearls and Diamonds.

<margin>4. Proof.</margin>
Fourthly / it will appear that there is a general fruitlessness under all the means of grace; because nowadays more people are turned away from the truth and the simplicity of the Gospel / than are converted by its powerful working. The conversion that happens in these days / has power only upon the Brains of men / and not upon their hearts: it works in them only imaginings of concepts, and not an active Godliness; they are not like the Sun / but like the Moon / whose influence indeed gives light / but no heat. The Word makes them refrain from drunkenness / but the devil makes them drunk with opinions and errors.

This now being so / I shall further give you some proofs / that we indeed stand in great danger / that the Kingdom of God / the Gospel of Jesus Christ shall be taken away from us / if not from the entire Nation / at least from certain specific places; therefore let us not be careless.

<margin>1. Proof that there is danger that the Gospel shall be taken from us.</margin>
First, this can be seen from that irreconcilable opposition of the Professors of the Gospel against the Preachers of the Gospel: For that People / who formerly esteemed the feet of their Ministers as very lovely / say now / that the mark of the beast is branded on their foreheads; that people / who formerly would have plucked out their eyes for the service of their Ministers / would now pluck out the eyes of their Ministers : that people / who held us for servants of Christ / and dispensers of the mysteries of salvation / judge us now to be emissaries of the Antichrist / and schismatics. Certainly there is now no more effective way to drive the Gospel from us / than that one sets oneself and fights against the Gospel and its Ministers; this shall be the approach (if God does not prevent it) to our complete destruction / and a departure of the Gospel of Jesus Christ. I wish / that such people / who would rather see the Godly Preachers in Prison than in the Pulpit / would consider / that if God takes them away / they shall get worse ones in their place. The Heretics were tired of the Godly and learned Junius, therefore God let Arminius rise up after him, who was a pestilential enemy of the Gospel of Christ: <note>Franciscus Junius (1545–1602) was a mainstream Reformed theologian; Jacobus Arminius (1560–1609) founded the Remonstrant movement, which the author here considers a "pestilential" error.</note> God would rightfully give us unfit and misleading Teachers / because we so little esteem these learned and Godly Ministers / who are among us: when Paul and Barnabas were contradicted and slandered by the unbelieving Jews, they said; Seeing you <margin>Acts 13:46.</margin> thrust the Word of God from you, and judge yourselves unworthy of everlasting life, lo, we turn to the Gentiles; they lost the Gospel thereby.

<margin>2. Proof.</margin> Secondly / it appears that there is a danger / that the Gospel shall be turned away from us / because of the general luxury and satiety <note>Satiety: the state of being overfilled or "full to bursting," leading to boredom or disgust.</note> of the people / who live under the Gospel. When children play with the bread in their hands / then the Father comes and takes it from them / and leaves them to fast: we have dealt with the Gospel / just as children do with bread / when their bellies are full; we have become luxurious and <term>bread-drunk</term> <note>Original: "broot-droncken." A 17th-century Dutch expression meaning to be so well-fed and prosperous that one becomes arrogant or reckless.</note>; so that / if a Minister of the Faith preaches / of conversion / of the killing of sins / of zeal / of self-denial / and of Heavenly-mindedness / men regard these Teachings as minor and all too common. Yet when God sees a people become full / and wantonly play with the Gospel; He shall soon strike them: He shall make them know and recognize the value of the Gospel / through the lack of the same; just as the Israelites once loathed the Manna, so God quickly let them perish through hunger. Anyone can easily notice our sin and unrestraint in this matter: for that people / who formerly observed the instituted means of Worship with delight / have now become entirely full and weary of the same; that people / who for six days were sorrowful / thinking it was too long / before the day of rest <note>The Sabbath.</note> came / now seek not / to hallow even one day of rest in the entire Year; that people who could not live one day without the Gospel / can now live not only without / but even above the Gospel / just like those of whom we read in 1 Cor. 1:12 <note>Original: "I am of Paul; and I of Apollos; and I of Cephas; and I of Christ."</note> who were so highly exalted in their own eyes / that they despised Paul, Apollos, and Cephas / and only accepted Christ. Yet when any people become weary of the Gospel / it shall not be long before the Gospel also becomes weary of them / and departs from them.

<margin>3. Proof.</margin> Thirdly / that there is danger / that the Gospel shall be taken away from us / appears from the great increase of such opinions / which are contrary to the Gospel, as those which overthrow its power and purity. When the people set their threshold by God’s threshold, and their post beside God’s post; that is / when they joined their traditions / and their own inventions to God’s Commandments. Thus there was a wall between God and them; this godlessness of theirs was like a partition wall; therefore God departed from them. All who plead for that deep toleration of all kinds of opinions / they place / as much as in them lies, a partition wall between God and England.

<margin>4. Proof.</margin> Fourthly / an increase of destructive errors and heresies is a proof / that the Gospel shall be taken away. The Gospel is the Sun / which shines on our Horizon / and the heresies are like mist and fog / which darken the clear rays of the Sun. It is very well noted by one / that the Roman Church is not corrupted by damnability in manners / but only by damnability in Doctrine; one reads in Rev. 12:15. That when the Woman fled into the Wilderness / the Serpent cast out of his mouth water as a flood after the Woman, that he might cause her to be carried away thereby. This flood was nothing else than heresies / and principally the heresy of <term>Arius</term> <note>Arianism: an early Christian belief that denied the full divinity of Jesus Christ, viewed here as a historical "flood" of error.</note>.

<margin>5. Proof.</margin> Fifthly / the irreconcilable opposition against the establishment of Church-government / is a proof of the removal of the Gospel. It is true / the Government is but the enclosure / and the Gospel is the fruit; but if you break down the enclosure / then the Fruit shall be little / and the Field shall be overrun by wild Bears. It was Luther’s word / in his first departure from the Church of Rome, that the Gospel had suffered more damage through a schismatic suspension or withholding of a well-ordered government / than it could recover in forty years thereafter; and God grant / that it was not so with us.

Now from this it can appear / that we are in great danger / that the Gospel shall be taken away from us; Oh how careful ought we then to be / in using the means of grace / while we still have them among us; for if the Gospel is gone / then everything is gone; it would be better for us to lose the light of the Sun / than the light of the Gospel: for

2. If the Gospel goes away from us / then fullness goes away with the peace.

The Ark was the salvation of the Israelites / and when the Ark was taken away / then their strongest defense and salvation was taken away. When the Jews rejected the Gospel / so that it was brought over to the Gentiles, then the Romans came, and took their place / and drove out their Nation.

If then God took the Gospel from us; then we would be as Bethlehem, the least of a thousand Cities. We must not measure the greatness of a City / by the great Commerce / that is driven therein / and the great number of people / which is in it / but by the flourishing of the Gospel in the same. -># True Blessedness.<-

...the Gospel be taken away from there.

How then ought we to strive / to understand and to acknowledge, even in this our day, the things that serve our peace; so that hereafter they may not be hidden from our eyes. <note>original: "voor onsen oogen." A reference to Luke 19:42, where Jesus weeps over Jerusalem because they did not recognize the time of God's coming.</note> Indeed, how we ought not to be satisfied with the mere hearing of the Word / but we must be doers of the same / expressing the power and the authority of it in our **dealings and conduct**.

<margin>
Blessed is the man who keeps that which he hears.
</margin>
But you will easily say / if only those shall be blessed / who hear God's word and keep the same, who put into practice what they hear; who then can be saved? For who lives that can keep it / who can answer through his life / for that which he hears? I hear many sins rebuked / which I cannot avoid / I hear many duties urged / which I cannot fulfill / I hear many virtues recommended / which I cannot bring about: Well, how can anyone be blessed; since no one can keep that which you hear.

<margin>
The Word, he takes the Covenant of Grace as the will for the deed.
</margin>
I answer / if you lived under a **Covenant of Works** <note>The "Covenant of Works" is a theological term for the idea that humanity could be saved by perfect obedience to God's laws, as originally expected of Adam.</note> / then you could never be saved; because you can never keep the heard Word according to that precise measure / which is required in the Covenant of Works; for the same commands a man to keep the entire Law perfectly / and that in his own person. But know this to your comfort / that you are under a **Covenant of Grace** <note>The "Covenant of Grace" is the Christian belief that God saves people through faith and mercy rather than through their own perfect performance of the law.</note> / which requires not a perfect / but a sincere obedience to God's Law / and which **takes the will for the deed**. <note>A common 17th-century sentiment meaning God accepts the sincere intention of the heart when the person lacks the strength to complete the action.</note> Oh remember / that you are not under the Covenant of Works but of Grace / which accepts Christ's obedience and suffering for you (if you are a believer) / as if it had been done by you in your own person. It is indeed true / that Christ said to the young man / *Matthew 19:17* **If you want to enter into life, keep the commandments**, but you must know that Christ said this to him / because he was of a Pharisaic spirit and disposition / and he thought to be saved through his own good works. But if Christ said to any of us, you shall come into Heaven / if—

<column-break/>

—if you keep all the Commandments / and you shall never be saved / if you break one commandment / then we would all be lost for eternity; but Christ says / **believe, and you shall live**; the promise and not the works are the object of our faith. *Romans 4:16.* Therefore **Ambrose** <note>Saint Ambrose (c. 340–397), an influential Bishop of Milan and one of the four original Doctors of the Church.</note> was accustomed to say; *let us hope for pardon through faith, and not as a debt.* <note>original: "Veniam tanquam ex fide non ex debito speremus."</note> In a word / strive as much as is in you / to do that which you hear / bewail your inability / to fulfill God's Law / do all that you can / weep / that you cannot do better / and then God shall say; although you cannot keep the Law perfectly; yet my Son has fulfilled the same for you. I accept His obedience as your obedience / and His righteousness as your righteousness. Oh, how great a grace and mercy is here! How this can refresh your heart in the midst of all your faint-heartedness? Again, know to your comfort / that if you strive in the sincerity of your heart to keep all that you hear / then this is accepted by God just as / if you had perfectly performed the heard Word. If you labor with an inner desire of your soul / to obey God's will / and to keep His Commandments / then it is accepted by God as if it had actually been done by you. It is remarkable what is written in *Hebrews 11:17* **By faith Abraham, when he was tested, offered up Isaac, and he who had received the promises offered up his only begotten son.** Abraham did not actually and truly do it; but because he intended it in his heart, and the desire and the intention of his soul was to obey God's command; therefore it was counted in the Scripture as done. Oh, take this to your comfort you who are a Son of Abraham / and walk in his footsteps and faith; even the desires and the intentions of your heart are regarded / as if they were truly and actually performed. If you truly wish you could pray better / hear God's word better / and put the same more into practice / than you do / then this is counted by God / as if you had already done it.

->2 Peter 1 verse 10.<-

->**Therefore, brothers, be all the more diligent to make your calling and election sure.**<-

<margin>1st Sermon</margin>

<image-desc>A large decorative woodcut initial 'D' featuring a haloed figure (likely an apostle) standing in a landscape, perhaps addressing a smaller figure or infant.</image-desc>The reason and cause why I have taken these words in hand is briefly this: Having spent seventeen sermons in treating the Glory of Heaven for the <term>Elect</term><note>The "Elect" (Uitverkorenen) refers to those chosen by God for salvation according to Reformed theology.</note> and the pains of Hell for the <term>Reprobate</term><note>The "Reprobate" (Verworpenen) refers to those not chosen for salvation.</note>; I therefore deemed it very fitting to conclude these two teachings with the sequel to this subject, namely, the assurance of our Election and Calling. For if this doctrine is well-applied, you may be firmly assured in your own heart that you shall be delivered from the pains of the damned, and trust that you shall be placed in the glory of Heaven, which God has prepared for all His saints. And to that end, that you may have assurance that you shall be delivered from the one and enjoy the other; you must make it your work, according to the words of my text, to make your calling and election sure: *Only make that certain, and you are certain of Heaven.*

This is the reason why I cling to this text; and that is my concern in preaching the word: not to choose those texts which are the most lofty or difficult to study, but those which are most advantageous for you to hear; so that in this way one subject may support and strengthen the other, and being put together, might serve more for your edification and knowledge.

I shall not dwell long on the introduction: All that I have to do in treating these words are these three things.

1. To show you the aim and the connection of the words.
2. The purpose and meaning.
3. To draw from them those practical observations which naturally flow therefrom; and to apply the expanded points of doctrine.

Regarding the aim and connection of these words; you can see that the situation is as follows:

<column-break/>

Peter, who was called an <term>Apostle of the circumcision</term><note>original: "Apostel der besnijdenisse." This refers to Peter’s primary mission to the Jewish people, as described in Galatians 2:7-8.</note>; that is, an Apostle whose work and ministry it was to preach to the circumcised Jews (just as it was the ministry of Paul to preach to the uncircumcised Gentiles) writes his Epistle to the scattered Jews, who were dispersed throughout the whole world, through Pontus, Asia, Cappadocia, Galatia, and Bithynia. Notice here then, that God's people are a scattered people. And to them he writes this Letter; although they were people who lived in various places, they nevertheless held the same faith; Simeon Peter, a servant and Apostle of Jesus Christ, to those who have obtained like precious faith with us. *So you see that where the Spirit of God works in men, even though they live in different places, they shall all believe the same truth, and all receive the same faith: although they differ in language, yet there is but one God and one faith.* The Spirit of God works one and the same faith among these scattered Christians. And the Apostle, writing to these Jews, begins his Epistle, 1. by way of greeting, verse 2: "grace and peace be multiplied to you." 2. He writes by way of comfort, verse 4: of the "divine nature," that they were called to Glory. And they would enjoy all the promises of the Gospel: These were great pillars with which he helped up their hearts and strengthened them. Then thirdly, he proceeds by way of exhortation and instruction, verse 5: And that is that they should be diligent to add grace to grace. That they should make that their most particular work for which they were sent into the world, not only to obtain grace, but to increase in grace; and he begins with faith, because the same is the foundation or "Mother-grace": And this he urges through a double argument. First, in view of the benefit which shall flow to them, provided they make it their duty to labor to increase in grace, verse 8. "If these things be in you, and abound in you, they shall make you neither idle nor unfruitful in the knowledge of our Lord Jesus Christ." If you [do] your work...

# On making our effectual Calling sure.
L 4
<meta>catchword: work</meta>

...make it your work to grow in grace, you shall never be a barren or unfruitful People; but you shall grow in grace, and steadily increase in God. 2. Concerning the damage that would come to them, should they neglect this work, verse 9: *But he that lacks these things is blind, and cannot see afar off.* That is, those who lack this grace—if you do not grow in grace, you shall be so short-sighted that you shall kill your own comforts and obscure your clear evidences, so that you shall be unable to have any certainty of your salvation. And then he comes with a general exhortation to support all of this; namely, that since good arises through the addition of grace upon grace, and since such evil shall proceed if you do not do so: he brings it all together through a practical conclusion in the words of my Text: *Therefore, Brothers; be all the more diligent to make your Calling and Election sure.*

The words are not difficult, although they have indeed had their limbs broken by the <term>Papists</term><note>A historical, often derogatory term for Roman Catholics; here Love refers to the theological dispute over whether a believer can be certain of their salvation.</note>, who martyr this Text with their perverse <gloss>interpretations</gloss>. I shall only give you a brief explanatory declaration, and so come to the teachings.

**Therefore** ] so that you may see the power of the connection; it is as if the Apostle said: Since such great good arises through growing in grace, and the neglect of the same brings such great damage—not only killing your hearts, but also darkening your comforts, so that you cannot have a clear and comfortable evidence of reaching Heaven; **Therefore** be diligent to make your Calling and Election sure.

**Therefore, the more, Brothers:** ] that is, Brothers not in the Flesh, but in the Faith of Christ, embracing the same faith, keeping themselves under the same head; these the Apostle calls "Brothers."

**Therefore, Brothers, be all the more diligent:** ] The word in the Greek Language is more expressive, and signifies doing a thing sufficiently: <note>original Latin: "non agere; sed sat agere"</note> not merely to act, but to act sufficiently; not in an outward and careless manner, but to do a thing with diligence, alertness, and tirelessness of spirit; it must not be forced, but free and voluntary: **Be diligent.** The diligence that you must use concerns the soul. **Be diligent.** In what? To make your Calling and Election sure. First: I must show you what is understood by "Calling"; then by "Election": and then show you why Calling is placed before Election, since in order of time, Election precedes Calling.

1. What is understood by the **Calling**; which, so that you may understand it, you must know that there is a twofold Calling: an external and an internal Calling.

The **external Calling** is that general invitation which is made to men through the Preaching of the Gospel, inviting them to come to Jesus Christ: And the majority in the World are called by this Calling, both the good and the evil.

2. The **internal Calling** is when the Spirit of God accompanies the external ministry of the word to call the Person from ignorance to knowledge, and from the state of nature to the state of grace; and it is of this Calling that my text speaks.

<column-break/>

**Make your Calling sure:** that is, you who live under the preaching of the Gospel, be assured within yourselves that you are called thereby. **Your Calling and Election** ] **Election** is an act of God, by which He has purposed within Himself from all eternity, according to His own good pleasure and will, to bring a certain number of Men to salvation through Jesus Christ.

But now, how can it be said that we must make our Calling and Election "sure"? Does not the *Foundation of God stand sure*, as the Apostle says? And are not the gifts and Calling of God without repentance? How then must we make our Election sure, since all the decrees of God stand firm?

<margin>Answer.</margin>
Beloved, when it is said that you must make it sure, you must take it in this sense: not to make it sure on God’s side; for it cannot be made surer there than it already is; whomever He has chosen shall be glorified. But make it sure on *your* side; that is, labor to have a true, firm, and grounded assurance that you are effectually called, and that you are chosen by God in His eternal decree to regain life and Glory through Jesus Christ.

<margin>Certainty of the object, and certainty of the subject.</margin>
<note>original Latin: "Certitudo objecti, & certitudo subjecti."</note>
Therefore the Divines give this distinction: that there is a **certainty of the object**, and that is sure enough; for if God has decided to glorify you, that shall remain firm for eternity. But now, there is a **certainty of the subject**, an assurance in the Person who is chosen; and that is when you, through a reflective act of faith, have a firm conviction in your own heart that you are effectually called and eternally chosen: an assurance in your own understanding and knowledge.

Lastly: Why is the Calling placed here before the Election, since, in order of time, Election is before Calling? You are called in time through the Preaching of the Gospel; you are chosen before all time, before the foundation of the world: *Before the foundation of the world, He hath chosen us in Christ*, Ephesians 1:4. If that is so, what is the reason that Calling in my Text is placed before Election?

<margin>Answer.</margin>
To this I answer: the Calling is, in the order of words, placed before the Election, not as if it were before Election in time; but to show that we can never be sure of our Election unless God has effectually called us through the Preaching of the Gospel: and therefore the Calling is placed before the Election.

Thus I have opened to you the weightiest matters, giving you the sense of the words. The entire verse consists of two parts.

First, a particular duty is commanded in these words: *Be diligent to make your calling and election sure.*

Secondly, there is a powerful incentive here to urge you to this duty; and that is in the last words: *for doing that, you shall never stumble.*

In the commanded duty, several things are to be noted:

1. The duty itself: To make your Calling and Election sure.

2. The manner how you must put this duty into **work**

The author argues that while salvation is objectively secure in God's mind, believers must labor for subjective certainty through growth in grace.</summary>

# On our powerful...
<meta>catchword: diligence</meta>

...set to work; and that is with **diligence**; exert yourselves.

3. The **motive** to set you in motion is found in the word **therefore**.

4. Here we should note a **comparison** between this duty and all other duties; **therefore, the more**: do this rather than all other things in the world.

And finally, here is that **lovely address** through which Peter seeks to win them over to the observance of this duty, in the word **Brothers**. *Therefore, Brothers, be diligent to make your Calling and Election sure.*

From these five parts, there are five **doctrines** to be observed.

First, from the duty itself: *Make your Election and Calling sure.* Note here:
<margin>1. Doctrine.</margin> 1. That it is the most special and principal duty of a Christian, in this life, to assure his soul of this: that he is <term>effectually called</term><note>A theological term meaning a person has not just heard the Gospel, but has been inwardly moved by God to respond in faith.</note>, and eternally chosen.

Secondly, from the way and manner in which you must set this duty to work; voluntarily, or diligently; learn from this:
<margin>2. Doctrine.</margin> 2. That Christians ought to make their effectual Calling and eternal <term>Election</term><note>The concept of being chosen by God for salvation before the beginning of time.</note> sure by applying a very great **diligence** to it.

Thirdly, from the **motive** for this duty; *therefore, Brothers*. Therefore, seeing the evil that arises through carelessness and neglect of the guidance of grace; therefore, be diligent. The observation from this is:
<margin>3. Doctrine.</margin> 3. That, since such great evil arises through the neglect of the guidance of grace, it ought to powerfully bind Christians to be all the more diligent in all matters of Religion.

Fourthly, from the comparison of this duty with others: *Therefore, the more, Brothers.* That is, rather than doing any other thing, do this: make your Calling and Election sure. Learn here:
<margin>4. Doctrine.</margin> 4. That among all the occupations in the world, you should most occupy yourself with making yourself sure of Heaven through diligence. To make sure that you are effectually called and eternally chosen.

Finally, from the address used by Peter; *Therefore, Brothers*, note:
<margin>5. Doctrine.</margin> 5. That when we wish to fix an exhortation upon others toward any duty, we must labor to express an abundance of affection to them. Peter, here, when he wants to urge a duty upon the Jews, he engages with them through a lovely address, calling them **Brothers**; *Therefore, Brothers, be diligent to make your Calling and Election sure.*

But if I were to speak of these five doctrines as drawn out here, I would both confuse your memories and go against my usual style. I would rather, instead of treating the Text in that way, present the aim and content of it to you in fewer doctrines. May it please you then that I divide the words into two parts.

1. Into a duty commanded in general, and that in these words: **Be diligent**.

2. Into those expressed parts toward which our diligence must go, and that in two things. First, in making our **Calling** sure,

<column-break/>

secondly, in making our **Election** sure.

The words being thus divided, they give us two pieces of teaching.
First, from the commanded duty: *Be diligent.* Learn:
<margin>1. Doctrine.</margin> 1. That Christians, in all matters concerning the soul, ought to apply a very great **diligence**.

Secondly, from the parts toward which this duty of diligence must go; namely, in making your Calling and Election sure. Note from that:
<margin>2. Doctrine.</margin> 2. That the greatest diligence of a Christian ought primarily to be spent on this: that he assures and makes certain to his soul that he is **effectually called** and **eternally chosen**. These are the two doctrines that I shall draw from these words.

I begin with the first: that Christians, in all matters concerning the soul, ought to apply a very great diligence. In the fifth verse, the same is said: *applying all diligence.* It is as if all your special considerations ought to be regarding those things that concern your soul.

In the handling of this doctrine, I shall present you with the proofs thereof; thereafter the reasons; and then apply the same.

First, regarding the proof of it: It appears that you ought to apply a great diligence in all matters concerning the soul through those **comparisons** by which the work concerning the <term>salvation</term><note>original: "Zalicheyt"</note> of the soul is compared in the **Scriptures**, such as:
<margin>1. P.</margin> 1. The work of Christianity in the saving of the soul is sometimes compared to a **race**; <note>Hebrews 12:1</note> *Let us lay aside every weight, and the sin which so easily ensnares us, and let us run with patience the race that is set before us.* Indeed, <note>1 Corinthians 9:24, 25</note>. When you walk in your gardens or galleries, you take no trouble; but when you run in a race, you labor and struggle hard and strain all your strength to reach the end. Therefore (beloved), the matters that concern the soul are compared to running in a race, to show what labor and diligence you must apply in all meditations of the soul.
<margin>2. R.</margin> 2. It is compared to a **wrestling**; <note>Ephesians 6:12</note> *We wrestle not against flesh and blood, but against principalities, and against powers.* And so, <note>2 Timothy 2:5</note>. It has its eye upon those **Olympic games** and public pastimes where men wrestled before the common multitude. There they brought forth all their strength and skill to throw one another down; to make it known that Christianity is not a **trifle**<note>original: "gherinckwerk", meaning a minor or insignificant task.</note>, but a wrestling work, in which a great diligence must be spent.
<margin>3. R.</margin> 3. It is expressed in the Scriptures as **fighting a fight**; <note>2 Timothy 4:7</note> *I have fought the good fight.* And, as good soldiers of Christ, endure afflictions <note>2 Timothy 2:3</note>. Now, when men fight for their lives, what care, what labor, and what diligence do they apply to protect themselves? And the work of Christianity, which concerns the soul, is presented by this comparison.

4. It is compared to one who is in distress...

# Making Your Calling Sure.

...is at its utmost;
> Luke 13:24. Strive to enter through the narrow gate;

the word in the Greek language is <term>agonizesthe</term><note>original: "AGOONIZESTHE"</note>, strive, while you are in distress or agony, just as Christ was: Christ was in agony in the Garden when he sweat drops of blood; as Luke says:
> Strive and strive while you are in distress;

so that you, in turn, sweat blood in the work of your soul. Put this together: that the work of Christianity is compared to a racetrack, to a battle, to an agony, to a wrestling match, in which people exert the utmost of their strength. Let these comparisons serve to show that you must apply the greatest diligence in all matters concerning the soul.

Now, regarding the **Reasons** why you ought to be so diligent in the matters of Christianity, I shall set ten before you.

<margin>1. Reason.</margin>
1. Because diligence is required in all things concerning the body; therefore, you ought to apply much more diligence in all matters concerning the soul. Diligence is required in all things concerning the body.
> Ecclesiastes 9:10. Whatever your hand finds to do, do it with [all] your might.

And we read in Psalm 127:2 of people who rise early, and stay up late, and eat the bread of sorrows. And all to maintain the body. Now, if you must apply so much diligence and use such great care to enrich the body, how much more then for the soul? The soul is much nobler than the body. And if you must work in your earthly calling, much more must you work out your salvation. If you must labor so for the earth, much more for Heaven. If you labor to lay up treasures here, much more should you labor to lay up treasures for the hereafter. If you labor and slave away to find maintenance for a mortal and insignificant body, much more should you be diligent and take pains for a glorious and immortal soul.

<margin>2. Reason.</margin>
2. Because multitudes have been lost for eternity through a lack of applying diligence in the matter of their salvation.
> Hebrews 12:15. Looking diligently lest anyone fall short of the grace of God.

Multitudes of people have fallen away from the grace of God because they did not reach out for grace with diligence. Therefore, alas, Beloved, how many lose grace, and lose Christ, through a lack of diligence? The five foolish virgins lost Christ through a lack of diligence (Matthew 25; Luke 8:13, 14). Multitudes have lost Heaven because they sought Heaven sluggishly.
> Strive, says Christ, to enter through the narrow gate, for many will seek to enter, and they shall not be able.

Through a lack of diligence, because they only "seek" and do not "strive" on the way to Heaven, they therefore fall short and miss the same.

<margin>3. Reason.</margin>
3. Because all that you can do for your soul to make it saved is little enough. I may draw a useful point here from the passage:
> 1 Peter 4:18. If the righteous is scarcely saved...

(Although I know that in some sense this can refer only to an outward preservation), nonetheless, I can make use of it for this purpose here: if the righteous is scarcely saved, where shall the ungodly and the sinner appear? All the diligence and contemplations you can apply are barely enough, and go very

<column-break/>

little toward making your souls saved.
> Ephesians 6:13. Take up the whole armor of God, that you may be able to withstand in the evil day, and having done all, to stand.

This is a remarkable passage; it is as much as if the Apostle said: all that you can do is barely enough to remain standing. When you have done everything to stand, you can scarcely stand; and when you have done everything to obtain grace, you can scarcely obtain grace. And therefore, all the diligence you can apply in the ways of God is little enough to make your soul saved, and little enough to maintain a good confession in the ways of grace; even when you have done all you can to remain standing.
> Proverbs 4:23. Keep your heart with all diligence, etc.

<margin>4. Reason.</margin>
4. You ought to apply a great diligence in all things concerning your soul because a great labor and diligence is used *against* your soul and against your salvation; primarily by the Devil.
> 1 Peter 5:8. He walks about like a roaring lion, seeking whom he may devour.

And in Job 1, when God asked the Devil where he came from, he said, "From going to and fro on the earth, and from walking back and forth on it." The Devil is always diligent and untiring in bringing souls to damnation; he traverses the earth to damn souls. Therefore, beloved, shall the Devil put such diligence into the work of bringing your soul to damnation, and you will not use any diligence to preserve it? Shall he traverse the earth to damn you, and you will not move a foot in the established means of religion and duties to preserve your poor soul? Furthermore, just as the Devil does, so also do wicked men use diligence against your soul.
> Matthew 23:15. It is said of the Pharisees that they traveled sea and land to make one proselyte; and when he had become one, they made him twice as much a son of hell as before.

Note how untiring they are, that they are willing to undertake such a great journey to bring one poor soul to damnation. So it is with wicked men; Ephesians 4:14 says of false teachers that they "lie in wait to deceive." They are so diligent and wait for a good opportunity of time and place. Beloved, look over the world: how diligent are your companions to draw you into sin, to draw you to the tavern, and to urge you toward ungodliness? And therefore, since wicked men use such diligence to bring your soul to damnation, do you not have good reason to apply a very great diligence in all matters that concern your soul?

<margin>5. Reason.</margin>
5. Because wicked men apply such great diligence to damn their own souls, and you yourselves did the same in the days of your <term>unregeneracy</term><note>The state of a person before they have been spiritually "born again" or converted to faith.</note>. What pains does a drunkard not take to sit by his jug day and night? What pains does a thief not take to endure the darkness of the night and the cold of the weather, and the peril of being hanged, to break into a house and gain a little profit? What diligence does an adulterer use to...

# Of our powerful [effort]

...wait for a prostitute <note>The text likely refers to the "strange woman" in Proverbs 7:9 who waits in the twilight.</note> in the twilight and in the evening hour? Will the godless people (as Habakkuk speaks) waste themselves in vanity, and boast of bringing their own souls to damnation, and will you do nothing to save your soul? It is said of the godless people in Micah 7:3: *That they do evil diligently with both hands:* A person can sin enough with one hand to be damned; yet they were so vehement they wanted to sin with both hands. Shall the godless stretch out both their hands to sin, and will you not stretch out one finger toward holiness, and one hand toward the ways of God? There stands a proverb in Jeremiah 23:10: *Their course is evil and their power is not right:* A remarkable passage! God complains there about those people, that they were not only godless, but that they were violently wicked; they were strong in their wickedness, and hardworking in their godlessness: now shall godless people do violence to God to damn themselves, as it were; shall the godless be powerful in the way of sin, and will you not labor with one hand to save your soul? 

An Ancient Father <note>Likely a reference to St. Jerome or Pambo, who famously wept upon seeing a woman dressed vanity.</note>, seeing a noble lady spend three hours looking in the mirror to dress herself up, began to weep when she came down; being asked why he wept, he answered, "Because this woman has spent more hours on a single morning to bring herself to damnation than I have spent in the duties of religion to save my soul." Alas! A multitude of people are more diligent to bring themselves to damnation than many of us are to save our souls; which should then powerfully stir you to apply great diligence in matters concerning the soul.

<margin>
6. Reason.
<note>original: "Ut jugulent homines surgunt de nocte latrones" — Robbers rise in the night to kill men (Horace, Epistles).</note>

6. Because the more diligent you are, the less the stirrings of sin and the promptings of Satan will be busy and active in your spirit. It is the saying of Bernard <note>St. Bernard of Clairvaux.</note>: "The more the devil finds a man busy," he says, "the less power he will have to fix his temptations upon him." The more diligent and industrious you are in the way of Heaven, the less power the temptation of the devil will have on your soul. I still remember it was the saying of Mr. Greenham <note>Richard Greenham (c. 1535–1594), a prominent English Puritan known for his practical divinity.</note>, when the devil assaulted a poor soul and she came to him for counsel on how to resist temptation, he gave her this answer: "Never be idle but always be busy; I have also found it by my own experience, when the devil came to assault me, I said to the devil, 'I have no time now to listen to your temptations': and by that means I resisted his attacks." Beloved, say to the devil, when he tempts you, that you have no time to lend your ears to his temptation, and then he will never take hold of you. 

The devil never gains an advantage over us except when we are off the path of God, or idle, or busy with some sinful work; and then the devil gains power over us. If you once slacken in diligence, in this spiritual industriousness, you yourself invite the devil to assault you; you lay yourself open to a world full of sin and a world full of snares, just as you know it is with water:

<column-break/>

as long as the stream flows, it remains pure; but let it stand still, and it produces frogs, toads, and all sorts of filth. So too, as long as you go forward, you remain pure; but if you only once slow down in your diligence and stand still, Oh, what a pool of filth and sin your heart will become! The keys you carry in your pocket and use daily remain bright, but keys you seldom use are eaten by rust. So it is with your graces; if they are not used with diligence, they will soon rust and come to nothing; the less diligent you are, the more sin and Satan will fix themselves upon you. 

Hebrews 6:11: *We desire,* says the Apostle, *that every one of you show the same diligence:* for what purpose? *so that you do not become sluggish.* As if he said; if you once slow down in diligence, the sin of sluggishness will soon grow within you. Therefore now, the more diligent you are, the less power and activity the promptings of Satan and the workings of sin will have on your soul. *While men slept, his enemy came and sowed weeds.* Matthew 13:25. 

Just as you know it is with the body: a person whose situation requires much sitting, and who often sits, their body is subject to many bad humors <note>In historical medicine, "humors" were bodily fluids thought to control health; "bad humors" caused disease.</note> (and therefore students are subject to many diseases), but those who occupy themselves with manual labor, always moving and stirring; that movement drives out those bad humors so that they cannot settle on the body. So it stands with the soul; the less you are busy and working in matters concerning your soul, the more spiritual diseases and weaknesses will arise therein; therefore the more active and diligent you are, the less power the evil dispositions and humors will have to settle on your soul.

<margin>7. Reason.</margin>
7. Because the more diligent you are in matters concerning the soul, the more you become conformed to Jesus Christ: you read of Christ that he went about always doing good: and when his father and mother missed him, they went for three days with anxiety seeking him, and having found him, asked, "Where have you been?" "Did you not know," said Christ, "that I must be in my Father's business?" <note>Luke 2:49.</note> As if he said: "I was not out to do any evil work, but to glorify my God, and to promote the honor of my Father: that was my work." And he says elsewhere that it was his food and drink to do the will of his Father. Truly, here was a diligent Person. Therefore the more industrious and diligent you are in the things concerning the soul, the more you become like Christ, and what better pattern could there be to compare yourself to, or a better prescription for you to copy?

<margin>8. Reason.</margin>
8. Because the more diligent you are in this work, the more peace and profit it will bring to your own soul. The more peace it will bring, the more diligent you are. 2 Peter 3:14: *Be diligent,* says the Apostle, *that you may be found by Christ spotless and blameless in peace.* So too, Isaiah 32:17: *The work of righteousness shall be peace: and the effect of righteousness shall be quietness and assurance forever.* It is not the mere state or the having of grace that is peace; but it is the working and the exercising of the same; the effects thereof in your life, that bring...

# Making [your] Calling Sure.

I may say even as Solomon says in Proverbs 10:4: *The hand of the diligent makes rich.* I am certain that the hand of a diligent Christian who is industrious in the ways of God shall make him rich in grace; while those who are spiritual sluggards shall come to spiritual poverty. So in 1 Corinthians 15, the last verse: *Be steadfast, immovable, always abounding in the work of the Lord, as those who know that your labor is not in vain in the Lord.* If you then are diligent in the work of grace, it shall not be in vain, but you shall gain through all that you do in the Lord.

<margin>Reason.</margin>
9. Because in a short time you have lost more grace than you could ever win back through all the diligence you might apply, even if you lived forever. You once had all graces in Adam; but Adam, through one bite of the Forbidden Fruit, lost all that grace, which you now cannot regain through however much diligence. Even if you prayed until you could no longer speak, and even if you sighed until your loins broke; and even if every word was a sigh, every sigh a tear, and every tear a drop of blood, yet you would never be powerful enough to regain that grace which you lost in Adam. You have erased that beautiful Image of God; you lost that knowledge through the committing of one sin, which you cannot regain through ten thousand sermons, or through the performance of ten thousand duties. Do you then not have great need for diligence, seeing as you have lost so much in so little time, which you can never fully recover through all your diligence?

### 2 Peter 1:10.

->Therefore, brothers, be all the more diligent to make your calling and election sure.<-

<margin>2nd Sermon.</margin>
Having handled the doctrine of this general chapter this morning, I shall now only make a short use of it; and then proceed to the specific parts in which you ought to be diligent.

<margin>1. Use</margin>
1. Now, if it be true that in all matters concerning the soul you must apply great diligence, I must first, in applying this doctrine, proceed by way of warning, and shall thus propose four warnings, so that you do not fall into any misunderstanding regarding this teaching.

<margin>1. Warning.</margin>
First, that although God requires a great diligence from your hands in the matters of your soul, this does not presuppose that you can produce and work out this diligence through your own natural strength, but that God, commanding that power of you, must give you the strength to do what he commands. Psalm 68:28: *Your GOD has commanded your strength;* what then? Does a man therefore produce his own strength? No, but there follows a prayer: *Strengthen, O GOD, that which you have wrought in us.* Indicating that, although God commands their strength, they could not produce the same through their own power: but that they had to pray to be able to fulfill this command: "Lord you command us to be strong, Lord then strengthen that which you command." So that although God calls you to diligence, and commands strength, yet you cannot produce any strength through your own power. Augustine <note>St. Augustine of Hippo (354–430 AD), influential Christian theologian.</note> on this passage has these observations: "When I have the will (he says) to do good, I have not the power; and when I have the power, I have not the will; and in this I see my own weakness, and that I must look to Christ for strength." You could as easily carry out the work of creation by your own power as the work of conversion. You alone could as easily conquer a world full of armed men as, by your own power, [conquer] a temptation from the devil. Although God calls you to obedience, and to apply your diligence, nonetheless that does not establish that you can do it through your own strength; but that God who commands the diligence must awaken the same in you.

<margin>2. Warning.</margin>
2. When God calls you to diligence in soul-concerning matters, take heed of this warning: that you do not fulfill your duty simply by expressing a great zeal and diligence in the matters of your soul, unless you do so in a right manner, and to a right end. The people think if they can only be diligent in hearing, diligent in reading, diligent in praying, and diligent in using the Sacraments, that they then fulfill their duty and answer the command of my text to be diligent. No, Beloved, you do not answer your duty to God by expressing diligence in that which is good in itself, unless you do so in a right manner and to a right end.

<summary>This page argues that spiritual diligence is vital due to the total loss of original righteousness in Adam and the tendency of humans to waste their lives. It clarifies that such diligence is a gift from God rather than a product of human will, and must be performed with correct intentions.</summary>

<meta>This page continues a sermon regarding the necessity of spiritual diligence based on 2 Peter 1:10. The previous page established that diligence is required because of the brevity of life and the great loss of grace in the Fall of Adam.</meta>

# Of our powerful [calling]

end. You have an example in Jehu (2 Kings 10). He was a wonderfully industrious man in many good things concerning the **divine service** <note>Dutch: "Godts dienst"; refers to religious worship and duties.</note>. At one time he killed the servants of Baal; at another time he tore down the House of Baal and smashed the standing images to pieces; yet again, he called Jonadab to him to witness his zeal for the Lord. A marvelous industry! But all of this was not done in a good manner, nor for a right end. Not in a good manner, because it was only half-done and performed hypocritically. For although he broke the images of Baal, he nevertheless served the idols at Bethel. And furthermore, it was not for a right end, because he did not show or direct his zeal and industry toward the glory of God, but solely toward a **political end** <note>In this context, "political" refers to worldly power and securing his own throne.</note>, to establish himself in his kingdom (2 Kings 10:30). So it is that you may apply such industry in reading, hearing, and using the **Sacraments**, and the like; and yet, if you do not do so in a proper way and for a right end, you do not fulfill the duty of my Text. For hold this as a rule in **theology** <note>Dutch: "Godtsgeleertheydt"</note>: that when God commands a duty, all the circumstances that are inherent in that duty must be observed, or else that duty is not rightly performed. Just as when you pray, you must not leave out any circumstance or quality required in prayer, otherwise God will not accept your prayer. So here: God commands you to be diligent; if you are not diligent in a right manner and for a right end, your diligence is not right.

<margin>
3. Warning.

Necessary conditions. <note>original: "Causæ sine quibus non"</note>
</margin>

3. Although you apply ever so much industry in the matters of your soul, none of the acts you perform are **meritorious**. You do not obtain Heaven through praying, nor through reading, nor through hearing, although you perhaps will not obtain Heaven without them. Good works may be **causes of salvation** in this sense: they are **necessary conditions** <note>original: "oorsaecken, sonder welcke"; literally "causes without which [one cannot be saved]." This is a classic distinction in Reformed theology between the "merit" of Christ and the "necessity" of holiness.</note> without which you cannot be saved; for all your obedience and all your industry are not the causes *on account of which* you are saved, or which in any way move God to save you. So, although you may be ever so diligent, this industry is not in the least bit meritorious. Why? Because, to make a thing meritorious, the **theologians** say three things must concur: First, it must be done voluntarily, not as a debt. Second, it must be done by a person's own natural power, not by a borrowed power. Third, it must be done perfectly. And therefore the theologians say (and with good reason) that all our obedience and all our acts in the ways of grace cannot be meritorious. Why?

Because, first, we do not perform them as a voluntary gift, but as a proper debt: we owe God this industry and duty, and therefore it cannot "earn" anything, because we are only paying God what is His. If you lent someone money, would you thank him and reward him for giving you back your own? No; it belongs to you, and he must give it back. All duties in matters of the soul belong to God by right, and therefore they cannot be meritorious.

<column-break/>

Secondly, if you could produce this industry through your own strength, you would have something to boast about; but all your industry is produced by a borrowed power—by a strength that flows from Jesus Christ, by a power of the **Covenant of Grace**. It is from there that you draw the strength to fulfill the acts of obedience and spiritual industry.

Thirdly, it cannot merit because it is not perfect. Indeed, it is so far from the case that you would merit anything through your obedience, that you deserve nothing but Hell because of the lack found in your obedience and the imperfections that remain in your best religious services.

<margin>
4. Warning.
</margin>

4. Take this as a warning: although all the industry you can apply is not meritorious before God to save you, nevertheless hold this as the truth: the more you overflow in spiritual industry in the matters of your soul, the more you shall likewise receive a more perfect joy and increase of grace in your soul. *To him who has shall be given, and he shall have in abundance.* That is, to him who has well-employed and used his graces, an abundance shall be given; *You have been faithful over a few things, I will set you over many.* The more you labor and the more diligent you are in the matters of your soul, the more you shall excel and grow in grace above others. It is an observation that a certain author has regarding the **Apostle Paul**: Paul was the most excellent of all the Apostles; no Apostle was like Paul, and no one surpassed him. Now, the theologians investigate the reason why Paul was more excellent than all the other Apostles—who saw Christ in the flesh, whereas Paul saw Him only in a vision and nothing more—and yet Paul was more excellent than any other Apostle. They give this reason: that Paul was more abundant in labor. Paul was more diligent in bringing forth his gifts and graces, and God blessed that industry with a greater increase of the graces of God's Spirit than the others had. So, although God does not give us Heaven *because* we grow in grace, nevertheless God ordinarily bestows a greater measure and increase of gifts upon those who use them well while they are in this world. *Open your mouth wide, and God will fill it.* The wider we are in our desires and expectations, the more we shall be filled.
