# Christ is the Life

...someone [perform] any virtuous work from an internal principle of grace? I answer:

1. If someone does something good from an internal seed of grace, then there is a natural pull and desire in his heart toward all virtues; someone who performs a good work only from an outward principle will perhaps perform some virtues, but he will not want to perform them all; those virtues which involve more **self-denial**, more difficulty and danger, he can never bring himself to do, for it is not out of love for virtue, but out of self-love that he does something good. But someone who performs any good work from an internal principle has a desire for all virtues in his heart.

2. He sees a lovely beauty in every virtue; many people can indeed do good works where they nevertheless notice nothing—they see no beauty in it at all, but rather profit, and that is why they practice them: but he who works from an internal principle sees a lovely beauty in grace, and therefore he loves it, and therefore he walks in it.

3. He carries in his heart a burning affection for virtue, because of the innate luster and beauty he sees therein; therefore love drives him to obtain and practice virtue. And now I pray you all this day: Through the Lord, examine your hearts, and notice whether you stand or fall by this test, whether you can say that *Jesus Christus* is your life.

Secondly, you can know whether you have this life of grace or not by what accompanies this life.

First, wherever the life of grace is, there the power of sin is nullified and put to death, *Colossians 3:3*. <note>original: "Col. 3. 3."</note> *You are dead*, namely to sin; the power and the ability of sin was brought under subjection in them; likewise *Romans 6 verse 11*. <note>original: "Rom. 6. vers 11."</note> *Even so consider yourselves also to be dead indeed unto sin, but alive unto God in Christ Jesus our Lord.* If sin reigns in you, etc., then you have no life of grace.

Secondly, wherever the life of grace is, there one is dead to the world, *Galatians 2 verse 20*. <note>original: "Gal. 2. vers 20."</note> *I live, yet not I, but Christ lives in me*, etc. Then one does not dwell on the things of this world; one is not preoccupied with them. Just as a dead man pays no heed to delightful pleasure, to magnificent displays, etc. If you still live continually for the world, if you still set your heart on these earthly things, then the life of grace is not in you.

Thirdly, wherever the life of grace is, there is also love for those who are partakers of that same grace of life; every creature loves most that creature which lives the same life as itself, so must all Christians also do. *1 John 3 verse 14*. <note>original: "1 Joh. 3. vers 14."</note> *We know that we have passed from death unto life, because we love the brothers.*

Now, to conclude everything in an application for the exercise of **Godliness**.

First, is it so, that *Jesus Christus* is the cause and worker of a Christian's life? This can then serve to condemn all those who are outside of Christ, who

<column-break/>

have no true right or part in *Jesus Christus*; you who are Christ-less people, you are dead people and shall also be damned people, because there is no life except in *Jesus Christus*.

Secondly, if Christ is the cause of your spiritual life, then that serves to reject the **Pelagians**, <note>Followers of Pelagius, a 5th-century theologian who argued that humans have the natural ability to fulfill divine commands without needing special biological or spiritual assistance from God; the author here argues against this "human-centered" view of salvation.</note> who contend that they are powerful by nature to work the deed of grace in their hearts; this teaching goes against those who think that the hand of nature is strong enough to work this life of grace in the soul.

Thirdly, if Christ is your life, then this serves as great comfort to you who do have this life of grace in your hearts, but nonetheless find some decay in that spiritual life; you who are in that miserable state in which God’s Church was, *Revelation 3 verse 2*. <note>original: "Openb. 3. vers 2."</note> *Strengthen the things which remain, that were ready to die.* Many of you have this seed of life, but perhaps only in a weak and declining form: well, even if you wither in your branches, you shall never wither in your root; *Jesus Christus*, the **root of Jesse**, <note>A biblical title for the Messiah, referring to King David's father, Jesse, symbolizing the lineage and enduring nature of Christ's authority.</note> is your root; this root has enough sap to share with all its branches; this head has enough spirit to distribute to all the members; fear not then. If Christ be the root and cause of your life, then you shall never die: you may come to weakness and withering, but you shall never die, because *Jesus Christus* is your life.

When I began to treat these words, I gave you the objective and the meaning; I gave you the parts to be observed and the teachings that flow therefrom, which were three. I said that a Christian's life is twofold: the **life of grace**, which we call **sanctification**; and the **life of glory**, called **glorification**. Of both of these, *Jesus Christus* is the cause. The first part I have finished handling, namely the life of grace.

Now I pass over to the second step of this doctrine: That *Jesus Christus* is not only our life in the sense that he works the life of grace in us, but that he is also our life in a second sense, so that he brings us to eternal life, the **life of glory**.

<meta>This page continues the sermon on the "life of a Christian," shifting the focus specifically to the "life of glory" (the afterlife in heaven) and how Jesus Christ serves as the sole source and cause of that eternal state.</meta>

gravity and truth regarding this matter. If the Sun blinds the eyes of those who look upon it, how much more shall that glory do so, which is ten thousand times clearer and brighter. Many engage in so much dispute and labor concerning this glory that they are often carried away so far that, before they can return, they drown in a labyrinth of error. It is a good saying of Gregory in his *Moral Sayings* <note>original: "Zeede-spreucken," referring to the *Moralia in Iob* by Pope Gregory the Great</note>: when a mortal man speaks of the coming eternal glory, it is as if a man born blind were disputing about light which he has never seen. So difficult and dangerous it is to set out deep into this sea. I shall not stand long on the instruction of this matter; I shall only explain, prove, and apply it.

First, regarding the explanation, two things are to be noted here.

1. What this life of glory is. 2. How Jesus Christ is the cause of that life of glory which the believers shall have in Heaven.

First, What is this life? To answer, this description serves: it is the glorious and blessed state which God, through Christ in His pure grace, has provided for all the <term>elect</term> <note>Those chosen by God for salvation</note> after the day of judgment, whereby their bodies shall be raised from the grave, and body and soul shall be glorified in a perfect communion, with the enjoyment of God the Father, Son, and Holy Spirit; and all the Saints and Angels in Heaven in eternity. This is glory in a general description. Many questions can be handled regarding this, such as the glorification of body and soul, and the degrees of the same, which shall more fittingly be addressed in the final teaching.

Secondly, How is Jesus the cause of that glorified life that the elect shall have in Heaven?

1. He is the **efficient cause** <note>The "acting cause" or the one who brings the effect into being</note> of this blessed state. Hebrews 5 verse 9: *He became the author of eternal salvation unto all them that obey him.* Eternal life and eternal salvation are one, of which the Apostle says that He is the cause. Likewise John 10 verse 28: *I give unto them eternal life; and they shall never perish, neither shall any man pluck them out of my hand.*

2. Jesus is the **meritorious cause** <note>The one who earned or deserved the reward on behalf of others</note> of this life; that is, through His shameful death He has obtained and deserved a glorious life for all the elect; therefore one reads Romans 5 verse 21: *That through Christ this life is acquired.* 1 John 5 verse 11: *God hath given to us eternal life, and this life is in his Son;* that is, it is given to us through the merit of His Son; He suffered a shameful death and has obtained a life of glory for the elect.

3. Christ is the **preparatory cause**; therefore He is said to be the cause because He prepares this glorified state for us, and prepares us for that state. First, it is He who prepares this glorified state for us. John 14 verse 3: *I will go to prepare a place for you,* (that is, to prepare for you this glorious state, 

<column-break/>

Heaven,) *that where I am, there ye may be also.* So also Matthew 25 verse 34: *Come, ye blessed of my Father, inherit the kingdom prepared for you.* Christ is then the cause of this state, since He prepares it for us. Secondly, not only so, but He also prepares us for that glorious state. Colossians 1 verse 12: *Giving thanks unto the Father, which hath made us meet to be partakers of the inheritance of the saints in light.* So Jesus Christ is also the cause who makes us fit for this glorious state. Therefore one reads, 2 Timothy 2 verse 21: *You are vessels made unto honor,* <note>original: "vaten ghermaeckt ter eeren"</note> that is, you are vessels ordained for Heaven; but how does this happen? He has sanctified you, and made you fit for the Master's use, and prepared you for every good work. If the Lord God brought a godless person into Heaven, Heaven would be a Hell to him; for he who does not love grace on earth shall not love it in Heaven either. Therefore, just as God must prepare Heaven for man, so must He also prepare man and make him fit for Heaven; and therein lies the happiness of his state.

4. Christ is the **promising cause** of this life, because He has promised it to all His elect, 1 John 2 verse 25: *And this is the promise that he hath promised us, even eternal life.*

Secondly, as proof of the Doctrine, I shall give you two or three scriptural texts (in the mouth of two or three witnesses shall every word be established); John 17 verses 1, 2: *Father, the hour is come; glorify thy Son, that thy Son also may glorify thee: As thou hast given him power over all flesh, that he should give eternal life to as many as thou hast given him.* As many as God the Father has given to Jesus Christ through election, so many does He give Heaven through redemption. Likewise, 1 John 5 verses 11, 12: *This is the record, that God hath given to us eternal life, and this life is in his Son.* That is: This life comes from Jesus, and it is obtained for us by Him and by no one else. And 1 Peter 5 verse 10: *The God of all grace, who hath called us unto his eternal glory by Christ Jesus.* God wills to have the grace to call each of us to Heaven; but this is only through Jesus Christ, so that He is the cause of all our glory. But this point is not so much to be spoken of through deep speculation and contemplation, as it is to be laid down for an active application. Therefore I shall bring it to some uses in the practice of godliness.

If it be so, that Jesus Christ is the cause of a Christian's life of glory, then two kinds of use follow from this, namely: 1. Of instruction. 2. Of examination.

First, For instruction, and so I shall draw eleven consequences from this doctrine which serve for practice.

First, If Jesus is the cause of your eternal and glorious life, which you [shall have] in

# Christ is the life

...you shall have Heaven / ☙ then strive to glorify Jesus while you are here in this world. This is more than reasonable / for as Christ becomes a Mediator for that purpose, and comes into the world for that end, to bring you to glory / and to be your life / so it is indeed right / that you should employ this small part and span of your life here / to glorify Jesus Christ. We read the reason / which Jesus used with his Father / as to why his Father should receive him in glory / read John 17 verse 4, 5.

Here Jesus makes this the basis of his reasoning / why he should be glorified by his Father with the glory that he had. Well / O Father / I have glorified you on the earth. Beloved / can you bring this proof before God / when you must die? Can you go to God like Jesus Christ / and on the same grounds desire glory from him? Can you say / Father I have glorified you on the earth? I have given you honor in my various states as Father or Son / Authority or Subject / etc. I have glorified you in my duties / I have glorified you in my confession of Religion? Can you say that you have thus glorified him on the earth? What glory have you brought to him who sought glory for you? Jesus made this a foundation / upon which he claimed glory in Heaven from his Father. This is the first consequence / if Christ has acquired a life of glory for you / then you are bound / to conduct your life in such a way / that you glorify Christ while you live in this world. And if you ask me / *How so*? Christ himself answers it / *Herein is my Father glorified that you bear much fruit*, John 15 verse 8. When you are fruitful under the use of the established <term>religious observances</term> <note>original: "Godts-dienst-pleeghingh," referring to the formal practices and sacraments of the church</note> / then you glorify the Father and Jesus Christ.

Secondly, if Jesus is the cause of your glorified life in Heaven / then turn your eyes to the discourtesy of your conduct regarding Jesus Christ / since you have lived in this world; Jesus is the cause of your life / but you have been the cause of his death. Jesus is the cause of your glory / but your sins have been the cause of his shame: You are ashamed of him here on earth / and he is not ashamed to make you appear before his Father and all the Saints and Angels in Heaven: You place a crown of thorns on Christ's head / but Christ lays a crown of glory on your head: You value the earth too much for Christ / not wanting to let him live here / and Christ does not value Heaven too much for you. If Christ has obtained a glorified life for you / oh then learn to cast your eyes on your discourtesy toward Jesus Christ / and let that work within you / and this shall cause your heart to melt in repentance and sorrow.

A certain King hearing this when he was called to reign over this People / was not <term>profligate</term> <note>original: "guyt-achtig," implying a rogue-like or wasteful spending of resources</note> with his income during that year in which he reigned / but gathered all the treasure that he could collect / and sent it to that place to which he would be banished / so that in that year of his reign he provided for himself with that / by which he would live with comfort all his life thereafter. Now remember while you live here to lay something up for the life of your exile / you are not here to rule for long / but to be banished from here. Therefore lay up provisions / for the time to come / and the future life / which you shall obtain in glory; work while it is day / the night comes when no man can work.

->of a Christian.<-

**Fifthly**, If Jesus Christ is the Author and cause of this glorious life / that must teach you to be always panting and longing for this glorious state during your natural life / and to desire all refreshments and comforts in light of it / for they are in no way to be compared to the invaluable blessings and happiness of this state. It is the saying of Augustine <note>original: "Augustini"</note>; that everyone who considers the happiness of eternal life / and the eternity of that blessed life / shall find an earnest longing for that same state kindled in his soul. I recall the saying of Pliny <note>original: "Plinii"</note> concerning a bird he calls a Bird of Paradise <note>In the 17th century, it was commonly believed that Birds of Paradise lacked feet and lived entirely in the air, never touching the "unclean" ground.</note> / and he explains the characteristics of this bird / that it cannot bear to fall upon the ground / but it always wants to alight upon the highest trees / and seldom or never upon the lowly earth / and therefore it is called by him a Bird of Paradise. Once, this bird was captured / and being tied fast by its leg / the historian says that it mourned night and day because it could not fly upward. Beloved / you are the sons of Paradise / here you are tied down with many obstacles / and are hindered and burdened with many temptations and various lusts / so that when you wish to go upward to your God and Savior / you are kept down by these things here below / you cannot lift up your spirit: now do as this bird did / mourn night and day / panting and longing for this glorious state / being a state of glory / obtained through Jesus Christ.

**Lastly**, if Jesus Christ is the Author of this glorious life / then beware of doing anything in this world / that might dishonor your glorious state / which you shall one day have through Christ Jesus / while you are here in the world. Alexander <note>Alexander the Great</note>, when he was invited to run a race among the common crowd / gave this answer / "It befits a King’s Son only to keep company with the sons of Princes in their exercises" / and thus he stood upon his birthright / and would not dishonor his Father nor his birth and princely nature / by mixing himself among the common people. **First**, Beware of falling into scandalous sins. Oh, how unbecoming is that for that glorious state! This is to change your honor into shame. Scandalous sins in those who shall be heirs of glory are like spots on a clean garment. Touch nothing unclean / you who expect that God shall receive you.

**Tenthly**, Christ is the cause of this glorified life! Oh, then glorify the riches of grace and mercy that are in Jesus Christ. Here is incomparable grace / that Christ brings life to you / who brought death to him! That Christ gives glory to you / who brought shame upon him! It is told of the **Elephant** <note>This refers to a common medieval and early modern belief, found in bestiaries, that elephants lacked joints in their legs or backs and could not get up if they fell.</note> / that because it lacks a bone in its back / if it falls / it cannot stand up / but must perish and die there; Once an elephant while sleeping fell down and could not get up / but lay there struggling to get up for the preservation of its life / and could not; a traveler on the road seeing this had pity on the creature / and did his best and helped him up. The elephant, by the instinct of Nature / to repay the man’s kindness / followed the man until his dying day; and the historians say that when this man died / the elephant went to lie on his Master’s grave / and died where his Master died. This elephant represents the fallen **Adam** <note>In Christian theology, "Adam" represents all of humanity in its fallen, sinful state.</note>, and all of us fallen in Adam / and that fall caused all our bones to break / we could never stand up by our own strength; now Christ / the **Good Samaritan** <note>The author blends the parable of the Good Samaritan with the fall of man; Christ is the traveler who rescues the helpless.</note> approached / and seeing us broken by our fall / stretched out his helping hand / and raised us from the state of death to a state of life. If the elephant wanted to repay the man’s goodness / oh, what shall you repay Christ / since you would have fallen into Hell / if he had not offered the helping hand? Oh, cling to Christ and love him / who is the cause of such a glorious life.

->So much has been said for Instruction.<-

The second **Benefit** <term>Nuttigheyt: A common sermon structure where the preacher explains the practical "uses" or "benefits" of a doctrine.</term> is for **testing**; I know that the deceitfulness of the heart is such / that it can immediately accept the comforting teachings / while turning a deaf ear to the threats and rebukes. Now, so that you are not lulled to sleep / and think / that you / who have hearts of iron / are vessels of honor / and that you / who are ashamed of Jesus Christ on earth / shall appear in glory with the Angels before God the Father on the day of judgment. So that you do not deceive yourselves / and think you shall partake of this glorious life / when you shall not / I shall present these hallmarks from the Scripture / by which you can assure your hearts / that you are those who shall have a glorified life through Jesus Christ.

**First**, If you are to have a part in this glorified life / then God the Lord will make you, before your death, have **repentance** <note>original: "berouw"</note> for all the evil you have done / during this your sinful life on earth. Acts 11, verse 18. *And when they heard these things, they were satisfied, and glorified God, saying: Then hath God also to the Gentiles granted repentance unto life.* Note / God has given life / that is salvation / being the state spoken of here. And on what condition? God has given repentance unto life. No life of glory is prepared for those who have no repentance for their sinful life. Therefore, oh you bold sinners / who have a forehead of brass and a neck of iron / whose hearts are like a Diamond / which cannot be pierced and wounded by all the sins of your life / for God has given the Gentiles repentance unto life: In this life you must first have repentance / if you expect glory in the life to come.

**Secondly**, You must **believe**. Acts 13, verse 48. *And as many as were ordained to eternal life believed,* and John 20, verse 31. *These are written, that ye might believe that Jesus is the Christ, the Son of God; and that believing ye might have eternal life through his Name.* Through Christ’s tears no life is to be obtained except through believing / therefore you who lie in the state of unbelief / cannot expect / that you shall have this life of glory through Jesus Christ.

**Thirdly**, Those who shall partake of this life / bear an unfeigned love for all those who shall enjoy this life of glory with them. 1 John 3, verse 14. *By this we know that we have passed from death unto life, because we love the brethren.* To love the Brethren is not a cause / but a sign that they were translated from death into life / that is from the state of sin to the obtaining of eternal life through Jesus Christ. Therefore you who carry an old grudge in your hearts against the godly / because they are godly; in that respect / if you live and die in that state / then you cannot expect that you shall have a glorious life with Christ Jesus; For how can you expect to live with them in glory / who, living here, quarrel with those / who are heirs of glory.

# Christ is the Life

<columns>
**Fourthly**, this glory is also tied to this condition / namely the saving knowledge of Jesus Christ. John 17, verse 3: *And this is life eternal, that they might know thee the only true God, and Jesus Christ, whom thou hast sent.* This is eternal life in two ways. 1. It is eternal life by connection / it is the beginning of glory / grace is the childhood of glory / and glory is the old age of grace. 2. It is eternal life by confirmation; if you know Christ for salvation / it can be a seal of confirmation for you / that you shall have eternal life through Jesus Christ; for *this is eternal life, to know*, that is / this gives us assurance of eternal life / if you know him in a saving way.

**Fifthly**, if you have a conscientious care / to walk in obedience and conformity with Christ / while you live in this world / then you have a seal for your heart / that you shall have a glorified life through Jesus Christ. 1 John 3, verses 2 and 3: *Beloved, now are we the sons of God, and it doth not yet appear what we shall be; but we know that, when he shall appear, we shall be like him* (just as in my text / *we shall appear with him in glory*) and what then? *And every man that hath this hope in him purifieth himself, even as he is pure.* That is / he who hopes to have this glorified life through Jesus Christ / everyone who looks forward to that state / desires to purify himself / just as Christ is pure / according to his ability and measure. Wherever Christ is the cause of this life / there he will work a conscientious care / to be conformed and obedient to him in this life. A similar excellent saying is found in Hebrews 5, verse 9: *He became the author of eternal salvation unto all them that obey him*, and also for no one else. And therefore, beloved / all of you / who take no care how you live / what sins you commit / what duties you neglect / what company you keep / what course you hold / hear this as if from God / you can have no pledge for your Soul that you shall have a life of glory through Jesus Christ.

**Sixthly**, those who, through the power of mortification <term>mortification: from the Latin 'mortificatio', the spiritual practice of "killing" or subduing the power of sin in one's life</term>, bring down the dominion and activity of sin in their hearts / they have a seal of glory in the world to come; This is set forth in the words / that precede my text. Colossians 3, verse 3: *Ye are dead, and your life is hid with Christ in God; when Christ, who is our life, shall appear, then shall ye also appear with him in glory.* Wherein the Apostle makes this a mark of those / who shall possess eternal life through Christ / that they are dead persons; dead / what is that? Not a natural death / for those to whom he spoke were still living; but they were dead to sin / sin had no power over them. Romans 6, verse 11: *Dead indeed unto sin, but alive unto God.* Through the power of mortifying grace, the supremacy of sin was taken away in them / and because they were thus dead / so this was to them

<column-break/>

a proof / that when Christ should be revealed / they also would appear with him in glory. I pray you / look over these conditions / which I have now presented / but do not misunderstand me; I do not say that these are the *causes* / for which you shall be glorified / but they are *required things* / without which you shall never be glorified.

When I first took up these words / I made known to you their sense and explanation. The observations flowing from them were three. I. That Jesus Christ is the life of a Christian; this I have finished / I proceed to the second / which is noteworthy here in the next words; namely, *Christ shall be revealed.*

But before I can draw the doctrine from it / I shall open the words. What is understood here by this revelation of Jesus Christ? So that you may know this / I shall first say what it is *not*. The revelation of Christ in glory in this text is not understood in the Jewish sense: The Jews believe that the revelation of Christ and the promises / which are in the Scriptures regarding it / refer to their promised Messiah in the flesh / and that he, as their temporal King, shall reign among them on earth in glory and Majesty. But this revelation of Christ in the flesh is already past / and shall not happen now / therefore in this sense it cannot be allowed. 2. The revelation of Christ cannot be understood in the sense of the Millenarians <term>Millenarians: those who believe Christ will return to establish a physical kingdom on earth for a literal thousand years</term>, that is / those who hold that Christ shall personally appear on earth for a thousand years / and live among his people / and that they shall see him face to face / and deal with him familiarly / as a man with his friend; since it says here / that when Christ shall be revealed / we also then shall appear with him in glory; Now / those who hold this belief / that Christ shall appear on earth / do not claim / that this is the time of the glorification of all the elect. But 3. by this is understood that glorious revelation of Jesus Christ on earth / at the time when he shall come on the last day to judge the living and the dead / those who shall be living on that day of judgment / and those who shall already be dead before that day; that coming to judgment is understood by his revelation in glory; That this is so / is evident because in the Scriptures the revelation of Christ in glory and the judging of the world are placed together / as being one and the same thing at the same time / as in Matthew 24, verses 30 and 31: *They shall see the Son of man coming in the clouds of heaven with power and great glory* (just as in my text) and when shall this be? *And he shall send his angels with a great sound of a trumpet, and they shall gather together his elect from the four winds.* So then, this appearance of Christ in glory refers to that time /

I begin with the first, namely what it is / that makes Christ's appearing so glorious. I answer / these eight special things come together / and make Christ’s appearing to judge the world so glorious. 1. The excellence and beauty of Christ's person. 2. His Princely attendants. 3. The breadth of Christ's authority <term>authority/awe</term> <note>original: 'ontzach', implying both terrifying power and the respect it commands</note>. 4. The fairness of Christ's dealings. 5. The acclamations and admiration of the elect. 6. The darkening and eclipses of the world’s glory. 7. Christ’s wonderful swiftness / in discerning the thoughts of the hearts of men. 8. First, that which makes Christ's appearing to judge the world so glorious is the excellence of Christ's person. pressed image of God and the reflection of the Father's glory; every grace in Christ Jesus gives greater luster / than the glisten of a Diamond before the Sun / indeed it is more gloriously shining / than the Sun itself / shining at noon. Secondly, the Royalty of his attendants makes Christ's appearing so glorious; when Christ comes to judge the world / he shall have his Princely attendants / to accompany him in a glorious and Royal manner. So it is with Jesus Christ / God the Father has given him the whole world to be judged by him. *John* 17. verse 2. *Behold, the Father hath given him power over all flesh*: and *John* 5. verse 22. *The Father judgeth no man, but hath committed all judgment unto the Son.* And 2 *Cor.* 5. verse 10. *We must all appear before the judgment seat of Christ; that every one may receive the things done in his body, according to that he hath done, whether it be good or bad.* This then must make Christ’s appearing glorious / that he is Judge

**Fourthly**, The equity of Christ’s proceedings at the time when he shall appear for judgment; Jesus Christ will work with such impartiality and equity / that the most wicked men will not be able to open their mouths against him. # Of a Christian

...until the Lord shall have come, who also will bring to light what was hidden in darkness, and reveal the counsels of the heart. When Christ shall come to judgment, he will make known what now lies hidden in darkness: your deceptions and lusts, and all that you are guilty of. Christ has a marvelous skill for knowing and seeing everything that falls under his judgment; he cannot be moved by delays nor deceived by secrets.

**Eighthly**, the speed which Christ will show in dispatching all those great matters of that Day of Judgment; Christ will have no postponement of time, like earthly Judges who must sit for a set duration and no longer, even if they have perhaps not finished half of their work; but Jesus Christ will have the ability to dispatch it in a wonderfully short time; Christ will very quickly make an end. If Christ needed a long time to judge the world, it would be a proof that Christ did not know the matter, or could not say what judgment he should pronounce over the known deed; neither of which can be applied to Christ, *1 Cor. 15 verses 51, 52.* Thus you see what it is that makes Jesus Christ so glorious when he shall come to judge the world.

**Secondly**, I shall give you the reasons why Christ will appear so gloriously: and I will bring forward only these three for this purpose.

**First**, it is God the Father's good pleasure that Jesus Christ in his second appearance shall be so glorious, to take away that contempt and scorn which was cast upon Christ in his first appearance; Christ first appeared in the form of a servant <note>Original: *gedaante van een dienstknecht*, a reference to Philippians 2:7, describing Christ’s humility as a human</note>, but in his second coming he shall appear in the Majesty of a King. In his first coming he appeared in contempt in a manger; in his second coming he will appear in glory in the clouds; in his first appearance he had only beasts as his companions; in his second appearance he will have Saints and Angels as his attendants. In his first appearance he was despised by all, *Isaiah 53 verse 2*: *We saw in him no form or glory* <note>Original: *Heerlykheydt*</note>; in his second appearance he will be wondered at by all because of that very glory. Thus then Christ shall have a glorious appearance, to wipe away that contempt which people did to him in his first coming into the world.

**Secondly**, Jesus Christ will be very glorious in his second appearance to take away that scorn and dishonor that people have done to his people; here, people scorn the believers as if religion were only an imagination, as if Hell were only a bogeyman <note>Original: *bulle-bak*, a folk monster used to frighten children</note>, and Heaven only a dream, as if the Day of Judgment were only a doctrine to make people afraid. God’s children are considered small in this world, as if they did not know whom they served or where they were going; their life is reckoned dishonorable and their death miserable. Now Jesus Christ will take away this scorn from his people; he will make it known to the world that Christ their head, in whom they have believed, whom they have served, through whose blood they were bought,

<column-break/>

whose name they glorified, and whose commandments they obeyed, will give them such a reward <note>Original: *vergelding*, meaning a just recompense</note> that the world will know they have not done this in vain; For just as Christ their Head is a glorified Head, so shall the members, according to their measure, also share with him in that glory; And this will wonderfully take away the disdain that lies on the heads of God's children, *1 Peter 2 verse 7*: *To you who believe, he is precious*: the word is more powerful in the Greek; *For you who believe, he is an honor and glory*, so that I may say: Beloved, since Christ is a glorious Christ, and will come in glory to judge the world, so through this Christ becomes an honor and glory for all of you who believe.

**Thirdly**, Jesus Christ appears so gloriously to inflict a greater terror, conviction, and torment upon the godless. It will bring them fear, that Christ, whom they wounded, wronged, and despised, is a person so entirely glorious. It will convict them, because they did not consider the ways of Christ glorious, the person of Christ lovely, nor the ordinances of Christ respectable, when they shall see that those who most honored and glorified Christ are now with him in glory. It will also cause them torment that this Christ, whom they blasphemed and cast out of the world, and those Saints, whom they could not bear on earth, are now glorified together in Heaven. All this will greatly pain the godless, and for these reasons then Jesus Christ, when he comes to judge the world, will appear in glory.

The utility which this doctrine will give is threefold: namely, for reproof, for direction, and for comfort.

**First**, it serves for reproof. Is it so, that Christ’s appearance to judge will be so glorious? Then I may, by the power of this point, drive the nail of terror into the heads and hearts of eight kinds of people, for whom this doctrine is very fearsome. And here I pray you, Beloved, if you fall under one of these sorts, then take the damnation and terror to heart.

The Scripture says, *Luke 9 verse 26*: *Whoever shall have been ashamed of me, of him will I be ashamed before my Father and the holy Angels in Heaven.* O Beloved, Christ’s appearance in glory on the last day will be fearsome for you who have no desire to confess and embrace Jesus Christ. But you will say, "This does not concern me; why should I be ashamed of Jesus Christ? Far be it from me! I love Christ with all my heart, and I wish him well, and I would that they were in Hell who do not do so." Would this damnation touch me? Well, pay attention to the...

Hell shall Christ then plunge those who threw his children into prison? And if Jesus Christ shall send those down to Hell who did not clothe his children when they were naked, into what kind of Hell shall Christ then cast those who, when his children have but a little to wear, destroy and take everything away—clothes, food, house, and wife, and everything? If a lack of mercy shall damn men on the day of judgment, what then shall cruelty and unmercifulness do?

**3.** The day of Christ’s glorious appearance to judge the world shall be a terrible day—for whom? For all those who lead a carnal <note>fleshly or worldly</note> and excessive life, seldom or never thinking of the account they must give to Jesus Christ at his appearance,

<margin>Luke 17 verses 26, 27.</margin>
Luke 17 verses 26, 27: *And as it was in the days of Noah, so shall it be also in the days of the Son of man.* How was it then? *They did eat, they drank, they married wives, they were given in marriage, until the day that Noah entered into the ark, and the flood came, and destroyed them all.* Just as they were drowned and perished by the coming of the flood, so shall Christ by his coming make a terrible day for those whom he finds entirely swimming in carnal and sensory lusts and pleasures. To seek carnal desires and the pleasures of the world is a state and temper of the Spirit that makes the heart utterly unfit for any serious thoughts of Christ’s coming.

<margin>Luke 21 verse 34.</margin>
Luke 21 verse 34: *And take heed to yourselves, lest at any time your hearts be overcharged,* etc. Therefore one sees in the Scripture that when Jesus Christ shall come to judge, he will specifically come against those who lie drowned in carnality and pleasure.

<margin>2 Peter 2 verses 9, 10.</margin>
2 Peter 2 verses 9, 10: *The Lord knoweth how to deliver the godly out of temptations, and to reserve the unjust unto the day of judgment to be punished.* Note: the Lord knows how to keep the bodies in the graves and the souls in Hell until the day of judgment. But who? *But chiefly them that walk after the flesh in the lust of uncleanness.* Those above all. You who gladly waste your days in banqueting (which is but fuel for lust), who live in a carnal way, giving free rein <note>Original: *de bolle toom*, meaning to let loose the bridle</note> to the sight of your eyes and the desires of your heart in sensory pleasures; what are you doing other than making yourselves a tastier morsel one day for worms and devils? Let me say to such people what **Solomon** said to the

<margin>Ecclesiastes 11 verse 9.</margin>
young man who wallowed in carnal pleasures, Ecclesiastes 11 verse 9: *Rejoice, O young man...* and *but know thou...* and note it well: the day of Christ's coming for judgment shall be a terrible day for you.

**4.** This day of judgment shall be terrifying for all who live and die without a sincere love for Jesus Christ;

<margin>1 Corinthians 16 verse 22.</margin>
read 1 Corinthians 16 verse 22: *If any man love not the Lord Jesus Christ, let him be Anathema Maranatha.* Let him be **Anathema**, that is, accursed; and then let him be **Maranatha**. (This is a Chaldean <note>Original: *Chaldeeusch*, referring to Aramaic</note> term composed of two words, and signifies in the Chaldean language: *Maran*, "Lord," and *Atha*, "comes.") <margin>Fourth Sermon.</margin>

THE Doctrine upon which I stand / is / that Christ, being the life of a Christian, shall one day appear in glory to judge the world. In the handling of this Doctrine, I have shown you what it is / that makes the appearance of Christ so glorious / and why it is so / and I have made an entrance into the application; The Utility was for the reproof of negligent people. So far I have come / now I proceed.

The next Utility is for guidance. For this doctrine of Christ's appearance in glory to judge the world / admonishes you / to put seven duties into practice.

First, Shall Jesus Christ appear to judge the world? Then put into practice the duty of repentance and godly sorrow / Revelation 1 verse 7. *Behold, he comes with clouds* (here is spoken of His coming for judgment) *and every eye shall see him, even those who pierced him; and all the tribes of the earth shall wail because of him. Even so, Amen.* <note>original: "Ja Amen." The author emphasizes the "Amen" as a solemn confirmation that this judgment is certain and unavoidable.</note> Here you see / that this Doctrine of Christ's coming in the clouds / of His appearance for judgment / calls you to this / that every eye that sees Him / and all the tribes of the earth should mourn over Him; that is / they should bewail their sinful heart and their evil / which they committed while living in this world / as sinning against such a glorious Christ / as He is. Even so, Amen, let it be so; as if he said / yes, may the Lord give His people a mourning heart / may His people have remorse / may the eyes that see Christ coming from Heaven / be able to weep over Him. You read Acts 17 verses 30, 31. *That God overlooked the times of ignorance, but now He commands all men everywhere to repent,* and on what ground? *Because He has appointed a day, on which He will judge the world, by that man Jesus Christ.* That is the reason; every person must repent / because God has appointed a day. If God had not destined a day / you might live as you please / and do what you want / and be merry / just like

the young man of Solomon, Ecclesiastes 11 verse 9. <note>The "young man of Solomon" refers to the target audience of the Book of Ecclesiastes, traditionally attributed to King Solomon, which warns youth to remember their Creator.</note> Who might walk in the sight of his eyes / and the ways of his heart; but know that God shall bring you into judgment for all these things; if no judgment followed / then the young man would have no hindrance in his path / but might go forward without contradiction; but there is a day; and on that day God shall judge the world; repent then / repent of all the evil that you have done in your life against Jesus Christ.

Secondly, Seek to maintain a good conscience / and to walk blamelessly / while you live here / before God and men. The Apostle draws this duty from this doctrine. Acts 24 verses 15, 16. Paul says that there shall be a resurrection, both of the just and the unjust; that is / all men shall appear before Christ for judgment / and what follows? *In this I exercise myself, to always have a conscience void of offense toward God and men.* The thought that the righteous as well as the unrighteous must rise / and be judged by Jesus Christ / was a motive in Paul's heart / that he wanted to labor / to keep his conscience without any offense before God and men. So also says Peter (speaking of Christ's coming for judgment /) 2 Peter 3 verses 11, 12. *Seeing then that you look for these things, what manner of persons ought you to be in holy conduct and godliness?* Here the Apostle binds them / if they expected / that the Heavens shall burn and pass away / and that Christ shall come in glory; what kind of persons ought they then to be in all manner of holiness? Christ's appearance must bind you / to maintain a conscience free from all sins.

Thirdly, This doctrine admonishes you to be patient under all difficulties and oppressions / that might be sent to you by God in this world / James 5 verse 8. *Be patient and establish your hearts; for the coming of the Lord draws near.* The coming of your Lord for judgment ought to arm you / to strengthen you with an abundance of patience under all that a man may lay upon you; for when Christ appears / He shall give full recompense for everything that you have suffered for Him. Do not faint / I say / whatever suffering or sorrow may befall you in particular or your Nation; For half an hour in glory will compensate for it all; as soon as Jesus Christ shall appear / to give you your pronouncement / you shall forget all the sorrow and the suffering that you have had in this world.

Fourthly, Employ then faithfully your gifts and talents / which God has given you / for the profit of your Lord; that is presented as a fruit of this Doctrine, Matthew 25 verse 14. Fifthly, This doctrine obligates you to wait and long for the glorious appearance of Jesus Christ. A guilty conscience cannot endure the thoughts of a judgment. As long as guilt lies upon the conscience, the Judgment is the most terrifying thing in the world to a person. Augustine confesses in one of his books that as long as his conscience was gnawed by the guilt of a youthful lust wherewith he was once entangled, even the hearing of a day of Judgment was a hell to him. <note>Refers to St. Augustine of Hippo (354–430 AD); this likely references his *Confessions* where he describes his inner torment before his conversion.</note> If you lie under guilt, you are a people unfit to put this duty—of waiting for the Lord’s coming—into practice. You have heard of a humble coming of your Savior; so it was, and so it was esteemed among men. Cry out like the Bride: *Come, Lord Jesus, come quickly.* **Luther**, in his **Explanation of Matthew 6**, regarding that petition of the Lord’s Prayer, **Thy Kingdom come**, has this expression: He cannot be a true Christian, nor truly pray the Lord’s Prayer, who does not have these wishes in his soul: that Christ’s Kingdom may come—meaning the coming of Christ as a King, appearing in glory to judge the world. And certainly, Christians have reasons to wish for this day: For 1. It is a day of vengeance upon their enemies, because of the suffering they have inflicted upon them. **2 Thessalonians 1 verses 5, 6, 7.** *It is righteous with God to repay with tribulation those who trouble you.* Then you shall be avenged of all your enemies; you shall receive compensation for all the wrong they have done to you. 2. It is a day of liberation from all your sins. This is the great Year of Jubilee, in which you shall be set free from the power of sin, death, and hell: they shall no longer have power to harm you. 3. It is a day of salvation for your soul, **Hebrews 9 verse 28.** That which was only begun in the world

Sixthly, If Christ shall thus appear in glory to judge the world, then consider yourself obligated to use all the comforts and refreshments you enjoy here in this life moderately. The Holy Spirit draws this application in **Philippians 4 verses 5, 6.** *Let your moderation be known to all men. The Lord is at hand. You must not look upon the comforts and pleasures of your life as if your flesh were iron and your bones copper; either Christ shall soon come from Heaven to judge you, or you must soon come from the earth to Him to be judged. The Lord is at hand, therefore be anxious for nothing. So it is written in **1 Thessalonians 5 verses 4, 6.** *You are not in darkness, that that day should overtake you as a thief; so then let us not sleep; but let us watch and be sober.* Christ, when He wished to teach His disciples how they should prepare themselves for His glorious coming to judgment, said to them, **Luke 21 verse 34.** *Take heed to yourselves, lest your hearts be weighed down at any time with carousing and drunkenness, and the cares of this life, and that day come upon you unawares.* **1 Peter 4 verse 7.** *The end of all things is at hand; be therefore sober and watch in prayer.* Be sober—that is, use all the enjoyments in the creatures that God gives you here to enjoy moderately and temperately. Therefore, those who stuff themselves with and wallow in fleshly pleasures, who wish like **Martinus Lepidus**, who, lying on the ground, said: *O, that this were the laborious life!* <note>original: "Och of dit was het arbeydtsame leven." You read Ephesians 5 verse 15: *See then, brothers, how you walk circumspectly.* The word *akribōs* <note>original: "akribōs," meaning accurately or precisely</note> comes from two Greek words and means to walk on one’s toes; that is, *akronbainein* <note>original: "akronbainein," literally to walk on the tips or peaks</note>. And the Careful Ones <note>Referring to meticulous biblical commentators or "Precisians"</note> give two explanations for that saying, "Walk circumspectly." First, that a person in a Christian life must strive to walk on the highest peak of godliness, not keeping oneself satisfied with a small measure of grace; others say, "Walk circumspectly," that is: walk as if on your toes, just as when you had to walk among snares; you would walk so cautiously and carefully that your foot would almost not touch the ground. So must you do here; you walk among snares and devils, therefore you must walk so neatly, precisely, and carefully that you are not entangled by the Devil's deceits. 3. Watch for the seasons <note>The original Dutch "faisoenen" refers to "fashions" or "opportune moments."</note> and suitable times of grace that God gives you to use in this world for your salvation. The Lord God sometimes gives suitable times of grace; if you let those slip away, you could run the risk of your eternal well-being. Certainly, all time is a time of grace, but not all time is a suitable time and opportunity—that is, a time serving such a good and such an end. All your life's time is a time of salvation, but not [always] a suitable opportunity to obtain salvation; therefore take care, and keep watch for such seasons and suitable times of grace which God gives you to observe in this world. But I leave this and pass over to a **third Utility**, namely, that of comfort.

Just as this teaching serves as a terror to the godless and an admonition to all kinds of people, so the appearance of Christ in glory to judge the world is ordained by God for the **Comfort** of the hearts of His children while they live here, before they come to Heaven; read 1 Thessalonians 4, verses 16, 17, 18. *The Lord himself shall descend from heaven with a shout, with the voice of the archangel, and with the trumpet of God: and the dead in Christ shall rise first: Then we which are alive and remain shall be caught up together with them in the clouds, to meet the Lord in the air: and so shall we ever be with the Lord. Wherefore comfort one another with these words.* The Lord wants this teaching of Christ's appearance for judgment to be a comfort to all His people; He wants all the elect who hear these words to be comforted by them. And this teaching also brings comfort.

First, to all conscientious and industrious Ministers of the Word who have taken much trouble in the work of the Lord and in the conversion of souls; this is a very comforting teaching for them, and so Paul uses it for himself in 1 Thessalonians 2, verses 19, 20. *For what is our hope, or joy, or crown of rejoicing? Secondly, This teaching of Christ's coming is comforting against all suffering of Christians, against the heavy battle of afflictions which they undergo for Christ’s sake. The Holy Spirit makes this use of it in 1 Peter 4, verses 12, 13. *Think it not strange concerning the fiery trial,* though you have much testing and hot afflictions here, do not think it strange, *but rejoice, inasmuch as ye are partakers of Christ's sufferings; that, when his glory shall be revealed, ye may be glad also with exceeding joy.* Beloved, the day of Christ's appearance may rightly be your joy, even though you must now suffer; only note those comforting names given to this day. Although you are worn out by affliction in this world, nevertheless the day of Christ's coming to judge the world will be a day of refreshing for you.

Thirdly, Christ's coming to judgment can serve as comfort to all Christians of whom the world judges poorly—whether it falsely attributes bad motives to their hearts, or charges them with offensive things of which they were never guilty, or whether they are accused of hypocrisy and dissimulation (even if they have only heard a sermon and carried a Bible under their arm); yes, even if one has been wrongly accused before a Court of Justice, and even if an unjust sentence has been passed upon you here, nevertheless this day of Christ's coming to judge the world will not only be for you to be judged anew, but Christ will go and re-judge all things that were poorly judged against you; He will judge your judges, and all those who have judged you poorly. Jude verses 14, 15. *Behold, the Lord cometh... to execute judgment.* Therefore the day of the Lord is called the day of the Revelation of the righteous judgment of God. Romans 2 verse 5. Here, people often judge you unrighteously—regarding your graces, your inclinations, your conduct—but that day will be a day of the righteous judgment of God, in which He will again judge those things that were poorly judged by the world.

# Christ is the Life

between snares or devils. You read in <margin>Ephesians 5 verse 15.</margin> *See then, brothers, how you walk circumspectly.* The word *akribōs* <note>original: "akribōs"; Greek for "accurately" or "perfectly"</note> comes from two Greek words and means "to walk on one's toes," *eis akrobainein*. <note>original: "eis akrobainein"; a Greek-based etymological explanation meaning to walk on the extremities or tips of the feet</note> And the precise interpreters give two explanations for that saying, *Walk circumspectly.* First, that a person in a Christian life must strive to walk upon the highest peak of godliness, not being satisfied with a small measure of grace; others say, *Walk circumspectly*, that is: walk as if on your toes, just as when you had to walk among snares; you would walk with such circumspection and care that your foot would hardly touch the ground. So must you do here; you walk among snares and the Devils; therefore you must walk so precisely, exactly, and carefully, that you are not ensnared by the Devil's deceits. 3. Watch for the seasons and fitting times of grace that God gives you to use in this world for your salvation. God the Lord sometimes gives fitting times of grace; if you let these slip away, you may run the risk of your eternal well-being. Certainly, all time is a time of grace, but not all time is a fitting time and opportunity—that is, a time useful for such a good and such an end. All your life's time is a time of salvation, but not every moment is a fitting opportunity to obtain salvation; therefore, take care and keep watch for such seasons and fitting times of grace which God gives you to observe in this world. But I leave this and pass over to a third Utility, namely of consolation.

Just as this doctrine serves for the terror of the godless and the exhortation of all types of people, so is the appearance of Christ in glory, to judge the world, ordained by God for the Consolation of the hearts of His children while they live here, before they come into Heaven; read <margin>1 Thessalonians 4 verses 16, 17, 18.</margin> *The Lord Himself shall descend from heaven with a shout, with the voice of the Archangel, and with the trumpet of God, and those who have died in Christ shall rise first; then we who are left alive shall be caught up together with them in the clouds to meet the Lord in the air, and so shall we always be with the Lord; therefore comfort one another with these words.* The Lord wants this Doctrine of Christ’s appearance for judgment to be a comfort to all His people; He wants all the elect who hear these words to be comforted by them. And this Doctrine also brings comfort in several ways.

First, to all conscientious and industrious Ministers of the Word who have taken much trouble in the work of the Lord and in the conversion of souls; this is a very comforting Doctrine for them, and so <margin>1 Thessalonians 2 verses 19, 20.</margin> Paul used it for himself: *For what is our hope, or joy, or crown of rejoicing? Is it not even you in the presence of our Lord Jesus Christ at his coming?* It is a joy for a Minister if God has made him an instrument for the conversion of a soul, or for doing good

<column-break/>

to any person while he was on earth, if he can say, when Christ comes to judgment, with Isaiah, <margin>Isaiah 8 verse 18.</margin> *Behold, I and the children whom the Lord has given me.* This day shall be a joyful day for all faithful Ministers of Jesus Christ.

Secondly, This Doctrine of Christ’s coming is comforting against all the suffering of Christians, against the heavy battle of afflictions which they undergo for Christ's sake. The Holy Spirit makes this use of it in <margin>1 Peter 4 verses 12, 13.</margin> *Do not think it strange concerning the fiery trial,* though you have much testing and hot afflictions here, do not think that strange, *but as you share in Christ's sufferings, so rejoice, that when His glory is revealed, you may also be glad with exceeding joy.* Beloved, the day of Christ's appearance may rightly be your joy; though you must suffer now, consider only those comforting names given to this day. It is the day of redemption; It is the Jubilee Year <note>A reference to the biblical Year of Jubilee where debts were forgiven and slaves freed.</note> in which the believer is freed from all suffering and afflictions that come upon them here. It is called the day of the Revelation of the Son of God. <margin>1 John 3 verse 2.</margin> *Now we are children of God, and it has not yet been revealed what we shall be: but we know that when He is revealed, we shall be like Him; for we shall see Him as He is.* And in <margin>Acts 3 verses 19, 20,</margin> it is called a day of refreshing from the presence of the Lord. Although you are worn out by affliction in this world, nonetheless the day of Christ's coming to judge the world shall be a day of refreshing for you.

Thirdly, Christ’s coming for judgment can serve for the comfort of all Christians of whom the world judges poorly—whether it be that they perversely and falsely slander them, or that they charge them with scandalous things of which they were never guilty, or whether they are accused of hypocrisy and pretense (even if they have only heard a Sermon and carried a Bible under their arm); yes, even if one has been unjustly accused before the Court of Justice, and even if an unjust sentence has been passed over you here, nonetheless this day of Christ’s coming to judge the world shall not only be for you to be judged anew; but Christ shall go and re-judge all things that were poorly judged against you; He shall judge your Judges and all those who have judged poorly of you. <margin>Jude verses 14, 15.</margin> *Behold, the Lord comes to execute judgment.* Therefore the day of the Lord is called the day of the Revelation of the righteous judgment of God. <margin>Romans 2 verse 5.</margin> Here, people often judge unrighteously of you, of your graces, of your inclinations, of your conduct; but that day shall be a day of the righteous judgment of God, wherein He shall judge again those things which were poorly judged by the world.

The Apostles considered this an unnecessary matter / to write to the people about / so that they might investigate it. *1 Thessalonians 5 verses 1, 2.* **But of the times and opportunities you have no need that one should write to you. And just as the fly, coming too close to the candle / burns its wings; and the Eagle, soaring too close to the Sun / singes its feathers; So also many might easily / who investigate the mysteries of God / more than he desires / get a glimmering in the eyes / and a dizziness in the understanding / because they go sniffing through such truths / which God has kept in his own heart. But / dearly Beloved / although one cannot absolutely determine the day / month / or year; Still the Scripture presents some prophecies / from which you can know / that the day and hour is not far off. 1. Christ’s coming for judgment is very near / when the world in general is over-

<column-break/>

grown with carnality and carelessness / *Luke 17 verses 26, 27.* **As it happened in the days of Noah, so shall it also be in the days of the Son of man, they shall eat, drink, take in marriage and give in marriage, and not think of the Flood, until it comes and destroys them all.** When you see a general carnality / then you may say; that the day is near. 2. When God the Lord shall bring in the Jews through an outstanding and general conversion / then you may conclude that the day is not far off: For so say all the Interpreters / that the conversion of the Jews and Christ’s coming for judgment shall not be far from each other. Huyt <note>Likely Ephraim Huit (d. 1644), a colonial minister who wrote a commentary on the Book of Daniel.</note>, writing on Daniel, thinks that it will be around the year 1650. Brightman <note>Thomas Brightman (1562–1607) was an English clergyman whose works on the Book of Revelation were popular among those looking for signs of the end times.</note>, on the Revelation, thinks from the year 1656. Others first begin to speak of the year 1668. Most interpreters say it is near. 3. When the nations of the earth are generally rolled in disagreements and wars / *Matthew 24 verse 6, 7.* **You shall hear of wars and rumors of wars; one nation shall rise against another nation;** and 2. Now although this certainly refers particularly to Jerusalem / it is nonetheless also an answer to that question / when the end of the world should be; then there shall be wars upon wars / and Kingdom against Kingdom; compare *Mark 13 verse 7, 8.* *Luke 21 verse 9, 10, 11.* So there is comfort here; if the world sees itself overgrown with carnality <note>original: "vreeslijkhheydt" – though the text likely intended "vleeschlijckheydt" (carnality) based on the previous context of Luke 17.</note>, the Jews generally called, and discord and wars covering the earth / if you see these things / then surely the coming of Christ is not far off.

Now to conclude everything regarding this doubt / namely / *When Christ shall come to judge the world*, I will only make this use of it / that God in wisdom has kept that time in his own power / so that you might undertake the work of your salvation in time. If man only knew / either when he would die / or when Christ would come for judgment / he would lead a sinful life until that very day / and only then would he first begin to think of the work of conversion. Therefore Christ keeps every day hidden / so that you should prepare yourself / as if it were to be the very next day. It is the saying of an Old Father <note>Usually attributed to St. Augustine.</note>, <term>The last day is hidden for this reason, so that all days might be observed</term> <note>original Latin: "Ideo latet ultimus dies, ut observentur omnes"</note>, Therefore one day is kept hidden / so that all days should be kept holy.

# Christ’s Glory

And the third order is concerning the place where this appearance of Jesus Christ shall be. And before I can speak of the place *where*; it is necessary (since there are some doubts and difficulties regarding it) that I first speak of the place *from which* Christ shall appear, and then of the place *to which* or in which he shall come to judge the world; what the Scripture writes of both, I shall now go and reveal.

First, regarding the place *from which*; all that the Scripture says about it in general is that Christ shall appear from **Heaven**, *Philippians 3 verse 20.* **Our citizenship is in the heavens, from which we also expect the Savior, namely the Lord Jesus Christ:** and *Acts 1 verse 11.* **This Jesus, who has been taken up from you into heaven, shall so come, in the same manner as you have seen him go into heaven.** The Scripture tells us only that Christ shall be revealed from Heaven, without making mention whether it shall be from the East, or from the West, or from the North, or from the South. **Damascenus** <note>John of Damascus (c. 675–749 AD), an influential monk and theologian in the Greek Church.</note> says, in the fourth book of *The Orthodox Faith* <note>original: "Recht-ghevoelighe Geloof," referring to the 'De Fide Orthodoxa'.</note>, Chapter 13: Jesus Christ, when he comes to judgment, shall appear in the Eastern parts of the world where the Sun rises. On this ground, the **Papists** <note>A term commonly used by 17th-century Protestants to refer to Roman Catholics.</note> bow toward the East and pray, and all our Churches are built against the East, and all graves are made East and West—all of which happens out of an imagination that Christ must come from the East. And they claim that they have the Scripture for this, *Matthew 24 verse 27.* **As the lightning comes out of the East, and shines to the West, so shall also the coming of the Son of man be.** Now this Text can easily be taken from them; for it speaks not of the place *from which*, but of the *manner* how Christ shall appear; that just as a lightning flash comes quickly and clearly, because it is a bright body, so also Christ, coming to judge, shall come shining and unexpected for the world.

This can teach us upon what bottomless guesses the superstitious actions are built in the minds of men; all the Churches in England are built in this manner, so that one should bow in this direction, while nonetheless the Scripture gives you freedom and takes away all distinction of places, and speaks not one word of Christ coming from the East. And even if it did speak of it, yet it speaks nothing of praying toward it, bowing our bodies, burying the dead, or making our Pulpits face that way. This is the superstition of men.

Now as for the second part, the place where he shall appear when he comes to judge the world, there are various guesses and opinions about it. The **Jewish Rabbis** say that the place shall be in the **Valley of Jehoshaphat**, in that Valley where Jehoshaphat conquered the Moabites and Ammonites, and where he dutifully praised God; there they believe Christ’s appearance shall be. The Scriptural text they insist upon is *Joel 3 verse 12.* — **The Heathen shall stir themselves and go up to the Valley of Jehoshaphat, for there I will sit to judge all the Heathen round about.** Mark, they say, the Heathen from all around must come up to the Valley; and

<column-break/>

there God shall sit for judgment. Before I give you the right sense of the place, I shall answer that this cannot be the place where Christ in glory shall appear to judge the world, and that for these four reasons: 1. Because the person who is said here to judge is God the Father, and not God the Son; but if this place had presented Christ’s appearance for judgment, then it must have spoken of God the Son, not of God the Father; for God the Father judges no one on that day, but he has given all judgment to the Son, *John 5 verse 22.* 2. Because this judgment concerns only the **Heathen** <note>The non-believing nations or Gentiles.</note>, but the day of judgment is a judging of all people, living and dead, good and evil. **We shall all appear before the Judgment Seat of Christ,** *2 Corinthians 5 verse 10.* Therefore this judgment cannot be the same as that day, since here only the Heathen are judged, and not the godly. 3. This judgment here does not concern all the Heathen in the world, but only those who were around that place. God wanted to judge those enemies and Heathen who lived near Jerusalem—that is, he wanted to destroy them. 4. This Valley of Jehoshaphat cannot be the place of judgment because one cannot imagine—since all people who have been, are, or shall be, must be judged on that day—that the same Valley could contain them all. Therefore the Valley of Jehoshaphat cannot be the place where Jesus Christ in glory shall appear to judge the world. 5. The time is recounted in verse 12. But to give you now the true sense of the place, namely: **The Heathen shall stir themselves and go up to the Valley of Jehoshaphat; for there I will sit to judge all the Heathen round about.** This place looks to a particular judgment of God over the enemies of Israel who lived around Jerusalem, and not at the day of the general Judgment in which Christ shall appear to judge the world; as **Calvin** <note>John Calvin (1509–1564), the French theologian whose commentaries were foundational for the Dutch Reformed tradition.</note> well observes, that God wanted to destroy the enemies of Israel around that place—the Ammonites, the Moabites, the Chaldeans, the Babylonians, and whatever other enemies might still be thereabouts; all those the Lord wanted to destroy; he wanted to judge them.

There is another opinion concerning the place of Christ’s coming which says that Christ shall come for judgment on the **Mount of Olives**. This they confirm from *Acts 1 verses 11, 12,* where it stands: **In the same way that you have seen him go to heaven, so shall you see him come down from heaven again. And then they returned from the mountain.** Now, they say, Christ ascended to heaven from the Mount of Olives, so he shall then also come down again upon that mountain. To this proof I answer: 1. This passage speaks only of the *manner* how Christ shall come, not of the *place* where he shall come; *Just as you see him ascend, so shall he descend.* You see Christ go away in the clouds, so shall you see him come with the clouds, in power and great glory, *Revelation 1 verse 7.* 2. Although it is in the Scripture that Christ ascended from the Mount of Olives, yet there is no sign in the entire Bible that he shall descend there. And that one accepts such a claim, of which the Scripture does not speak,

But now, so that you might not be wise above that which is written <note>A reference to 1 Corinthians 4:6, advising against speculating beyond biblical text.</note>, I shall present in words of truth and moderation what the Scripture says regarding the place. When Jesus Christ was asked in what place this judgment would be, he answered indefinitely; he described the place only in general, not in particular. Luke 17 verse 37: And they said to him, "Where, Lord?" And Christ said, "Well, where the body is, there the eagles will be gathered together." The place where I shall come to judge the world shall be where the believers shall be gathered together. So, Christ leaves the place undefined. And one reads only in the Scripture, 1 Thessalonians 4 verses 16, 17: That at the last trumpet the dead shall rise, and then what? And the Lord shall descend from Heaven, and we shall be caught up in the clouds, to meet the Lord in the Air. This is all that is spoken of the place in the Scripture: namely, that Christ shall come from Heaven, shining in glory above the entire world, and that the saints shall be taken away from the wicked of the world, and meet the Lord in the air.

What use shall we make of this? Well, let it be this: that there is no place on earth that can shelter you from the judgment of Jesus Christ; even if you cry to the mountains and rocks to cover my presence from you, you cannot remain hidden. The Psalmist speaks excellently well in Psalm 139 verses 8, 9, 10. If I ascend to Heaven, you are there; or if I made my bed in Hell <note>original: "Helle," referring to Sheol or the depths</note>, behold, you are there. If I took the wings of the morning, and dwelt in the uttermost parts of the sea; even there your hand would lead me, and your right hand would hold me. Wherever the place may be where Christ shall appear, be certain: he shall surely find out your sins and your person. No place shall hide you from the judgment of Jesus Christ.

## The fourth Question is: Whether Jesus Christ, before his glorious revelation to judge the world, shall personally appear on earth and reign as King for a thousand years? And whether this can be proven from the Scripture?

This doubt has caused much trouble, and the judgment of some in ancient times, such as Justin Martyr and others, was taken by this imagination, which first came from the Jewish Rabbis. Therefore, in speaking of this, I shall maintain this course: first, I shall show you the origin of this opinion, and how it came to be spread across the world. Then I shall point out what objections may be put forward that seem to support this opinion; and finally, that this opinion cannot be made true from the Scripture.

First, concerning the origin of this opinion: the historians say that the first who held it in the early Church was one Cerinthus <note>A gnostic heretic of the 1st century who was a contemporary of the Apostle John.</note>, a great heretic, who maintained that Christ was not God, and that he was not born of a Virgin, but through the union of man and woman; he advocated for circumcision; and Augustine believes that the Synod held in

<column-break/>

Acts 15 was established to counter that error, which was stirred up and nurtured by him. Regarding different parts of the world, there was one Augustin Webber in Germany (a leather-seller <note>original: "Leer-verkoper"; likely referring to Augustin Bader, a radical Anabaptist and millenarian who was a skinner by trade.</note> by profession) who first brought this opinion into play among his people. The historians say that he and this Cerinthus, by listening to Jewish traditions and abandoning the explanations of the Apostles, were thrust into the depths of this error. After him, it was accepted by Thomas Müntzer and Jan van Leiden <note>Leaders of radical Anabaptist movements in the 1520s and 30s who attempted to establish a "New Jerusalem" by force.</note>. We find that it is an old opinion; they were called Chiliasts <note>From the Greek word for "one thousand."</note> in ancient times. Augustine, in *The City of God* <note>original: "stalt Gods," referring to 'De Civitate Dei'</note>, Book 20, Chapter 7, calls them Chilionites; by Damascene <note>John of Damascus</note>, in the *Book of Heresies*, Page 579, they are called Millenarians. Philastrius <note>A 4th-century bishop and writer on heresies.</note>, in the *Book of Heresies*, chapter 59, calls them Pepuziani, because they thought that a city named Pepuzium, which separated Galatia from Cappadocia and Phrygia, would be the place where Christ would come from Heaven. Among us, they may be called Thousand-yearists <note>original: "Duyſent-jarige"</note>, and that is because they hold that Jesus Christ shall come down from Heaven before the day of judgment, and shall reign here on earth in person for a thousand years among his elect. At which time the Church shall have peace and no persecution at all, and the enemies of God shall be powerfully struck down by the godly. We also find that they differ in this opinion. Some are very crude and say that there shall be no sin in those days. Others say the dead shall rise, especially those who have been Martyrs; some are so crude that they hold that there shall be fleshly pleasures in that time; and though they do not all go so far, they nevertheless all agree that there shall be a personal reign for so many years. So this is the question: Whether Jesus Christ shall come down from Heaven in person, and reign here among his people and baptized Saints, and that for 1,000 years, before he shall come in glory to judge the world?

The objections that have the most weight, and upon which most depends, are these. First, upon Ephesians 5 verses 5, 6: "Let no one deceive you, no fornicator, or unclean person, or covetous man, who is an idolater, has an inheritance in the Kingdom of Christ and of God." Here, they say, a Kingdom of God is explicitly spoken of as distinct from the Kingdom of Christ; therefore they think this gives some strength to their opinion. To this I answer: 1. Everyone admits that Jesus Christ has a Kingdom distinct from the Kingdom of God, for he must hand over the Kingdom to his Father; and Christ was King in this Kingdom even when he was born into the world, for so it says in Psalm 2 verses 6, 7: "I have anointed my King over Zion, the hill of my holiness, today I have begotten you"; and in Acts 4 verses 26, 27, the Apostle applies that saying to show that Christ was King when he was on earth, and rose from the dead, until this day. Jesus Christ is both King of the nations and King of the Saints; King of the nations through his providence, and King of the Saints through his Spirit. But this being admitted by all, what does this do for a Kingdom of a thousand years? And how does this prove that there is a Kingdom where...

No / **Paul** says / that he was one born out of
