Secondly, if the damned in Hell, being so far from Heaven and in a place so contrary to Heaven, shall know who is glorified in Heaven, then certainly the glorified shall know each other much more. Now, we find in Scripture that people in Hell know glorified saints in Heaven: for in Luke 16 verse 23, the Rich Man in Hell knew Abraham and Lazarus in his bosom in Heaven. But, you might say, this is a parable, and perhaps parables do not prove as much as clear Scripture? To which I answered: it is true, perhaps it is a parable (although some doubt that, and believe that it truly happened so—that there was such a Rich Man and a Lazarus, and that God allowed such a thing to occur outside the usual order); nonetheless, I know for certain that other Texts confirm it clearly. In Luke 13 verse 28, it says that on the day of judgment, they shall see Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob in the Kingdom of God, and themselves shut out. Note: not only the Rich Man, but all the damned in Hell shall see Abraham, to their great haste <note>In this context, "haste" likely implies a sense of agitation or urgency in their regret</note>, because they would not walk in the footsteps and the faith of Abraham; they shall see Abraham to their greater shame and conviction, because they would not walk as the seed and the Children of Abraham.

<margin>*</margin> If, then, damned men shall know the glorified Saints in Heaven, it follows much more that the blessed shall also know them.

Thirdly, if the glorified in Heaven shall know the damned in Hell and who they are, they shall certainly much more know those who are glorified among them. Fourthly, Scripture says in another place at least as much in confirmation of this. Read Matthew 8 verse 11: I say unto you, that many shall come from the East and West, and shall sit down with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob in the Kingdom of Heaven. From this I prove thus: what more comfort would it be to be in the Heavens than to be here among glorified bodies, if Scripture did not make this a special comfort—that one shall be there with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob? For without doubt, the manner of speaking implies that when we are there with them, we shall distinguish them from the others; otherwise, we would not know this privilege. Because it is promised as a privilege that we shall sit with them, we shall then undoubtedly distinguish them from the others.

<column-break/>

Fifthly, (and this is Mr. Bolton's <note>Robert Bolton (1572–1631), an influential English Puritan clergyman and scholar</note> proof) if Adam in his innocence knew his wife and did not even ask who she was or where she came from, but knew through a Divine knowledge that she was bone of his bone and flesh of his flesh; so shall we have much more of this light and knowledge to know Wife, children, and friends when we come into glory. Anselm <note>Anselm of Canterbury (c. 1033–1109), a prominent medieval philosopher and theologian</note> says: *there all will be known by each, and each will be known by all* <note>original Latin: "ibi a singulis omnes, ibi ab omnibus singuli cognoscentur, Anselm. de Similit. cap. 59."</note>.

Sixthly, knowing one another in Heaven shall be for this reason: because this will wonderfully exalt and increase the joy of the glorified Saints. Now, it is beyond doubt true that whatever can increase or cause the joy of the Elect to grow shall be in Heaven; but beyond all contradiction, knowing one another in Heaven will wonderfully increase the joy. When you shall know Abraham and all the Patriarchs; when you shall see David and all the Kings who were godly like him; when you shall see Elijah and all the godly Prophets with him; when you shall see Paul and all the Apostles with him; when you shall see Stephen and all the Holy Martyrs with him; when you shall see all your friends; when the Mother shall say, "here is my tender Child, who was taken from me by an untimely death"; when the Wife shall say, "here is my dear Husband, who lay by my side for so long"; when the people shall say, "here is the Minister <term>Dienaar</term> <note>Literally "servant," referring here to a pastor or preacher</note> who converted my soul and was an instrument to bring me to glory"; when the Ministers shall say, "these are the persons whom God, through my humble service on earth as through an instrument, willed to bring to salvation." Certainly, this will greatly increase the joy and comfort which the Elect shall have in Heaven; and therefore it shall undoubtedly be so.

But now we must ward off an objection. You will say: "Perhaps Scripture gives us something to comfort us in these thoughts, but this might perhaps in turn awaken a great sadness in us—that if we knew one another in Heaven, we would also then know who the damned were; and so the Husband would know that his Wife, the Father that his Child, and a friend that his friend would be in Hell. For if we shall know all the Elect in Heaven and do not find them there, we may well think that they are damned, and so this would wonderfully grieve us." To which I answer: It is so, and I truly believe that people shall know who are damned in Hell; but those who know it shall not know it with compassion or sadness that will affect them; they shall not know it in such a way that the knowledge of it will diminish their joy; but they shall know it in such a way that God has executed vengeance and justice upon the people who led a godless life in this world. Yet they shall not know it so that they would murmur against God or His will because of it, or diminish their own joy: for as Anselm says, they shall be so taken up with the enjoyment of Christ, with the blessed vision of God, and with the company of the

1. 3. Shall you know one another in glory? Then this ought to powerfully spur you on / to earnestly strive for a true, well-grounded knowledge / that you shall come into glory: For what use will it be to you / that the Saints of God shall know one another in glory / if you do not know whether you shall be a glorified Saint / or not? Oh labor then / to make this sure for your soul / that you shall appear in glory / when Christ appears.

4. Learn from this / O you children of men / to labor / while you are on earth / for the conversion of your Friends and Kindred. Labor (O Husband) to convert your Wife: Labor (O Wife) to convert your Husband: Labor (O Parents) to convert your children; and labor (O Friends) to convert your Friends. Do your best to convert them here on earth / so that / although you part from one another for a little while through death / you may nonetheless meet one another in Heaven / and know each other again in glory.

A fourth Doubt is this: Whether one must believe that / besides that at Christ's appearance for judgment / soul and body shall be glorified / the souls of men before Christ's glorious appearance / so immediately after death shall go into glory / and be with Christ Jesus? It is true / there are two or three "blue-books" <note>Cheaply printed pamphlets or sensationalist booklets popular in the 17th century</note> and blunt writings come out / that partly deny this: And although to deny this makes a person almost an Atheist / yet they are so bold / that they are not ashamed to reveal their feelings in the sight of the world. Well / to hold any of this / or all at once is to make a Person into an Atheist; for if the Soul goes to Hell after Death; why should we strive to lead a Godly life here? The last two are equally absurd; and there is no other place left for the Elect Souls / but the glorious Heaven.

I answer / that according to the declaration of Scripture / the word Paradise is often taken for Heaven; so Paul <note>original: "Paulus"</note> takes it, who calls the third Heaven, where he was caught up / which all Interpreters take for the place of the glorified Saints / nonetheless Paradise / 2 Corinthians 12 verse 4. > When Christ shall appear, who is our life, then shall we also appear with him in glory.

<margin>Ninth Sermon.</margin>
The doctrine / as you may remember / is this: That Jesus Christ has reserved the full glorification of his <term>elect</term> <note>those chosen by God</note> until that time in which he himself shall appear in glory to judge the world. In the treatment of which we have resolved some doubts / which afterwards came into my reflection; I shall now finish these / and then proceed to the general application of everything.

The fifth doubt concerning the glorification of the elect is this: Whether these same bodies / which we carry about with us here in this world / shall rise and be glorified with Jesus Christ in Heaven? It is necessary that these questions be spoken of / especially in these <term>wandering-spirited times</term> <note>a reference to a perceived era of religious confusion or heresy</note>; in which all old heresies are being pulled out of the dust / and are now called "New Light" <note>original: "Nieuw Light"; a term often used mockingly by traditionalists to describe radical or mystical religious movements of the 17th century</note>. Books have now been printed that deny all this / that deny the resurrection / or argue that if the body shall rise / it will not be glorified. This then is the doubt: whether the Scripture gives us certainty / that the bodies of the elect / these very same bodies / shall be with Christ in glory in Heaven?

Those who deny this stand on two grounds; they think they have the Scripture on their side / 

<column-break/>

and they also think they have reason. I shall examine both / and then present the truth. The Scripture passage they cite is 1 Corinthians Chapter 15 verse 50: *Flesh and Blood shall not inherit the Kingdom of God.* From this they argue thus: "Flesh and Blood," that is the body composed of Flesh and Blood together / shall never reign / shall never come into Heaven; for Flesh and Blood shall never come there. But if the body were to come there / then the Flesh would come there / which the Scripture here says shall not be; to which I answer:

First, that this cannot be the meaning of the text / as if Flesh and Blood literally should not enter Heaven: for this would conflict with other Scripture passages / such as when it states that Christ's body is in Heaven. If his body is there / then his Flesh must also be there. Christ is now in Heaven as a man and according to his human nature / so his flesh is also there. Likewise Elijah, who was taken up in a fiery chariot / his flesh is also in Heaven; and Enoch is in Heaven / and Peter saw in a vision Moses, Elijah, and Christ in their bodies. So this cannot be the meaning of the text.

Secondly, some give it this meaning (which, although consistent with the "proportion of faith," is nevertheless not true in this specific case): "Flesh and Blood" (they say) means a person in an unregenerate state shall not enter Heaven. Although it is true that "flesh" is elsewhere used to mean corruption / just as it says that *those who are in the flesh* (meaning in a natural, sinful state) *can do nothing that is well-pleasing to God*; nevertheless, that is not the meaning here. Rather, it refers to something else / namely / *Flesh and Blood shall not be able to inherit the Kingdom of Heaven* in so far as it is corrupt. Thus, the body in its current state will never enter Heaven / for when we arrive there / we must be changed into the likeness of his most glorious body. Your body / as it is now / subject to decay / will not enter Heaven / but it will be a glorified body; this corrupt quality will be removed. *Your humble bodies shall be made like unto the glorious body of Christ* (Philippians 3 verse 21). This is what most interpreters say is the meaning of the passage.

Furthermore, just as they rely on Scripture, so they also give their "reasons," saying: It is impossible and against reason that our bodies / which shall rot in the grave / and of which thousands of worms eat / should rise again / and that those worms should give back this eaten Flesh / this is not believable. 2. Suppose a person drowns / and the fish eat that man's flesh; and suppose those fish are caught / and other people eat those fish / and those people die / and the worms eat them; how is it possible that this same body, thus consumed, should rise and be glorified? This they think is a great argument. On this point stand all the <term>Epicureans</term> <note>here used to describe people who live only for the present and deny the resurrection</note>, saying / "Let us eat, drink, and be merry / for after death there is no pain in the grave." They cannot imagine that a body / eaten by so many / could ever again be united into a perfect body.

### In glory with Christ.

This argument is easily set aside; for an answer, let this serve:

First, if a human being, through the art of using ash, can create such beautiful work—namely, glass—why cannot the Almighty God make glorified bodies, as beautiful as crystal, out of dust and ash? If, in mixed substances, the mixture can be removed and the object returned to a perfect state; just as a refiner <note>original: "Louteraar"; a person who purifies metals through melting</note> who has a mixed lump consisting of four kinds of metal—gold, silver, iron, and tin—can sift and separate them all through the use of fire and art, bringing the gold together by itself, and the silver by itself, and so each in its own order and state; can the Almighty not do this? Do you wish to give a human being such freedom and yet restrict God’s power? Even if a person’s flesh is mingled among a thousand worms, can the mighty God not bring this flesh back together by His power? And could we not, therefore, be with this very flesh of ours in glory with Him in Heaven?

Secondly, when they say that this is against reason, we deny that, although it is truly *above* reason. Reason cannot grasp how these bodies of ours, which shall rot in the dust and be eaten by worms, shall be glorified. If we only believed that which reason could reach, we would be nothing but atheists. Reason cannot grasp the mystery of the Trinity; shall we therefore not believe in the Trinity because reason cannot comprehend it? That there are three persons in one Godhead, that the Divinity and humanity are united in one person—reason cannot believe this. Therefore, if we believed no more than reason, we would be the most terrible atheists in the world.

But to answer the doubt now, and to show that the bodies of the elect shall be glorified, I shall give three scriptural texts as proof; first, Job 19, verses 25, 26, 27:

> I know my Redeemer lives, and after they have gnawed through my skin and this flesh (first they take the skin, and then he says, after the skin, my flesh), so shall I behold God from my flesh, whom I shall behold for myself, and my eyes shall see, and not a stranger.

Well! What can be clearer than this: that these same eyes, and these same limbs, and this very same body in essence, which you have on Earth, shall be glorified with Christ in Heaven? For although the worms shall gnaw through my skin and my flesh, yet this body of mine shall see God; my eyes shall behold Him. So also 1 Corinthians 15, verses 35, 36. Notice the doubt that Paul puts forward: *But someone will say, how shall the dead be raised? And with what kind of body shall they come?* Notice now how the Apostle answers:

> You fool, that which you sow is not made alive unless it dies.

The Apostle draws this from a comparison to corn. When one sows the corn, it dies and rots in the ground before it rises as a blade; so your bodies cannot be raised unless they first die and rot in the grave. And then the Apostle says:

> God gives it a body as He wills, and to every seed its own body.

If you then sow a grain of wheat,

<column-break/>

no barley shall sprout from it, but the essential seed being sown shall grow up again. Likewise, these very bodies of yours, which are laid in the Earth like seed, shall be raised, and every one of you shall have the same body; just as the seed receives its own, so shall you. Likewise 2 Corinthians 5, verses 2, 4:

> In this we groan, longing to be clothed over with our dwelling which is from Heaven; for we groan in this being burdened; since we shall not be unclothed, but clothed over.

That is, we groan, not as if we wished to be in Heaven without a body, but to be *clothed over*, that is, that our very same bodies might wear garments of glory and excellence which they do not wear now, so that mortality might be swallowed up by life; so that our mortal bodies might be always living and enduring bodies. Thus you see clearly from the Scriptures that the body shall rise to glory after death. And the Reason can be this: because the body has done good or evil together with the soul, it must therefore, with the soul, either be condemned in Hell or blessed in Heaven, according to whether the person was good or evil. 2 Corinthians 5, verse 10:

> We must all be made manifest before the judgment seat of Christ, so that each one may carry away what was done through the body, according to what he has done, whether good or evil.

The body must also give an account, since it had a part in all the actions that were done, whether good or evil.

The usefulness <note>original: "Nuttigheyt"; the practical application of the doctrine</note> that I shall draw from this resolved doubt shall be fourfold, and that for instruction.

First: Is it so, that these bodies of yours shall rise and be in glory with Jesus Christ? Well, oh all you elect of God, do not fear death then, since death makes your bodies fit for that state in which you shall live eternally with Christ in glory. If death destroyed you and made you miss the glory, you might fear death; but death treats you as a farmer treats his corn. Should he keep his corn in the house forever, he would soon become a beggar; but he throws his corn into the Earth, and there it lies and rots, so that fivefold profit might come to him. Likewise, God lets you be laid in the grave and rot there, not forever, but so that He may show His power in raising you on the last day. Do not fear death then, since it only unclothes you of your rags and makes you fit to be clothed with your garment which is from Heaven. 2 Corinthians 5, verse 1.

Secondly: Do not become faint-hearted and do not faint under all the suffering to which your bodies are subject in this world. Perhaps you have a weak body, a poorly made body, or even poor and lowly bodies in this world; well, do not faint under all this, since God wants to raise these very bodies of yours to be glorified with Jesus Christ. Hebrews 11, verse 35:

> Women were stretched out <note>A reference to martyrdom or torture</note>, not accepting the offered deliverance, so that they might obtain a better resurrection.

They did not ask about the pains of the flesh; the violence of the fire, and the roaring of the

**Thirdly,** these bodies of yours, which rot in the grave, shall be in glory with Christ Jesus; so let this teach you that you should not be immeasurably grieved over the death of your friends. If your friends died and you were never to see them again, then you might rightly be very sorrowful; but now, though your friends shall die, these same bodies shall be raised again to be glorified, where you—who are ordained to glory—shall meet your friends one day. Do not grieve too much then over the loss of a friend; for you lose them only for a time, to enjoy them in eternity. The Apostle <note>Referring to the Apostle Paul.</note> makes use of this in 1 Thessalonians 4, verses 13 and 14: *Brothers, I do not want you to be ignorant concerning those who have fallen asleep, lest you sorrow as others who have no hope. For if we believe that Jesus died and rose again, even so God will bring with Him those who sleep in Jesus.* That is, those who are dead and belong to Jesus Christ shall be brought back by the power of God the Father, through the power of Christ’s Resurrection, to live together with Him in glory in Heaven. Weep not then as others who have no hope: neither cry nor mourn too much over the death of your friends, since you shall see the bodies of those from whom you part here again in Heaven, and you shall be glorified together.

**Fourthly,** learn from this that you must not give these members of your body to be instruments for God's dishonor, as if you would use them for sin, rather than for the display of His holiness. O beloved, you shall see Jesus with these very eyes which you now have in your head. You, who are God’s elect, shall sing Hallelujahs in Heaven with this very same tongue with which you converse among men. You shall lift up your hands in praise to God. Use them not now (to use the Apostle’s way of speaking) as *weapons of unrighteousness* to wage war against Heaven. Use not your eyes as windows for lusts, nor your tongue as an axe for divisive speech, nor your hands to deceive, nor your feet to be swift to shed blood. O, do not misuse the members of your body—which shall be glorified with Jesus Christ—in such sinful works as these. And thus I have finished the fifth question.

A **sixth doubt** is this: Since the bodies of all God’s elect shall be in glory with Jesus Christ, will those bodies also need clothing, food, and other natural refreshments, just as here in this world? Certainly there are some who insist upon this, and hold that they shall be dressed in pearls, diamonds, and other glorious garments; and to this end, they poorly apply that passage in Revelation 4, verse 4, where it says: *The twenty-four elders were clothed in white robes, and had crowns of gold on their heads.* But to clear this away, know that this saying is not literal, but is spoken as a simile <note>original: "gelijckenis"</note>, just as in Psalm 104, verse 2. Because, just as wearing white clothes and

<column-break/>

crowns are signs of majesty, purity, and victory, so the Saints of God in Heaven shall be in a state of purity, free from sin, in a state of victory over their enemies, and in a state of glory far above all creatures in the world. In answer to the question, I say: no clothing shall be necessary there. Why? For these reasons:

1. Because in the state of innocence <note>original: "onnoozelheydt"; referring to the state of humanity before the Fall.</note> there was no use for clothing. Adam and Eve were naked, and they were not ashamed. Clothing only came into use through sin; no garments were worn in the world before sin was in the world. Well, we shall be in glory just as Adam was in innocence; as he used no clothing, so we also shall not have it in Heaven.

2. Clothing is either for adornment or for protection against wind and weather; yet for neither of these do we have need of clothes in Heaven. Not for adornment, because our humble bodies shall be like the glorious body of Christ; not for the weather, since neither wind nor weather shall do us any harm there.

**Utility.** If this is so, that our bodies shall need no clothing in Heaven, then this ought to teach you to beware of being proud of your clothes with which you cover your bodies here on Earth. If clothing came in through sin, oh, then be not proud of that which sin brought into the world! Sin brought in the use of clothing; well, do not pride yourself on the brood of sin; garments only hide your shame; oh, do not be vain over that which only covers your shame. If the body were a glorified body, it would have no need of clothes, but you are accustomed to hiding things that are foul and stained. It is a proof that the body is a humble <note>original: "geringh"; meaning lowly or of little value compared to the divine.</note> body, since it has need of clothes. Your garments only cover a clump of earth, a lowly creature, an ugly body; be not then proud of your clothes, which are only a covering to hide your shame.

The **seventh and last question**: whether the Saints of God, who shall appear in glory with Christ, shall speak with an audible voice to make heard the glory of God and Christ in Heaven? This is, I confess, a curious and unnecessary question raised by the Scholastic teachers <note>original: "School-leeraeren"; referring to medieval academic theologians.</note> on this matter; therefore I shall pass over it with only a word. Namely, that the Scripture indicates this: that having your bodies in Heaven, you shall also have your tongues to sing Hallelujahs among the Angels, and to praise Him who sits upon the Throne for eternity. But what kind of language it shall be, the Scripture says nothing. Some plead very strongly for this: that we shall all speak Hebrew in Heaven, because it says in Revelation 19, verse 4: *They said Amen, Hallelujah*, which are Hebrew words; and that just as Adam had the Hebrew tongue in the state of innocence, so also the Saints in glory shall use it. And when it says in 1 Corinthians 13, verse 8, *Languages shall cease*, Galatinus <note>Pietro Galatino (c. 1460–1540), an Italian theologian and scholar of Hebrew.</note> answers in book 12, *De Arcanis*, chapter 4: *He says that languages shall cease* <note>original Latin: "Dicit linguas cessaturas"</note>...

*But not that the language shall cease.* <note>original Latin: *non autem linguam cessaturam*</note> The Apostle says that languages (in the plural number) shall cease; but not the language (in the singular number). However, this is merely a particular opinion and is not at all grounded in the Scriptures. Others believe that they shall speak all kinds of languages; but it cannot be determined which language it shall be; although I truly believe that there shall be but one, and not a mixture. This is because: 1. they shall be one people; 2. the diversity of languages came about through sin; there was but one language in the world until the great destruction of Babel, <margin>Genesis 11</margin>. At that time, the people were confused in their speech; but in Heaven, all nations shall cry out as with one voice the praise of the three Persons in the Godhead. But I pass over this; since the Scripture is silent, it is not fitting that we speak much of it. There are many other doubts which we will not be able to solve until we enter Heaven.

Now I come to the second point which I proposed in treating this doctrine: Namely;
Why has Christ reserved the full glorification of his elect <term>the elect: those chosen by God for salvation</term> until that time when he shall appear in glory to judge the world? The reasons are these, which I shall only name.
1. Christ does it to make the glory of his elect more visible to all the wicked, to their torment and the aggravation of their pain; so that when they see the chosen Saints of God shining in glory and themselves excluded, they might then gnash their teeth in fury. For that end, Christ has kept their glory until that day.
2. Because it is very pleasant for the Saints of God to be glorified when Christ is glorified; not without Christ, not before Christ, but as he is. And
3. Because it will best suit the glory of Jesus Christ that when he comes to reveal his glory, he shall then bring with him all the elect—those who were, are, or shall be in the four corners of the world—and raise them up by his own power, so that they might shine together with him in glory on the last day. This shall wonderfully set forth the glory of Christ. For these reasons, then, Jesus Christ has reserved the glorification of his elect until he shall come in glory to judge the world.

And thus I come to the third and last proposed matter, namely, the general application of this entire doctrine.
To this end, I shall first present some propositions, so that all misunderstanding regarding this doctrine may be prevented.

God does not wish to bring any unbelievers to eternal life. And this subverts that unholy saying of some / *If I am to be damned / then I shall be damned; if I am to be saved / then I shall be saved / even if I live according to my own pleasure.* This is hereby taken away / I say / because if God intends for them to come to glory / God will work faith and conversion in them / while they live in this world; for as many as he has ordained to eternal life / those shall believe.

### A second Utility is by way of guidance and awakening / and contains six conclusions / serving for practice.

First, has Jesus Christ ordained all the elect / to come to glory / then know / O you elect of God / that a Christian walk can bring no shame nor

<column-break/>

disgrace on Earth. That is shame / which ends in shame; that is no shameful path / which shall end in such glory / as this shall be / wherein your Bodies and Souls shall be so glorious with Christ. O you elect of God / then count it no shame / to be a Christian; and O you all who are yet strangers to godliness / do not reckon it a shame to be a Confessor. Secondly, shall Christ bring you to glory? Secondly, exalt his faithfulness / 2 Thessalonians 3 verse 3. *The Lord is faithful, who shall strengthen you.* Thirdly, exalt God’s power / 2 Timothy 1 verse 12. *The Lord is able to keep that which I have committed unto him, against that day;* Yes, fourthly, exalt God’s justice / 2 Thessalonians 1 verse 5. *It is a righteous thing with God;* that thus glorifies God’s grace / power / faithfulness and righteousness / and breaks out in wonder over all his attributes.

Thirdly, shall you be partakers of this glorious state? Oh / then walk in the world while you live / so / that you bring Christ much glory here. This use is made of it / Romans 15 verses 6 and 7. *That you may with one mind and one mouth glorify the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ. Wherefore receive one another, as Christ also received us to the glory of God.* The proof of the Apostle is / that since Christ has received you into the glory of his Father / this ought to be a bond for you / to glorify God on Earth. So also 1 Thessalonians 2 verse 12. *I testify to you (says Paul) that you walk worthily of God, who calls you to his Kingdom and glory.* Here the Apostle draws this conclusion / that you must walk worthily of this grace / namely to glorify God / who has called you to such a glorious Kingdom. Therefore you who have brought Jesus Christ no glory / while you are on Earth / do not expect to be glorified in Heaven.

Fourthly, do not lose heart over any difficulty or suffering / which you encounter in this world; for whatever you come to endure here in this life / your being in glory shall compensate for it all. This instruction the Apostle gives / 1 Peter 4 verse 13. *As you are partakers of Christ's sufferings, so rejoice; that when his glory shall be revealed, you may be glad also with exceeding joy.* As a Martyr said / half an hour in glory / will make us forget all our pain: be content then / to carry the Cross here / because hereafter you shall wear the Crown.

Fifthly, shall you be partakers of the glory? then you are bound to love your brothers / who shall have a share in the glory with you / as well as you. Upon this duty the Holy Spirit presses / Romans 15:7. *Receive one another, as Christ also received us*

The Doctrine / which I am still upon / you may remember / is this /
**That Jesus Christ has reserved the full glorification of his elect until that time, when he himself shall appear in glory, to judge the world.**

<column-break/>

In the handling of the same, I have passed over many main points / and answered some doubts. I shall now proceed to the general application of all / that I have said concerning this Doctrine. And the remaining Usefulnesses, of which I shall yet speak / shall be three / A usefulness of **Refutation**, of **Examination**, and of **Consolation**.

### First Usefulness, for refutation.
Is it so / that Jesus Christ has reserved the full glorification of his elect until the time / that he shall appear to judge the world? then by virtue of this point, three errors are refuted.

1. The opinion of the **Platonic Philosophers** / that the soul is mortal, and dies with the body. But if the soul were mortal / then this Text could not be true / because the soul would then not appear in glory with Jesus Christ / so this Doctrine overthrows that opinion.

2. This also condemns the opinion of **Origen**, whose opinion was; it is true (said he) now there is a place of torment; but in the day of Christ's appearing for judgment all men shall be saved; yes, not only men, but even the devils in Hell, and the fallen Angels. <note>Origen of Alexandria (c. 184–253 AD) was an early Christian theologian who proposed 'apokatastasis,' the idea that all created beings would eventually be reconciled to God.</note> Origen thinks that they shall all be revealed in glory with Jesus Christ and be saved through his blood. This is a bold opinion / and is overturned by this Doctrine: for the Text says / that those alone shall appear in glory with Christ, who have Christ as their life: but the Devils and the damned in Hell have never had Christ as their life; so they shall never come to glory. Furthermore / this opinion can easily be refuted by observing just two or three Scripture Texts / such as <margin>Dan. 12 verse 2.</margin> *Many of those who sleep in the dust of the earth shall awake, some to everlasting life, and others to shame, and to everlasting contempt.* So that on the day of resurrection all men shall not come to eternal life / but some to glory / and some to contempt. So it is also written <margin>John 5 verses 28, 29.</margin> *The hour is coming, in which all who are in the grave shall hear his voice, and shall come forth, some to the resurrection of life, others to the resurrection of damnation,* and <margin>Matth. 25 verse 46.</margin> *These shall go into everlasting punishment, but the righteous into that eternal life.* So the Scripture makes a clear distinction / that they shall not all come to glory through Jesus Christ. The wisest word which we find in the Scripture regarding this, is <margin>Heb. 2 verse 10.</margin> *It became him, for whom are all things, and by whom are all things, that he, bringing many children unto glory, should make the captain of their salvation perfect through sufferings:* or as others read / *to complete;* <note>The author is discussing the Greek word *teleiōsai*, which can mean to make perfect, complete, or to consecrate.</note> Christ was, before the time of his suffering, not a complete Christ in the point of Mediatorship / although he was perfect in his Essence; and you who were thus perfect / brought only "many" children to glory; they are many when considered by themselves / yet but few / in respect to the other multitude. Christ shall bring many / but not all to glory.

# In Glory with Christ

...with eternal glory. This is a faithful word: if we have died with him, so shall we also live with him; if we endure, we shall also reign with him. <note>2 Timothy 2:11-12</note> So you see that the Scripture says those who shall reign and live with Christ must suffer and die with Christ—not dying through sin, but dying through the persecution of the people of this world. So also *1 Peter 4:13* and *Hebrews 10:36.*

**Thirdly**, whoever shall be in glory with Christ will be so powerfully persuaded by the Lord that they will use all possible means to glorify Jesus Christ while they live in this world. This can be a <term>pledge|an assurance or down payment</term> to them that they shall be glorified in Heaven. You who bring no income of glory to Christ, you can have no assurance in yourself that you will be glorified through him. You who have arranged all your life and deeds to display and dishonor Jesus Christ, with what face can you expect glory from him? Whoever expects glory through Christ, this must be his work: he must glorify Christ. *Romans 15:6, 7.* "That you may with one mind and one mouth glorify God. Receive one another, just as Christ also received us to the glory of God." Here the Apostle makes it a distinguishing mark of a person who shall be received into glory, that he glorifies God. We read in *John 17:4, 5* that Christ makes this a proof of why he should be glorified by God the Father in Heaven: because he had glorified him on earth: "I have glorified you on the earth, I have finished the work which you gave me to do; and now, Father, glorify me with yourself." Here Christ did not wish to speak of glory except on this ground: "for I have glorified you, O Father, on earth." Therefore, all of you who live worldly and godless lives—of which your conscience can testify—since you came into the world, you have hardly done anything for the honor and glorification of God: Well, take this to heart: you shall have no part in that eternal glory that is to be expected through Jesus Christ.

**Fourthly**, whoever shall partake in this glory shall find, before he dies, that the workings of the Word come upon his conscience with power, glory, and authority. The Word shall come so powerfully upon the soul that it will convince the judgment, terrify the conscience, stir the passions, work upon the heart, and change the life. In one way or another (before you die) it will thus work with majesty and power upon your conscience. *1 Thessalonians 2:12, 13.* "We testify to you, that you would walk worthily of God, who calls you to his Kingdom and glory." But who are those? Note the following words: "For this reason we also thank God without ceasing, because when you received the Word of God which you heard from us, you welcomed it not as the word of men, but as it is in truth, the Word of God, which also effectively works in you who believe." As if he said: Other people have heard us preach who were not ordained to glory; but they did not hear this as the Word of a God; they did not hear the Majesty of a God and the Authority of a God; convinc-

<column-break/>

-ing the judgment and persuading the conscience, working on the inclinations and winning the heart; but in you the Word has worked powerfully. In many godless people, it has a common working: sometimes the enlightenment of the understanding, sometimes the terror of judgment. The heart of <note>Felix was a Roman governor who trembled when Paul spoke of judgment but did not change his ways (Acts 24:25).</note> Felix trembled when he heard Paul preach of the coming judgment. But you who are ordained to the Kingdom of glory, you receive it not as a man's word, but as God’s Word, which worked powerfully in you. Examine now your hearts: you all have heard the Word of God, but have you heard it as the Word of a God? Has it had power and awe over you as God's Word? And has it had a powerful working upon you, to wake and make alive your hearts and consciences when they are insensitive and dead? Have you found this in yourselves? Certainly, before you die, if God the Lord brings you to glory, he will cause the majesty and power of the Word to come upon your conscience with awe, to work strongly in you. Therefore (what God might do, I do not know), until now you can have no certainty for your souls that you shall come into glory with Jesus Christ, since as long as you have lived under the Word, the Word has never had any <term>saving work|a spiritual transformation leading to eternal salvation</term> upon you; but you have been as if dead, insensitive, and hard under the <term>established means|the 'means of grace,' such as preaching and sacraments</term>, like the pews you sit in and the pillars you lean on: If it is so with you, you may rightly have suspicions that you will never come to this place of glory.

**Fifthly**, if God has ordained you to glory, you can know it from this: that God will work this disposition in you, that he will cause you to constantly long, wait, and look out for this glorious appearance of Jesus Christ, so that you may thus be in glory together with him. *2 Timothy 4:8.* "The crown of righteousness" (this Paul says in respect to that glorious state) "is laid up for me; and not only for me, but also for all those who love his appearing." Paul did not wish to keep this right for himself alone (although he was the most prominent among all the Apostles) that he alone should wear this crown of glory on his head; but it is for me and for all who love the appearance of Jesus Christ. He shall be seen by those who wait for him; *Hebrews 9:28.* "Looking for and hastening to the coming of the day of God," says Peter, *2 Peter 3:12.* <note>original Latin: "Non potest esse verus Christianus, nec recitare orationem Dominicam, qui non toto corde hunc diem desiderat"</note> Luther says regarding *Matthew 6:10*: "One cannot be a true Christian, nor recite the Lord's Prayer, who does not desire this day with his whole heart." That which makes them long for this time is because it is a day: 1. Of vengeance over their enemies. *2 Thessalonians 1:5.* "It is righteous with God to repay with affliction those who afflict you." And 2. Of forgiveness of their sins. This is the great <term>Jubilee year|In biblical tradition, a year of total debt release and liberation</term>, in which all debts shall be forgiven. 3. Of salvation for body and soul, *Hebrews 9:28.* Well, beloved, I pray you, take note: have you ever had such wishes and speakings of the heart as these? Oh, that Christ appeared! Oh, that Christ came! So that the misfortune done to his people might be avenged, on...

<meta>This page continues the list of "marks" or signs by which a believer may know they are destined for glory with Christ. It transitions from the inner desire for Christ's return to the necessity of love for his person and the active "mortification" (putting to death) of sin.</meta>

->### The Appearance of the Saints<-

...that her bonds were destroyed, so that my sins might be brought down and my soul might be saved, and these burdens and deformities that lie upon my spirit in holy services might be taken away, so that I may serve him without fear all my days. Have you had these longings of your soul within you? If this is not so—if you do not crave and long for Christ's appearance—it must proceed from one of two grounds: 

1. Either that you harbor some known transgression in your conscience, and then that sin brings an unwillingness to die and to come to judgment; and so the thoughts of Christ’s appearance to judge the world disturb the person. Sin on the conscience is like wind in the hollows and bowels of the earth: the <term>Philosophers|referring to ancient natural philosophy, such as Aristotle’s theory that trapped wind caused earthquakes</term> say that before an earthquake the air is still, but when wind is gathered in the innermost parts of the earth, it will cause ruptures, and burst out, and overset the greatest buildings, even mountains, where the wind is enclosed. So is sin in a person’s conscience; if sin be there, there shall be ruptures, assaults, and great disturbances; yes, there shall be "heart-quakes" if sin remains therein. And when this terror lies upon your soul, you would sooner wish that the rocks covered you, and that the mountains fell upon you, than that Christ should come to judgment. If you do not long for Jesus Christ, it is a proof that you allow the guilt of some sin to lie upon your conscience against your better knowledge. 

Or else, 2. That you bear little love for Jesus Christ. If Christ were loved by you, that love would desire the presence and enjoyment of Christ. Therefore, all you who have no longing of the soul for the coming of Jesus Christ, you cannot expect to be glorified by him.

**Sixthly**, all you who shall appear in glory with Jesus Christ: God the Lord shall ignite your hearts in love for the person of Christ while you live on Earth. You shall not pass immediately from a state of sin, of enmity, and of strife against Christ, to glory; but God will work this condition in you, that you shall love Christ before you come to glory with him. In *1 Peter 1:7*, the Apostle says of some that their faith, being tested and more precious than gold, was "found to result in praise, honor, and glory at the revelation of Jesus Christ." And who are these? Verse 8: they are those who, though they have not seen him, yet love him, and rejoice with an unspeakable joy. Those who have not seen Christ, and yet love him, shall be revealed at the appearance of Christ to praise, honor, and glory. Now I pray you, take note of this: you who do not carry in your hearts a true and upright love for the person of Christ—not only for Christ as a Savior, or in one of his offices, but for his person, for the whole Christ—you who do not love Christ for the beauty of his graces, as the Bride did in *Song of Solomon 1:3*: "Because of the savor of your good ointments, the virgins love you." <note>original: *Hoogl.* (Hooglied), the Dutch name for the Song of Solomon</note> God's virginal people, who are not defiled by foul desires, shall love Christ because of the "oil"—that is, for the sake of his graces. Well then, you who have no upright love in your heart for the person of Christ, do not expect to be glorified by him.

<column-break/>

**Seventhly**, to those who shall be glorified with Jesus Christ, God the Lord shall give <term>mortifying grace|the spiritual power to "kill" or subdue sinful impulses</term>, through which they shall overcome, keep under, and crucify the reigning power of sin and lusts in their hearts. God will work this in you at one time or another. And this is proven in the words that precede my text, *Colossians 3:3*: *“For you died, and your life is hidden with Christ in God; when Christ shall appear, you also shall be revealed with him in glory.”* You have died; what does that mean? Not naturally died, for then it would be in vain to speak to you; not died or dead in sins, as the godless are, otherwise you could not draw this comfort for yourself; but you have died, namely, to sin and to the world. You have power over sin by the strength of Christ’s Spirit sending mortifying grace into you. The power of sin is crucified and died in you, and accordingly, when Christ shall appear, you shall appear with him. *"Mortify therefore your members which are upon the earth,"* verse 5. 

All you, then, who live in the power of your lusts, who have a "law in your members" <note>A reference to Romans 7:23</note> not only fighting against the law of your mind like a tyrant—treating the law of your mind as a rebellious law—but you who consider the law of sin a law to which you willingly dispose your heart, and who do not reckon it slavery to live under the command of sin: all of you, take this as from God: you can have no proof for your soul that you shall be with Christ in glory. For if you are to be with Christ in glory, so shall you die—die to sin—and your life shall be hidden with Christ in God. Beloved, I pray you, bring your hearts to the touchstone of the Word, and measure your conduct accordingly, and see whether they are vessels of honor, ordained to appear with Christ in glory, yes or no.

**Eighthly**, it is a mark of one who shall be in glory with Jesus Christ to be steadfast in doing well, notwithstanding the perils and difficulties that might follow the practice of godliness. This is a mark of one who shall have glory with Jesus Christ. *Romans 2:7, 8, 9, 10*: *“God will render to everyone according to his deeds; but to whom will he give glory? To those who by persistence in doing good seek glory and honor, etc., eternal life.”* He shall give eternal life and honor and glory to those who, through patient persistence in well-doing, seek those things. So also verses 9 and 10: *“Glory, honor, and peace shall be for everyone who works good, first to the Jew, and also to the Greeks; but tribulation and anguish shall be upon every soul that works evil.”* Put these two things together: steadfastness in a good course, despite the danger and difficulty following it, is a sign that you shall have glory, immortality, honor, and eternal life.

Now I pray you, test yourselves whether you are so or not. Perhaps some of you make a profession of faith now: but what were you in the days of the <term>Bishops|likely referring to the period of Episcopacy before the English Civil War</term>? What were you when worldliness had much prestige? What were you before <term>Parliament|referring to the Long Parliament (1640-1660) which favored Puritan reforms</term> sat? What were you in those old days? Yes, what would you be, if the...

Ninthly; All who are ordained to glory, the Lord shall begin the work of sanctification in their heart in this world; wherever there shall be glorification, there must first be sanctification: for glorification must follow sanctification; the one cannot be without the other, **2 Thessalonians 2 verse 13.** > *We are bound to give thanks always to God for you, brethren beloved of the Lord, because God hath from the beginning chosen you to salvation:* but how was this? *In sanctification of the Spirit,* whereunto he called you by our Gospel; to the obtaining of the glory of our Lord Jesus Christ; note well, Paul says, we thank God that he has called you to salvation in sanctification of the Spirit. So that (beloved) you may never claim glorification for yourself if you never find sanctification within you; if God does not intend and purpose to sanctify you, he shall also never glorify you. You read that <term>golden chain|A theological term for the sequence of salvation described in Romans 8</term> of the Apostle, **Romans 8 verse 30.** > *Whom he did predestinate, them he also called* to be conformed to the image of his Son, *and whom he called, them he also justified, and whom he justified, them he also sanctified, and whom he sanctified, them he also glorified.* <note>The original Dutch text adds "sanctified" to this famous verse, which usually moves directly from "justified" to "glorified" in English translations</note> God does not glorify anyone who is not sanctified. **1 John 3 verse 3.** So that I would have all unsanctified people prayed for, who have not swept their houses with the broom of sanctification, and who have not been washed in the bath of rebirth: Do not be so bold as to harbor a confidence in your heart that you shall appear with Christ in glory; for those who are glorified must first be sanctified.

**Secondly**, He also brings this reason: although they would encounter difficulties in the flesh, nonetheless Christ would make their souls blessed; though their bodies suffered, their souls would be preserved, verse 22. For he who shall remain steadfast until the end, he shall be saved.

**Thirdly**, Christ promises them that, before they should have preached in every city, he would come with the blessing of his Spirit, to make their souls powerful for the conversion of souls, verse 23. Matthew 16 verse 28. Some believe that this is to be understood as until Jerusalem is destroyed; but Calvin <note>original: "Kalvin" — referring to the Protestant Reformer John Calvin.</note> understands it as the giving of his Spirit.

**Fourthly**, He supports them with this comfort: that Jesus Christ had a share with them in suffering; they must not strive to be above Christ, above their Master, verses 24, 25. *The Disciple is not above the Master, nor the Servant above his Lord; let it be enough for the disciple to be like his Master.* As if he said, do not let your courage sink; I, your Lord and Master, have suffered, and must suffer more; I must suffer death; do not then be discouraged, for the Disciple is not above his Master.

And then **fifthly**, there is another motivating reason in my Text: be not afraid, because the power of your enemies is limited. All that your enemies can do will only touch the body, but they shall not be able to do any harm to your soul. *Fear not them who kill the body, and cannot kill the soul*; thus telling them whom they should, and whom they should not fear: *But fear him much more, who can destroy both soul and body in Hell.*

Thus I have brought you to the words; now I shall give you the meaning thereof. *But fear him much more.* This word *much more* <note>original: "Mállon", a Greek adverb indicating a higher degree or "rather".</note> must not be taken in a comparative sense; as if you may fear men, but you must fear God more; rather, it is a word of contrast: you must not fear men at all, but God alone.

*But fear him much more, who can destroy body and soul.*] "Destroy" in this place is not taken for the annihilation of the body, but for a continual torment of body and soul under the wrath of God for all eternity. And so it is explained in Luke 12 verse 5. *Who has power to cast body and soul into Hell*, that is, to destroy soul and body. It would be good for the damned if soul and body were destroyed in the sense that they were brought to nothing; and the reason why both the body and the soul are spoken of is because the body had a share with the soul in sin, and therefore it shall also have a share in the punishment. *Fear him who can destroy soul and body in hell.* To destroy <note>original: "Apolesai"</note> and hell <note>original: "gehénne"</note>. The word Hell has a fourfold meaning in Scripture.

<margin>X</margin>
1. It is taken for the grave, Psalm 16 verse 10. *You shall not leave my soul in Hell; you shall not allow your holy one to see corruption*, that is, Christ would not lie rotting in the grave, but he would rise again. And so the Apostle Peter makes mention of this Prophecy, that he should not see corruption, nor be left in the grave

<column-break/>

<margin>]</margin>
Acts 2 verse 41. This he spoke of the resurrection of Christ from the dead.

2. It is taken in Scripture for the belly of the Whale, into which Jonah was cast; so it stands in Jonah 2 verse 2. *Out of the belly of hell I cried, and you heard my voice.* Jonah was never in hell, but the belly of the Whale is called Hell, because it is a dark place, like Hell. But you must not take it in this sense either. 3. Hell is taken in Scripture for the Devil himself, or for his evil Spirits; so it stands in James 3 verse 6. *The tongue is set on fire by Hell*, not hell the place itself, but the Devil in hell; it is he who lights the fire of a grim and fierce Spirit; the tongue is set into the fire by the Devil of hell. 4. It is taken in Scripture for the place of the damned, where God torments and plagues the souls and bodies of the reprobate unto all eternity; in this sense it is often taken, as in Matthew 5 verse 29, Luke 12 verse 5, Luke 16 verse 23, and so it is taken here in this place. *Fear him who can cast body and soul into hell*, that is, into that place of torment, which God preserves unto eternity for the punishment and tormenting of all godless men and women. Thus I have opened that expression, "in the Hell."

<margin>]</margin>
The word *hell* <note>original: "gehénne"</note>, which is translated here as Hell, comes from a Hebrew word, *Ge-hinnom*. Which means the Valley of Hinnom; it was a valley near Jerusalem, which was occupied by Hinnom, or his son, Joshua 15 verse 8, Nehemiah 11 verse 30. Hell is named in Scripture after the name of that place in a particular respect, because (as Lyranus <note>original: "Liranus" — Nicholas of Lyra, a prominent medieval biblical exegete.</note> relates regarding Leviticus 18 from the Rabbis) the idolatrous Jews erected an Idol in this Valley, named Molech, which was made of copper, in the shape of a human, hollow inside, in which the Jews lit a fire; then the children were placed in the hands of the Idol, and so burned. The Jews believed that the Father who gave up one of his children to this Idol would have a blessing upon all his other children. Well, from this comes that Greek word *hell* <note>original: "gehénne"</note>, and it has its reference to this place, because, just as there was a continual fire in that Idol, and a continual screaming and crying of children—so that they had to ring bells and play on all kinds of musical instruments, so that the cry of the children should not be heard—so shall it be in these fiery torments of Hell. You can read this History in 2 Chronicles 33 verse 6, 2 Kings 16 verse 3, 2 Chronicles 28 verse 3, Jeremiah 7 verse 31, Jeremiah 32 verse 35, Leviticus 18 verse 21. The pious King Josiah destroyed this place, 2 Kings 23 verse 10. Having thus explained the words, nothing remains for me to do but to give you the observations which the Text provides. Two Doctrines can be drawn from these words.

**First**, from the context, *But fear him much more.* That the fear of God strengthens the heart against the fear of man; the more you fear God, the less you shall fear men, Isaiah 8 verses 12, 13. *Fear not their fear, but sanctify the Lord of Hosts in your hearts, let him be your fear, and let him be your dread.*

<meta>This page continues the sermon on Matthew 10, specifically verse 28, moving from the comforting promises for believers to the terrifying reality of God’s power to punish the soul and body in Hell.</meta>

# Hellish Terror.

But I pass over this doctrine, because I have only intended, in the handling of this text, to set before you the pains of the damned in Hell, which may perhaps wake up some sleepy consciences; and I know for certain that it can greatly increase the joy of the Believers, who are delivered from these hellish pains. The observation then, which contains the essence of this entire text in itself, is this:

->That the consideration that God has an unlimited power over Men and Women, to cast their bodies and souls into Hell, must work a great fear of God in the hearts of his own people. This is the Point of Doctrine—a doctrine that brings terror and trembling.<-

First then, to handle this doctrine distinctly, I must necessarily present reasons why I am going to preach on this fearful subject, and then answer some objections that might be raised against preaching on such a terrifying doctrine as this is.

First, the reasons why I handle this are here:

1. Because I have handled at such length the glory of the chosen <note>original: "uytverkoorne" — the elect.</note> in Heaven, for the comfort of the godly; now I shall speak of the pains of Hell, for the punishment of the godless, so that if the glory of the chosen has not drawn your affections, the hearing of the pains of the damned in Hell may disturb your consciences and wake you from your carelessness.

2. I handle this so that none of you might become careless and presumptuous in feeding unfounded hopes of being in glory with Jesus Christ based on the previous sermons. So that you might not hope in vain, I have seen fit to add this material to it, so that you might be restrained in equal measure from presumption on the one hand, and from despair on the other.

3. Because it is a doctrine that is so little preached and written about in our days. I know of only one book in English written on this matter, by Mr. Bolton <note>Robert Bolton (1572–1631), a prominent English Puritan known for his vivid descriptions of the afterlife.</note>, and very few in Latin. Since it is then such a useful point—useful for the godless and useful for the godly—and yet so little handled, and in these days so much attacked and contradicted, I was driven by this to handle this doctrine.

4. I handle this doctrine because I am certain that if many people distinctly knew the pains of Hell, they would not walk in the way of sin which leads to Hell as they do now. I imagine to myself that if this doctrine of Hell were well considered and better known among the people, they would take more care to avoid Hell and obtain glory than they do now. If people only knew that those who live and die unconverted, lying and raving in their lusts, shall one day burn in the fire; if they only knew that those who can now swallow wine so immoderately and drink excessively shall one day drink sulfur <note>original: "Sulphur" — brimstone.</note> in Hell; if people only knew that those who now bite their teeth in hate and indignation against the godly shall one day gnash their teeth in Hell; if people only knew that those who now suppress God's children through persecutions and cast them into prison,

<column-break/>

shall one day be cast into an eternal prison, and shall be fetched by the Devils in Hell; if they knew that those who could not bear the company of the Saints here on earth shall be with the Devils and damned Spirits in Hell; if only people knew this doctrine well, they would not be so unholy and so godlessly godless as they are today. But the lack of consideration of this point opens a door for a multitude of wicked acts. For these reasons then, I have resolved to handle a little of this matter.

Now, there are two objections as to why one should not preach on such a point.

**First**, some will say, "This is Law-preaching <note>The speaker is defending against the accusation of "legalism" or preaching only the terrors of the Old Testament Law rather than the grace of the Gospel.</note>, throwing flashes of Hellfire into the congregations. This is not preaching the Gospel, but the Law." To remove this, I shall present four things in answer.

1. Certainly Jesus Christ was no Law-preacher, and yet he preached this doctrine; for these are his own words. Thus, the preaching of Hell and its pains cannot rightly be called Law-preaching, because Jesus Christ, the Minister of the New Covenant, was the one who preached most of all about Hell. It is remarkable that neither the Apostles nor all the Evangelists preached as much about Hell as Jesus Christ; for he has seven particular texts about Hell and the pains of the damned, which the Apostles did not have in that way. Therefore I say, it is no Law-preaching, since it is the doctrine of the Lord Jesus himself.

2. It is the great cunning of the Devil to rock people into carelessness in their sins so that he causes all soul-searching, sin-rebuking, conscience-waking, duty-urging preaching to be called Law-preaching. That is his great craftiness, to give such a bad name to such a good work.

3. If preaching terror is Law-preaching, then the Law is preached more in the New Testament than it was in the Old. I prove this thus: for more terrifying and fearful doctrines are scattered here and there in the New Testament than in the Old. It is noted by Chrysostom <note>John Chrysostom (c. 347–407), an early Church Father known for his powerful oratory.</note> that the word "damnation" is not used once in the entire Old Testament, but in the New it is used thirteen times. And it is further remarkable that although the word "Hell" is often used in the Old Testament, it is nevertheless generally taken for the grave, and not for the place of the damned; but in the New Testament it is always taken for the place of the damned, except for two places, namely Acts 2 verses 27 and 31. It is then patently clear that the Gospel is presented more with terror, and with doctrines of Hell and damnation, than the Law ever was. The preaching of the Law has only "Accursed" <note>original: "Anathema" — a formal curse or excommunication.</note>, but the Gospel has also "The Lord comes" <note>original: "Maranatha" — an Aramaic phrase used by early Christians.</note>. Therefore all those who are of the Antinomian error <note>The "Antinomian error" refers to the belief that Christians are released by grace from the obligation of observing the moral law.</note>, who do not want one to urge duties, calling it Law-preaching, such people deceive themselves greatly; for Christ himself, and the Apostles and Evangelists, all preached more to terror than any of the Prophets. Where it is said that preaching terror is Law-preaching, I say this, that Ministers...

<summary>In this passage, the preacher justifies his shift to the "terrifying" topic of Hell, arguing that it is necessary to awaken dormant consciences and prevent presumption. # Hellish Terror.

of terror have done more good for unconverted souls than the preaching of comfort. Preaching about Hell can keep many out of Hell. I have often read of Mr. Throgmorton <note>original: "Mr. Trogmorton"; likely Job Throgmorton, a prominent 16th-century English Puritan</note> that he was converted by a sermon of terror delivered on the text: *How shall you flee the judgment to come?* I have heard of another famous theologian who tells us that he was converted by the text: *Christ preaching to the spirits who are in prison.* I have read of Mr. Greenham <note>Richard Greenham (c. 1535–1594), an influential Puritan minister known for his practical divinity</note>, a famous preacher, who, hearing a sermon on the Last Judgment and the pains of the damned, was thereby converted and first called. I have read the same from various other ancient writers. Jerome <note>original: "Hieronymus"</note> says of himself: <note>original: "’t zy ik eet / ’t zy ik drink / ik hoor een stemme / klinkende in mijne ooren ; Staet op, staet op gy doode, en komt ten oordeel"</note> *Whether I eat or whether I drink, I hear a voice sounding in my ears: "Arise, arise you dead, and come to judgment,"* and this sound converted him; and so there are many more. Beloved, God has sanctified the doctrine of terror for the conversion of souls more than any other doctrine. And therefore it is noteworthy of John the Baptist, the forerunner of Christ, who prepared the way for Christ, that the first sermon he preached was a sermon of terror and coming wrath: *You brood of vipers, who has warned you to flee from the wrath to come?* And so this was the second sermon that Christ preached, and here he preaches a terrifying sermon on Hell. <note>original: "Ne fugiamus sermones de gehenna, ut gehennam fugiamus"</note> *Let us not shun sermons about hell, so that we may shun hell,* says Gregory <note>Pope Gregory the Great</note> in his *Moralia*.

But perhaps some will object and say: "It is true, preaching of Hell is permitted; but preaching of Christ's love and of free grace can win more souls; and these are the doctrines upon which one must mostly build, and which more refresh and gladden the hearts of God's children, and also have more power over men than such terrifying doctrines." I pray you, consider these five things in answer to this objection.

First: It is certainly so that if all our hearts were converted, then the doctrines of grace, love, and comfort would serve most for building up; but since we have to deal with a mixed people, so our teachings must also be mixed, otherwise we would not do much profit.

Second: It is certainly so that if all human natures were alike—if they were all of a soft and tender disposition, and were all troubled in mind and under a sense of God's wrath—then we would only preach of love and grace to lift up their hearts; <note>original: "nam ingenium potius trahitur quam ducitur" — for character is more often dragged than led</note> But since the Scripture tells us that the temperaments of men are diverse—some of a soft nature and disposition, others of a knotty and rough spirit; some want to be won by mercy, and some by judgment and damnation—so then our teaching must also be diverse; sometimes of Grace, sometimes of Judgment, so that just as the preachers of love shall win over soft hearts, so also the doctrines of terror may be for gnarled spirits. *Jude verses 22, 23: And on some have compassion, making a distinction; but others save*

<column-break/>

with fear; and snatch them out of the fire; and hate even the garment spotted by the flesh. Some, says the Apostle, you must show compassion, and preach of love and kindness; but others you must save through fire—that is, show them the Hellish fire and terrify them with the fear of God's wrath. Some are more pliable and tender; these one must handle with gentleness. Others, who are bolder sinners, must be saved through fear, pulling them out of the fire of hell. This is my second answer: some men's natures are more easily led than dragged; but others are so bold and hard that nothing but the flashes of Hellfire can make their consciences tremble.

Third: To those who plead so much for the doctrines of free grace and the binding up of comforts, and cannot bear to hear those terrifying things preached, I answer: human nature is readier to abuse the doctrine of free grace (although that must also be preached in its time) than they are inclined to abuse the doctrine of terror and coming wrath. This Jude tells us in *Jude verse 4: They change the grace of God into lewdness;* and the Apostle Paul brings up this objection: *Shall we sin, that grace may abound? God forbid.* Sufficiently indicating that some people did so; because grace was abundant, they also wanted to be abundant in sin.

Fourth: How can a preacher discharge his conscience before God, that he has preached the whole counsel of God to his people, if in the course of his ministry he shall only stand upon the doctrines of free grace, of Christ's love, and of comfort? What are the doctrines of terror—are they not also the will of God, which must be preached as well as comfort?

Fifth: These people who cry out so much about their preaching of love and free grace—I know for certain, following what some are accustomed to do, they have hardened more souls than they have ever converted through those sermons. As for me, Beloved, I know no one who has been converted by these new teachers <note>likely a reference to radical "Antinomians" or those who rejected the law in preaching</note> who pretend to have more light than their brothers and to present Christ more clearly than their brothers. I see no holiness shining in their lives above others. Whereas I am certain that those who have preached mixed doctrines—sometimes of fear, sometimes of love, sometimes of wrath, sometimes of grace—have worked most powerfully upon the consciences of men. I have read of Mr. Hildersham <note>Arthur Hildersham (1563–1632), a notable non-conformist preacher</note>, Minister of the Word at Ashby-de-la-Zouch, a very terrifying preacher, that it is said of him that God gave more success to his service for the conversion of souls than to all the preachers thereabouts. And when Paul delivered a sermon on the judgment to come, it made the heart of Felix tremble. And we find in the Scripture that just as God has his *Barnabas* <note>term: Barnabas — translated in the text as "Son of Consolation"</note>, sons of consolation, so he also has his *Boanerges* <note>term: Boanerges — translated in the text as "Sons of Thunder"</note>, sons of thunder, to make the undaunted hearts of men tremble. And so, that no one might be led away by deception, I am—

-># Hellish Terrors.<-

...thinking that all this is in accordance with the Law, I deem it appropriate to make this defense in my introduction to this matter.

Remember the Doctrine that was previously stated: That the consideration of this (that God has full power over the souls and bodies of Men and Women, to cast them both into Hell) must work a reverent fear of God even in God’s own children.

In handling this mournful subject, I have sixteen questions to work through. First, I shall investigate whether there is a Hell or not? Secondly, why there must be a Hell to receive the bodies and souls of the godless? Thirdly, what this Hell is? Fourthly, whether there are degrees of torment in Hell? etc.

**First: Whether there be a Hell, or not?** To answer this, I shall provide evidence from the confession of the Pagans—who had only the glimmers of nature and never saw the Bible—and secondly, I shall bring forward the testimony of the Scriptures.

<margin>1</margin>
1. It is evident from the confession of the Pagans; though they could not speak of it with precise distinction (having had no knowledge of the Word), they nonetheless had some imaginations and perceptions of this place of damnation through the glimmering light of nature. <margin>Virgil, book 6.</margin> Virgil tells us, <note>original: "facilis descensus Averni. &c. Æneid. lib. 6."</note> *the descent into the underworld is easy.* For this reason, they named one "Pluto," who was the supreme ruler in hell and who primarily tormented those who were most godless. And they had their "Charon’s Boat," <note>In Greek mythology, Charon is the ferryman who carries souls across the river Styx to the underworld.</note> convincing themselves that there was a man who transported the godless into Hell by boat. They also had their Etna—their burning mountains—which they believed were Hell. They also believed that the pain of hell consisted of continually rolling stones over dead bodies <margin>Virgil, book 6.</margin> <note>original: "saxum jugens volvvuntali. Virg. lib. 6."</note> (*they roll a huge stone*), along with many other imaginings. Thus they also believed that Pluto had many levels of Hellish pains; so that whoever receives no punishment after death must still have some iniquity within him to torment and plague him. All these were mere perceptions and imaginations of Hell. But I pass over this.

<margin>2. Deut. 32 verse 22. Psal. 9 verse 18. Psal. 11 verse 6. Matth. 23 verse 33. 2 Pet. 2 verse 4. Jude verse 6.</margin>
2. Just as you have testimony from the Pagans, so is this truth clearly presented in the Scriptures. But now:

**Secondly: Why must there be a Hell?**
<margin>It is evident from these arguments.</margin>
1. Because of the loathsome nature of sin. Sin is committed against an infinite God; and since the debt is infinite, the punishment must also be infinite. But punishment on earth cannot be infinite, for one remains 

<column-break/>

here only a short time, and bodies rot in the graves; therefore, there must necessarily be a Hell to hold the bodies and souls of men, so that they may receive the punishment that corresponds to the sins they committed on earth.

2. Because otherwise, the justice of God could not be satisfied for the sins the godless have committed here on earth. The reason is: 1. Because Christ was not willing to satisfy for those godless ones, nor to bear God’s wrath for them; so they must bear it themselves. 2. On earth, they cannot sufficiently satisfy God’s wrath. Why? Because since sin is an infinite debt, and punishment here can only be finite (lasting for a time), all their sufferings here cannot satisfy God’s wrath which is due to their sins. Therefore, there must necessarily be a Hell to contain men eternally, so that through eternal torments God’s justice might be satisfied, which otherwise could not happen. <margin>2 Thess. 1 verse 5.</margin> 2 Thessalonians 1, verse 5.

3. It is clear that there must be a Hell from those tremors and terrors of <term>Conscience</term> <note>The "inner witness" or moral sense, often personified in 17th-century theology as a judge within the soul.</note> that are within the godless when they die. Many a man, when he is healthy, will joke and mock Hell and hellfire. Many a man in health may never think of Hell, but can drink one day, swear the next, play the adulterer the third day, and sin thus day after day without the thoughts of Hell ever upsetting him. But bring this man to his sickbed, and what trembling and fear then seize his soul? I appeal to you, from a healthy drunkard to that same man as he is dying. (Just as someone said he wished to appeal from King Philip drunk to King Philip sober, <note>An ancient anecdote regarding Philip II of Macedon; a woman requested he reconsider a judgment once he was no longer intoxicated.</note> whereupon he revoked his sentence and did the man justice.) You who have spent your strength and your status in drinking and sinning until death, and who do not even think of Hell while you are drunk: I appeal to you when you lie on your deathbed, and ask, what would you say then? What would you give then for a Christ? Even those terrors and wounds of your conscience on your dying day prove that there is a time of torment which you will have to suffer; otherwise, how could the conscience be such a terrible plague to the souls of men on that day if Hell were not prepared for them? What made the Roman Emperors so afraid of death that they hid under their beds when it thundered? Only this: that the workings of the conscience showed them that something would come after this life. Thus, the terrors of conscience prove that there is a Hell—that is, a place ordained for the torment of the godless.

7. **It is called chains of darkness.** 2 Peter 2 verse 4. They are delivered into chains of darkness, to be reserved unto Judgment. This is because a person will be just as powerless to escape from Hell once they are in it as a person bound with chains and living in darkness is powerless to free or unbind themselves, or to find the way out of that dark place.
