<margin>Matt. 25: 34.</margin>
Now I come to the second Question, which is this: How can this passage say / That Christ, ascending, prepares Heaven for us / when in another place / in the Scripture / it says / That Heaven is prepared for us from the beginning of the World? Matthew 25:34. *Come, you blessed of my Father, inherit the Kingdom, which is prepared for you from the foundation of the World.* Now / If a Kingdom is prepared from the beginning of the world, how can it then be said in our Text, that heaven is prepared only from the Ascension of Christ?

The theologians <note>original: "Gods-geleerden," literally "the God-learned."</note> answer / That we must make a distinction between the decree of God, and between the revelation and execution of that decree. If you consider the decree of God, then that passage is true / That the Kingdom of Heaven is prepared from the beginning of the world; for the decree and purpose of God was / before the World was / that the Elect should have heaven as an Inheritance: But if you look at the revelation of the same / then it was not before Jesus Christ ascended; and this distinction is commonly used in Holy Scripture / and in the matter of justification. <margin>Hebr. 9: 8.</margin> You also have Hebrews 9:8. *Whereby the Holy Ghost signified this, that the way into the Sanctuary was not yet made manifest, while the first Tabernacle was still standing.* The meaning is this / That the way to heaven was not revealed to the Jews / while their Tabernacle stood; that is / while their Levitical Ceremonies were in use: The Godly went to heaven before the times of Christ / but it was not revealed to the common sort of Jews / who did not understand that they must come to heaven through the Suffering and Resurrection of Jesus Christ; therefore the Apostle says / *The way into the Sanctuary was not yet made manifest, while the first Tabernacle was still standing:* So is my Text true / that heaven is prepared for the believers through the Ascension of Jesus Christ.

The third Question is this / But (you will say) if Christ by his Ascension has prepared a place for the Believers, what then is to be held of the People of God, and of the Saints in the Old Testament? Or where have they gone!

The Jesuits make a difficulty of this Text / and say / That no one, before Christ's Ascension, went to Heaven, and that Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, with all the Patriarchs and Saints of God, were in a place called the <term>Limbus Patrum</term> <note>original: "Limbo of the Fathers." In Catholic theology, this was a temporary state for the souls of those who died in God's grace before Christ's resurrection.</note>, until Christ ascended to Heaven. They also say / That there is the <term>Limbus Infantum</term> <note>Limbo of Infants.</note>, a place for young Children, a <term>Purgatory</term> <note>original: "Vagevyer."</note> for great Sinners. Heaven and hell they mingle. The <term>Limbus Patrum</term> (they say) was the place that received all Believers, until Christ ascended, and then he took them with him to Heaven. The Protestant theologians have gone to much trouble / to free this Text from this deceptive opinion.

If you ask me / What became of the Patriarchs, and of all Believers, before Christ’s Ascension, how they came to Heaven— <note>The text ends with the catchword "geko-", the start of "gekomen," meaning "come."</note>

# To Prepare for the Believers

...come, if Heaven was first prepared for her in Christ’s ascension?

<margin>The benefits of Christ are valid not only forward but backward. Gerhard, *Loci Communes* <note>original: "Beneficia Christi valent non solum antrorsum sed retrorsum." First / I may say of Christ’s Ascension / just as Gerhard says of Christ’s suffering / Christ’s Death was profitable / before it happened; so I may speak of Christ’s Ascension / that it was profitable before it occurred. Gerhard has yet another reason / that the benefits we have through Christ / do not only move forward / to those who came after Christ / but also backward to all who were before him. *Revelation 5 verse 9: And they sang a new song / saying, You are worthy to take the Book, and to open its seals: For you were slain, and have bought us for God with your blood out of every tribe, and tongue, and people, and nation.* Not only was the Lamb slain in God’s decree / or in prefiguration / in all those ceremonial offerings / but effectively-daily; there was such a power in Jesus Christ / that all godly Jews had a share in his Death; this is my first answer.

Secondly, observe / that the Scripture does not say that Christ through his Ascension opened Heaven for us / and he being our Mediator seated at the Right Hand of God in Heaven / but Heaven was already opened beforehand / though not in such a full expansion as in the Ascension of Christ. *Hebrews 9 verse 8. Whereby the Holy Spirit signified this, that the way into the Sanctuary was not yet made manifest, as long as the first Tabernacle was still standing.* The Greeks note / that Christ here uses no word / which signifies opening a thing for the first time, but opening more clearly, and revealing a thing that was dark / and previously opened.

### Christ Ascends to Heaven

...will they go to the same place / as the believers go under the New Testament? Because they had the same Spirit / the same Faith / the same Gospel / the same Christ / and lived under the same Covenant / therefore they must necessarily go to the same place: And although Heaven is prepared through Christ’s Ascension / nevertheless it was already opened before / but not as clearly as after the Death / Resurrection / and Ascension of Christ.

**1. Application.** Now I come to the appropriation, which I shall set forth in four instructions from this Doctrine: If it is so / that Jesus Christ / by his going to Heaven / has prepared a place there for the Elect / then learn / by way of recompense / to show gratitude to Jesus Christ. Oh! prepare a heart for Christ / who has prepared Heaven for you. Shall Christ go to Heaven / to prepare a place for you? and will you not sell him a corner in your heart? You let your lusts sit on the throne in your heart / and do not give Christ any room there. We read Revelation 19:7. *Let us be glad and rejoice, and give honor to him: for the marriage of the Lamb is come, and his wife hath made herself ready.* Oh! are you like the Bride! make yourself ready against the Wedding-day: The Betrothal-day was / when Christ ascended to Heaven; the Wedding-day is the Day of Death. Oh! against the Wedding-day of the Lamb / you who are his Bride / make yourself ready! Prepare a heart for your Savior / who has prepared a place for you in Heaven. Origen has a good passage on Luke 22 verse 12. *And he shall shew you a large upper room furnished, prepare there;* <note>original: "Ende hy sal u een groote toegeryste Opper-zale wijsen, bereydt her aldaar." Origen (c. 185–253 AD) was an early Christian scholar and theologian.</note> although it is outside the scope of that Scripture passage. There were three divisions in the Hall / in which Christ ate his Supper / a lower, an upper, and a highest Hall, of which he makes this allegory: (which I give you not as the true sense / but as his gloss) That if you want to come to eat with Christ, you must make your heart like an Upper Hall, a heart uplifted in Divine meditations; and not only an Upper Hall, but also a lower Hall, a humble heart; an Upper Hall, adorned with graces. Oh! prepare a lower / an upper, and a highest Hall for Christ.

**Secondly,** if Christ has gone to Heaven / to prepare a place for the Elect / then we lose nothing by Christ’s bodily presence; and we are therefore no less blessed / than if we had Christ upon the Earth / even though he is in Heaven: For we receive more through Christ now he is in Heaven / than if he were in Person with us on the earth. The theologians illuminate this / and say / The body of the Sun stands fixed in the Firmament <term>Firmament: an old word for the sky or the heavens, thought of as a solid dome</term>, and gives its light to the whole World. Now / if the body of the Sun were taken out of the Firmament / and were on the Earth among us / it would not have that power upon us as it has now: The Sun of Righteousness, now he is in Heaven / is of greater profit to us / than if he were on the Earth: For if he were on the Earth / all the World could not see him at once; so that we now receive more through his going to Heaven / than if he were in Person even among us; just as

<column-break/>

Christ says / John 14:28. *Ye have heard how I said unto you, I go away, and come again unto you. If ye loved me, ye would rejoice, because I said, I go unto the Father: for my Father is greater than I.* And truly / it is a matter of joy / and not of sorrow / that Christ has left the World / and has ascended to Heaven / because he / going there / has prepared a place for us. I am eager to know / if Jacob would have been so troubled over his son Joseph, had he known that his son had gone to Egypt, to prepare a place for him and all his Brothers / against the hunger? Surely it would never have grieved him. Truly / your Joseph, your Jesus, has gone to Heaven / to prepare a place for you there; therefore do not let this disturb you / seeing that you are more blessed / by Christ’s presence in Heaven / than if you had him Bodily present on the Earth.

**Thirdly,** although Christ has gone Bodily to Heaven / yet this is the ground of your comfort; for although you have no place / to lay your head down / in the World / nonetheless remember that Christ has gone away to prepare Heaven for you. It may be that many of you have poor huts / smoky houses; truly this shall make your heart leap with joy / that Christ has gone into Heaven / to prepare a wide place for you there. Valens, the Arian <note>Arianism was a belief that Jesus was a created being, subordinate to God the Father, which was declared heretical at the Council of Nicaea.</note> Emperor / when he threatened Basil / and said / That he would protect him neither by Sea, nor by Land, from his Power; yet Basil said (notwithstanding all the Emperor’s raging) *I shall be in or under Heaven.* So likewise / although you may be driven across the Sea / and from the Land / having no place to rest your head / nonetheless / in spite of Men and Devils / you shall either be in Heaven / or under the same. A Cardinal threatened Luther with this / That there would be no place for him in the whole Empire. Oh! says Luther (laughing a little) *if the Earth cannot hold me, Heaven shall do it.* Beloved / lay this to your heart / that although you have no lasting place here on the Earth / nonetheless you have a prepared place for you in Heaven.

**Fourthly,** has Christ ascended to Heaven to prepare a place for the Believers? then all un-Christians and graceless People have no benefit through the Suffering or Resurrection of our Lord Jesus Christ. Christ has died / and risen again / but not for them: He has not prepared a place in Heaven for all; but they go to their own place / as is spoken of Judas / Acts 1:25 <note>The OCR says 12:5, but the context of Judas "going to his own place" refers to Acts 1:25.</note>. *That he may take part of this ministry and apostleship, from which Judas by transgression fell, that he might go to his own place.* It was not the place of Christ’s Ministry / but a place of old / prepared for damnation: Tophet <term>Tophet: a place in the valley of Hinnom near Jerusalem where fires burned; used as a biblical symbol for Hell</term> is prepared of old; prepared by an angry God / and not through a Mediator. This shall therefore be a matter of terror to all un-Christians and graceless People; for although Christ has gone to Heaven / nonetheless you shall never follow him there. Although he prepares a place for his Elect / nonetheless not for you; you have a place / prepared by a stern God / in...

## The Third Teaching
is a teaching of Christ’s return / *When I shall have gone away, and shall have prepared a place for you, then I will come again.* **Christ may tarry long / yet he shall not always tarry / for he who said / I go away, has also said / I will come again.** To now explain these words / *so I come again*; what is meant here by Christ’s return? Beloved / there are four kinds of interpretations of these words / of which only the last is true.

1. **By this return some understand Christ’s first coming** / just as the Jews do / (for some of them also study the Evangelists / though wrongly / not believing that Christ has come) of his coming in the flesh / John 4. **This was the feeling of a woman regarding Christ’s coming / Verse 25.** The woman said to him, *I know that the Messiah comes (who is called Christ) when he shall have come, so he shall declare all things to us.* When he shall have come; but she did not think that he had already come: Oh! says **Jesus Christ / It is I: I have** already come. The Jews and the Samaritans do not understand this saying as Christ’s coming for Judgment / but of his coming in the flesh.

2. **This cannot be understood as Christ’s coming through his Spirit** / as some interpreters take these words; *I shall come again through my Spirit*: and they match these words with that saying *I go away, yet I shall be with you until the end of the world*: But **Calvin** <note>John Calvin (1509–1564), the influential French theologian of the Reformation.</note> rejects this / because of the following words / *I come again, and shall take you to myself.*

3. **It cannot be understood / as the <term>Millenarians</term> <note>original: "Duyfent-Jaars-gesinden"; those who believe in a literal 1,000-year earthly reign of Christ.</note> take it** / for Christ’s return for a thousand years upon the earth; and of this I shall give you proofs from the Scripture / when I shall deal with that.

4. **By Christ’s return is here to be understood / as Calvin, and most interpreters take it / his coming to prepare heaven for you / and I promise to come again / and although your bodies shall be dead and rotted in the grave / nevertheless I shall by my return on that day cause you to rise again / and take you to myself;** And so this is to be understood as his final coming. And this much is said of the interpretation of these words.

Here we have then to learn / that Christ’s return for Judgment, is a teaching full of comfort for all believers while they live here on the earth: To prove this / read 1 Thessalonians 4. verse 15. until the end; *for that we say to you by the word of the Lord, that we who remain alive until the coming of the Lord, shall not precede those who have fallen asleep, for the Lord himself shall with a shout, with the voice of the Archangel, and*

<column-break/>

*with the Trumpet of God descend from Heaven, and those who have died in Christ, shall first rise: thereafter we who have remained alive, shall together with them be caught up in the clouds, to meet the Lord, in the Air: and so shall we always be with the Lord. Therefore, comfort one another with these words.* In the treatment of this / there are four questions to be answered.

1. **The first Question** is like an Objection / What comfort is this to us, that he commands we shall not be troubled, because he returns, when between the time of this promise, and the fulfillment of the same, already over sixteen hundred years have passed, and still he does not come.
1. **Answer.** The delay of time cannot weaken the promise / nor the comfort of that promise: what is promised / is comforting / whether it comes sooner or later? Daniel 10. verse 1. *In the third year of Cyrus king of Persia, a thing was revealed unto Daniel, whose name was called Belteshazzar; and the thing was true, but the time appointed was long: and he understood the thing, and had understanding of the vision.* It is a promise that Christ makes / to all you who are troubled in this World / he shall return: and although the time of his coming may seem long / nevertheless this does not take away the truth; it is certain / though it be long.

2. **The Godly in the ages before us** / could be joyful in the promises / made to them / although the fulfillment did not happen until after many years: and why should the Disciples not do as they did / or why should we now likewise not do so? I shall give you two or three examples / John 8. verse 56. *Your father Abraham rejoiced to see my day: and he saw it, and was glad.* The promise was made to Abraham more than a thousand years before / ere he saw him / and yet he was glad. An excellent text you have in Isaiah Chapter 9. *For unto us a child is born, unto us a son is given: and the government shall be upon his shoulder, etc.* See, this is a matter of joy / *for a child is born to us, a son is given to us.* They might have said / Lord what is this to us? we have rolled our garments in blood / and are choked by the War / and can you tell us / what shall happen after many years? and yet the Prophet deems / no more suitable promise to give them / than that a Virgin should conceive a Son. I relate this for this reason / that although the promises tarry long / that you nevertheless keep your heart at rest / for it shall truly and surely happen one day.

1. **Answer.** It appears from the expectation of the believers for Christ’s coming for Judgment. It is a characteristic of God’s People / to wait and to long for Christ / for this troubles their heart <note>The author contrasts the believer's longing with the trembling of the ungodly, like Felix in the Book of Acts.</note> / as in Felix. teaching of great comfort to the believers / and therefore it is called a day of release <note>Original Dutch: *verloffinge*, meaning a discharge from debt, a release from prison, or a day of redemption.</note>, and Peter calls it a day of renewal, which causes the Church to say / Come Lord Jesus, come quickly; This shows that no teaching is more comforting to God’s people / than the teaching of Christ’s return for Judgment. <margin>Tit. 2: 13.</margin> *Looking for that blessed hope, and the glorious appearing of the great God and our Savior Jesus Christ.*

2. It is a teaching of consolation / because Jesus Christ has preserved the full glory of the Elect until that time. Although Christ brings the souls into Heaven before his coming / nevertheless he does not fully glorify any of his servants / until his return for Judgment / <margin>1 John 3: 2.</margin> *Beloved, now are we the sons of God, and it doth not yet appear what we shall be: but we know that, when he shall appear, we shall be like him; for we shall see him as he is.* And <margin>Col. 3: 4.</margin> *When Christ, who is our life, shall appear, then shall ye also appear with him in glory.* God has reserved the full glorification of the Elect for the time of his coming / <margin>1 Pet. 5: 4.</margin> *And when the chief Shepherd shall appear, ye shall receive a crown of glory that fadeth not away.* There are abundant texts in the Scripture / to prove in detail that which we have said.

Thirdly, it is asked / is then this teaching of Christ’s return so comforting for the Believers? Answer: Yes, it is comforting to all believers in four cases.

First, in the case of any scandals or oppression / or any unjust suffering / which lies upon them / <margin>1 Cor. 4: 3, 4.</margin> *This is comforting / But with me it is a very small thing that I should be judged of you, or of man’s judgment: yea, I judge not mine own self. For I know nothing by myself; yet am I not hereby justified: but he that judgeth me is the Lord.*

*Punish me as you will / and judge me according to your pleasure / for he who shall judge me is the Lord / therefore it is my wish to be judged by you.* Suppose you were judged / slandered / and treated poorly in the World / appeal to Jesus Christ in Heaven / for he who judges there is the Lord, and so we shall find that Christ has done / <margin>1 Pet. 2: 23.</margin> *Who, when he was reviled, reviled not again; when he suffered, he threatened not; but committed himself to him that judgeth righteously.* When

you are reviled and insulted / do not revile or insult in return / but do as Christ did / commend your cause to him who shall judge the World righteously. Secondly, the teaching of Christ’s return is comforting / in the case of all persecution that you must endure for Christ and for the Gospel / <margin>2 Thess. 1: 6, 7.</margin> *Seeing it is a righteous thing with God to recompense tribulation to them that trouble you; And to you who are troubled rest with us, when the Lord Jesus shall be revealed from heaven with his mighty angels.* As if he had meant to say / you are troubled and persecuted for the Gospel and for the cause of Christ / truly / be not troubled / Christ shall come from Heaven / <margin>1 Pet. 4: 13.</margin> *But rejoice, inasmuch as ye are partakers of Christ’s sufferings; that, when his glory shall be revealed, ye may be glad also with exceeding joy.* When Christ reveals himself to judge the World / then you shall rejoice and be glad. This is a second case / in which this teaching is comforting.

Thirdly, this is a teaching of consolation / in the case of any internal accusations of the Conscience / in the understanding of your own guilt; it may be that you judge yourself / and count yourself among the damned Creatures / remember then that there is still a future Judgment over your failures / and torments / namely Christ’s Judgment / and this shall comfort you against your internal accusations / because he / who is Jesus / is your Judge / your Advocate / who shall plead those things for you. Suppose your Conscience accused you / and you condemned yourself to Hell / nonetheless comfort yourself with this / that Jesus hereafter shall come to judge you.

For although you may be insulted and wronged in the Law / it does no harm / for Christ’s coming for judgment shall be a great comfort for you. 6. Christ’s coming will make us preserve a good conscience, both before God and men, while living here in this world, Acts 24:15, 16. *And have hope toward God, which they themselves also allow, that there shall be a resurrection of the dead, both of the just and unjust. And herein do I exercise myself, to have always a conscience void of offence toward God, and toward men.* The thought of Christ’s coming to judge the living and the dead will make us preserve a good conscience, both before God and men. 2 Pet. 3:11. *Seeing then that all these things shall be dissolved, what manner of persons ought ye to be in all holy conversation and godliness?* And let this much be said of the first precaution: that you must look upon the teaching of Christ’s coming and practice holy duties just as much as you take the same for your comfort.

The second caution is this: to beware of making any peremptory <note>meaning final or absolute, leaving no room for debate</note> decisions regarding the obscure doctrine of Christ’s coming for judgment. There are many who have unnecessary thoughts concerning the place of this judgment; others wish to determine the time, which the Scripture itself does not determine; I shall not weary you with speculation on things that the Scripture does not reveal to us; to that end, guard yourselves against these things.

1. Beware of determining the place from which Christ shall come. The Papists <note>a historical term for Roman Catholics</note> maintain that he will come from the East; on this ground, they have built all churches facing East and West, because Christ shall come from the East. The Scripture does indeed say that Christ shall come like lightning from the East, but that does not indicate that he will come from that specific place; rather, when it is said that Christ will come like lightning, that signifies the visibility and speed of his coming: lightning is visible, and so shall Christ’s coming be; they shall all see him just as you see lightning. Now, to hold fast to the aforementioned idea would bring much superstition with it; the Scripture only says that Christ shall come from Heaven; but from which part of Heaven, it makes no mention.

Again, we must not determine the place where Christ will come to judge the world; many people wish to determine this place, which the Scripture does not do. There are many books written in which this opinion is maintained: that the place of Christ’s coming shall be the Valley of Jehoshaphat, and for that purpose they use a passage of Scripture, Joel 3:12. *Let the heathen be wakened, and come up to the valley of Jehoshaphat: for there will I sit to judge all the heathen round about.* From this, they conclude that Christ will come to the Valley of Jehoshaphat to judge the world there; I shall show you the vanity and godlessness of this opinion through these five arguments:

1. Because the Person who is said there

<column-break/>

to be about to judge is God the Father, not God the Son. If this passage were to be understood as Christ’s appearance for Judgment, it would have to speak of God the Son and not of the Father, for *the Father judgeth no man, but hath committed all judgment unto the Son*, John 5:22.

2. Because this judgment is only a judgment of the heathens. But on the day of the last Judgment, there shall be a judgment of all people, living and dead, good and evil. *For we must all appear before the judgment seat of Christ*, 2 Cor. 5:10. Therefore, this judgment cannot be meant here, seeing as only the heathens, and not the children of God, shall be judged there.

3. This judgment here is not a judgment of all the heathens in the entire world, but only of those who were around that place and near Jerusalem: *And those heathens round about* God wants to judge; that is, he wants to scatter them.

4. This Valley of Jehoshaphat cannot be the place of Judgment because it is not believable, considering all the people who have been, now are, or shall be, that the valley could contain them all. And therefore, the Valley of Jehoshaphat cannot be the place where Jesus Christ shall appear in glory to judge the world.

5. The time of this judgment is named in verses 1 and 2. Now, to give you the true sense of this passage: *Let the heathen be wakened, and come up to the valley of Jehoshaphat: for there will I sit to judge all the heathen round about.* This passage belongs to and has its view toward a particular judgment of God upon Israel's enemies who lived around Jerusalem, and not to the general day of Judgment in which Christ shall appear to judge the world—as Calvin <note>John Calvin (1509–1564), the influential Reformer</note> rightly observes—that God intended to scatter the enemies of Israel near that place: the Ammonites, Moabites, Chaldeans, and Babylonians; and the Lord wished to scatter all the enemies thereabouts. He wished to judge them there.

So this place is not the Valley of Jehoshaphat or the Mount of Olives, but only the Air, 1 Thess. 4:17. *Then we which are alive and remain shall be caught up together with them in the clouds, to meet the Lord in the air: and so shall we ever be with the Lord.* The Scripture makes no mention at all of Christ’s coming onto the earth. Beware then of determining the place of this Judgment.

Thirdly, restrain yourself from determining the time of the Judgment; there have been many who have committed great godlessness in this regard. Gerardus <note>Likely Johann Gerhard (1582–1637), a Lutheran scholastic theologian</note> points out the folly of those people who wished to determine the time of the Judgment. Augustine <note>St. Augustine of Hippo (354–430 AD)</note> makes mention of some in his time who held that Christ would come to judge a thousand years after his death; but experience has already revealed their folly. Others recount some who said it would be 364 years after his death.

This is likewise a great folly, for many more years have already passed. Luther <note>Martin Luther (1483–1546), leader of the Reformation</note> tells of Anabaptists <note>original: "Wederdoopers"</note> who said that Christ would come to judge the world in the year 1530. Likewise a palpable lie. Napier <note>original: "Napler." Refers to John Napier (1550–1617), the Scottish mathematician and theologian who predicted the end of the world in his work on the Book of Revelation.</note>, a Scottish nobleman—

->to prepare for the Believers. 542<-

is also carried away in this determination of the time, and says, that Christ's coming seems likely to fall in the Year 1688. <note>The year 1688 was a focus of intense apocalyptic expectation among 17th-century Protestants, coinciding with the "Glorious Revolution" in England.</note> But Beloved, Christ’s coming for Judgment cannot be determined, since Christ did not wish to do that favor for his own Apostles, to reveal this to them, Matthew 24. He did not want to recount to them when the end of the world would be. It is a great pride of the heart to strive for the knowledge of this time; Christ did not consider it necessary for his Apostles to know, 1 Thessalonians 5:1. *But of the times and the seasons, brethren, ye have no need that I write unto you.* Indeed, the Angels in Heaven, and Christ, according to his human nature, could not know this time, Mark 13:32. *But of that day and that hour knoweth no man, no, not the Son, but the Father.* Matthew 24:36. I recount this only to see the foolishness of our Age, and of those who want to investigate the specific day of Christ's coming for Judgment, which the Creator of the times did not wish to reveal.

I remember what a learned man says, writing about my Text: "There is nothing that hinders the Christian Religion more than when Preachers and listeners make questions of, and want to know, that which is not released to them or revealed in the Scripture; and to Jews and Heathens the entire Gospel becomes suspect, because they see men striving after those things which are not revealed in the Gospel, and so they make their foolishness apparent to all." Do not strive then for the determination of the time or place of Christ’s coming, since the Scripture does not reveal it. When Christ was about to die, his Disciples asked him where he would return? Luke 17 verse 37. *And he said unto them, Wheresoever the body is, thither will the eagles be gathered together.* He spoke to them of the destruction of Jerusalem and the end of the World; then his Disciples said, "But Lord, where will you come?" Christ gives them only this Answer: *where the Body is, there shall the Eagles be gathered*; that is, where Christ is, all the Elect shall gather, just as Birds gather by a dead Body; so that Christ never wanted to recount the place where, or the time when, and this shall make men cease to speak of those things of which the Scripture does not speak.

Finally, guard yourselves against taking up any wrong opinion concerning the matter of Christ's coming for Judgment, through idle and fleshly delusions of a temporal Kingdom of Christ. <note>The author is attacking "Millenarianism" or "Chiliasm"—the belief in a literal 1,000-year reign of Christ on earth before the final judgment.</note> Many give their judgments on this, and there are a multitude of Books written in which the specific manner of his coming is expressed: That Christ shall come from Heaven and be on the earth for a thousand Years, in which the Dead shall rise and live in this World; but these are such things of which the Scripture has no knowledge. And while I handle this promise of Christ, *I shall come again*, so this Question arises: Whether Christ spoke and understood this of his coming and reign here on the Earth for a thousand years, or whether he understood this of his final coming to Judge the world. This Scripture passage and others are brought forward to prove that Christ shall come from Heaven and Per-

<column-break/>

sonally live on the Earth for a thousand Years; they also imagine that when Christ shall establish this personal Kingdom, he will then cause the Martyrs to rise who have suffered for his sake, the Devil shall be bound so as to no longer tempt men to sin, and the godless shall be noted down <note>original: "opgeteekent" — perhaps meaning marked for judgment or restrained</note> so as to no longer persecute the Church of God. I recount this only to see the foolishness of our age and of those who wish to investigate the specific day of Christ’s coming for Judgment, which the Creator of time did not wish to reveal.

I remember what a learned man said, writing about my Text: "There is nothing that hinders the Christian Religion more than that the Preachers and listeners make a dispute of, and wish to know, that which is not allowed them or revealed in the Scripture; and to Jews and Heathens the whole Gospel becomes suspect because they see men striving after those things which are not revealed in the Gospel, and so make their foolishness apparent to all." Do not, then, seek after the determination of the time or place of Christ’s coming, since the Scripture does not reveal it. When Christ was about to die, his Disciples asked him where he would return? Luke 17, verse 37. And he said to them, *where the body is, there will the Eagles be gathered.* He spoke to them of the destruction of Jerusalem and the end of the World; then his Disciples said, "But Lord, where will you come?" Christ gives them only this Answer: *where the Body is, there will the Eagles be gathered*; that is, where Christ is, all the Elect shall gather, just as Birds gather upon a dead Body; so that Christ wished to recount neither the place where, nor the time when, and this should make men keep silent about speaking of those things of which the Scripture does not speak.

### Christ ascends to Heaven

Creation remains in subjection as long as the end of the world has not come, because other passages of Scripture tell you that the time of the <term>restoration of all things</term><note>The original Dutch 'weder-oprechtinge' refers to the 'apokatastasis' mentioned in Acts 3:21—the final renewal of the world.</note> cannot be until our bodies have risen from the dead. <margin>Romans 8:23.</margin> And not only this, but also we ourselves, who have the firstfruits of the Spirit, even we ourselves, I say, groan within ourselves, waiting for the adoption as children, namely the redemption of our body. That is to say: the creatures groan, still being instruments for God’s dishonor, as long as the bodies of the elect are not redeemed and glorified, lying under the curse because of sin. And even those who advocate for Christ’s personal reign of a thousand years here on earth—although they maintain that the martyrs shall rise in that time—nevertheless, they do not wish for all the elect to rise in that time. Therefore, the Apostle says explicitly that the Heavens must receive Christ until the time of the restoration of all things; until the bodies of the Elect rise from the dead. Again, it is evident from the preceding text, <margin>Acts 3.</margin> that the restoration of all things has no other focus than the time of Christ’s coming for Judgment.

1. Because the time spoken of here is the "time of Jewish refreshing" <margin>verses 19, 20, 21.</margin> from the presence of the Lord. *Repent then, and be converted, that your sins may be blotted out: when the times of refreshing shall come from the presence of the Lord. And he shall have sent Jesus Christ, who was preached to you before: Whom the heaven must receive, etc.* And they cannot be refreshed by the presence of the Lord before Christ’s Judgment and their resurrection comes.

2. It was the time in which God solemnly declared the forgiveness of sins to all the Elect: *Repent then, and be converted, that your sins may be blotted out.*

3. It is spoken of there as that which all the Prophets have testified to; now, those who push for Christ’s thousand-year reign here on the earth cannot say that all the Prophets have spoken of it: neither Moses, nor Daniel, nor any of the prophets together speak of this; therefore, this cannot be applied to Christ’s Thousand-Year Reign here on the earth. The second Scripture passage is found in <margin>Psalm 110:1.</margin> *The Lord said unto my Lord: Sit at my right hand, until I make thine enemies thy footstool.* Here it stands explicitly, that Jesus Christ, who has gone to Heaven and sits at the right hand of God, shall sit there until he has made his enemies a footstool for his feet. The Apostles also recount, <margin>1 Corinthians 15:23, 24, 25, 26.</margin> that all enemies shall be subjected to Christ’s feet, which cannot be before the final time. There is a coming of Christ which concerns all the righteous and the unrighteous; note now, Christ must reign in Heaven until he has placed all his enemies under his feet; now, in these thousand years, all enemies shall not be under his feet. Why? Because death will still be there, which shall not yet have been destroyed, and when the end comes, he shall deliver the Kingdom to his Father: and what is clearer than this,

<column-break/>

that the Heavens must receive him until the restoration of all things, and this can only be on the Day of Judgment.

Furthermore, Christ must reign until the end of the world. The third Scripture passage is <margin>1 Corinthians 15:23, 24.</margin> *But every man in his own order: Christ the firstfruits; afterward they that are Christ's at his coming. Then cometh the end, when he shall have delivered up the kingdom to God, even the Father; when he shall have put down all rule and all authority and power.* This passage tells you that when Christ comes out of Heaven, three things shall and must happen.

1. All people must rise, <margin>verse 23.</margin> Now that cannot be in the thousand years, for they [the Millenarians] themselves maintain that there shall only be a resurrection of the Martyrs, while the Scripture nevertheless says that all people shall rise, which cannot be before the Judgment.

2. When Christ comes, then comes the end; the Apostle joins them both together to indicate that Christ’s coming and the end of the world shall come at the same time.

3. He shall deliver his Kingdom to the Father; now if Christ were to reign here for a thousand years, he could not be said to deliver up his Kingdom, but would have to take possession of it; he would have to receive it from God his Father. When the Scripture expresses this so clearly, it is a wonder that people can still have such fantastical thoughts that Christ must come here to establish an earthly monarchy for a thousand years. The fourth passage is <margin>Hebrews 9:28.</margin> *So Christ was once offered to bear the sins of many; and unto them that look for him shall he appear the second time without sin unto salvation.* From these Scripture passages, I wish to argue against the <term>Thousand-Year-minded</term><note>original: "Duyſent-Jaars-geſinden" — a term for Millenarians or Chiliasts who believed in a literal 1,000-year earthly kingdom.</note>.

Firstly, it is clear that the coming spoken of here belongs to the Day of Judgment, verse 27: *It is appointed unto men once to die, but after this the judgment.* There, Christ’s second coming is linked to the Day of Judgment. Now if the Scripture calls this the "second coming," which is his coming for Judgment, then Christ cannot come to reign on the earth before that time; for if that were true, the Apostle would have to call it his "third coming." There has only been one coming from Heaven into a Virgin, and there is no other coming to follow but his second coming, which is for Judgment.

Secondly, it is said there that Christ’s second coming shall be for our <term>salvation</term><note>original: "Saligheyt" — often translated as blessedness or eternal salvation.</note>. If his coming were to reign for a thousand years on earth, that would only be a temporary good. But Christ’s coming must be applied to his final and greatest coming, in which he shall judge the world and make the souls of the Elect blessed and glorious. Beloved, these Scripture passages are clear to me. The reasons are two: that Christ shall not come personally out of Heaven to reign on the earth for a thousand years. This is because the Scripture indicates such accompanying things with his coming that can only be applied to his final coming to judge the world.

1. When **Christ** is said to come from Heaven / the Scripture tells you / that the Saints shall accompany him, <margin>Jude 14.</margin> And of these also Enoch, the seventh from Adam, prophesied, saying, behold, the Lord has come with his many thousand Saints. So that / when **Christ** comes from heaven / he must come with his Saints / indeed he must come with his Angels, <margin>2 Thessalonians 1:7.</margin> And to you who are troubled, rest with us, at the revelation of the Lord Jesus from Heaven, with the angels of his power. Place these two Scripture passages together / **Christ** must come with his Saints and Angels. But those who dream of Christ’s thousand-year coming / they cannot prove that **Christ** shall come with his Saints and Angels / because those Scripture passages / which seem to lean toward that / speak neither of the coming of the Angels nor the Saints.

2. It is said of Christ’s coming / that he shall then gather the good and the evil together, and judge them; now this cannot be understood as Christ’s reign upon the Earth; you have this in <margin>2 Thessalonians 2:1.</margin> And we beseech you, Brothers, by the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ, and our gathering together unto him. So that the coming of the Lord and our gathering unto him / to be judged / go together; see also <margin>Matthew 25:31, 32.</margin> And when the Son of man shall come in his glory, and all the holy Angels with him, then shall he sit upon the Throne of his glory and before him shall all the nations be gathered, and he shall separate them from one another, as the Shepherd separates the sheep from the goats. And <margin>2 Timothy 4:1.</margin> I charge you therefore before God and the Lord Jesus Christ, who shall judge the living and the dead at his appearing and in his Kingdom. The Scripture tells you / that when **Christ** shall appear to Judge the World / this shall accompany his coming / That he shall gather together the good and the evil, to judge. These / who hold that **Christ** shall reign here upon the Earth for a thousand Years, cannot prove / that they shall then all be gathered together; they say only the Martyrs and not the others, therefore this cannot be applied to his coming for a thousand Years upon the Earth.

3. When **Christ** comes / then is the end of the World / a complete end of the World, <margin>1 Corinthians 15:24.</margin> After that shall be the end, when he shall have delivered up the Kingdom to God and the Father, etc. When **Christ** comes / then comes the end; now / those who maintain Christ’s personal reign / do not want the end of the World to be / until after a thousand years / because **Christ** must reign for a thousand years.

4. The resurrection of both the Just and the unjust accompanies Christ’s coming, <margin>1 Corinthians 15:23.</margin> But every man in his own order: the firstfruits **Christ**, afterward those who are Christ’s at his coming. So that at Christ’s coming there shall be a general Resurrection of the Just and the unjust.

5. Finally / there shall be a state of blessedness for the souls of all the Elect / at his coming, <margin>Hebrews 9:28.</margin> So also **Chri-**

<column-break/>

**stus** having been once offered to take away the sins of many, shall be seen a second time without sin by those who wait for him unto salvation. This cannot be applied to Christ’s thousand-year reign here on the earth / because he does not then come to make the souls of all the elect blessed; This is the first reason / why **Christ** cannot come here for a thousand Years upon the earth / because of these five things which the Scripture tells us shall accompany his coming / when he comes to Judge the World. The second Reason / why **Christ** cannot come to reign for a thousand Years upon the earth / is / that in that time / it would be worse for him than before / because he would have to leave heaven / and come onto the earth / separating from the Saints / and Angels / and heaven / and dwell among the Godless and the pious on the earth / they themselves confess that there shall also be Godless people on the earth. In addition to this they dream of earthly pleasures / that the fruit of the vine shall not perish as it does now / nonetheless they diminish Christ’s glory / because he now sits at the right hand of his Father: Again / if their dreams were true / it would diminish the glory of the Elect / for they have obtained an eternal benefit through Christ’s intercession; and if **Christ** were on the earth / we would lose that benefit, <margin>Hebrews 8:4.</margin> For if he were on the earth, then he would not even be a Priest, while there are Priests there who offer gifts according to the Law. So that / if he were on the earth / we would lose the benefit of his Priestly Office <term>Priestly Office</term><note>The 'Priester-Ampt' refers to the theological concept of Christ's ongoing work in heaven as a mediator between God and humanity.</note>; Therefore / it would be a great injustice to us / to have **Christ** here on the earth / because the benefit of his Priestly office would not be so powerful for us as it is in heaven. Thus have I given you Scripture passages and reasons / why **Christ** cannot come before his final coming.

->Now there are seven inconveniences or absurdities, which would follow / in case you held fast / that **Christ** would come to reign for a thousand Years on the earth.<-

1. From this it would follow that men would truly know the perfect time of Christ’s coming to Judge the World; for those who drive the aforementioned opinion / hold to the time as well as the matter / and say when this reign shall begin; for this reason some have thought that **Christ** would come to reign on Earth in the Year 1650. Another says / If it shall not be in the Year 1650, it shall be in the Year 1694. Now / if that time were true / one would necessarily be able to know the exact time of the day of judgment / because it will be immediately after the passing of the thousand Years. Now Beloved / this opinion includes this absurdity / that one would then know Christ's coming to Judgment / which **Christ** says no one in the World can know, <margin>Mark 13:32.</margin> But of that day and that hour knows no man, no, not the Angels who are in heaven, nor the Son, but the Father.

2. Through Christ’s coming for a thousand Years here on the earth / great dishonor would happen to **Christ**; he would have to leave his Father and Heaven / and come to possess only the earth. Now / **Christ** has more blessedness in the immediate enjoyment of his Father in heaven / than he can have here on the earth:

### To prepare for the Believers

<margin>Signature: Zz 3</margin>

1. When Christ is said to come from Heaven, the Scripture tells you that the Saints shall accompany him, <margin>Jude 14.</margin> *And Enoch also, the seventh from Adam, prophesied of these, saying, Behold, the Lord cometh with ten thousands of his saints.* So that when Christ comes from heaven, he must come with his Saints; indeed, he must come with his Angels, <margin>2 Thessalonians 1:7.</margin> *And to you who are troubled rest with us, when the Lord Jesus shall be revealed from heaven with his mighty angels.* Set these two scriptural passages together: Christ must come with his Saints and Angels. But those who dream of Christ’s thousand-year coming cannot prove that Christ shall come with his Saints and Angels; for those scriptural passages that seem to lean that way do not speak of the coming of the Angels nor the Saints.

2. It is said of Christ’s coming that he shall then gather the good and the evil together and judge them; now, this cannot be reconciled with Christ’s reign on the Earth. You have this in <margin>2 Thessalonians 2:1.</margin> *Now we beseech you, brethren, by the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ, and by our gathering together unto him.* Thus, the coming of the Lord and our gathering to him to be judged go together; see also <margin>Matthew 25:31, 32.</margin> *When the Son of man shall come in his glory, and all the holy angels with him, then shall he sit upon the throne of his glory: And before him shall be gathered all nations: and he shall separate them one from another, as a shepherd divideth his sheep from the goats.* And <margin>2 Timothy 4:1.</margin> *I charge thee therefore before God, and the Lord Jesus Christ, who shall judge the quick and the dead at his appearing and his kingdom.* The Scripture tells you that when Christ shall appear to judge the World, this shall accompany his coming: that he shall gather together the good and the bad to judge them. Those who hold that Christ shall reign here on Earth for a thousand years cannot prove that they shall all be gathered together then; they say only the Martyrs [will rise] and not the others; therefore, this cannot be applied to his coming for a thousand years on the Earth.

3. When Christ comes, then is the end of the World, a complete end of the World, <margin>1 Corinthians 15:24.</margin> *Then cometh the end, when he shall have delivered up the kingdom to God, even the Father,* etc. When Christ comes, then comes the end; now, those who maintain Christ’s personal reign do not want it to be the end of the world until after a thousand years, because Christ must reign for those thousand years.

4. The resurrection of both the Just and the unjust accompanies Christ’s coming, <margin>1 Corinthians 15:23.</margin> *But every man in his own order: Christ the firstfruits; afterward they that are Christ’s at his coming.* So that at Christ’s coming there shall be a general Resurrection of the Just and the unjust.

5. Lastly, there shall be a salvation for the souls of all the elect at his coming, <margin>Hebrews 9:28.</margin> So also Chri-

<column-break/>

stus, having been offered once to take away the sins of many, shall appear a second time, without sin, to those who wait for him unto salvation. This cannot be applied to Christ’s thousand-year Reign here on earth, because he does not then come to save the souls of all the elect. This is the first reason why Christ cannot come for a thousand years here on earth: because of these five things which the Scripture tells us shall accompany his coming when he comes to Judge the World. The second Reason why Christ cannot come to reign for a thousand years on the earth is that, at that time, it would be worse for him than before, because he would have to leave heaven and come to the earth, separating from the Saints, and Angels, and heaven, and dwelling among the Godless and the godly on the earth; they themselves confess that there shall also be Godless people on the earth. Besides this, they dream of earthly pleasures—that the fruit of the vine shall not perish as it does now—yet they diminish Christ’s glory, because he now sits at the right hand of his Father. Again, if their dreams were true, it would diminish the glory of the Elect, for they have obtained an eternal benefit through Christ’s intercession <note>The original Dutch 'voorspiddinge' refers to Christ’s role as mediator and intercessor.</note>; and if Christ were on the earth, we would lose that benefit, <margin>Hebrews 8:4.</margin> *For if he were on earth, he should not be a priest, seeing that there are priests that offer gifts according to the law.* So that if he were on the earth, we would lose the benefit of his Priestly Office; therefore, it would be a great injustice to us to have Christ here on the earth, because the benefit of his Priestly Office would not be as powerful for us as it is in heaven. Thus I have given you scriptural passages and reasons why Christ cannot come before his final coming.

->Now, there are seven inconveniences or absurdities that would follow if you firmly established that Christ would come to reign for a thousand years on the earth.<-

1. From this it would follow that men would truly know the exact time of Christ’s coming to Judge the world; for those who drive this aforementioned opinion hold to the time as much as the event, and say when this reign shall begin; for this reason, some have thought that Christ would come to reign on Earth in the Year 1650. Another says, if it shall not be in the Year 1650, it shall be in the Year 1694. <note>These dates refer to specific predictions made by radical Protestant groups like the Fifth Monarchists who expected the apocalypse in the mid-17th century.</note> Now, if that time were true, one would necessarily be able to know the precise time of the day of judgment, for it would be immediately after the passing of the thousand years. Now, Beloved, this opinion strikes against this absurdity: that one would then know Christ’s coming for Judgment, which Christ says no one in the World can know, <margin>Mark 13:32.</margin> *But of that day and that hour knoweth no man, no, not the angels which are in heaven, neither the Son, but the Father.*

2. Through Christ’s coming for a thousand years here on the earth, great dishonor would happen to Christ; he would have to leave his Father and Heaven, and come only to possess the earth. Now, Christ has more blessedness in the immediate enjoyment of his Father in heaven than he can have here on the earth.

### Christ ascends to Heaven

Likewise, it would result in damage and a diminishing of our being, as we have shown above.

3. Note that if Christ were to come to reign here on the earth for a thousand years, he would then, after those thousand years, leave his Church in a worse condition than he found it; this is proven from <margin>Revelation 20:5, 7, 8.</margin> *But the rest of the dead lived not again until the thousand years were finished. This is the first resurrection. And when the thousand years are expired, Satan shall be loosed out of his prison. And shall go out to deceive the nations which are in the four quarters of the earth, Gog and Magog, to gather them together to battle: the number of whom is as the sand of the sea.* So that after the thousand years, the devil shall be loosed again, and there shall be an innumerable number of enemies, and so the multitude of the godly shall be scattered <note>original: "verstropen," likely meaning scattered or overwhelmed</note>; therefore Christ would leave his Church in a worse state than before, if it were true that Christ should reign on the earth for a thousand years.

4. This further inconsistency would follow: that there would be a three-fold coming of Jesus Christ. 1. His coming in the flesh. 2. His coming in these thousand years. 3. His coming for Judgment, which is his final coming. But the Scripture mentions only two comings of Christ: one in the flesh, when he was born; and one when he shall come again to judge the world.

5. If Christ were to come personally from heaven to reign for a thousand years, then this absurdity must follow: that either the Saints and Angels come with him, or they do not. If they were to come with Christ, it diminishes their state, for they currently enjoy the immediate presence of God, and coming to earth they would be among the ungodly. Or, if they do not come with him, it is likewise to their disadvantage, for then they would lose Christ’s bodily presence for a thousand years. If Christ is on the earth, he cannot be in heaven at the same time; therefore, this would serve to diminish the joy of the Saints and Angels, if Christ were to come to the earth for a thousand years.

6. If the opinion of the <term>Millenarians<note>original: "Duyfent-Iaars-gesinde," literally "Thousand-year-minded"; those who believe in a literal thousand-year earthly reign of Christ.</note></term> were true, then Christ must have an earthly and physical Kingdom, visible to the Jews and visible to the entire world; but this contradicts God’s word, <margin>John 18:36.</margin> *Jesus answered, My kingdom is not of this world: if my kingdom were of this world, then would my servants fight, that I should not be delivered to the Jews: but now is my kingdom not from hence.* <margin>Luke 17:20.</margin> *And when he was demanded of the Pharisees, when the kingdom of God should come, he answered them and said, The kingdom of God cometh not with outward show.* Should the whole world not take note of this? Christ would come physically from Heaven in the majesty of a Monarch, yet his Kingdom would "not come with outward show"? When the Disciples looked for an earthly Kingdom, Christ said: No, my Kingdom is to reign in your hearts; you shall never see me be a pompous king of this world, for my Kingdom is a spiritual Kingdom.

<column-break/>

7. It would also follow as if Jesus Christ had no Kingdom, and were no King of the earth, for all the time while he is in heaven; they deny the passage in Daniel, and all those sayings in the New Testament, that the Kingdom of the World is a Kingdom of the Lord; they deny that Christ is King in Heaven. At the very hour when he lay in the manger and was born in the stable, he was King, <margin>Psalm 2.</margin> The Apostle applies this to Christ’s birth and Resurrection. When Christ rose from the dead, then he was King, and the Gospel in the times of Christ was called a Kingdom. It is to be noted what is written in <margin>John 18:37.</margin> *Pilate therefore said unto him, Art thou a king then? Jesus answered, Thou sayest that I am a king.* Christ was a King, though no earthly King <note>original: "Aarts Koning," meaning a temporal or worldly ruler</note> intended to displace earthly governments; therefore, when the people in a riot wanted to make him King, he would not have it. <margin>Zechariah 9:9.</margin> *Rejoice greatly, O daughter of Zion; shout, O daughter of Jerusalem: behold, thy King cometh unto thee: he is just, and having salvation; lowly, and riding upon an ass, and upon a colt the foal of an ass.* He was King when he was regarded as a despised creature; so that to say Christ shall now come to reign as King in the world, as if he were not King at this time, would diminish his Royal dignity; for he is King of Kings and Lord of Lords in heaven; therefore he cannot come to reign for a thousand years here on the earth.

Now I wish to go further and show you the strongest passages of Scripture which seem to confirm this opinion, and then I shall labor to take those away from you and explain them. There are many places upon which they wish to ground this sentiment of theirs; nevertheless, I shall stand mostly upon their specific passages; their primary passage stands in <margin>Revelation 20:2, 3, 4, 5, 6.</margin> *And he laid hold on the dragon, that old serpent, which is the Devil, and Satan, and bound him a thousand years, and cast him into the bottomless pit... And after that he must be loosed a little season... And I saw the souls of them that were beheaded for the witness of Jesus, and for the word of God, and which had not worshipped the beast, neither his image, neither had received his mark upon their foreheads, or in their hands; and they lived and reigned with Christ a thousand years. But the rest of the dead lived not again until the thousand years were finished. This is the first resurrection. Blessed and holy is he that hath part in the first resurrection: on such the second death hath no power, but they shall be priests of God and of Christ, and shall reign with him a thousand years. And when the thousand years are expired, Satan shall be loosed out of his prison, etc.* Now, from this text they draw primarily two things.

Firstly, that Christ shall come and live on the earth, and the Saints shall reign with him for a thousand years.

Secondly, that those who were martyred by the Antichrist shall rise from the dead, come upon the earth, and converse with Jesus Christ for a thousand years. This they build... <note>The text cuts off mid-sentence, leading into the next page.</note>

# to prepare for the Believers.

...to build upon Christ’s thousand-year reign on the earth. But I shall show you that this is not the meaning of this text, and give you six answers.

1. Although Scripture says that the Saints who were beheaded shall live with Christ for a thousand years, nonetheless the text does not say that Christ shall come with them to reign for a thousand years.

2. Although the text says they shall live and reign with Christ for a thousand years, the text does not say they shall reign with him here on the Earth.

3. Although it is said that the Saints shall live and reign with Christ for a thousand years, this life and this reign do not necessarily need to be in the same place where Christ is; for then you would want to twist many Scripture passages. For behold, Christ says, "I am with you until the end of the world." Therefore it does not follow that he is on the Earth from that time until the end of the world. For Christ is with us, and we with him, through his Spirit.
<margin>Romans 8:17</margin>
> *And if we are children, then we are heirs; heirs of God, and joint-heirs with Christ; if so be that we suffer with him, that we may be also glorified together.*

This text is not to be understood as a familiarity of place <note>meaning physical proximity or occupying the same location</note>, but of the Spirit.

4. It is clear that Scripture cannot be a foundation upon which to build the idea that Christ shall come to reign on Earth for a thousand years; because it would then follow not only that people would have to live that long, but also reign with Christ on Earth for that long. Methuselah lived only nine hundred and sixty-nine years, and David says the life of man is cut off and shortened. If this "thousand-year-edifice" <note>meaning the theological theory of the Millennium</note> were true, all people together would have to live a thousand years. Furthermore, this cannot be the meaning of the aforementioned Scripture passage because the meaning of one passage cannot contradict another. One cannot conclude from one passage that Christ shall come and reign for a thousand years on earth, while another Scripture passage says Christ shall remain in Heaven until such time as all people shall rise from the dead, and then the end shall be.
<margin>1 Corinthians 15:23, 24</margin>
> *But every man in his own order: Christ the firstfruits; afterward they that are Christ’s at his coming. Then cometh the end, etc.*
<margin>2 Thessalonians 2:1</margin>
> *Now we beseech you, brethren, by the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ, and by our gathering together unto him.*

Moreover, it contradicts Scripture that only some, and not all people, should rise.
<margin>Job 14:10, 11, 12</margin>
> *But man dieth, and wasteth away: yea, man giveth up the ghost, and where is he? As the waters fail from the sea, and the flood decayeth and drieth up: So man lieth down, and riseth not: till the heavens be no more, they shall not awake, nor be raised out of their sleep.*

There Job tells you explicitly that the dead shall not be raised until the Heavens are no more. And this cannot be understood as the thousand years, for then there shall still be heaven and earth; Peter also says the Heavens shall melt, etc. Now, to make a resurrection before the true resurrection—of that the Scripture makes

<column-break/>

no mention.
<margin>John 5:28, 29</margin>
> *Marvel not at this: for the hour is coming, in the which all that are in the graves shall hear his voice, And shall come forth; they that have done good, unto the resurrection of life; and they that have done evil, unto the resurrection of damnation.*

The judgment of the Righteous and Unrighteous shall be at the same hour, and at the coming of Christ all people shall be judged.
<margin>2 Timothy 4:1</margin>
> *I charge thee therefore before God, and the Lord Jesus Christ, who shall judge the living and the dead at his appearing and in his kingdom.*

So that at Christ’s appearing and coming, the living and the dead shall be judged. Now beloved, since Christ’s coming for a thousand years <note>referring to a separate coming before the final judgment</note> would overthrow his final coming, this cannot be the objective of that text, for there is no contradiction in Scripture.

5. When the Scripture says there that they shall live and reign with Christ a thousand years, that is not spoken of reigning with Christ in Heaven or on the Earth; the phrase indicates neither one nor the other.

6. John does not say that he saw the *bodies* that were beheaded reigning with Christ for a thousand years; but he saw in a vision the *souls* that were beheaded. Now, to say that they must come and reign for a thousand years on the earth would be a great lessening <note>original: "verkleeninge," meaning a reduction in status or a demotion from heavenly glory</note> for them. The thousand years cannot be applied to Christ’s personal reign on the earth; for Christ has an eternal Kingdom; he does not reign for a thousand years on the earth or in Heaven, but eternally. The kingdoms and states of this world last for years, but Christ’s Kingdom lasts longer, even eternally. This I find to be the sense of this text, after I have consulted with many writers, although there are some who want the Devil to be bound for a thousand years, and during that time, the Saints shall reign with Christ for a thousand years. The sense and the objective of that passage is this:

The perfection of the time when the devil was bound—all interpreters agree on this—is that this time began in the reign of **Constantine the Great**, the first Christian Emperor. He came after the 300-year persecution carried out by the Roman Emperors, who caused great killings and decays in the Church of God; so that, as we read in the books of Martyrs, often in one day of the year, five thousand Christians were slain; an early persecution, a terrible raging and unleashing of the Devil. Now, in the reign of Constantine, the Devil was bound up; that is, the Roman Emperors—cruel instruments of the Devil—were brought to naught through his reign, as he gave a law for the free exercise of the Christian Religion; and thus the persecution by the Roman Emperors ceased. This is the meaning of many interpreters regarding these thousand years, with which **Brightman**, **Napier**, and **Gerhardus** <note>Thomas Brightman, John Napier, and Johann Gerhard were prominent 16th/17th-century Protestant theologians and biblical commentators</note> also agree.

1. **Objection:** But you will say, that is well regarding the binding of the Devil, but how and at what time was he loosed again?

**Answer:** This happened in the year 1300, when the Turkish Emperors <note>the Ottomans</note> took the upper hand, and conquered Gog and Magog...

# Christ ascends, for Heaven

conquered, and mastered the greatest part of the World; these *Gog* and *Magog* <note>In biblical prophecy, these names represent the forces of evil that gather for a final battle against God's people</note> were those who persecuted the Saints and scattered them across nearly the entire earth; and truly, if you compare the Scripture and the Histories together, you shall find that this is the true meaning of this passage.

->Those who believe in the thousand-year reign <note>original: "duyfent-jaars-gesinden"; also known as Chiliasts</note> raise two Objections here.<-

1. We read that the Church was persecuted by the Emperor *Valens* after the three-hundred years, and by *Julian* the Apostate, who persecuted the Christians exceedingly; how can this be true, since we read of such persecutions after the Devil was bound?

**Answer:** When it says that the Devil would be bound, it is not to be understood simply as if there would be no temptation to sin—no, that shall always be there. The Emperor *Valens* confirmed the *Arian Doctrine* <note>Arianism: a belief that Jesus was not fully God, which was declared a heresy by the early Church</note> and troubled the Church of God. One Answer is: That this persecution had no equal to those carried out by the Roman Emperors, as it was not so long or difficult; for previously, 5,000 Christians were killed in a single day. Under the reign of *Diocletian*, 17,000 Christians were killed in one month, so that the persecution under *Valens* and *Julian* was but a small and shadow-persecution in comparison to the former ones under the Heathen Emperors.

2. **Objection:** But the Scripture says, That this is the first resurrection, that the Saints shall live and reign with Christ a thousand years; how can this be applied to the restoration under *Constantine*?

**Answer:** In the Scripture, the word Resurrection is taken not only for the bodily rising from the grave, but for a rising up out of a state of oppression and sin; this is expressed in the Scripture as a resurrection, *Romans 11:10*: "Let their eyes be darkened, that they may not see: and bow down their back alway."

I say, have they then stumbled so as to fall? God far prefers to prevent their fall; Salvation comes from the Gentiles, for he is jealous because of this, *Isaiah 22 verse 19*: "And I will drive thee from thy station, and from thy state shall I pull thee down." Those people who were poor and humble in the captivity of *Babylon* would rise again, which can in no way be applied to the resurrection on the last day. So also a resurrection from sin is spoken of, *Colossians 2:12*: "Being buried with him in baptism, in which you also are raised with him through faith in the working of God, who raised him from the dead." We have risen with Christ, not bodily, but out of our sins, *Colossians 3:1*: "If ye then be risen with Christ, seek those things which are above, where Christ sitteth at the right hand of God." So this is the meaning of the first Resurrection: they preserved themselves during the persecution from the Idolatry of the Heathens and from the corruptions of the Antichrist, and for this reason they are said to have a part in the first Resurrection. Blessed are they who through Christ have risen from sins, from Heresies, Superstitions, and Idolatry, both of the Antichrist and of the Heathens.

Beloved, it is further said there, That they

<column-break/>

shall live and reign with Christ; although some Interpreters apply this to Heaven, nonetheless it is better, following *Brightman* <note>Thomas Brightman (1562–1607), an English clergyman and influential biblical commentator</note> and others, in agreement with *Bernard* <note>Saint Bernard of Clairvaux (1090–1153)</note>, to apply this to the following Ages, in which they enjoyed freedom in the Christian Religion under *Constantine the Great*. Being delivered from oppressions and preserved by the power of Christ from the Idolatry of those times and of the Antichrist, they are said to live with Christ a thousand years because they lived under him, clung to him, and did not involve themselves in the godlessness of those times. And this is the explanation of many Writers on that Text, which also accords best with the truth, giving no ground at all for Christ’s personal Reign for a thousand years upon the earth.

The second Scripture passage from which they intend to establish Christ’s Personal reign on the earth for a thousand years is *2 Peter 3:7, 10, 11, 12, 13*: "But the heavens and the earth which are now, by the same word are kept in store, reserved unto fire against the day of judgment and perdition of ungodly men... But the day of the Lord will come as a thief in the night; in the which the heavens shall pass away with a great noise, and the elements shall melt with fervent heat, the earth also and the works that are therein shall be burned up. Seeing then that all these things shall be dissolved, what manner of persons ought ye to be in all holy conversation and godliness, Looking for and hasting unto the coming of the day of God, wherein the heavens being on fire shall be dissolved, and the elements shall melt with fervent heat? Nevertheless we, according to his promise, look for new heavens and a new earth, wherein dwelleth righteousness." Mention is made there of a coming of Christ—a hasty coming—and that his coming shall be a new earth. Now, they say, in what sense can there be a new earth if Christ were not to come down upon the earth and the Saints were not to rule with him for a thousand years?

First, note the objective and the context of this Text, and it shall explain itself. It was brought in against the *Epicureans* <note>Followers of Epicurus, here used to mean those who live for pleasure and doubt divine providence</note> and scoffers of that time, *verses 3, 4*: "Knowing this first, that there shall come in the last days scoffers, walking after their own lusts, And saying, Where is the promise of his coming? for since the fathers fell asleep, all things continue as they were from the beginning of the creation." We see no change in providence, they say, therefore where is the promise of his coming? They mocked Christ because he had been a despised Man in the World; and to this it is answered in the 7th verse: "But the heavens and the earth which are now... are reserved unto fire against the day of judgment." Peter says distinctly that the time of Christ’s coming (which they mock) was not a time of a thousand years, but of the day of judgment; therefore, this coming of which *Peter* speaks here is not to be understood as that time of a thousand years, but as the Day of Judgment.

Secondly, Note that the day of the destruction of the ungodly is then; they say that Christ shall suffer and live with the god-
