But I pause when I consider to whom I now write, one who I am certain is full of such goodness that he believes what I say; and will forgive whatever harm I have done him; and I trust, shall pray for me to his God and my God, to your Father, that He will not count this against me; for you might accuse me of being one of those whom Paul accuses in 2 Timothy 4:16: <note>original: "2. Tim. 4. 16."</note> *At my first defense no one stood with me, but everyone deserted me. May it not be held against them.* Worthy Sir, if the Lord lets me behold your face once more so that I may open my heart to you again, I trust that I shall still remain upright in your affections.

There are some promises that I have encountered in the Scriptures, which (it seems to me) give, as it were, wings to my faith, that God shall not let you fall by the hands of the violent, such as Psalm 79, Psalm 91, Psalm 94, Psalm 3, Isaiah 41:10, and Isaiah 66:5. <note>original citations: "Psal. 79. Psal. 91. Psal. 94. Psal. 3. Jef. 41. 10. Jef. 66. 5." The Dutch "Jef." refers to Jesaja (Isaiah).</note> And many others which I do not doubt are better known to you than to me, and can be examined by you; keep them by you like a flask of heart-strengthening water <note>A "cordial" or medicinal tonic used for fainting or distress.</note> in times of weakness. Worthy Sir, let me earnestly entreat you to employ all means for your own preservation and to persist as far as you may and can with those in whose power your life rests, and that for several reasons as follows:

1. Because if you fall, oh, how the Enemies will rejoice! Malignants <note>term: Malignants. A political label used by Parliamentarians for Royalist supporters of King Charles.</note> and others will compose ballads because of your death and say: what has become of all his fast-days and prayers? His God will not deliver him. Oh Sir! It shall be a day of railing and slander, and furthermore...

2. Think to yourself how it will grieve the hearts of God’s people, and how it will make them wring their hands if they should come to be deprived of the fruit of their prayers for your deliverance, which I am certain have been poured out for you in an extraordinary measure; and furthermore...

3. Consider with yourself the service you can perform for the Church of Jesus Christ, and to how many souls God may use you as an instrument to bring to Christ; and what service this poor bleeding Nation might yet receive through your life; and furthermore...

4. It is not necessary that I remind you of your worthy and dear companion <note>referring to Mary Love</note> who, I am certain, is precious and lives near to God’s heart, as well as to yours! Her life being bound up in yours, and her condition being as it is; and moreover, I humbly request that you would remember my own condition; for surely, on the day that I shall hear that your life has been taken from you by violence, mine shall be able to bring me but little comfort, having been complicit <note>original: "hatdadigh" (handdadig), meaning "hand-active" or involved.</note> in the taking away of yours; although (the Lord knows it) it was not with intent or purpose to do such a thing, but happened by chance.

Therefore, for these reasons, I pray you in all humility again and again, that you will put into work everything you dare, and venture yourself as far as you can for your own preservation. And the Lord shall make you an instrument of His honor; if it is not here, it shall be in another place.

And [it seems to me] wherever the Lord shall place you, I would very gladly make that promise, and also fulfill it, which Ruth made to Naomi; <note>referring to Ruth 1:16, "Where you go, I will go."</note> and so I trust my dear Wife could also do, whose soul [I know] for...

<column-break/>

...cries out for you, and whose eyes drip with tears to God for you. Good Friend! In your approach to the throne of grace, be mindful of me before God, that I may learn to lean more strongly upon Him; and to cast my trust upon the Rock of Ages, and not upon broken reeds; and (I hope) through the strength of Christ and the help of your prayers, that for the future I shall be more strengthened, just as Peter was after his fall.

I wish that you would give my regards to Dr. Drake; <note>Dr. Roger Drake, a physician and minister involved in the same Presbyterian plot.</note> I hope that I have obtained better armor than before, but trust that it shall not be necessary to show such in respect to his person. Poor P.O. <note>Likely referring to Captain Potter, another witness/conspirator.</note> has done himself more wrong than anyone else can. For I hear that since he was there, he has found even more letters of his confession.

Good Sir, I have many more things to say but shall not trouble you further for this time. Would the Lord but let me behold your face once more; I hope He will do it, but however it be, it shall not be long before we shall enjoy one another's company in that place where the hands of the cruel and violent shall not touch us, and then eternity shall be little time enough to praise and glorify the Lord for the riches of His grace shown to us.

The Lord stand by you, the Lord preserve you; and support you with His everlasting arms, and deliver you; which shall be the earnest sighs and prayers of him who is [as he hopes] a dear although unworthy Friend, not worthy to be beheld by Your Honor.

***

## Dr. Drake’s Letters to Mr. Love.

I cannot refrain from greeting your liberty, and the singular honor which the Lord has been pleased to bestow upon Your Honor, etc. The Captain of our salvation is wise, and knows whom He calls out to be His soldiers! It has pleased Him to call Your Honor to lead the forlorn hope: <note>term: forlorn hope. From the Dutch "verloren hoop," referring to the lead party of soldiers in a dangerous attack; here used metaphorically for those facing martyrdom.</note> we bring up the vanguard; our Brothers in the black roll <note>A list of those condemned or imprisoned.</note> shall perhaps bring up the main body. And as for our rearguard [blessed be God], we have armies of prayers and tears: yes, by grace, we may say it. *Our righteousness shall go before our face, and the glory of the Lord shall be our rearguard.* Isaiah 58:8. <note>original: "Jefa. 58. 8."</note> Rightly might we fear, had we not a good God, a good cause, and a good conscience; but if God justifies, who shall condemn? Truly that God, who has done us so much good through a prison (blessed be His name), can do us much more good through our trial: He commands us not to fear those who, at the worst, can only kill the body; and why should we be afraid of Man, who shall die, etc., and forget God our Creator and Redeemer? It is too great an honor that God bestows upon us, to suffer anything for His name and covenant's sake, that we should hereby be so dear and pleasant in the hearts of His faithful people, and have been the occasion for the awakening of the spirit of prayer, which was nearly extinguished? Shall God then not hear, when He has prepared the heart? Has He set His children to praying, that He might not [hear] them?

### Another Letter from Dr. DRAKE to Mr. LOVE,

->The 17th of June, 1651.<-

**D**EAR Friend,

I can forget neither your person nor condition, 
being not only in the 
body, but also bound with you in a special way, 
Hebrews 13:3. <note>original: "Hebr. 13. 3." Which says, "Remember those in prison as if you were their fellow prisoners."</note> And truly, if habitual 
and actual grace are such motives to 
Christian love, is not suffering grace 
much more so? To suffer for Christ is an honor just as 
believing in Him is, Philippians 1:29. <note>original: "Phil. 1. 29."</note> *To you it has been granted.* <note>original Latin/Greek: "Hymin echaristhe, vobis datum est."</note> 
Christ and His people are never love-

<column-break/>

lier than upon the cross; may we not, after 
God, thank our prison, that we today 
have become so pleasing in the eyes of 
God’s people, and indeed, I trust, in the eyes of some 
of our enemies? Must we not enter 
into glory through suffering, just as our blessed 
Savior did? Luke 24:46. <note>original: "Luc. 24. 46."</note> By this means, the 
Lord Christ comes to set a higher price and value 
upon the reformation, the church service, and 
government; how highly do the peoples in the 
north value the sun, which appears to them only once 
in 3 or 6 months? and do our stinking, foul hearts 
not ordinarily estimate God’s blessing more 
in the wanting than in the enjoying?

In particular, [Sir], how dear and pleasing 
are you in this your calling to God and 
men, in that you are the first Proto-confessor 
or Proto-martyr; <note>A "Proto-martyr" is the first martyr of a particular cause or region.</note> may the Lord support 
your Honor through His grace, that you may bear the 
honor as well as the burden; I thank God for 
your boldness and steadfastness, whose 
flame contributes so much to keep my poor 
sparks of courage alive.

My message to you is, if it may be, 
to prevent the end, if it may stand with the will 
of the Lord. I would not yet have your Honor be a martyr; 
perhaps you shall say, I wish your 
Honor worse than your enemies do? Let it be so, 
nevertheless I am assured that I do it 
with a more upright heart, etc.

Sir, I have only one matter to add: 
which I perceive as a providence 
that is not to be despised, namely; that your day of 
examination is the day of your Jubilee, or your 
Pentecost, it being exactly the 50th day of your 
imprisonment, so ordained [without doubt] 
by a special providence, not by the design 
of your adversaries; may the Lord make it a 
Jubilee to you, to the freedom of the Spirit: and a 
Pentecost for the outpouring of the Spirit of 
grace, wisdom, and utterance: I shall say Amen 
to the omen, and shall always follow it with 
all my power in Heaven; always choosing 
rather to die with Love than to rule with immoderate 
lusts or desires, which is the "Magna Charta" <note>The Great Charter. Drake is satirizing the political manifestos of the Parliamentarians as being based on self-interest rather than law.</note> 
of these apostate times. My service and affection 
be presented to your Honor and your Honor’s 
most dear company. I request your prayers, and shall remain,

->Yours, etc.<-

I had a misconception, dreaming of an earthly Pentecost <note>original: "pinster" (Pinksteren)</note> and Jubilee; that fiftieth day, I now perceive, was but a reminder and an act of gratitude to call Your Honor <note>original: "U E." - Uwe Edelheid</note> to the eternal Jubilee above (Hebrews 12:22, 24), a preparation for the eternal Sabbath (Hebrews 4:9, 10).

How much are we beholden to our enemies (or rather to God for them), who are never more favorable to us than when they most intend to harm us. I no longer wonder at the Song of Victory <note>original Latin: "Epinicium"</note> of the Apostle in Romans 1:22 and 33 <note>The author likely refers to the victory song in Romans 8:31-39; the chapter numbers in the text may be a printing error</note> and 1 Corinthians 3:21, 22, 23. Death is so far from separating us from Christ that it brings us immediately to Him (Philippians 1:23), and that by a blow which is so honorable, so easy, so comforting, and so swift, that you have but to close your eyes and you are in Heaven. The Lord is pleased to give you a discharge and to give you your reward at the sixth hour <note>A reference to the Parable of the Workers in the Vineyard in Matthew 20</note>: praised be God, we serve a good Lord who only sets us to work on excellent and honorable things; who makes our cause light and brief; who performs all our works in us and for us; and then still rewards us, after everything, as graciously and richly as if we had earned our own wages. It is better to be God’s hireling than the world’s darling (Luke 15:17, 19).

Worthy Lord, I thank God for your faithfulness, timeliness, courage, and wisdom, through which you have both tested and discovered the craftiness and strength of your adversaries, and shown to your humble, unworthy companions in your suffering that they are conquerable through grace. The Lord is with you, you valiant warrior <note>original: "strijtbare Helt"</note>: go forth in this your strength and strike the host of Midian as one man (Judges 6:12, 14, 16). The Lord make you a true Samson, that you may do more damage to the kingdom of the devils in your death than you ever did in your life. The Lord is now merely following His old method, making the blood of the martyrs the seed of His Church <note>original Latin: "Sanguis martyrum semen ecclesiae," referenced here via Colossians 2:4</note>. Hiel deserved a curse in the rebuilding of Jericho (Joshua 6:26), but God is worthy to be blessed when He builds the new Jerusalem, even if He lays its foundation in Abiram, his firstborn [so is Christ our Father; compare Genesis 17:5 with Isaiah 9:6] and sets up its gates in His only son Segub [1 Kings 16, the end] <note>The author uses the tragic story of Hiel, whose sons died during the rebuilding of Jericho, as a typology for the sacrifice required to build God's Kingdom</note>. Such are we—poor, despised creatures, glorified and strengthened by the Lord, not only to act but also to suffer for the name of Christ (Acts 5:4, Philippians 1:29), His cause, Church, and covenant. The Lord is now making you a blessed Segub! May your honor, strength, and salvation be that which many thought would lead to your shame, weakness, and danger. Worthy Lord: God dignifies you to be the Elijah, to be the first to climb into the fiery chariot: <gloss>[Might I (without presumption) but be the Elisha, I shall make two or three bold requests of you: and that is first: 1. That I may obtain your prayers for a double portion of your Spirit; 2. Let me behold you once more (if it be possible) before your Ascension, even if it were but through the bars, even if only on the morning when your wedding shall begin; 3. Let your mantle fall, that by that means I may be strengthened to part the Jordan, yes, the Red Sea, if the Lord shall call me to it; and not...]</gloss>

<column-break/>

sink to the bottom like an Egyptian in mighty waters! 4. If there is any memory in Heaven of those things which are here on earth (Luke 16:24, 25, 28); would you then [when you have landed in that blessed Harbor] think once upon your humble friend and your old remaining comrades who still labor in the storm until Christ comes to them, just as He has come to you. Truly! The church triumphant does not forget the church militant, and prayer is not a strange or unusual language in Heaven until the body of Christ shall be made perfect (Revelation 6:9, 10). If justice causes them to pray against their enemies, why shall not their love awaken prayers for their friends? Surely; there is a communion of saints between the church militant and triumphant. We may praise God for them, and shall they not be able to pray for us? The martyrs refused to pray *to* departed saints, but some of them desired living saints to pray for them both on earth and in heaven, and I believe that they were not superstitious in that.

Dear Friend! I know to whom I speak, and am assured that Love <note>A pun on the recipient's name, Christopher Love</note> or Charity shall not be puffed up with that which would much sooner cause a bladder of pride to burst. No one is higher in God’s eyes than he who is lowest in his own. I see that your time is short, and therefore, although my affection and inclination are like the Jordan at the time of harvest <note>Overflowing</note>, I must nevertheless set limits and boundaries to my words, so that I do not distract or trouble you on your journey! I do not doubt that you remember that you must go through the Jordan toward the fiery chariot. The Jordan was not so powerful to cleanse Naaman of his leprosy as the river of penitent tears is to cleanse the leprosy of sin (Psalm 119:136), next to the immeasurable ocean of Christ’s blood. It is not Abana and Pharpar <note>Rivers of Damascus</note> that shall wash away your leprosy, but the Jordan; nor do all sorts of tears wash away sins, but only penitent tears.

You have but little time remaining to mourn, and Christ stands by you with His handkerchief and cloth (Psalm 56:8; read Revelation 7 and chapter 21:4; Isaiah 25:8). Spiritual sorrow and joy are inseparable companions in this life, and the spirit of consolation (like the Dove) governs these streams (Canticles 3:12, Matthew 3:16). Every true Christian has his Baptism of the River <note>original Latin: "Baptismum Fluminis" - water baptism</note>, united with his Baptism of the Spirit <note>original Latin: "Baptis. Flaminis"</note>, and God, to glorify you, adds also the Baptism of Blood <note>original Latin: "Baptis. Sanguinis" - martyrdom</note>. A cup of tears and a cup of consolation may well go together: and well-blessed is he who can mingle his drink with tears (Psalm 102:9). Such people need not fear to do as Christ did and drink from a bloody cup; and they shall undoubtedly sit at Christ’s right hand in His Kingdom (Matthew 20:22, 23). However, not according to the [selfish] meaning of those two ambitious brothers. If we were to weep or have regrets in Heaven, truly it would be because we did not weep and mourn more or better while on earth. The Lord make you and us all fit to finish much work in a short time.

If I see Your Honor no more, then I am forced here to take my long farewell of you; but why do I say such? It may...

## Mr. ROBINSON’S Letter to Mr. LOVE.

**D**EAR FRIEND,

The loss that God’s Church will come to suffer through your death is a great cross to me, and I doubt not even greater to others whose hearts God has made more sensitive to perceive His hand. I trust this blow shall be to your happiness, but to a great misery and a grievous punishment to many! When God intends to punish many at once, He is accustomed to hold this course! The extinguishing of such a star [I do not flatter you, God knows it] cannot but bring great darkness and sadness upon the whole world.

I wish from my heart (if God would grant me that grace) that I might see you before the day of your wedding, for I dare not call it the day of your death. I hope that I shall be in your thoughts when you are at the throne of grace. Good Sir! Pray heap up as many prayers as you can for God’s poor Church before you come to leave us. It shall be the best legacy that you can leave us, for you shall sow, and there are those yet living who shall gather it, and you shall not be unrewarded. Jesus Christ had thoughts for His congregation until the hour of His death. Dear Sir! Follow herein your Lord and Master. It is not necessary that I say this to comfort and strengthen you against the fear of that day which is approaching; I will not doubt that you have many times overcome fear through Jesus Christ <note>original: "C. J." — Christus Jesus</note>. [What you think is death, is a profession of faith] <note>original Latin: "Professio est quam putas mortem"</note>. It is but the beginning of a journey, and although the way is deep, it is nonetheless short. God brings you by the nearest way: no one ever had a shorter passage to rest.

I know that you have often been upon Mount Nebo <note>A reference to Deuteronomy 34, where Moses viewed the Promised Land (Canaan) before his death</note>, from where you have gazed upon Canaan, towards which you now turn. The hidden head, Jesus Christ, cannot be kept away! You have now finished your testimony, and do not fear now to receive your reward. Christ has changed that black messenger <note>Death</note> into an Angel of Light for you. How soon others shall follow you is known only to God; if we linger here longer, it is but to row in a stormy sea.

Moses was very willing to die; God said "go up and die," and he went up and died. Let

<column-break/>

not the care for those who belong to you trouble you in any way: the earth is the Lord’s, together with its fullness. Leave your fatherless children; God shall take care of them. Let your widow trust in God; your dear companion is a partaker of the same grace that you have received. and how rich then are those who are heirs to the promise? You can commit your spirit into God’s hands; how much more then your wife and children? Remember the promise: *I shall be your God and the God of your seed!* Lord, it is a richer portion than all the mines of the Indies. You were to them but as a channel or a conduit; the fountain lives, and shall live when you are dead. God can take care of them without you; you cannot be without God. Dear Sir! Be of good courage; I hear how full of joy you are, the Lord be praised for that; but all this is but a few drops compared to the ocean. I have written this to fulfill you more and more: an axe and a rope are all one. You shall die without sickness. When you think of the present shame, then behold the coming joy: you shall be with God, Christ, Angels, and the spirits of the perfectly righteous in a short time.

What a happiness it is to enjoy grace in perfection; to behold God face to face; to be freed from sin, the temptations of the Devil, and the company of evil men. You have fought a good fight, you have finished the course, you have kept the faith, etc. And now you are on the way to receive your crown, a crown of glory that does not fade. You go now to that place where the voice of the oppressor shall not be heard; you go now to your bed, the best and safest on which you have ever slept.

The steps to the scaffold <note>original: "Schavot"</note> shall be like Jacob’s ladder, upon which you shall ascend to your beloved Father! The scaffold shall be like Mount Nebo, and the executioner's axe shall strike off the head of sin, and make an end of all your misery and wretchedness.

Be assured, Sir! The Angels of God shall not only support you and strengthen you exceedingly, but the God of Angels shall do so as well! If your death, and this sort of death, did not serve for God’s honor and the benefit of His congregation, I firmly believe God would have delivered you from this hour.

I have written such things, not because you lack counsel, but to show my love and my tender affection for you, and so that you might be mindful of me and mine before you depart from the earth. Dear Sir! Accept it as my last adieu! Farewell! Farewell! Dear friend! May God, who has bound up your soul in the bundle of the living, be your comfort, joy, longing, peace, and trust in life and death unto eternity. Yea, He shall be your guide unto death: He shall be a husband and head to your dearest wife, He shall be a tender father to your little children.

This is the trust, and this shall be the prayer of:

->August 19,<-
->1651.<-

->Sir, your beloved friend,<-

This page introduces two letters from "Mr. Jenkyn" (William Jenkyn), a fellow Presbyterian minister who was also imprisoned for the same royalist plot but was eventually spared while Love was not. These letters are deeply emotional, intended to provide "spiritual medicine" against the fear of the scaffold.</meta>

### A Letter from Mr. JENKYN to Mr. LOVE.

MY dearest, dearest heart,

You lie close to my soul! The Lord J[esus] C[hrist] smiled upon you with the sweetest face that He ever showed to anyone who has been in suffering. I send herewith a book in which I have been greatly comforted in my imprisonment: what are 10,000 deaths when Christ is received through faith?

<margin>[P. 335.]</margin> These reflections, where the page is turned down, strengthen faith very beautifully. I am almost hesitant <note>original: "bescheuwt," meaning shy or bashful</note> to send you these meditations, out of fear that too many considerations might trouble you. I judged these to be more profitable than speculative discourses on death. May the great God, who established the foundations of the earth on nothing but His word, support your soul with His promises; oh! sweet, very firm, firm, firm [oh! maintain the firm] promises, as firm as the essence of God Himself; for whose fulfillment God has pledged His very being: *As truly as I live,* etc.

My heart, I love you, I kiss you, I weep over you; I am glad because of you! I shall see you in glory. The Lord Jesus strengthen you: He will do it.

---

### Mr. JENKYN’S Letter to Mr. LOVE.

MY dearest soul.

Do not accuse me of slowness for sending you this mite <note>original: "mijtjen," referring to a small gift or offering, like the widow’s mite in the Bible</note>; I did not know if it was timely. Your great peril lies in the abundance of these mementos, when I consider your own store of strength; however bold your appetite may be, it is impossible for you to digest all the food that has been composed for you and by you in books, letters from friends, and your own meditations. I shall attempt to make up for the lack of letters with prayers. And alas! That I might pray so for this journey, that I should not have to do it a second time!

My only advice to Your Honor <note>original: "U. E." (Uwe Edelheydt), a formal address</note> shall be that which I know has been your only concern, and shall be your only comfort, namely: that you may fall asleep in Christ.

<margin>1 Cor. 15:18.</margin> Yes! You shall not only sleep in the lap and bosom and arms of J[esus] C[hrist] (although that is exceedingly much), but He looks upon you as a part of Himself, as a member—yes, a precious member; in your dying, you shall not die: *those who have fallen asleep in Christ are not lost.* 1 Cor. 15:18.

<margin>1 Cor. 15:20. Col. 1:18.</margin> *Christ the firstfruits of those who have fallen asleep,* 1 Cor. 15:20, *the firstborn from the dead,* Col. 1:18. The head of the body has risen from the dead as a head, etc., and not as a private person; so that our resurrection [is already now accomplished] with respect to its cause.

The union between Christ and Your Honor cannot be broken by death (and this union and bond is not only between Christ and your soul, but also your body). Christ would be rebelling against His Father’s will [which is blasphemous to even think] if He should lose anything of what His Father has given Him; now He would do such a thing if He did not raise it up on the last day.

Christ is the resurrection, and he who be-

<column-break/>

-lieves in Him, though he were dead, yet shall he live. Oh, how Christ has perfumed the grave, and how pleasant He has made for us the ghastly and horrible appearance of death?

Death is (now) an advantage to us, your privilege, and next to Christ, our best friend.

And to speak the truth, all our sighing and mourning in this life comes through the lack of that which we so fear, which is death; just as a child cries for lack of sleep, and yet is no less unwilling to be undressed and go to bed.

My precious soul, you have more glorious robes to put on in the morning of the resurrection: *this mortal shall put on immortality.* This garment of righteousness has perhaps had many stains here: today you shall mourn for them for the last time! The Lord, therefore, give you fine grace, that you may be sorrowful for them in a holier and more abundant measure than ever before; for the garment of glory shall then be spotless. <margin>Jude 24.</margin> Jude 24.

Good God, is there such a condition and state where I shall never sin again, where I shall enjoy as much grace as I can grasp, wish, or desire; where I shall no longer wash the feet of J.C. but may now and then kiss them myself; where I shall rest in His blessed bosom and be embraced in His glorified arms unto all eternity. This is your blessedness which is now near at hand, and every comfort is so much more pleasant the more it approaches us; *now is your salvation nearer than when you first believed.*

Oh, worthy Lord! He who now had a strong faith; oh! wrestle manfully with the great God for strength; to overcome Him, keep hanging onto the promises—the precious promises—not only regarding their fullness but their infallibility; venture your soul upon them. The faithfulness of the Lord is a foundation which carries the weightiest building and the heaviest burden of sin and expectation; Jesus Christ calls, pleads, commands, threatens, all to make you believe.

The Lord increase your faith; you must now undertake a great work, but Christ has labored and you shall only enter into His labor. Labor: death has only the name of an enemy once Christ has disarmed him; there is more terror and fear in the pomp of it [as Seneca <note>Lucius Annaeus Seneca, a Roman Stoic philosopher who wrote extensively on facing death with composure.</note> says]—the scaffold, the axe, the spectators, the rumors—than in the thing itself.

Oh! how a Christian may then boast over it: *O death, where is your sting?* Christ has stripped the principalities and powers, He has disarmed them and robbed them of their clothing; His death is the death of death; all its perils have remained stuck in His side.

Therefore do not say (dear friend), *who shall roll the stone away from the mouth of the grave?* When you arrive there, you shall find it taken away for you; if there be difficulties or distresses, they are all taken away in Christ.

To this worthy Savior I commend you, who in His appointed time shall wipe away all tears from your eyes and all sins from the souls of His poor servants; who shall bring us out of all our waves and storms to that haven where we wish to be. I know not where I shall break off, just as little as I know where I shall leave you: but can I leave you better than in His arms? There I commend you.

Yours, in the bowels <note>In the 17th century, the "bowels" (ingewanden) were considered the seat of deep compassion and tender affection.</note> of this Savior.

### Mr. CASE to Mr. LOVE.

Heavenly Saint,

<margin>Revelation 24:3, 4, 5. <note>The original text cites Revelation (Apoc.) chapter 24, though the book only has 22 chapters; this is likely a printer's error for chapter 22, which describes the city where there is no night.</note></margin>
You have now awakened from your last natural rest, to go to your eternal rest: the night is over; you shall never behold the night again, but God shall be your light, and you shall reign with him forever and ever.

You go now where you shall be [in a true sense] above ordinances and above the Scripture; where God in Christ shall be everything to you. Your prison shall be changed into a palace, and your unclean clothes shall be taken from you, and you shall be clothed with long white robes; and in that moment when your body shall be separated from your head, you shall be united with Christ your head; in him you shall be crowned, and with him you shall reign for eternity.

### Another Letter from Mr. CASE to Mr. LOVE.

DEar Soul!

You go now to Heaven; to make your desires and longings for that place even greater, take these observations with you, which seem to agree greatly with your condition.
<margin>Revelation 14:13; Isaiah 57:12.</margin>
There is rest for the weary.
<margin>2 Corinthians 5:6.</margin>
For the exiles, a home.
<margin>Romans 5:2.</margin>
For the despised, Glory.
<margin>Romans 8:21.</margin>
For those imprisoned with corruption, the glorious liberty of the sons of God.
<margin>Romans 8:17.</margin>
For those who resisted unto blood, victory.
For those plagued with sin and misery, an annihilation of both.
<margin>Revelation 22:17.</margin>
For the hungering soul, the hidden Manna.
<margin>Revelation 22:17; Psalm 36:8, 9.</margin>
For the thirsty, a river of joy, water of life, a fountain of life.
<margin>Psalm 16:8.</margin>
For the anxious soul, fullness of joy, and for the sorrowful heart, His pleasures forevermore.

In a word, for those who have lain here as if upon a dung-heap and have preserved their integrity, it is a throne upon which they shall sit and reign with Christ forever.
<margin>Revelation 3:21 <note>Original text says 3.31, a typo for 3.21</note> and 22:5.</margin>
Dear soul! Courage, it is a sharp breakfast but a blessed Supper <note>A famous metaphor for a morning execution followed by the "Marriage Supper of the Lamb" in heaven.</note>; the Supper of the Lamb follows upon it. The Bridegroom says, "Behold, I come quickly"; let your joyful soul give this echo: "Even so, come, Lord Jesus."

There is but a little time remaining for prayer; please remember me therein: and then everlasting hallelujahs shall be your work, and rest; live forever with your God. Amen.

I shall accompany you with my prayers, even if I cannot be there in person.

### Mrs. LOVE’S Letter to her Husband Mr. LOVE.

MY most beloved.

Before I write a word further, I request of you that you would think that it is not your wife, but a friend, who now writes to you. I hope indeed that you have willingly offered up your wife and children to that God who said in Jeremiah 49:11: *Leave your orphans behind, and I will keep them alive; and let your widows trust in me.* Your Creator shall be my husband, and a Father to your children. Oh, that the Lord would free you from having any troublesome thoughts for those who belong to you.

I am willing to give you over into the hands of your Father: and I accept it not only as a crown of glory that you die for Christ, but as an honor for me that I have a husband to lose for Christ.

I dare not speak to you, nor harbor a thought in my soul, of my unspeakable loss: but I keep my eye fixed fast upon your unspeakable, inconceivable gain.

You leave only a sinful mortal wife to be eternally wedded to the Lord of Glory; you leave only children, brothers, and sisters, to go to the Lord Jesus, your eldest brother; you leave friends on earth to go to the assembly of saints and angels, and the spirits of the just made perfect in glory; you leave only the earth for Heaven, and make an exchange of a dungeon for a palace. And if your natural affections should be ignited within you, I hope that the Spirit of grace which is in you shall lay them down, knowing well that all things here below are but dung and loss compared to those things which are above. I know that you keep your eye constantly on the hope of glory, and that makes you despise earthly loss.

My beloved, I know the Lord has not only prepared glory and majesty for you, and you for the same: but I am assured He shall also make the way to the enjoyment of it sweet for you.

When you put on your clothes that morning, oh! think then: "Now I put on my wedding garment, to go to be eternally wedded to my Redeemer"; and when the messenger of death <note>The executioner or the guard.</note> shall come to you, let him not be terrifying to you: but look upon him as a messenger who brings you tidings of eternal life.

When you go up the scaffold, think (as you said to me) it is but your fiery chariot to carry you to your Father’s house; and

When you lay down your precious head to receive your Father's blow <note>A common 17th-century spiritual perspective: seeing the executioner's axe as a tool of God's will rather than human malice.</note> [remember what you said to me], although your head should be separated from your body, that nonetheless, in that moment, your soul should be so united with your Head, the Lord Jesus in Heaven!

And though it seems a bit bitter that we are separated by human hands a little sooner than we otherwise might have been, nonetheless, let us consider it is the decree and will of our Father, and...

## Another Letter from Mrs. Love to Mr. Love

My Heavenly love,

I call you so, because God has filled you with Heaven before he has taken you up to Heaven: you now behold God, Christ, and Glory as if in a mirror, but tomorrow the doors of Heaven shall be opened; you shall be in the full enjoyment of all these glories, which eye has never seen, nor ear ever heard, nor can the human heart conceive them! God has now swallowed up your heart with thoughts of Heaven; but before long, you shall be swallowed up in the enjoyment of Heaven. And is it then a wonder that there is such a calm and tranquility in your mind while you sail in this stormy sea? Since you perceive, through the eye of faith, a haven of rest where you shall be richly laden with the glories of Heaven.

Oh lift up your heart with joy when you lay down your dear head upon the block with these thoughts: that you are laying your head down to rest in your Father’s lap, which, when you shall awake, shall be crowned, not with an earthly perishable crown, but with a Heavenly eternal crown of Glory.

And be not faint-hearted when you shall see a guard of Soldiers triumphing with their trumpets around you: but then lift up your head, and you shall see God, with a guard of holy Angels, triumphing and rejoicing to receive you into glory.

Be not dismayed by the mockery and reproach you may meet on your short way to Heaven: but be assured God shall not only glorify your Soul and body in Heaven: but he shall also make your memory glorious upon the earth.

Oh let not a troubling thought for your Wife and Children awake within you; your God shall

<column-break/>

be our God, and our inheritance; he shall be a Husband to your Widow, and a Father to your Children; the grace of your God shall be sufficient for us.

And now my dearest, I am ready willingly and with joy to resign my right and property that I have in you to your Father and my Father, who has the greatest right to you; and this is my confidence: although men have separated us for a time, nevertheless our God, before long, shall bring us together again: where we shall eternally have one another's company, and never more be separated.

Oh let me understand how the Lord supports your heart, and let me also taste and enjoy those comforts that support you; so that they, like marble Pillars, may uphold my sinking Soul.

I can write no more; fare well, fare well my dearest! until we meet each other there where we shall never take our leave again; in the meantime, I leave you in the lap of a tender, affectionate Father, and shall break off here, and rest.

->Until I shall rest forever in Heaven.<-

->MARIA LOVE.<-

## Mr. Love’s Letter to his Wife, written when he was first intended to die. <note>Love was originally scheduled for execution in July, but received a short reprieve before being beheaded on August 22, 1651.</note>

My very dear love,

I go now to my house above! nonetheless I must write you a short letter before I depart and shall be seen no more; and it is to request of you that you would comfort yourself in my well-being and not trouble your soul too much in your loss. Labor now to keep down your inner fears while you are under outward visitations; as your outward suffering is abundant, so let the comfort of Christ also be abundant in you:

I know that you are a woman of a sorrowful spirit. My time is short; I have but a few words of good counsel to add: and then I shall commend you to that God who cares for you and yours.

1. While you are under God’s desertion <term>desertion: a spiritual state where a believer feels abandoned or lacks the "sensible" presence of God</term>, labor more to strengthen your evidences and grounds of promise for Heaven, and to assure them to your soul, than to call them into doubt.

2. Remember that a faith of Adherence <note>original: 'Adherentie', meaning a steadfast clinging to God’s promises even when one lacks a feeling of certainty</note> or of trust in the Lord Jesus Christ can make you enter Heaven, even if you do not have the faith of Evidence or assurance.

3. Endeavor then to find in God, <insert>yes, even more abundantly</insert>, what you have lost in the creature <note>“The creature” refers to any created being—in this case, her husband.</note>.

4. Do not spend your days in sorrow over my death; if there were knowledge in Heaven of things here below, or also sorrow, I would mourn there if I thought that my beloved mourned on earth.

5. Keep yourself always under a soul-searching ministry: I know that you are not one of those sponge-like listeners who soak up foul water as well as clean: God has bestowed on you a sound judgment, that you may distinguish things that differ; as the mouth tastes food, so let your ear test words.

6. Be often in Christian gatherings, and devote yourself much to the exercise of the duties of Mortification <term>mortification: the spiritual practice of subduing or "killing" sinful desires and worldly attachments</term>, in fasting and prayers...

My dear, I pray you, be content; my soul is greatly comforted in the Lord. I can willingly submit myself to the good pleasure of His will, and I hope you do the same. I have been delivered up by the fore-ordained counsel of God; the will of the Lord be done. Read for your comfort, when I shall be dead and gone: Jeremiah 49:11, Isaiah 54:6, 7, 8, Psalm 146:9, 2 Corinthians 4:17, 18, Hebrews 12:6, 7. <note>These verses focus on God’s protection of widows and orphans and the temporary nature of earthly suffering compared to eternal glory.</note>

### Another letter from Mr. Love to his Wife.

Worthy beloved, worthier now than ever before.

It increases my joy not a little that I have such a good and virtuous wife to leave for the sake of the Lord Christ. In your sorrow, I have been sorrowful, but in your joy, I have also been comforted. Truly! Had you possessed nothing but nature <note>original: "nature", meaning human instinct or emotion without divine grace</note>, it could not have strengthened you to bear such a heavy blow with such silence and submission to God's hand.

Oh, most beloved, every line that you write gladdens my heart. I cannot believe that there is such a <term>creature</term> <note>In the 17th century, "creature" was a common term for a fellow human being, signifying a created soul.</note> as *Mary Love* in the whole world. As for *Kate* and *Mary*, I can think of them without sadness, leaving them to such a good God and such a good mother.

Be comforted regarding your husband, whom God may glorify more in his death than in his life: the will of the Lord be done! He is perfectly content with the hand of God.

Although there is but a little between him and death, he also knows that there is but a little between him and Heaven, and that rejoices his heart.

The Lord bless you and reward you for your wise and good counsel. You have anticipated me; the same things that I intended to have written to you, you have written to me! I have had more comfort from your godly letter than from all the advice I have had from anyone else in the world! Rest assured, we shall meet one another in Heaven. Here I shall break off and rest, until I rest in Heaven.

From the Tower on Sunday.

->Your dying, yet comforted Friend,<-
->Christopher Love.<-

### Another from the same.

My dearest delight on earth!

I was fast asleep when your letter came; I thank God, I did not miss an hour of sleep on account of my suffering. I know that they <note>likely referring to his prayers or his hopes for the future</note> watch over me—an exceeding, eternal weight of glory. I slept this night from 10 o'clock last night until seven this morning, without once waking.

<column-break/>

My dearest, I am so rejoiced in that gracious comfort which God gives you, that my burdens lie the lighter upon my shoulders because they are not so heavy upon yours—or if they are heavy, that God nonetheless supports you so that you can bear them. May the Lord plant it in our hearts forever, that we may submit to His good pleasure. I thank God, I find my soul in such a quiet, calm temperament as I have ever had in my life; I am [ready] unto death.

->From the Tower, August 18, 1651.<-
->Your affectionate Husband,<-
->CHRISTOPHER LOVE.<-

### Mr. LOVE’S last letter to his Wife, on the day he died.

My godly beloved,

I am now ready to go from a prison house to a palace; I have finished my work, and I go now to receive my reward. I go now to Heaven, where two of my children are, and leave you here on earth where three of my little ones still are. Those two who are above have no need of my care; but the three below have need of yours.

It gladdens me to think that two of my children are in <term>Abraham’s bosom</term> <note>A biblical metaphor for the place of rest in Heaven.</note>, and three of them in the arms and care of such a tender and godly mother. I know that you are a woman of a sorrowful spirit; but be comforted! Although your sorrow is great through the departure of your husband from this world, may your pains be the less in the bearing of your child into this world. You shall be a joyful mother though you remain a distressed widow. God has laid up many mercies for you. The prayers of a dying man for you shall not be in vain.

To my shame I say it: I have never prayed so much for you in my freedom as I have done in my bonds. I can write no more, only I have a few short pieces of advice to leave you, which concern [your] practice:

1. Always keep yourself under a sound, righteous, and soul-searching ministry. Oh! Many deceivers have gone out into the world; but the sheep of Christ know His word, and a stranger they will not follow. Listen to the preaching that teaches the way of God in truth and follow Solomon’s advice, Proverbs 19:27.
2. Raise your children in the teaching and admonition of the Lord; the mother must be a teacher in the absence of the father. Solomon, Proverbs 19:27: the words of his mother instructed him, and Timothy was instructed by his grandmother Lois and his mother Eunice, 2 Timothy 1:5.
3. Pray daily in your family, so that your dwelling may be among the number of those families that call upon the name of the Lord.
4. Be diligent to obtain a meek and quiet spirit, which is precious before God, 1 Peter 3:4.
5. Do not always fix your eyes upon the blessings you lack, but upon the grace you have.
6. Look rather toward God’s purpose in the visitation <note>original: "besoeckinge", meaning a trial or test from God</note> than toward the measure and degree of your oppression.
7. Whenever God strips you of earthly delights, strive then to obtain clear evidence of your right and title to Heaven; so that just as your suffering is abundant, so also, through Christ, your comfort may be abundant, 2 Corinthians 1:4.

<meta>This page continues the final correspondence and public testimony of Christopher Love (1618–1651), a prominent Presbyterian minister and Covenanter. Having been convicted of treason for communicating with the exiled Charles II during the English Civil War, he spent his final months in the Tower of London. This page transitions from his private pastoral advice to his wife, Mary, to the official record of his final speech delivered upon the scaffold just moments before his beheading.</meta>

8. Although it is good to always be watchful <note>original: "jalours", meaning spiritually vigilant or cautious</note> over the deceitfulness of your heart; nonetheless it is bad for you to nourish fears and doubts regarding the truth and sincerity of your grace. If I have ever had any assurance of another’s state, I am assured of the grace that is in you; I can say to you, as Peter said to Silvanus, that I testify that this is the true grace of God in which you stand (1 Peter 5:12). Oh! My dear soul, why do you doubt—you whose heart has been upright and whose footsteps holy? I would dare to place my own soul in the place of yours, such is the confidence I have in you.

9. Whenever you find your heart careless, presumptuous, or puffed up, let your eye fall more upon your corruptions than your spiritual gifts: but when you find your heart leaning toward despondency or unbelief, then behold your saving gifts and not your weaknesses.

10. Study the covenant of grace and the merits of Christ, and then be troubled if you can; you are included in such a covenant that accepts the will for the deed, desires for actions, and sincerity for perfection—the righteousness of another, namely of Christ Jesus <note>original abbreviation: "C.I." for Christus Iesus</note>, as if it were your own. Oh, my dearest! Rest, rest, rest then in the love of God and in the bosom of Christ.

11. Let your will be subject to God’s will; it is a bitter cup <note>original: "drinck-beecker", literally drinking-vessel</note> that we must drink; but it is the chalice that our Father has placed in our hand. When Paul went to Jerusalem to suffer, the Christians could say, "the will of the Lord be done"; oh! say the same, as I go to Tower Hill <note>The traditional site of execution for high-status prisoners near the Tower of London.</note>, "the will of the Lord be done."

12. Rejoice in my joy, rather than mourning immoderately for me, which would suggest that you either envy or suspect my blessedness. The joy of the Lord is my strength; let it also be yours.

Worthy Wife! Fare well; I shall no longer call you Wife, I shall behold your face no more: and yet I am not troubled by this; for now I go to meet the Bridegroom, the Lord Jesus Christ, to whom I shall be wed for all eternity.

->From the Tower of London, the 22nd of August, 1651.<-
->The day of my glorification.<-
->Your dying, yet affectionate Friend unto Death,<-
->CHRISTOPHER LOVE.<-

### The Last
# REASONS,
### OR
# ORATION
### OF
## Mr. CHRISTOPHER LOVE
### Preacher of the true Reformed Religion; delivered upon the Scaffold on Tower Hill, the 22nd of August 1651. And who, according to his declaration, was killed in innocence.

<image-desc>Decorative drop cap 'B' featuring intricate leaf and vine patterns within a square frame.</image-desc>

Beloved Christians; I have become this day a spectacle to God, to Angels, and to Men. I have become a sorrow to the godly, a mockery

<column-break/>

to the godless, and a theater for all people. Nonetheless, God be praised, there is no terror for myself. Although there is little between me and death, nevertheless, that which refreshes my heart is that there is little between me and Heaven. It was no small comfort to Dr. Taylor <note>Rowland Taylor (d. 1555), a famous Protestant martyr during the reign of Queen Mary I.</note>, that renowned Martyr, as he went to his death, to think that there were but two little bridges between him and his Father’s house; there is even less between me and Glory: I must only lay down upon the block, and shall then climb upon a throne. I am today on a journey to the great Ocean or Sea of eternity, through a great storm, toward the harbor of rest; through the Red Sea toward the promised land. It seems to me I hear God speaking, just as He said to Moses: go up to the top of Mount Nebo and die there. So He says to me: go up to Tower Hill and die there. Jacob was old, yet he did not know the day of his death; but I am young, and yet I know the day of my death, the manner of my death, and the place of my death. Whereby two renowned Preachers of the Divine Word died before me, namely John the Baptist and Paul the Apostle, both beheaded—one as recounted in the Scriptures, and the other in the ecclesiastical histories. These and other holy men (of whom I have read) were beheaded for the Word of the Lord and for the testimony of Jesus Christ; but in this I am less than they, for it seems to me that I do not suffer for the sake of religion or conscience, but because I have mixed religion with state affairs <note>original: "staetsche affairen", referring to the political conflict between the Parliamentarian government and the supporters of the King.</note>—an old practice of the Devil to attribute the cause of death to one's involvement with policy or state affairs. The rulers of Israel wanted to kill Jeremiah because he meddled with policy and wanted to side with the Chaldeans, and as the people said, wanted to bring in foreign people to defile them; which is also charged against me, though I am as innocent in this as Jeremiah was. I find in the Scriptures that the cause of man's suffering is often attributed to matters of state. Paul would have had to die (if the people could have had their way) because he had preached Christ; yet he was held by them to be an insurrectionist. For matters of state I am deprived of my life, yet I have never carried out anything against the present government. I shall this day make a double exchange: a pulpit for a scaffold, and a scaffold for a throne; and I shall perhaps add a great number of Saints on Tower Hill to the innumerable company on Mount Zion, and the guard of Soldiers who stand around here for a guard of Angels who shall carry my soul into Abraham's bosom. This is the best pulpit I have ever been upon. God has previously made me an instrument to bring other men to Heaven, but through this, God Himself brings me to Heaven. These are the last words I shall speak; and perhaps these my last words may bring God greater honor than my previously delivered sermons, before I [lay] my neck upon the block <meta>catchword: down</meta>

<meta>This page transitions from Christopher Love’s private letters to his wife to the public record of his final speech on the scaffold. Having been convicted of high treason for his involvement in a plot to restore Charles II through negotiations with the Scots, Love uses these final moments to proclaim his innocence and spiritual readiness.</meta>

-># of Mr. LOVE.<-

lay down, I wish to present my affairs to the people. I speak the truth, and I do not lie; God is my witness, whom I serve in my spirit. I bring no vengeful heart to the Scaffold, but am free from all hatred and envy. I have sought mercy from those who have denied me mercy. I pray to God for forgiveness for those who will not forgive me; and the worst that I wish for them is that I may meet their souls in Heaven.

Regarding my accusation: the same is heavy and shocking, in which many things are very falsely laid upon me; but not one thing was actually proven against me. My accusation is high and full; but the proof is low and empty, although there were eight witnesses against me, yet not one of them has proven that I sent any letter; that I collected any pence <note>money or funds</note> for the King, Queen, or anyone of the Scottish Nation. Regarding my accusers: I have forgiven them from the bottom of my heart, and I pray God that He will also forgive them. They do not agree among themselves; for some of them (previously) being terrified, did not wish to testify against me; another of them wrote to me with his own hand, praying for forgiveness for what he had done to me, and telling me that if I were to die an untimely death, his life would always gnaw at him as he was instrumental in taking mine. Regarding my accusers, just as I do not wish to condemn them, so I do not wish to justify them. I believe that what moved Herod <note>original: "Herodus"</note> to behead John <note>original: "Joannes"</note> is also the cause of my death—because he had reproached Herod for his incest, and for his oath's sake he commanded John to be killed. To avoid perjury, he chose to commit a murder; yet had the head of John remained on his shoulders, he would have been guilty of neither.

Regarding myself: I have walked through many and various rumors. Every person stood ready to sink my name into the earth even before my ends were ready to bury my body. God shall not only wipe away all tears from my eyes after my death, but shall also wash away all stains from my name. My hope is that my name shall not perish above the earth, although my body shall rot under the earth and turn to dust. I am well mindful of what calumnies and scandals were cast upon me this last month, on the very night before I was to die—how a mocking letter came into my hands, suggesting that something would be written against me after my death. But I hope that you will be reasonable and not believe the same, as I shall not then be able to answer for myself, nor defend myself. I have been slandered regarding new practices and foundations; five slanders are laid upon me. First, regarding my practice: that I am a liar. I hope that you will give credit to a dying man, who will not dare to appear before God with lies in his mouth. I did not deny before the court what was true; that which I then denied, some say I later

<column-break/>

confessed: that I never wrote any letters to the King, Queen, or the Church and State of Scotland. That I never received any letters that were written to me. Through some of the same (I say) that I never collected, gave, or lent a single penny to one or another private person, or to anyone of the Scottish nation. I am further accused of having sent money to the King and State of Scotland, which I never did. And therefore, what I said before the bench after my sentence was pronounced, I say still: that neither God nor my own conscience condemns me for that of which I have been condemned. I was also accused of being a usurer, and that I took 30 pounds in interest for 300 pounds—which in the presence of God and all of you is a notorious fable. I was accused of being an adulterer; but just as Luther <note>original: "Lutherus"</note> said in another matter, that he was never tempted by greed, so may I also say that by the grace of God, I have never in my whole life been assailed by impurity. It does not grieve me much that these slanders are laid upon me, just as Athanasius (who, although he was very chaste) was accused by two harlots that he had committed folly with them. But what goes most to my heart is that I am accused of being a murderer, and burdened with all the blood that has been shed in Scotland. Had I been guilty of a single drop thereof, I would not then be filled with so much tranquility and peace of mind, with so much clarity and rest of spirit, with which I am currently filled. I am (God be praised) free and clean of the blood of all men. They do to me as Nero did to the Christians: he set Rome on fire and accused the Christians thereof. They set England and Scotland on fire and lay the blame on me, which the pride and lust of the wicked has ignited. Have I ever invited or incited our English Army to invade Scotland? This I have done and I stand by it: as a private person, I have prayed to God and humbly requested that there might be an accord or agreement between the King and the Scots for the sake of religion.

It happened only in a meeting that it was proposed—namely, that one should seek to promote the agreement between the King and the Scots. I declare against the Commissions <note>Love is likely referring to the High Court of Justice or specific political committees</note>, as they call them, that it is also an act of high presumption and known falsehood to say such was a conspiracy of the Presbyterian Faction <note>original: "Presbyteriaensche Factie"</note>. Such is but the craftiness of a political faction, to spread such rumors and thereby cause the Presbyterian parties to be hated, who are the best-ordered persons in the world regarding governance. It is said that I am a person of a troublesome spirit and an enemy of the peace of these lands. I am indeed born a man of strife—not active, but passive. Many men fight and strive with me; I strive with no one. The sadness of my heart has been over the disagreements, and the desire

-># The Last Words<-

of my soul is for a union among the people of God. I do not mean by this a political Union of State, to bind ourselves against the present power; that is more a combination and a conspiracy than a Union. Those who have obtained power through cunning and use it with cruelty shall lose it with shame. I am reminded of a noteworthy matter regarding the holy man Greenwood <note>John Greenwood (died 1593), a Puritan separatist and martyr</note>, who gave his judgment concerning state government: he feared the introduction of Popery; but I fear that Atheism, blasphemy, and all kinds of heresy are afoot to storm this Land. As far as my own practice goes, now regarding my foundations: I am accused of being an **Apostate** <note>original: "Apostaet"</note>, a deserter, that I am this or that—that I am everything except what I actually am. A high court, a long sword, and a bloody scaffold have not been able to force me to abandon or change my firm purpose. What I shall say is not to incite anyone; I die with my conscience set only against the malevolent. I do not consider the Godly party (those who entered into the <term>Covenant|The Solemn League and Covenant, an agreement between English and Scottish parliaments for religious reform and mutual defense</term> in Scotland) to be <term>Malignants|A term used by Parliamentarians to describe aggressive Royalist supporters of the King</term> or evildoers, because they wish to defend their lands against those who would attack them; though they are against the malevolent, they are not against a **mixed monarchy**. I have fought against the powers of a deceased King in my place and calling, and were he still alive and I to live longer, I would still oppose those same powers. I opposed his powers, but I have never been an enemy to the office or position of a King. I am as much an enemy of courtly sycophants who wished to elevate Monarchy into tyranny, as I am of those who wish to press it down into Anarchy. I never wished to kill him, nor have I ever been an enemy of his person. There is a rumor concerning a certain **Sermon** <note>original: "Predicatie"</note> delivered at Uxbridge, suggesting that matters would never be well until the King was bled in the jugular vein; but such rumors, like many others, are full of vanity and folly. I die with my judgment unsatisfied, unable to take the new oath or <term>Engagement|An oath of loyalty to the Commonwealth of England "without King or House of Lords"</term>; may God preserve those who refuse it. I also do not wish to be counted among those who approve of the present government. I die with my judgment entirely against it. Regarding the matter of my life, I presented a request to them, giving them the title of honor as others do. Hagar gave the title to Absalom, even though David was her lawful King; Calvin gave the King of France the title of **Most Christian King** <note>original: "Rex Christianissimus"</note>; we also gave the same to Henry the Eighth, calling him **Defender of the Faith** <note>original: "Beschermheer des Geloofs"</note>. He had no right to that title of honor because it was given to him on a bad foundation by the Pope, for opposing the teachings of **Luther** <note>original: "Lutheri"</note>, yet no one thereafter refused to give him the title. I do not wish to provoke anyone, but my judgment is against the war with the Scottish Nation, which is united with us and took up the sword in our Quarrel; and currently, because they do not wish to be a Republic, it is willed that they shall no longer be a people, and they are to be denounced because they will not make a shipwreck of their 

<column-break/>

conscience. I die clinging fast to all the oaths, promises, protestations, and that **Solemn League and Covenant** or treaty, which was established by the two houses of Parliament; and I would much rather die keeping the covenant than live longer by breaking that same covenant.

The third and last part of my **funeral oration** <note>original: "Lijkredenen"</note> shall be a word of warning to this great City, and I shall then commend my soul into the hands of Him who gave it to me. I have wished for you an abundance of all happiness. O London! London! God has prepared [judgment for] the pride of all your glory and the contempt for the office of Preaching; resistance to Reformation has brought London low, and it is to be feared that she shall sink even lower. I shrink in contemplating the great miseries that are approaching; for just as merchandise has been distributed from you to all corners of the land, so too have all the heresies and blasphemies of this Nation taken their origin from you. First, I request that you shall love the diligent and Godly Ministers, for if they are taken away from you, you shall certainly receive worse in their place. Ministers who were once regarded as the **chariots and horsemen of Israel** <note>A biblical reference to 2 Kings 2:12, denoting spiritual protectors</note> are nowadays held [in contempt] by the worst and most harmful men. Because of this, all kinds of religious opinions and sects, as well as <note>original: "byp-geesten"</note> fanatic spirits, have crept in here. Submit yourselves to Church government: which shall be a bridle [to your sins] and a golden yoke for your pleasure; but in case you do not wish to submit to it, God has the power to lay an iron yoke upon you. Beware of the teachings which come under the name of **New Lights**; when the introducers of these say they are new, it is much to be doubted if they are true. In the 5th Book of Moses <note>Deuteronomy</note> in the 32nd chapter, 7th verse, it is said: *they sacrificed to devils, not to God; but to gods they did not know; to new gods, who had newly come up.* Their "new gods" were nothing other than old devils. Many of the same things going under the name of **New Lights** are merely old darknesses and errors, gathered from this dungheap of heresies which have been cast out by the Church and buried in shame by the Church.

Finally, mourn the great loss you must endure through the Ministers who have already been taken from you; ten Ministers at once who have been burning and shining lights to their respective followers, and bright stars in their particular paths. I am not worthy of the world; I am taken out of it; but regarding my brothers, who are in suffering, under bonds, and in exile in this age, the world is not worthy of them. Beware of starting a war against your friends. I have opposed the tyrannies of a King, but I have never spoken against the office and title. Beware how you treat the Godly Ministers of this City; if I did not have to die, I would say something more, for many years teach wisdom, but therefore I will remain silent. I pray that God may please to show them mercy; this I only request of them: that just as they have not been ashamed of my chains, they may likewise...

->### From Mr. Love.<-

...remaining strengthened through my bonds and blood.
<margin>Acts 4:29</margin> "And now, Lord, behold their threatenings, and grant unto thy servants, that with all boldness they may speak thy word." <note>original: "Actor. 4. 29." Love is quoting the prayer of the Apostles under persecution.</note> Though I am young, nonetheless I will sacrifice my young experience to their old wisdom, and say that I have set myself against sin and apostasy, and have thereby earned the disfavor of men, but obtained the peace of my God. I have lived in peace, and I shall die in peace. The government of the Church shall remain standing; indeed, I die with this resolution: that the <term>Presbyterian government|A form of church governance by assemblies of elders, which Love defended against both the Episcopacy of the King and the Independency of Cromwell’s supporters</term> most serves the superiority of unity in the churches of the saints. Beware of the general admission of all people to the Holy Supper of the Lord; do not be extravagant with the blood of Jesus Christ, speaking now to those present. I shall say a word regarding the same and conclude therewith. There are many rumors that all the ministers of this City were complicit in this design for which I am condemned to die here. I say to you still that all the ministers who were present in person in the aforementioned gathering, or complicit in that matter, are already imprisoned or discovered; therefore, I clear all the other ministers with my death. My conscience testifies that I have done no wrong in this matter. I shall soon be finished, for I long to be in my God's house. I wish to speak a word to my own parochial assembly, to thank God for them and to thank them as well; for they (with the exception of a few) have granted me great love and liberal support. All that I still desire from them is that they would choose a learned, godly, and <term>Orthodox|Love uses both "Orthodoxen" and the Dutch "recht-sinnigen" to emphasize correct, traditional doctrine</term> minister to occupy my place. It would also greatly comfort me, before I travel from here to Heaven, if I might hear that such a one filled my place, where he shall enjoy good support and much love. I would never have left them, but am separated from them by death, to which I submit myself with all Christian meekness and joy. I approach the end of my speech and the end of my life at once; but before I draw my last breath, I must justify God and condemn myself, for God is righteous but I am a sinful man, even though He lets me be cut off in the midst of my days and from my preaching office. I cannot complain, however, as it is written in the 44th Psalm: that you sell your people for nothing. My blood shall not be shed in vain; I shall possibly do more good by my death and bring greater honor to God on this scaffold than if I were to die in my bed. God be praised, I have not the slightest worry in my soul. I will voluntarily lay myself down upon the block. I perceive that men hunger for my flesh and thirst for my blood, which shall heighten my happiness and be their ruin and destruction. My blood, however, is not that of nobles, but my blood is Christ's blood—yes, a minister's blood—and what is more, innocent blood. My dead body shall be a little difficult to digest, an old dish upon which this <term>young Republic|A jab at the newly formed Commonwealth of England</term> (as Mr. Prideaux calls it) <note>Edmund Prideaux was the Attorney General who prosecuted Love.</note> shall fall silent. But God is righteous, that He has not made my imprisonment a Hell, nor this

<column-break/>

scaffold into an abyss; it is His pure and singular mercy. I do not only wish to justify God, but I must likewise exalt the riches of His grace toward me. Even though I was born in <term>Wales|A region then considered remote and less "noble" than London</term> (an ignoble place and of common parents), I was not excluded from this: for in fourteen years' time I did not hear a single sermon, but in the fifteenth year it pleased God to convert me. God be praised, who has not only made me a Christian, but also a minister; and He, finding that I would be faithful, entrusted the preaching office to me. It is an honor to me that I die thus; I would rather be a minister in a pulpit than a king on a throne. I would rather be an instrument to bring souls to Heaven than have all nations pay me toll and tribute. Let men judge of me what they will; I am nonetheless a martyr. Had I been willing to burden my conscience and risk my soul, I would have had good hope of keeping my life. But God be praised, I have done no wrong; I have chosen chastisement rather than to commit sin. Welcome death! Welcome axe! Welcome scaffold! All is welcome, because they shall provide me a dwelling in my Father's house. Praise be to God, who has stood by me in my imprisonment; He has strengthened me, He supports me. Although I die an untimely death, death holds no fear for me, for God is no terror to me; therefore my death is not hideous. I have previously been under the spirit of constraint and had more fear of pulling out a tooth than I currently fear the striking off of my head. When fear was upon me then, death was not near; but now that death is near, the fear has vanished. I thank God that, although men judge me to be cast out of the world, God has nonetheless not cast me out from His people. Some think I am not worthy of life; others judge that I have not deserved death. I shall conclude; I have no more to say, but request the assistance of your prayers, that God will be a constant support to me and grant me His divine grace, which may carry me through this great work I have before me. That I, doing a work I have never done before, may obtain greater strength than I have ever had, so that I may lay down this body with as great a joy of spirit as I have ever undressed myself to go to bed. Now I will commend my soul to God and receive my mortal blow; though men thrust me out of this world, they cannot shut me out of Heaven. I stand ready to make my long journey, and you shall make a short journey to your houses; but I tell you, I shall be home before you come home. I stand on my journey to the Heavenly Jerusalem, to an innumerable company of angels, to the spirits of the righteous who are made perfect, and to God the judge of all, in whose presence I shall have the fullness of joy and gladness unto eternity. I conclude my last words from the Apostle Paul, 2 Timothy 4:6, 7: "For I am now ready to be offered as a drink offering, and the time of my departure is at hand; I have fought a good fight..."

Then, having said farewell to the people, he requested their Christian assistance [in prayer], and he prayed as follows:

> O! Eternal and glorious Lord and God, I, your poor and unworthy creature, humble myself before your Divine Majesty, praying that for the sake of the merits of Jesus Christ, my blessed Savior and Redeemer, you would be pleased to be merciful to me. And dear Father, I humbly pray that you would be pleased to strengthen me with your gracious Spirit in this great work: so that I may voluntarily lay down my head upon the block. All this I pray and desire, not only for myself, but also for my dear Brother <note>Refers to John Gibbons, a fellow conspirator executed on the same day</note>, who shall follow me to death this day, whom I hope to meet victoriously in your glorious and eternal kingdom. Having thus ended his prayer, he turned himself toward the Executioner, saying: "Friend, are all things ready?" To which the Executioner said, "Yes, my Lord." Whereupon, unbuttoning his doublet <note>A close-fitting buttoned jacket</note>, he handed it to his friend; he then pulled a red veil <note>original: "roode sluyer," likely a cloth to cover his eyes or face</note> out of his pocket and gave it to the Executioner, saying: "Do with this according to your discretion," which he then did, and laid it over the sawdust and upon the block.

Then Mr. Love put his hand into his pocket and took out three pounds sterling (wrapped in a white paper) and gave them to the Executioner, saying, "Friend, there are three pounds for you; do that which you have to do, and God forgive you, just as I have forgiven you."

Furthermore, Mr. Love knelt down and laid his neck upon the block, and when he lifted up his left hand (being the signal he had given), the Executioner let the axe fall and separated the head from his body with a single stroke. This being done, he took the head in his hand, and shortly thereafter he laid both body and head together in a black coffin, which was immediately carried away, covered with a mourning cloth. The surgeon Dr. Dun followed behind, in order to sew the same back together <note>It was common for families of high-ranking executed men to have the head sewn back to the body for a more dignified burial</note>.

These words contain within themselves the blessed conclusion and end of Stephen’s life; in which we have three main points to note:

1. The Person who fell asleep.
2. The speech <note>original: "reden," which can mean both "reason" and "discourse" or "speech"</note> which he made as he fell asleep.
3. What he did when he had ended his speech.

First, we have the Person who fell asleep, and this was Stephen; he was a man full of faith, and filled with the Holy Spirit: as you may see in Acts 6:5. He was the first Martyr who ever suffered for the cause of Christ; from this I could gather this doctrine, namely:
