you were without Christ: 2. Alienated from the citizenship of Israel; 3. You were strangers to the covenants of promise: 4. You were without hope: 5. And you were without God in this world.

Now, these five things contain within them an entirely miserable condition for Man; here is also described the length of time that Man is in this state, namely *that you were at that time*, that is, the time during your unconverted state. As long as you are unconverted, so long are you without Christ, and alienated from the citizenship of Israel, and strangers to the covenants of promise, having no hope, and without God in the world.

What a sorrowful Text I have now to handle, and what a distressing tragedy must I now speak of? And yet, from every small part follows a great comfort for us. I shall only make an entrance to these words, and speak a little of those [preceding them] in reverse; *that you were at that time without Christ, that you were at that time*; Beloved, here something is missing from the sense of the words, and therefore read the preceding passage, and you shall find what must be brought in; in verse 11 at the beginning it stands thus: *therefore remember that you, being in time past Gentiles in the flesh,* etc. Therefore "remember"—these words must come first—*therefore remember, that you were at that time without Christ, alienated from the Citizenship of Israel,* etc. I shall here in passing note this one teaching, from the connection of these words: *therefore remember, that you at that time*; the Apostle wants these converted Ephesians to remember that they were once men without Christ, alienated from the citizenship of Israel, and strangers to the covenants of promise, having no hope, and without God in the world: and from this I wish to commend this Teaching to you.

<margin>1. Teaching.</margin>
That it is the will of God that people in a converted state should often reflect in their minds upon the misery to which they were liable before their Conversion.

Beloved, this is a subject upon which I have never before had the opportunity to speak to you, and yet it is a point of wonderful use, especially in these times. In which the People think, once they are brought into a state of grace, they must live in Divine revelation and spiritual joy, under duties and ordinances, and never look back at their previous sinfulness and godlessness to which they were liable before their conversion. Truly, the Ephesians were converted and had extraordinary privileges; they were brought to sit in Heavenly places with Jesus Christ; and yet the Apostle prays them to remember their former sin and misery; remember, O you Ephesians! that you were without Christ, alienated from the citizenship of Israel, etc. Therefore beware of thinking, now that you are converted, that you are taken up into the third Heaven and do not need to remember your former state; you see here that the Apostle prays you to remember what you were during the time of your unconverted state: that you were without Christ, etc. So you see it is the will of God that people in a converted condition should often reflect in their minds upon the misery in which they were before their conversion.

Now, before I come to give you the reasons for this point, allow me to set these precautions: when I tell you that after

conversion, you shall reflect in your mind upon your sin and misery before conversion, you must not do it: 1. with delight of the Spirit; nor 2. with hardness of heart; nor 3. with weakening of the mind.

<margin>1.</margin>

You must reflect in your mind upon your former sinfulness, not with delight, but with bitterness of Spirit: with sorrow and contrition of heart. Many people want to tell you long stories of the godlessness they have committed; yet they do so with delight, and if they had the strength and opportunity, they would still be guilty of the same sin and godlessness; which is an ungodly practice, for which the scripture damns men, Ezekiel 23:19, 21. *Yet she multiplied her harlotries, in calling to remembrance the days of her youth, wherein she had played the harlot in the land of Egypt. ...those who have the greatest wonder at God’s grace and mercy are those who are most busy reflecting on their own sin and misery. # The Miserable State in Nature

<margin>Observation</margin>
No one has greater wonder for God's grace and mercy than those who are most busy in contemplating their own sin and misery. You shall never glorify God's mercy until you are brought to a feeling of your own wretchedness and see in what a miserable and pitiable state you were before your conversion. Then you will want to magnify the riches of God's free grace, once you have been brought from that state into the state of grace. Just as in 1 Timothy 1:13, when the Apostle wanted to magnify the free grace of God toward him, he says:
> I, who was before a blasphemer, and a persecutor, and an oppressor: and yet, out of the abundance of God’s free grace, mercy was shown to me.

The consideration of his former sinful life stirred his heart to wonder at God's grace toward his soul; a man can never rightly praise freedom if he has never been a prisoner.

<margin>2nd Reason</margin>
2. God desires this because it should serve as a spur to stir up and advance men to excel more in grace. It is truly noteworthy of Paul that, regarding all the impieties of which he was guilty before his conversion, he was most grieved by them, and in response, he worked hardest to excel in the opposite graces after his conversion. For example: before his conversion, he labored to bring others into prison for the sake of Christ; but after his conversion, he applied himself to bring others to Christ. # A true account of man’s
<margin>Application.</margin>
The Apostle makes use of this here, in Ephesians 5:8: 
*For you were once darkness, but now you are light in the Lord; walk as children of light.* We shall now hate and abhor those sins which we formerly loved.

These are the Reasons for this point; I shall only make a brief application of it, which is contained in this: that (notwithstanding it being the will of God that people, after their conversion, should reflect upon the sins they were guilty of before conversion) nevertheless, people resist this teaching in their judgment and practice.

1. This rebukes those who act contrary to this teaching in judgment, and think that once they are converted, they never need to look back at their former godlessness, but now live only in Divine Revelations and spiritual Comforts; for if Paul is trustworthy, then this opinion is untrue; for he tells us that we must remember what we were in our unconverted state, that we were at that time without Christ, without hope, and without God in the world.

2. Paul tells the Ephesians that they, who were a chosen people, chosen before the beginning of the world, had to remember that they were dead in sins and trespasses, although they now lived. And if Paul commanded this of them, why then should we not do it?

2. <note>The original text repeats the number 2 for this second point of rebuke.</note> This rebukes those who do not deny this teaching in their judgment, yet do not make it their practice to reflect in their minds on their former sins, of which they were guilty before conversion. I believe that many of you well remember what you have done, what debts you have from over twenty years ago, but yet your conscience cannot recount what sins you committed twenty years ago; it may be that some of you have been cursers, swearers, adulterers, and unholy, and yet now you never think of it, but imagine to yourself that all is well. Now you do not know how to say in what a sad and lamentable state your poor soul has been; you do not think of your former sins. But let this much be enough said of the first doctrine.

### Ephesians 2:12

> That at that time you were without Christ, being aliens from the commonwealth of Israel, and strangers from the covenants of promise, having no hope, and without God in the world.

<margin>2nd Predicate.</margin>
We now come to the body and core of the words: *That at that time you were without Christ*; note this from these words:

<margin>2nd Doctrine.</margin>
**Doctrine:** *That every person, during the time of their unregeneracy <note>original: "onwedergeboorte," referring to the state before being "born again" or spiritually renewed</note>, is in a state without Jesus Christ.*

My beloved, if I were now to tell you that when you had come home, you would never have a morsel of bread to put in your mouths, that all your means of life were taken away, and you would never have a foot of land, nothing to live on—that would indeed be a hard thing. But I say to you, my brothers, that to be without Christ is by far the worst case and most miserable thing in this world. When I tell you that you are without Christ, I tell you the saddest news in the world; but before I handle this doctrine, there is an objection and a question, with the answer to which I must spend a little <column-break/> time.

**Objection.** How can it be said of these Ephesians, since they were chosen, that before their conversion they were without Christ, seeing they were chosen by God in Christ before the foundation of the world? And therefore, how can the Apostle say that when they were born, they were without Christ, considering they were chosen in Christ from the foundation of the world?

**Answer.** The same person in a different sense may be said to be "in Christ" and "without Christ." It is true the Apostle says in the first chapter that they were chosen in Christ before the foundation of the world.

1. If you consider the eternal decree of God, they were "in Christ," for God had intended that Jesus Christ should be a Mediator <note>original: "Middelaars"</note> between Him and man, through whose blood they should be saved.

2. Although they were "in Christ" in respect to God's decree, yet they were "without Christ" in respect to the actual application <note>original: "toe-eygeninge"</note> of the blood of Christ to their souls. For where a person does not have faith, he cannot claim God's love for himself; he who does not have the Spirit of Christ is none of His. Although they were then "in Christ" in respect to God's decree, yet they were "without Christ" in respect to the actual application of God's love to them; for they could not claim for their souls that Christ loved them and accepted them as His children until they were brought into a converted state.

Now I come to the Question which I promised to answer, which is this: What is it to be "without Christ"?

**Answer.** It includes in itself these three things:
1. To be without the blessed knowledge of Christ;
2. To be without any actual interest in Christ;
3. To be without any spiritual communion with Christ.

Now, if you ask me which is primarily meant here, of which the Ephesians were without? I answer: primarily these two, for they were both without the true knowledge of Christ and without any actual interest in Christ.

1. To be without Christ is to be without the blessed knowledge of Jesus Christ. Although a person during their unconverted state may have a large share of public knowledge, yet the Scripture says he is in a state without Christ. Now a person may be said to be without the true knowledge of Christ in these five things:

**First**, A person may have a common knowledge of Christ, and yet be without fine spiritual knowledge; he may have a natural knowledge through the works of God, through hearing, reading, or the like, and yet be without spiritual knowledge—of knowing Christ in a spiritual manner.

2. A person may have a noting knowledge <note>original: "noterende kennisie," referring to "notional" or theoretical knowledge as opposed to heartfelt understanding</note>, and yet be without experiential knowledge of Jesus Christ. And herein the Scripture expresses the distinction between the knowledge of the Righteous and the Ungodly: The Lord plants His wisdom in the hidden parts of His children, but the ungodly have the outward parts in their heads and brains.

3. An unregenerate person has a contemplative, but no affective knowledge <note>An "affective" knowledge is one that moves the heart or emotions, rather than just the intellect.</note> of Christ. The ungodly can have a speculative knowledge of Christ; they know Him just as a man knows his neighbor; but the believers know Christ as a wife knows her husband; she knows and loves

# The Miserable State in Nature

### Doctrine. That every person, during the time of their un-regeneration, is without any actual interest in Christ.

In the handling of this point, I shall only do these three things:

2. I shall point out to you the **Signs** of a person without Christ.
3. I shall point out to you the **Misery** of a person without Christ: and then come to the applications.

First, I shall point out to you the Properties of a person without Christ; and in the handling of this subject, I wish from the bottom of my Soul that if I cannot draw you, I may nonetheless wake you up to see how necessary it is to gain an interest in Jesus Christ; and here I shall reveal to you eight particular properties of a person without Christ.

1. Every person without Christ is an **unworthy** person.
2. He is a **servile** person.

It is said of Jacob in *Genesis* 27 that he obtained his Father’s blessing in the garment of his eldest brother, and so we are only blessed by God our Father when we are clothed with the garments of our eldest brother, Jesus Christ. <note>The author uses the biblical story of Jacob disguised as Esau to illustrate "imputed righteousness"—the idea that God accepts believers because they are "clothed" in the perfection of Jesus.</note>

# The Miserable State in Nature

...does not have life. From this it comes that we read in Ephesians 2:1 that an unregenerate <note>A person who has not undergone a spiritual rebirth or conversion.</note> person is dead in trespasses and sins. The reason is that Christ is the life of believers, Colossians 3:3: *Your life is hidden with Christ in God.* Take Christ away from a person, and he is a dead lump of flesh. Unregenerate people are opponents of the life of the godly, and therefore they must necessarily be dead in their sins; although they visibly live, nonetheless their life is no life through faith in the Son of God; they are spiritually dead. As for example:

1. You know a dead person has no feeling; you do to him whatever you want, and he does not feel it. Likewise, a person who is spiritually dead does not feel the weight of his sins, even though they press upon him like heavy burdens, thrusting him down into Hell. He is a stranger to the life of godliness and feeling, but given over to a perverse mind, so that he does not feel the weight or the burden of sin.

2. A person has a name and nothing else in this life; however rich he may be, in death he loses it, and it passes from him to another. Truly, if you are spiritually dead, you can claim nothing: neither grace, nor mercy, nor heaven, nor blessedness through Jesus Christ.

3. A dead man rots and returns to dust, as he once was; and a person who is spiritually dead falls from iniquity to iniquity, from one sin into another, until he comes into the hellish fire.

The 8th and last property: a person without Christ is a damned person. If he lives and dies without Christ, he is damned. John 3:18: *He who does not believe is condemned already.* He is as certainly damned as if he were already in hell. He who is without Christ does not enter Heaven, for Heaven and even blessedness itself are closed to him. Heaven is for no one except those who have a share in Christ, and therefore you who are without Christ must necessarily be without Heaven, and consequently without Salvation or Glory, but damned in Hell. So you see in these eight particular properties in what a sad and miserable state a person is without Christ. And oh! that what has now been explained might serve to awaken all people outside of Christ, and give to every soul a holy alertness and readiness of spirit in your labor to obtain Jesus Christ.

<margin>7. Seven signs of a person without Christ.</margin>
We come now to the second question which I promised to answer.
**Question:** What are the signs of a person without Christ?
**Answer:** This question is truly necessary, so that we may know through it whether we are without Christ or not. Now, I shall reduce these signs to seven, and go over them briefly.

<column-break/>

First, the person who is without the Spirit of Christ is without an actual interest <note>In this context, "interest" means a legal or spiritual stake or claim in Christ's benefits.</note> in Christ. This the Apostle makes known in many explicit places, Romans 8:9: *If any man have not the Spirit of Christ, he is none of his.* Christ and the Spirit are inseparable companions; if you have the one, you also enjoy the other; if you lack the one, you also lack the other. And, beloved, to go into more detail: if you are without an interest in Christ, you are without the Spirit in these three types of operations:

1. If you are without the enlightening work of the Spirit that teaches your minds to know Christ.

2. If you are without the inclination of the Spirit that makes your hearts love Christ.

3. If you are without the movement of the Spirit that makes your will obey Christ.

1. If you are without the Spirit of Christ in these three things, you cannot rightly claim to have an interest in Jesus Christ. With what reason can any of you claim for yourselves Christ’s Person, while having no share in His Spirit? But instead, do you still follow the corrupt promptings of your own heart, the desires of the flesh and of the mind? You who are so, can have no share in Jesus Christ, for *if any man have not his Spirit, he is none of his*; and this is the first sign.

2. He who is without any protective power, coming from Jesus Christ, to kill his inner lusts. A person is without Christ, as the Apostle tells us in Galatians 5:24: *They that are Christ’s have crucified the flesh with the affections and lusts.* Thereby giving it to be understood that they who have not crucified the flesh with its affections and lusts have no share in the Lord Jesus Christ. When Christ came in the flesh, they crucified Him; but when Christ comes into the soul, He wants to crucify it <note>Meaning Christ crucifies the sinful nature within the person.</note>. They that are Christ's have crucified the flesh. Christ wants to be a punisher of sin, to crucify the lusts and kill the corruptions when He enters the soul. But, beloved, this is not to be understood as a total subduing of sin and corruption, but only so far as to give a deadly sting to sin, so that it no longer reigns in the soul. Sin in the heart of one who is in Christ shall be like the Monarchs spoken of in Daniel 7:12: *Their dominion was taken away, yet their lives were prolonged for a season and time.* Even so it is with sin in the heart of a believer: the dominion of sin is taken away, but the life and essence remain for a short time. There shall still be some remnants of sin in the best of God’s children, yet they shall not reign in their mortal bodies. And therefore, you who [lack] <note>The original Dutch "ooit" (ever) appears to be a printer's error for "niet" (not) or "noit" (never) given the context of the warning.</note> any power to kill your sins, even though you still retain some remnants, you have no share in Jesus Christ, for *they have crucified the flesh with its lusts.* I may here make use of a story (which I have often told you): In the History of Scotland, mention is made of an island named Yllandt <note>Likely referring to a legend regarding the Isle of Man or a similar territory between Scotland and Ireland; the test involves whether venomous animals can survive on the soil.</note>, lying in the middle of the sea between Scotland and Ireland. The story concludes that if the venomous animals survived, the land was Scottish; if they died, it was Irish (due to the blessing of St. Patrick).</note>

### A True Account of Man's State

...were to gather toads <note>original: "vorſchen" – can refer to frogs or toads, here implying "unclean" or venomous creatures</note> and place them on an island; and if these unclean animals were to stay alive there, that island would then belong to Scotland. But if they died, it would belong to Ireland, for no unclean creatures exist or remain there. <note>This refers to a popular medieval and early modern legend that Ireland was blessed (often attributed to St. Patrick) so that no venomous or "unclean" animals could survive on its soil. It was used here as a spiritual "litmus test."</note> Just so it is with us: there is a great dispute between Christ and the Devil as to whom your soul belongs. If your harmful lusts and poisonous sins can live and dwell in your soul, then you belong to the Devil; but if these lusts and sins die in your soul, then you belong to Jesus Christ.

3. The person who does not have a sincere <note>original: "ongebveynſde" - literally "unfeigned" or without hypocrisy</note> love for the Person of Christ, has no **interest** <term>interest: a legal and spiritual stake or rightful claim to the benefits of Christ's salvation</term> in Christ. For everyone who has Christ, loves Him; and he who does not have Him, does not love Him. **1 Corinthians 16:22**:
> If anyone does not love the Lord Jesus Christ, let him be accursed. <note>original: "Vervloeckinge" - a translation of the biblical 'Anathema.'</note>

He who does not love Christ has no part in Him, and shall be cursed when Christ comes to judge the world.

**Objection.** But some will be ready to say: "If it is so, that not loving Christ is an argument for not having Him, then I have enough; I love Christ with all my heart."

**Answer.** I shall tell you in Christ’s own words who the one is that loves Him. **John 14:24**:
> He who does not love me, does not keep my words.

O man, does your conscience say that you have obeyed every one of Christ's commands? Let Him command what He will, yet you do what you want. You see here that Christ expressly says that he who does not love Him does not keep His words. I pray you, therefore, in the fear of God, beware of damaging your own souls by thinking you love Christ when He is not there; but labor to love Him in truth, and prove your love by the keeping of His commandments.

4. The person who is without any saving knowledge of Christ, and without any actual enjoyment of Him: there is no one who has Christ who does not know Him. (Do not misunderstand my words.) I do not say that everyone knows that they have Him, for a person can have Christ and yet not know it for the present time; but this I say: he who has a part in Christ, whoever he be, must know Christ to some degree. **John 8:54, 55**:
> You say that God is your God, and yet you do not know Him.

It is a powerful passage: you say that God, and salvation through Him, is yours, and yet you do not know Him! Oh, my beloved! You say that you know Christ, and you do not know Him; He will hide Himself from you until the last day. You have a false imagination that you know Him; read **John 1:12**, compared with **verses 24 and 25**.

Now when I tell you that a person without the knowledge of Christ has no interest in Christ, I am not saying that those who are without Christ are those who simply lack a great degree of knowledge like others. But if you are without the knowledge of Christ, accompanied by these two circumstances, then I can firmly assure you: you are a Christ-less person.

First, if you are without the knowledge of Christ and yet are content in your ignorance, neither desiring nor laboring for His knowledge, then I may firmly say that for the present you are without Christ—if you are like those spoken of in **2 Peter 3**:

<column-break/>

5. 
> For they are willfully ignorant of this: that by the word of God the heavens were of old,

Or like **Job 21:14**:
> Depart from us, for we have no desire for the knowledge of your ways.

If you are so, you are truly without Christ.

Secondly, not only when you are content in your ignorance, but likewise when, with darkening in your judgments, you obstinately give up your will—being ignorant of what you do not know, or refusing to know what you have not learned, or refusing to learn—then you are like those spoken of in **Psalm 82:5**:
> They do not know, nor do they understand,

That is, they *will* not know. A godly person can have a shadow of this; though you may be very ignorant, yet if you strive for knowledge, you have a part in Christ. But I am bound to say that if you are ignorant, and remain content in it, and obstinately refuse to learn more, then you have no interest in Christ. Therefore, take your hands off Christ; you have no part in Him, you have nothing to do with Him; He is not yours.

5. <note>The author repeats the number 5 in the original list.</note> A person who does not have a hearing ear for the voice of Christ, and an obedient heart for the commands of Christ, has no part in Christ. I shall give you two clear texts that prove this. **John 8:47**:
> He who is of God hears God’s words; therefore you do not hear them, because you are not of God.

So those who are of God hear His word. Those who love Christ and have a part in Him hear His word, not only with the ear but with the heart. And **1 John 4:6**:
> We are of God; he who knows God hears us; he who is not of God does not hear us. By this we know the Spirit of truth and the spirit of error.

And therefore, you obstinate and bold-hearted, wretched people, who can lie under the word of God like a stone, and endure that no command is worked out through your spirit—truly, you have no right to Jesus Christ.

6. The person who uses greater diligence and takes greater pleasure in committing sin than in working out any grace or the fulfilling of any duty, is without Christ. You have an excellent passage for this purpose in **1 John 3:8, 10**:
> He who does sin is of the Devil.

He does not say simply "he who does sin," but "he who commits it" (as the word actually signifies): commits it with pleasure and love for the same—this one is of the Devil. And **verse 10**:
> In this the children of God and the children of the Devil are manifest: whoever does not practice righteousness is not of God.

He has no part in God who does not practice righteousness with pleasure, delight, joy, and diligence. Just as he who commits sin with pleasure is of the Devil, so he who does righteousness with joy, gladness, and care is of Christ. You then, who can sin with pleasure and extinguish your spirit in holy duties—you who never strive to hallow the Sabbath day as much as you previously desecrated it—you who have never been as zealous in your duties to God as you were in sinning against God—keep your hands off Jesus Christ! Your hearts shall be of sin; you can have no part in Him. **John 9:16**:
> Therefore some of the Pharisees said, "This man is not from God, because he does not keep the Sabbath."

This would indeed have been a good argument, had it been correctly applied.

# Miserable State in Nature

...had Christ not kept the Sabbath; if it can truly be said of you that you have no **conscience** <term>conscience: an inner moral sense or "scruple" that compels a person to follow God’s laws</term> to keep the Sabbath, or to fulfill any holy duties, I can truly say to you: you are not of God. Now then, examine yourselves by this argument: whether you are of God or not. If you violate the Sabbath day and make no conscience of neglecting holy duties nor of sinning against God, this indicates that you are not of God. The person who performs sin with more pleasure than holy duties has no right to Christ. **1 John 5:18**: *We know that everyone who has been born of God does not keep on sinning*; that is, he does not commit it with pleasure as the ungodly do. But he who has a part in God *keeps himself, and the evil one does not touch him*; that is, not in such a way that he commits sin in the aforementioned sense, but he guards himself; he does not give himself over to greedily commit sin as the ungodly do. And therefore the Apostle says in **1 John 5:19**: *We know that we are from God, and the whole world lies in the power of the evil one.*

7. The final mark is this: a person is without any right to Christ who deviates from the ways of Christ, both in **judgment** <term>judgment: in this context, one's intellectual beliefs, doctrine, or theological convictions</term> and in **practice** <term>practice: the outward behavior, habits, and lifestyle of a person</term>. When a person deviates from the truth of Christ in judgment, and from the exercise of holy duties in practice—deviating from both these ways—he is not of Christ. **2 John verse 9**: *Everyone who goes on ahead and does not abide in the teaching of Christ, does not have God; he who abides in the teaching has both the Father and the Son.* The person who sins both in judgment and in practice is not of God; but he who remains in the truth of God, both in judgment and in practice, has both the Father and the Son.

Oh, therefore, I pray you in the fear of God, see for yourself whether you have a part in Christ or not. Are you without the Spirit of Christ? Or are you without the protecting power of Christ to kill your inner lusts? Are you without a true, saving knowledge of Christ? Are you content to be ignorant of Christ and desire to know no more? Or are you obstinately ignorant and refuse to learn more? Are you without a hearing ear and an obedient heart toward the Word of Christ? Do you show more diligence and take more pleasure in committing sin than in performing holy duties? Do you deviate from the ways of Christ, both in judgment and in practice? If all these seven marks are found in you together, then I conclude that you have no part at all in Christ, and at that time you are without Christ. And thus I have handled and answered the second question; I shall now suspend it for a little while, due to certain **uses** <term>uses: also called "applications," these were sections of a sermon or treatise where the author applies the theological points to the specific lives of the readers</term>, and then come to the third question.

And in the application of this, I shall direct myself to speak to two sorts of people.

1. To those who are so far carried away in a spiritual pride <note>original: "opgeblaſenthepdt" – puffiness or conceit</note> that they say they have a part in Christ when they do not.

2. To those who say they have no right to Christ when they actually do.

<margin>1. Use.</margin> 1. To you who say you have a part in Christ when you do not; give me leave to propose these three or four questions to you. 1. Let me ask you: were you ever without Christ, yes or no? If you answer no, then I say: a person who says he has always had Christ

<column-break/>

truly never has Him at all. You who dare to say that you have always had Christ from your birth—to you I say: you have never had Him after your birth, for every person is born a "Christless" person.

2. I ask you: how did you come by your part in Christ? Or do you think that Christ fell from Heaven into your bosom, whether you wanted Him or not? How then did you come to Christ? Did you offer a mighty prayer to God for Him? Did you ever see your misery without Him? Did you earnestly request Him from the Father? For God is not ready to give His Son to those who never ask Him for it.

3. Did you ever see an absolute necessity in your own soul to have a part in Jesus Christ? Were you ever sensitive to the lack of Christ and the Word? Or how necessary Christ is for you? In what a sorrowful, miserable, and damnable state you are without Christ? If you are not sensitive to this, you are still without Christ.

4. How can you assure yourself that you have a part in Christ by your **walk** <term>walk: a common biblical metaphor for a person's daily conduct and lifestyle</term>? What does the Apostle say in **2 Corinthians 5:17**? *Therefore, if anyone is in Christ, he is a new creation; the old has passed away, behold, all things have become new.* Are you new creatures? Have all your old sins been put away? The Apostle tells you: *those who belong to Christ have crucified the flesh with its passions.* But now, have you killed the lusts of your heart? Do not lusts rather rule in you with as much power as they ever did? If this is so, you have no interest at all in Christ.

<margin>2. Use.</margin> 2. So much for the first sort; we now come to the second. These are doubting and perplexed souls who say they have no part in Christ when they do. These say they are without Christ, and truly they are not; there are many such people in the world. Now, to such as these, I have these three or four words of comfort.

1. Let me say this for your comfort: it is common for the people of God to pass hard and heavy sentences upon their own souls, and to heap up the failings of their own salvation. A child of God sees so many lusts in his heart, and so many sins within him, that he finds it difficult to have lovely thoughts of his own soul, just as David did when he said: *The Lord has forsaken me and cast me off forever.* <note>The author likely refers to the spirit of Psalms like Psalm 77 or 88, where the psalmist feels abandoned by God.</note>

2. You can have Christ and yet not know that you have Him; it can be with you just as it was with **Mary Magdalene** when she saw Christ face to face, yet she said in **John 20:13**: *They have taken away my Lord, and I do not know where they have laid Him.* So you can have a part in Christ and not know it. Christ says to His disciples in **John 14:4**: *And you know the way where I am going.* Thomas said to Him: *Lord, we do not know where you are going, and how can we know the way?* Now, the reason why they did not know this, as **Augustine** <note>St. Augustine of Hippo (354–430 AD), a foundational theologian in Western Christianity often cited in Reformed works.</note> well notes, was because they did not know their own thoughts; they thought they did not know this, but nevertheless Christ knew that it was known to them. It is with believers sometimes just as it was with **Benjamin**: the cup was in his sack and he did not know it. <note>Referring to Genesis 44, where Joseph hides a silver cup in his brother Benjamin’s sack to test him.</note> Now Benjamin was the most beloved in Joseph's eyes; so you are the dearest in Christ's sight, and yet you do not know it.

3. You who think that you are without Christ and you are not; let this be for your comfort...

# A True Account of Man's 

...comfort; although having a **Christian departure** <note>original: "Christen-affscheydelyk"; likely referring to the necessity of a holy death or the soul's departure from the world</note> is necessary to bring your souls to heaven, nevertheless, the certain knowledge that we have Christ is not as strictly necessary. It is like a man who sleeps in a ship; the ship can bring him to his house or inn while he does not even know it. So a Christian may, in his thoughts, be in a sea of struggling sighs and temptations toward Heaven—the heaven of rest—and yet we do not know it until we arrive there.

4. Let this likewise be for your comfort: although you do not know that Christ is yours, nevertheless Christ knows that you are His. Would you consider your child unfortunate because he does not know that you are his father? Is it not enough—even if the child does not know it—that he is your child? So too, although you do not know that Christ is yours, it is enough that you know that you are His; for *the firm foundation of God stands, the Lord knows those who are His*, **2 Timothy 2:19**. Thus, beloved, I have finished this practice of your **examination** <term>examination: the spiritual discipline of "self-testing" to see if one’s faith is genuine</term>, both for those who say they have Christ when they have him not, and likewise for those who say they have not Christ when they do have him.

<margin>4th Point</margin>
**I** come now to the third question which I promised to handle, which is this: to show the misery and sorrowful condition in which a person exists without any **right to Christ** <term>right to Christ: a legal or spiritual claim to the benefits of salvation through union with Jesus</term>. And oh, that I could speak it and you could hear it with a moved heart, to see in what a sad and lamentable state every poor soul lies in the world without Christ. I shall include all that I have to say regarding this specifically under these two headings, showing you: 1. **Positively** <term>positively: in a theological sense, referring to the actual punishments or evils present in a person's life</term>, what happens to him; and 2. **Privatively** <term>privatively: referring to the good things that are absent or "deprived" from a person</term>, what he lacks. I shall go over it briefly.

First, **Positively**: The miseries of a person without Christ consist in these three things. There are three great evils under which every person lies who is without Christ.

Firstly, a person without Christ is surrounded with miseries, whatever he may tell himself. And to expand on this somewhat more, I shall set down eight directions in which a person without Christ is surrounded with miseries on all sides. O man without Christ, whether you look outward or inward, upward or downward, forward or backward, to the right hand or to the left, nothing but miseries accompany you.

1. If you look **outward**, all creatures are armed against you; and from this it is often expressed in the Scripture that the beasts are at odds with the ungodly, but at peace with the godly. All creatures are against you, to quarrel with their Master.

2. Look **within** you, and there you shall find a bitter and gnawing **conscience** <term>conscience: the internal "judge" that accuses or excuses a person based on God's law</term>, like a seat 

<column-break/>

of judgment, recording everything against you. Your conscience shall be to you as much as a thousand witnesses testifying against you—like a register and roll of your sins on the Day of Judgment.

3. Look **upward** into the Heavens, and there is nothing but a wrathful God, a strict Judge, who has a flaming fire, a consuming sword, a sharp arrow, and many more things against you, **Romans 1:18**. *For the wrath of God is revealed from heaven against all ungodliness and unrighteousness of men.*

4. If you look **downward**, there is Death ready to receive you, which is but like a back-door to lead you into Hell. And if you look yet further, there is nothing but gloom and darkness, where the evil spirits are kept in a dark dungeon until the judgment of the Great Day. When a man without Christ looks at this, nothing but miseries accompany him: outwardly all creatures are against him; inwardly he has a gnawing and accusing conscience; above him he has a wrathful God against him; below him the Devil is ready to receive him. Such a person is in the most sorrowful state, as can be shown by this common comparison: suppose a man were thrown into the largest and darkest prison, in which there were nothing but toads and serpents and all kinds of venomous creatures, and a great stone was rolled over it, or a tree grew before the entrance of the dungeon, at whose trunk the venomous creatures constantly gnawed. Think in what a miserable state that poor man would be? Truly, even so it is with you, O man without Christ. Your life is this tree; death is a venomous beast that constantly gnaws the shoots of that tree, and then you fall down into gloom and darkness. There is nothing more than a small growth of life between you and Hell.

5. If you look **before** you, there is likewise nothing but misery; there are the deceptions and temptations of the Devil, who seeks to catch you on the road and drive you to sin. There is not a single footstep you take but the Devil has a snare in it to catch you.

6. If you look **beside** you <note>likely meaning "behind" or "all around" in the sense of an accumulating burden</note>, there is nothing but a heaped-up pile of sins, unrepented and unsatisfied, which make you fit to sink down into the bottomless pit of Hell. How can you then think that you are freed from your sins with a peaceful heart? How sorrowful is the consideration of so many thousands of sins you have committed, for which you have never humbled yourself. The guilt and burden of this is enough to cast you into Hell forever.

7. If you look to the **right hand**, there are all the blessings of God, all fullness, his riches, great status, and whatever one can wish for. Yet God gives an ungodly man riches to his own hurt; *the prosperity of the ungodly shall kill their soul*. Oh, man without Christ, your riches and prosperity bring you all the sooner into eternal destruction.

8. If you look to the **left hand**, there are all miseries, oppressions, sufferings, and sorrows; terrifying accidents that shall meet you like many heavy and unbearable burdens, which a person without Christ shall endure for eternity.

# The Miserable State in Nature

...right to Jesus Christ! Above you, below you, before you, and behind you, at your right and at your left hand, there are nothing but miseries that surround you on all sides. This much regarding the positive part of the misery of a man without Christ; it is truly a sad point that I am now handling, and therefore I will conclude it with some words of comfort. But—

Secondly, (Beloved, follow me now) you, man or woman, who are without Christ, you are godlessly miserable, because there is nothing in the world so sad and unbearable to your soul as the conception of a God without Christ. God is generally good in Christ; yet without Christ, this great God who is so good and rich in mercy and rich in grace is clothed in glow and scarlet <note>original: "gloet ende schaerlaken"; likely referring to the terrifying fire of divine judgment and the traditional red robes of a judge</note>. You who are without Christ cannot look upon God except with sadness: you cannot see Him as a God of mercy, forgiving you, but as a strict Judge, ready to damn you; not as a Friend who seeks your welfare, but as an Enemy who sets Himself for battle against you to destroy you. You cannot look upon Him as a Rock of Salvation in whose clefts you find rest, but as a heavy burdensome stone, whose weight presses you down. You cannot look upon Him as a goldsmith's fire, which purifies you from dross, but as a consuming fire, which burns you eternally to ashes. These are the thoughts that every soul that is without Christ has; the very thought of God is sad to him.

Thirdly, your misery also consists in this: that all the creatures and blessings that you enjoy here in this world are a curse to you; for all blessings are given in and through Christ. No blessing is a blessing, nor a mercy, if Christ, with the grace of all mercies, is not added to it. And here I will point out your misery in these five particular things:

1. Having a condition <note>original: "Conditie"; here referring to one's social standing, livelihood, or state of life</note> is a blessing from God; but nevertheless, all conditions in themselves—the labor of your hands, the sweat of your brow—are entirely cursed to you if you have no part in Jesus Christ. **Deuteronomy 28:16-18**: *Cursed shall you be in the city, and cursed shall you be in the field. Cursed shall be your basket and your kneading-trough. Cursed shall be the fruit of your body, and the fruit of your land: the increase of your cattle and the flocks of your small livestock. Cursed shall you be in your coming in, and cursed shall you be in your going out.* And so **Job 20:15**: *He has swallowed down riches, but shall vomit them up.* And in **Ecclesiastes 5:12**, Solomon says: *There is an evil which brings sickness, which I saw under the sun: riches kept by their owners to their own hurt.*

2. You are likewise cursed in your house. <margin>Job 18:13</margin> *The King of Terrors shall cast down her tent, his dwelling shall be scattered with sulfur.* Likewise in the previously mentioned place, **Deuteronomy 28:19**.

3. Cursed is he in his name. Solomon says, *The name of the wicked shall perish.*

4. He is cursed in his calling <note>original: "beroepinge"; one's daily work or vocation</note>. **Proverbs 21:4**: *The plowing of the wicked is sin.* And **Deuteronomy 28:20**: *The Lord shall send upon you the curse, the vexation, and the destruction in all that you set your hand to, whatever you shall do.*

5. He is cursed not only in his state, his house, his land, and his calling, but likewise in his eating and drinking. You

<column-break/>

have an excellent scripture passage <margin>Job 20:23</margin>: *While he is about to fill his belly, God shall send the heat of His wrath upon him, and rain it upon him on his food.* See also <margin>Psalm 38:30-31</margin> <note>Likely referring to Psalm 78:30-31 in standard English Bibles</note>.

Thus you see the positive part of man’s misery without Christ: what befalls him and what he has. We come now to the privative <term>privative: referring to the lack or absence of something, rather than the presence of an active punishment</term> part; what he lacks. And here is a wider field of misery in a man without Christ; but I will run over this briefly and encompass everything under these six things, and then come to the application.

First, you are without Christ, you are without strength. <margin>John 15:5</margin> *Without me you can do nothing,* says Christ. And the Apostle goes even further, saying in **2 Corinthians 3:5**: *Not that we are sufficient of ourselves to think anything as of ourselves: but our sufficiency is from God.* In this lies the misery of man: that he is not capable of doing anything. He is like Samson without his hair; he who before could break iron bands and strong ropes, then his strength was no more than another man's. Beloved, you are truly very weak if you lack Christ. In <margin>Isaiah 45</margin> it is said that Christ is the believers' Righteousness and strength. Now, if you lack Christ, then you lack the righteousness of acceptance and the strength of support. But to expand on this a bit more, I shall point out five things in which a man without Christ lacks strength.

1. Every man without Christ lacks strength to fulfill any duty. <margin>Romans 8:26</margin> *We do not know what we should pray for as we ought.* We are not capable of doing any spiritual good of ourselves; all our duties and services, without the added Righteousness of Christ, are just like many zeros <note>original: "ootjes"; referring to the letter 'o' used as a placeholder for zero</note>. Now you know, if you put a thousand zeros together, they do not make a number; but if a one or a two is placed before them, then they make a vast number. Even so, your duties by themselves are nothing at all; but when Christ is added to them, then they come into esteem and are made a considerable and glorious work.

2. You are without strength to exercise any grace. A dead man is as capable of moving himself as a man without Christ is capable of walking one step toward Heaven. If God should say, "I will save your soul and give you Heaven if you can only fulfill one duty or exercise any grace," you could not do it. And therefore Christ tells us in <margin>John 15</margin>: *Without me you can bring forth no fruit.*

3. Without Christ, you are without strength to subdue any lusts. Oh, how incapable you are to resist and subdue your reigning sins and lusts in your soul! In **Galatians 2:20**, Paul says: *I am crucified with Christ, and the life I now live in the flesh, I live by the faith of the Son of God.* The messenger of Satan who came to strike Paul would have triumphed over him if Christ had not helped him. You are not capable of subduing any lusts without Christ.

4. You are without strength to resist any temptations of the Devil. In **Ephesians 6:10**, Paul admonishes us *to be strong in the Lord, and in the strength of His power.* Not in the strength of their own power, for they were not capable of standing of themselves by their own strength; but be strong in the Lord, and in the strength of His...

his power; If David, when he went to fight against Goliath, had come in his own strength, he would have been conquered and cast down; but he went against him in the name and strength of the Lord of Hosts.

2. A person without Christ is without strength to endure any afflictions; every affliction is more than a feather <note>In 17th-century preaching, a "feather" represents the lightest possible burden; the author argues that without Christ, even the smallest trouble is too heavy to bear.</note> for those who are in Christ: therefore he can say with assurance, **Philippians 1:29**, *It is given to us by grace in the cause of Christ, not only to believe in him, but also to suffer for him.* Meaning to say: that without God we are not capable of keeping our Spirit up under any affliction.

And thus you see, if you lack Christ, that you lack strength in these five things: to perform any duty, to practice grace, to subdue lusts, to resist temptation, and to endure affliction. But 2. if you are without Christ, you are not only without strength, but likewise without wisdom. Jesus Christ is to the souls of men what the Sun with its rays is to the earth; take away the power and warmth of the Sun from the earth, and all the grass of the field and herbs shall immediately die and perish: likewise, Christ is our **Sun of Righteousness**, take him away from man, and no blossoms of <term>grace</term> <note>Divine favor or help given to humans for their regeneration or sanctification.</note> shall come forth from his heart: Adam’s Stock <note>original: "Adams Stamme"; referring to the fallen lineage of all humanity descending from Adam.</note> is a withered root, from which no branches of grace will come forth; You cannot bring forth any fruit to God as long as you are not taken away from Adam’s Stock and grafted onto the **Stem and root of Jesse** <note>A biblical reference to the lineage of King David, from which the Messiah was prophesied to emerge.</note>. A person during his unconverted state is a Slave to the Devil, who can never bear fruit unless he is in Christ; only in and through Christ are we capable of bringing fruit to God.

3. Without Christ you are likewise unregarded, even if you are the Son of a Nobleman and descended from Princes, so that you could count your lineage for thousands and tens of thousands of years, so to speak; nonetheless, without Christ you are *poor, miserable, blind, and naked*, **Revelation 3:17**. For it is Christ alone who makes Lineages wise and noble, and all treasures are bound up in him.

4. Without Christ, you are without comfort: This is a lamentable misery. This would be a comfortless dwelling where the sun would not shine by day, nor the Moon by night, and even more comfortless shall this be to the Soul if Christ does not rise in your heart: the comfort of a child of God is like the Ebb and Flow, as Christ comes down to him or goes from him.

5. Without Christ, you are without freedom: *If the Son has made you free, you are truly free,* **John 8:36**. And if the Son does not make you free, you are slaves to your lusts, slaves to the creatures, and slaves of the Devil, by whom you were captured according to his will: you are never free men and women until the Son makes you free.

6. If you are without Christ, you are without Salvation; you are like a dead body without life, or a body without a head; it is Christ alone who gives us happiness and glory, **Ezekiel 16:14**. *Therefore a name went out from you among the Heathen because of your beauty: for it was perfect through my glory, which I had laid upon you, saith the Lord God.* If we do not have the beauty of Christ upon us, we are not beautiful; you have

<column-break/>

an excellent passage, **Luke 2:32**, where Christ is called *the Glory of the Lord of Israel*. Christ is the Glory of the children of Israel who believe in him: There is no Glory, but a body full of sores and festering boils, in all those who are without Christ.

And so much for the Doctrine, Beloved, that a person in the unregenerate state is, in every part, [separated] from Christ. We come now to the **application**: and here I may say to you what an old Teacher was accustomed to say when he had handled some fearful matter; he always concluded it with this: *O godless people, this does not belong to you*; so I may say to you, O Godly Soul, this does not belong to you. The miserable and sad state of a person without Christ does not belong to you; you have not now heard the sentence that shall pass over you, but you have heard the misery from which you are free and delivered. Oh, I wish that what I make of this is for your strengthening.

1. Happy, thrice happy are you, that as soon as you were born, you have had faith in Jesus Christ, for before God you are clothed with great Majestic arrangement in him; nonetheless, He comes to look upon you under the conception of love, mercy, peace, goodness, tenderness, and gentleness; you look upon God not as a cruel judge to damn you, but as a merciful Father to comfort you; not as an adversary who stands against you in war, but as a friend counseling with you; not as a crushing stone to destroy you by his power, but as the **Rock of Salvation** in whose clefts you rest. You do not look upon God as a consuming fire, but as a goldsmith's fire, which purifies from sin and corruption: the heart of Christ alone extinguishes the fire of God’s Wrath. So that you may now look upon God under all these conceptions of love, mercy, peace, and reconciliation, etc., if you have a right to the Savior.

2. Happy, yes thrice happy you who have a part in Christ, for although you have nothing here in this world, nonetheless you have all things: you have all things if you have Christ, in whom everything is: you can say just as Paul said of himself, **2 Corinthians 6:10**, *As having nothing, and yet possessing all things.* Although you lack many things here below, nonetheless if you have a part in Christ, you have everything; it may be that you eat here the bread of affliction and drink from the waters of adversity, nonetheless you are happy, **Song of Solomon 5:1**: *Eat, friends, drink, and become drunk with love.* Blessed are you who are clothed with the long white robe of Christ’s Righteousness: although you have nothing here below, nonetheless you have all things if you have Christ, who has everything, **1 Corinthians 3:22**, *All is yours, if you are Christ’s.*

**Objection.** But here some shall object and say, how can this be, that the Believers have all things, while they nonetheless have the least of the things of this world?

**Answer.** A Believer may be said to have all things in these four ways:
1. He has all things equally.

# Miserable State in Nature.

3. All things / finally, and
4. All things hereditarily,

1. A Believer has all things equally, that is / in Christ he has the ground of all things / that which is worth more / than the entire world: a person is not to be considered a rich man / who has much clutter or household furniture in his house / but he who has many jewels in his cabinet <note>In the 17th century, a "cabinet" was a small, private room or a specialized piece of furniture used to store precious items and curiosities.</note>: Truly Jesus Christ is the **Pearl of great price**, a Jewel of all Jewels: if you have Christ / you have all things / you have more than if you had the entire World.

2. A Believer has all things on condition; if a thing is good for you in which you apply yourself / you shall have it / whatever it may be / <margin>Psalm 84:11</margin> <note>Original margin cites Psalm 84:12, following the numbering in older Dutch bibles.</note> *The Lord shall give grace and glory: he shall not withhold any good thing from those who walk in uprightness.* He has all things on condition.

3. A Believer has all things finally, that is / the Lord has intended that every Creature he has made / should be for his use / the Sun / Moon / Stars / and all other creatures are made for him / yes, all Angels in Heaven / are ministering Spirits for their salvation.

4. There are still some things regarding comfort / but I must postpone those until another occasion.

# A True Account of Man's...

...whether we live, we live to the Lord; and whether we die, we die to the Lord <note>original: "dat wy leven, wy leven den Heere; het zy dat wy sterven, wy sterven den Heere." A reference to Romans 14:8.</note>.

5. **Present things** are yours / which include present grace / or present afflictions / 1. *Present mercies* are yours / as you have a right to them / and behold the goodness of God in them / and praise God for the same / and as you serve God with them / and do good to others through them. 2. *Present afflictions* are likewise yours / to humble your hearts / and to wean you from the world / to stir up your desires for Heaven / to purge out your corruptions / and to exercise your grace / etc. In whatever present state you are / all things shall work together for your good <note>A paraphrase of Romans 8:28.</note>.

6. **Future things** are yours / if afflictions or temptations come / or want / or hunger / or plague / or anything similar / they are ordained by Christ for your good; and so / if any grace or blessing comes / it is yours / Heaven / life / glory / happiness / they are all yours.

Here then / *Beloved* / you see the first branch of a man’s happiness / who has a part in *Christ* / for in *Christ* he has all things / though he has nothing <note>Reference to 2 Corinthians 6:10: "as having nothing, and yet possessing all things."</note> / because he has Him who is all things.

**Secondly**, for the one who has a part in *Christ* / his second comfort lies in this / that everything which *Christ* has / is his: And oh, my *Beloved* / this is a **Gold-mine** / which shall deliver to you / many precious comforts / I shall give you only six.

1. If you have a part in Christ / Christ’s Father is your Father.
2. Christ’s Spirit is your Spirit.
3. Christ’s righteousness is your righteousness.
4. Christ’s graces are your graces.
5. Christ’s peace is your peace.
6. Christ’s sufferings are your sufferings.

O Beloved, see here what a great field / in which to walk.

1. If you have a right to *Christ* / his Father is your Father / *John 20:17* / *Christ* says / I ascend to my Father and your Father / to my God and your God. Christ’s Father is the Father of believers.

2. Christ’s Spirit is your Spirit / *John 14:16, 17* / *Christ* says / I will pray to the Father / and he shall give you another Comforter / that he may abide with you forever. Namely, the Spirit of truth / whom the world cannot receive, because it sees him not, but you know him, for he dwells with you, and shall be in you.

3. Christ’s Righteousness is your Righteousness / *Jeremiah 23:6*. This shall be his name / by which he shall be called: The Lord our Righteousness. So also *1 Corinthians 1:30* <note>The text likely refers to 1 Corinthians 1:30, though the theology is central to Reformed teaching.</note>. Christ is made unto us by God: Wisdom, righteousness, Sanctification, and Redemption.

4. Christ’s graces are your graces / *John 1:14*. Christ is full of grace and truth, why? so that out of his fullness we might receive grace for grace <note>original: "genade voor genade." This refers to the continuous flow of divine favor from Christ to the believer.</note>.

That in all grace / which is in Jesus Christ / we shall receive from him according to our proportion and capacity.

5. His peace is your peace / *John 14:27*. Peace I leave with you, says Christ, my peace I give to you. The peace that we enjoy is from Christ.

6. Lastly / Christ’s sufferings are your

<column-break/>

**sufferings** / God looks upon his suffering / as if you had suffered in your own person: the righteous has suffered for the unrighteous / to bring you to God; the suffering of Christ is so powerful for you before God / as if you had suffered in your own person on the cross / yes, much more / for our suffering could not accomplish that.

Thus, having a part in Christ / all that Christ has is yours.

**Thirdly**, take this for your comfort / that everything you have / is Christ’s; I shall include all this under these three things.

1. Your sins are Christ’s / to pardon and to satisfy for <note>term: satisfy <gloss>the theological concept of "satisfaction," where Christ pays the legal debt of sin owed to God's justice</gloss></note>.
2. Your sufferings are Christ’s / who sanctifies the same.
3. Your bodies and souls are Christ’s / to make them blessed.

1. You who have a part in Christ / your sins are his to be pardoned. *Isaiah 53:6*. The Lord has laid on him the iniquity of us all, the punishment that brought us peace was upon him, and by his stripes we are healed.

He bore the sins in his own body on the wood / and to this purpose the Apostle says expressly / *1 Corinthians 5:21* <note>The original manuscript cites 1 Cor. 5:21, but the verse quoted is actually 2 Corinthians 5:21.</note>. He was made [sin] for us, so that we might become the Righteousness of God in him. Christ was a sinner / yet a "made" sinner for us / he bore our sins upon him / and sins are Christ’s / to be pardoned.

2. Our suffering is Christ’s suffering / he suffers the same for us / *Acts 9*. Christ said: Saul, Saul, why do you persecute me? he looks upon the wrong done to his people / as if it happened to himself.

3. Your bodies and souls are Christ’s / to make them blessed; your members are members of Christ’s body / *1 Corinthians 6:15* / the Apostle says / Do you not know that your bodies are members of Christ? shall I then take the members of Christ / and make them members of a harlot? God forbid: The body is Christ’s / and your soul is Christ’s / *1 Corinthians 6:19, 20*. .... Glorify God then in your body, and in your spirit, which are God’s. Thus you see what a broad field of mercies you have / which are in Christ; you have all things equally / by condition, finally / and in inheritance: All the servants of Christ are yours / the whole world is yours / life and death are yours / present things are yours / whether present afflictions / or present graces / future things are yours / whether temptations / want or any other thing. Likewise eternal life and happiness are yours / all that Christ has is yours / Christ’s Father is your Father / and Christ’s Spirit is your Spirit / his Righteousness is your righteousness / his grace your grace / his peace your peace / and his suffering your sufferings—and all that is yours is Christ’s / your sins are Christ’s / which he pardons; your suffering he sanctifies / your bodies and souls are his / to make them blessed: I may add something more to this / all your duties and services are Jesus Christ’s / these he sweetens <note>original: "supvert," likely a variant or error for "zuivert" (purifies) or "zoetert" (sweetens).</note> with the fragrance of his grace / and makes them acceptable to God; this is why you read in the Revelation, that Christ adds his incense / to the prayers of his saints; and this is a very great comfort.

### The Wretched State of Nature.

...been / all crosses and oppressions are softened / and whatever adversity you might have here in this world; this I have already recounted to you before. What the wood was to the waters of Marah, Christ wishes to be to every smitten and sorrowful soul: the waters of Marah were so exceedingly bitter / that no one could drink them / Exodus 15. But when the wood was cast into them / they were sweet; truly, so it can be with your state in this world / full of bitterness and sadness like the waters of Marah, yet only cast the tree of life / the Lord Jesus Christ into these waters / He shall change the same / from bitter and troubled waters into waters of joy and consolation. Christ wishes to be to the soul / what the honey from the lion / was to Samson / sweet and pleasant, Judges 14. Oppressions may come upon you / like a fierce lion / yet Christ is like the honey in this lion / who sweetens all your sorrows / makes the same pleasant / and comforting for you. I may apply to this proposition / what a writer remarks concerning the waters of the sea / they are very salty in themselves / but when they run through the earth / then they lose their saltiness and become sweet: truly / although your state in this world / is full of sharp and heavy oppressions / nonetheless when the same run through Christ / He sweetens them all for you. Great is your consolation / if you have a part in Christ / for He is the one who sweetens all your sorrows: And beloved / mark this earnestly / although you feel sadness in your mind, how can you be comfortless / while you feel therein / the life of Jesus Christ in your soul: although you drink here the waters of oppression / and the wine of terror / nonetheless / how can you be without comfort / so long as you drink drops of Christ's blood? Although you have no house to lay down your head / nonetheless be comforted / that you have a house kept for you / not built with hands / but eternal in the Heavens: although you now have nothing but stones for your pillows / the night shall come / when you shall lay your head in the bosom of Jesus Christ.

**Fifthly.** All you who truly have a part in Christ / herein also lies your consolation / that in and through Christ / you may look upon God / (who in Himself is clothed with fear and terror) with great joy and consolation. Christ makes all the attributes of God / pleasant and comforting for you / so that although God is a consuming fire / and the soul without Christ would burn like stubble; nonetheless in Christ you look upon God as a fire / but between which two Christ is placed: Christ is like a shield <note>The Dutch "Schot" here refers to a partition or bulk-head, acting as a protective barrier.</note> between the fire of God's wrath and you / you look upon God not as an enemy who sets Himself against you / but as a reconciled friend; not only as a strict Judge / but as a merciful Father; you do not view God as clothed with terror / but with mercy and compassion. O beloved / you are at peace with God in Christ / you are in Christ / and Christ is in you / and God, who has a well-pleasing in His Son / must necessarily also have a well-pleasing in you: Great is your benefit if you have Christ; I may say in this case / what the Prophet Elisha said to King Jeroboam <note>original: "Jeroboam." This is likely a printer's error for Jehoram, as Elisha's encounter in 2 Kings 3:14 was with Jehoram of Israel and Jehoshaphat of Judah.</note>, 2 Kings 3:14. *As surely as the Lord of Hosts lives, if I did not regard the presence of Jehoshaphat the King of Judah,*

<column-break/>

*I would not look at you, nor see you.* Even so says God to us / were it not for the sake of my Son Jesus Christ / you would never see my face / nor have a good sight of me.

**Sixthly.** This is also comforting / that God the Father so truly accepts you in His Son / as if you had done in your own person / what Christ has done: this is a great benefit / that God accepts what Christ has done for us / as if we had done it ourselves. Ephesians 1:6. *He has made us accepted in the beloved.* That is / in Christ. God looks upon you in Christ / and accepts all your duties / as if they were performed by Christ Himself.

**Seventhly.** Are you now in Christ? Well, take this for your consolation / that wherever you may be / you shall one day be with Christ. This is the final consolation / and I shall give you an excellent text to prove this / although in the common translation / it is not so easily expressed / Romans 8:10. (says the Apostle) *If Christ is in you, the body is indeed dead because of sin: but the Spirit is life because of righteousness.* What is the meaning of this / *the body is dead because of sin*, the meaning is not / that the body kills the sin / but the body is dead because of sin; that is / sin shall bring your bodies into the grave / yet your Spirits shall live because of righteousness, that is / the righteousness of Jesus Christ / through the righteousness of Jesus Christ your souls shall always live in Glory with Christ / although your bodies die / and are brought into the grave through sin / nonetheless the killing of your bodies / shall only be a way to the quickening <note>The making-alive or resurrection.</note> of your souls; if you are here in Christ / you shall always live with Him in Glory hereafter / the death of your body shall only be a way to Glory / and therefore / why should death be terrifying / to you who are in Christ Jesus? For Death is but like her wedding-day / in which Christ and her soul unite together; If Christ is in you / your bodies shall die because of sin / but your Spirits shall live because of righteousness: you have another and clear passage which proves this / John 17:23, 24. *I in them, and Thou in me: that they may be made perfect in one: and that the world may know, that Thou hast sent me, and hast loved them, as Thou hast loved me. Father, I will that where I am, those also whom Thou hast given me may be with me: that they may behold my Glory, which Thou hast given me.* Some wish / that this prayer of Christ was only for His Apostles / so that they might be where Christ was in Heaven / but if you take note of the preceding words / you shall find / that it was for all believers / see verse 20 <note>The OCR says "V. 22," but verse 20 is where Jesus specifies He prays for all who will believe through the apostles' word.</note>. O great is your comfort if you have a part in Christ here / you shall one day reign with Him eternally in Glory.

### A True Account of Man's...

Christ softens all your oppressions and crosses for you; and when you have Christ, God the Father reveals Himself to you, not with terror and severity <note>The OCR reads "sweetshept," which is likely a transcription error for "strengheyt" (severity), a common antonym for grace in this period.</note>, but with goodness, love, and grace; and what Christ has done is credited to you as if you had done it in your own person. Being here in Christ, you shall live eternally with Christ hereafter: Oh, how all these graces and privileges ought to stir up those who have no part in Christ, never to give rest to their eyes or slumber to their eyelids until they have obtained a part in Him.

->Ephesians 2:12.<-

> That at that time you were without Christ, being aliens from the commonwealth of Israel, and strangers from the covenants of promise, having no hope, and without God in the world.

<margin>6th Sermon.</margin>
It may easily happen that some who have heard me this day may lie under a tranquility of spirit, claiming for themselves the blessedness of those who are in Christ, while they nonetheless have no part in Him. Therefore, I shall spend this hour giving you some **Marks** <note>Dutch: "Merk-tekenen" — evidentiary signs used in Puritan-style preaching to help believers verify their salvation.</note> by which you may know whether you actually have a part in Christ or not. This is the most necessary point on which I have often spoken to you, and may the Lord give you grace to take these marks to heart and to earnestly examine your own souls as to whether you have a part in Christ or not. But before I give you these marks, allow me to set forth these three or four cautions, which will better pave the way for the following point.

<margin>1st Caution.</margin>
1. Take this caution: that many people can strongly imagine they have a part in Christ when they do not. I shall give you a clear text for this, 2 Corinthians 10:7. *Do ye look on things after the outward appearance?* says the Apostle, *If any man trust to himself that he is Christ's, let him of himself think this again, that, as he is Christ's, even so are we Christ's.* This is a noteworthy passage; there were some among the Corinthians who strongly imagined they had a part in Christ and had a low opinion of the Apostles, although they did not belong to Christ; to such the Apostle spoke. So it was also with the Church of Laodicea, Revelation 3:17. *Thou sayest, I am rich, and increased with goods, and have need of nothing; and knowest not that thou art wretched, and miserable, and poor, and blind, and naked.*

<margin>2nd Caution.</margin>
2. I want you to take notice of this: that these marks of a person who is in Christ all need to be found in you if you are to have a part in Him; for if you find even one of them in you, truly and certainly, it is a firm proof that you have a right to Christ. I give this caution for a poor and dejected soul: if you have but one link of this **Golden Chain**, you have it as surely as if you had them all.

<margin>3rd Caution.</margin>
3. I set these Marks of one who is in Christ only *Affirmative* <note>original: "Affirmative" — meaning these are positive indicators.</note>, not *Nega-

<column-break/>

tive* <note>original: "Negative" — meaning the absence of a sign does not automatically prove one is damned.</note>, that is: all those who find these signs in themselves may firmly assure themselves that they have a part in Christ. But I do not say that those who do not find these signs in themselves have no right to Christ; for should I say that, I would strike down many humble souls. Oh no; only you can firmly assure yourself when you find these marks in you.

<margin>4th.</margin>
4. Finally, take this caution: that in recounting these Marks, I do not state them such that there must always be an exercise and feeling of them in your perception for you to have a part in Christ. No; but the same must dwell in you in truth, even though they do not show themselves in exercise and practice; this proves sufficiently that you have a part in Christ. For a poor soul may truly have many graces of God's Spirit in him, although he does not feel, exercise, or perceive them in himself, just as I have recounted to you it was with Mary Magdalene: she spoke with Christ face to face, and yet she said, *they have taken away my Lord, and I know not where they have laid him.* And so much for the cautions; now I shall proceed to the Marks, and these are eleven.

<margin>1.</margin>
1. The person who has a right to Christ is cast out of himself; that is, he casts out of himself all his own righteousness, good works, or merits. No one is in Christ unless he is outside of himself; the Apostle gives you this mark in Philippians chapter 3, verses 8 and 9. *Yea doubtless, and I count all things but loss for the excellency of the knowledge of Christ Jesus my Lord: for whom I have suffered the loss of all things, and do count them but dung, that I may win Christ, and be found in him, not having mine own righteousness.* Paul could not have Christ while holding onto his own righteousness—not in its existence, but in its accounting; not having his own righteousness so as to be justified by it; in that respect, he would not stand upon it. So also in 1 Corinthians 4:4, the Apostle says, *For I know nothing by myself* <note>original: "Ick ben my selven geens-dinghs bewust" — meaning he is not conscious of any unconfessed sin.</note>. Now someone might think, that man was a holy and eminent man, for he says, "I am conscious of nothing in myself," that is, I know no sin in my soul that I have knowingly or willingly committed. But mark the following words: *yet am I not hereby justified*; he renounced all those good works he had often done. Every person in Christ is outside of himself; he sees his own impotence and Christ's power; he sees his emptiness of grace and Christ's fullness; he sees himself to be nothing, and Christ to be all in all. In Luke 16:15, Christ says to the Pharisees, *Ye are they which justify yourselves before men; but God knoweth your hearts.* As if He had said: you think much of yourselves and your graces, but God knows your hearts, that you are not such as you appear to be. And therefore, Beloved, mark this diligently: if God has wrought His grace in your nakedness, ugliness, and lack of Christ—Oh, when such a work of grace is wrought in you, then you may certainly know that you have a part and portion in Jesus Christ.

<margin>2.</margin>
2. A person in Christ makes it a matter of conscience to keep every known commandment of Christ;
