# Miserable state in nature.

<columns>
<margin>Keeping</margin>
This you have / 1 John 2:5. Whoever keeps His Word, in him truly the love of God is perfected: by this we know that we are in Him. By this we know that we are in Christ, if we keep the commands of Christ; but go into your own heart and seek to have authority over your conscience, to bring yourself under subjection; although you have many weaknesses and failings, nonetheless this is an infallible sign <note>Dutch: "kenteken" — a term used in Reformed theology to describe evidence of one's election or salvation.</note> that you are in Christ: 1 John 4:24. That which you have heard from the beginning, let that remain in you. If that which you have heard from the beginning remains in you, so shall you also remain in the Father and in the Son. You who keep Christ’s commands have a part in Him, and He is in you: and therefore Beloved, all you who make it a matter of conscience to keep His commands and to fulfill the Will of God, who have no known sin but labor to root it out, or known grace and strive to practice it, or known duty and seek to obey it—if it stands so with you, you may comfort yourself in this, that you have an actual interest in Christ.

<margin>
3rd Mark.
Marks
of a
part in
Christ.
</margin>
3. A person in Christ has power from Christ to bring under subjection and to kill his inward lusts of the flesh, Gal. 5:24. Those who are Christ's have crucified the flesh with its passions and desires. When Christ came in the flesh among us, we crucified Him; but if Christ rises up in the heart, He will crucify that heart. The crucifying of the flesh with its passions, of which the Apostle speaks here, is not a [total] killing and total eradication of sins, but giving a death-blow to them, so that sin no longer reigns in us. If you are in Christ, sin shall be like the beasts spoken of in Daniel <note>A reference to Daniel 7:12, where the beasts' dominion was taken away, though their lives were prolonged for a season.</note>, whose lives remained for a short time. So, the dominion of sin shall be taken away; it shall no longer reign in you, yet its life and remnants shall still be for a short time. Sin shall become weaker and weaker, like those of the house of Saul, while the house of David becomes stronger and stronger, 2 Sam. 3:1. So likewise, if Christ dwells in the heart, sin shall become weaker and weaker every day, and the grace in you shall grow stronger and stronger. And therefore Beloved, all you whose hearts have this testimony—that you have the power of killing grace <note>Refers to "mortifying grace," the spiritual strength given to "kill" or subdue sinful impulses.</note> in your soul to make your lusts retreat, to bring your beloved sins under subjection, and to compel the pride of the heart—you shall then undoubtedly have fellowship with Jesus Christ.

<margin>4th Mark.</margin>
4. The person who has an interest in Christ keeps a strong watch over his own heart, so as not to sin willfully and knowingly to the dishonor of God: A person in Christ has a careful eye over himself, so as not to commit any sin to the dishonor of Jesus Christ. 1 John 5:18. We know that whoever is born of God does not sin; but he who is born of God keeps himself, and the evil one does not touch him. He who is born of God keeps himself, not from all sins, but as much as is in him, he resists every sin and temptation; he keeps himself from every known sin, 1 John 3:6. Whoever remains in Him does not sin: This is not said absolutely, but by comparison; he does not sin in comparison to those great sins that the godless commit, for they are slaves to their lusts: and

<margin>Mark.</margin>

<column-break/>

secondly, he does not sin, that is, with deliberation <term>deliberation: intentional, premeditated planning of an act</term>, or with a delightful pleasure, nor with a total persistence or final impenitence: in this regard, a person in Christ does not sin. And now Beloved, whose hearts and consciences infallibly testify that they keep watch over their own souls, and that you seek [not] to commit even a small sin against God by which He is dishonored; if it is so with you, you can infallibly assure yourself of your part in Christ: The person who keeps sin out of his heart may firmly assure himself that he has Christ in his heart.

<margin>5th Mark.</margin>
5. A person who is in Christ—in this person Christ has wrought an actual change, both in his life and nature; if you are in Christ, He will be in you to work an actual and powerful change, both in your heart and life, as the Apostle says in 2 Cor. 5:17. If anyone is in Christ, he is a new creature, the old has passed away, behold, all has become new. And Beloved, take this text, lay it upon your hearts; has God made you new creatures, and wrought a blessed change in your heart? Can you assure your soul that after your first birth you have been born again? If this is so, you can firmly assure yourself of fellowship in Christ; if anyone is in Christ, he is a new creature.

<margin>6th Mark.</margin>
6. The person who is in Christ grows up in Christ, to be fruitful in every good work: It is for this reason that you often read in the Scripture of growing in Christ, and increasing in Christ, with the increase of God. Christ is the Root of Jesse <note>A messianic title referring to the father of King David; here it implies Christ is the source of all spiritual life.</note>, in whom everyone who is engrafted in Christ brings forth fruits of righteousness, to the praise and glory of God. John 15:5. I am the Vine, and you are the branches: he who remains in me and I in him, he bears much fruit: for without me you can do nothing. Now Beloved, go into your own souls and see if you increase in grace, knowledge, understanding, sanctification, humility, and the killing of lusts; it is a firm argument that you are planted in the Root of Jesse, which makes you bring forth fruits unto God.

<margin>7th Mark.</margin>
7. The person who has a right to Christ is most humble, and despised in his own eyes. Of all people in the world, there is no one so humbled in his own self as he who has a right to Christ; mark Paul’s description of a man in Christ, 2 Cor. 12:2. I know a man in Christ, he says, fourteen years ago (whether it happened in the body, I do not know, or out of the body, I do not know, God knows) that such a one was caught up into the third heaven... of such a one I will boast: yet of myself I will not boast, except in my weaknesses. Paul, speaking here of himself, did not want to boast of what he had or who he was, or what glory he had seen, so that people would not think more of him than he was. This is a sign of a person in Christ, that he is humble in his own eyes. Those vessels that are full make the least sound, and empty ones clank the most: so also, those Christians who are full of grace are humblest and make the least noise; whereas people without Christ, empty of all grace and goodness, rattle the most: small rivers make the greatest noise, while the deep waters

# A true account of man's...

...flow silently. So also the empty brains, which know little or nothing, make the greatest bravado; but those who know more and are more deeply learned, go quietly along. It is truly noteworthy what one observes concerning the Prophet Ezekiel, a man who had many visions and revelations, full of wonderful gifts and grace, yet the Holy Spirit calls him ninety-three times by the name of the **Son of Man**, which was (says that Teacher) to keep him humble and to let no haughtiness find a home in his heart, so as to show that where Christ is most present with His grace in the heart, there the person is most humble and lowly in his own eyes.

<margin>8. Mark.</margin>
8. A person in Christ makes it a matter of conscience to walk worthily of his right to Christ: Colossians 2:6. *As you have therefore received Christ Jesus the Lord, so walk in Him.* That is, just as you began to live in Christ, so continue, holily and purely, as you received Him: go forward in Him every day, and walk before Him honorably: 1 John 2:6. *He who says he abides in Him ought himself also so to walk, even as He walked.* For this reason you find in the Scripture that to be in Christ and to live a godly life are joined together, 2 Timothy 3:12. *All who desire to live godly in Christ Jesus.* The person whose **Person** is in Christ will also labor that his **works** are in Christ; many want their person to be in Christ, but not their life. But those whose person and life are both in Christ have a comforting fellowship with Him. The difference between a person in Christ and one outside Him, I shall show you through this common example: You know a person who knows through experience what it takes to make a place clean; he is careful on all occasions not to defile it again, because he knows what trouble and labor the cleaning cost; but a block of wood <note>original: "houdt", likely referring to a piece of timber or an unfeeling, inanimate object</note>, or if dogs come in, they take no care to keep it clean, because they do not know what it is to make something clean. So too a godly person: he walks worthily of his calling in Christ, since he knows how much it costs him, how many tears, sighs, and prayers precede his portion in Christ and the assurance of His love; but a godless person makes no conscience of sinning against Christ and displeasing Him, since he does not know what it is to obtain a portion in Him. In Galatians 3:27, the Apostle says, *For as many of you as were baptized into Christ have put on Christ.* A certain Teacher has a very good explanation of this text; he says that the Apostle here speaks and makes an **allusion** <note>a literary or historical reference</note> to the old custom among the heathens who, when they made profession of their faith, laid aside their old clothes and put on new white ones, to symbolize that if anyone is in Christ, he must lay aside his old ways and conduct, and henceforth labor to live holily and uprightly in all godliness before God. So, Beloved, if you have a part in Christ and have put Him on, walk worthily of Him in a holy and spotless **Conversation** <note>in this period, "conversation" meant one's entire way of life, conduct, and social interactions</note>.

<margin>9. Mark.</margin>
9. A person who has a part in Christ values Him so highly that he would not be without Him for the whole world; he looks upon Him more than upon the chief good in the world,

<column-break/>

he knows the word of Christ and values Him as an invaluable treasure, 1 Peter 2:7. The Apostle, after he had told them that they were built upon a precious **Cornerstone**, concludes: *To you who believe He is precious*; indicating that everyone who is built and grounded on Christ finds Christ precious to his soul. And therefore my Beloved, you who have a certain testimony in your own conscience that you hold Christ in high esteem and value, above all things in the world, counting all things but loss and dung <note>original: "schade en drek", a direct reference to the Apostle Paul's words in Philippians 3:8</note> in comparison to a part in Christ—this is an infallible sign that you have a right to Him. It was an excellent saying of one concerning his part in Christ, saying: "If all the stones in my house were diamonds, and all the dust of the same were scrapings of gold, and all common stones were pearls of the East, yet I would not value these in comparison to my part in Christ."

<margin>10.</margin>
10. He who has a part in Christ has the Spirit of Christ dwelling in his soul, 1 John 4:13. *By this we know that we abide in Him, and He in us, because He has given us of His Spirit.* He pours out His Spirit through the **golden conduit-pipes** <note>a metaphor for the "means of grace," such as the Bible, preaching, and sacraments, through which God's grace was thought to flow</note> of His ordinances into your heart. This is a certain sign that you are in Christ, if you have the Spirit of Christ dwelling in you in these three workings: 1. If you have the **Enlightenment** of the Spirit, enlightening your mind in the knowledge of Christ; 2. If you have the **Inclination** of the Spirit, to incline your hearts to the love of Christ; and 3. If you have the **powerful working** of the Spirit, to draw your will to the obedience of Christ. If you enjoy the Spirit of God in these three workings, then you may certainly know that you have a part in Christ.

<margin>11.</margin>
11. He who has a part in Christ labors by all possible means to bring others to the knowledge of Christ. Paul, before he was in Christ, labored to pull people away from Christ, but afterwards, after his conversion, he labored more than all the other Apostles to bring people to Christ. O Beloved, you who have compassion for poor souls in their natural state, and can heartily wish that all people were in Christ as well as yourself; you who bewail the miserable state of your friends and neighbors, can firmly assure yourself of your part in Christ.

And thus I have shown you the signs of a person in Christ; if you are out of yourself regarding your **justification** <note>the theological state of being declared righteous before God</note>; if you make it a matter of conscience to keep all the commands of Christ, and have received power from Him to bring your lusts under subjection; if you guard against all sins that dishonor Christ, and more besides, as we have recounted before: if you find any of these truly and sincerely in your heart, it is a firm proof that you have a portion in Christ. Now, I shall speak only a word or two for the examination of those who are **without Christ**, and show their sorrowful state in which they remain, to stir them up to strive for fellowship and a portion in Christ.

<margin>1.</margin>
1. Are you without Christ? Likely you are without satisfaction and contentment in all things that you enjoy in this world; for Solomon's saying is true for you, that

# The miserable state in nature.

...your eye shall not be satisfied with seeing, nor your ears with hearing. Without Christ, nothing can give satisfaction to the desires of an immortal soul: the World is round, and your heart is triangular <note>Original: "driekantigh." This was a common seventeenth-century theological metaphor: a round world cannot fill the three corners of a human heart, which was thought to be shaped for the Trinity.</note>, and you know that a round thing cannot fill a triangular space; so it is also impossible that the World, or anything in it, can satisfy the desires of your heart.

<margin>Mark.</margin>
2. Furthermore, you cannot be received by God; God will say to you as Joseph said to his brothers: *If you do not bring your brother Benjamin with you, you shall not see my face.* **Genesis 43:5.** Even so will God say to you: if you do not bring Jesus Christ, your eldest Brother, with you, you shall not see my face. Here is the misery of a person without Christ: that he cannot be received by God.

<margin>Mark.</margin>
3. Without a share in Christ, you can have no Salvation; for Christ has earned Salvation for all those who are in Him, and for no others; **John 17:12.** *Those whom you gave me, I have kept, and none of them is lost.* If you are without Christ, your state is like that of the first World before the Deluge <note>The Great Flood of Noah.</note>; all who were in the Ark were saved, but all those who were outside drowned. So Jesus Christ is the Ark of your preservation and Salvation, but all who are without Christ shall be drowned in a River of sulfurous water <note>Original: "Sulpher-water," referring to the lake of fire/brimstone.</note> and be damned forever. If you are without Christ, you are without satisfaction from created things, without God's acceptance, and without Christ’s Salvation.

And thus I have shown you in these six Sermons the happiness of a person in Christ, the identifying marks of a person in Christ, and the misery of a person without Christ; and so we have handled the first part of the Misery of man in nature, and the first branch of our Text: *That at that time you were without Christ.*

---

->Ephesians 2:12<-

> That at that time you were without Christ, alienated from the commonwealth of Israel, and strangers from the covenants of promise, having no hope, and without God in the world.

<columns>2</columns>

<margin>7th Sermon.</margin>
**H**aving handled the first part, I come to the second part of man’s miserable state, in these words: **Alienated from the commonwealth of Israel.** But first I must say something regarding the order of these words: why being *without Christ* stands here in the first place. I answer: because having Christ is the foundation and the groundwork of all happiness and blessings. If your share in Christ is lacking, you do not have the Spring-head or Fountain which can wash away all miseries and sorrows from the Children of Men. And for this reason, this is placed first; for if you are without Christ, you must necessarily be alienated from the commonwealth of Israel, and from the covenants of promise,

<column-break/>

without hope, and without God in this world.

But then again, why does *alienated from the commonwealth of Israel* stand here in the second place? Answer: Because he who is without Christ, the Head, must necessarily be without the Church, the body; for by the **commonwealth of Israel** <term>commonwealth: "Burgers-chap," referring to the community, citizenship, and legal rights of God's people.</term> is understood the entire body of the church. They were alienated from the commonwealth of Israel; that is, this was the misery of the Ephesians while they were in the state of Heathendom, not converted to Faith in Christ through the Gospel; they had no share in the benefits and privileges that the People of God enjoyed. Whatever was in the church of Israel, they had none of those spiritual and special privileges and blessings which God poured out over all those who were in covenant with Him. They were alienated from the commonwealth of Israel; that is, they were alienated from the Ordinances of God which were in use in the Jewish church; they were without all the ordinances of Jesus Christ. All the Privileges of God's People were lacking to the Heathens as long as they were without Christ. Here you see then the full Sorrow of those people in the state of Heathendom: they were alienated from the commonwealth of Israel, and deprived of that precious Worship which He had established and commanded in His church, and of all the Privileges and rights which the People of God enjoyed.

In these words, two parts are to be noted: 1. A description of the church of God, expressed as a commonwealth; the church of God is called the commonwealth of Israel. 2. Here is recounted the alienation of the Ephesians from the church, from this commonwealth, before their conversion.

<columns>1</columns>

Now, Beloved, from this I shall note only two Lessons with which I shall end this Sermon.

1. **Lesson:** That the Church of God is a Spiritual Commonwealth.
2. **Lesson:** That it is a great part of man’s Misery to be a stranger to the true Church of God.

Regarding the first Lesson: That the Church of God is <margin>Lesson.</margin> a Spiritual Commonwealth. In the handling of this, I shall do these two things: 1. I shall show in what ways the Church may be compared to a commonwealth. And 2. In what ways it differs from the same.

First, the Church may be compared to a commonwealth in these four things.

1. In a commonwealth, there are People of various Ranks and states, differing in qualities; they are not all Princes, nor Rulers, nor rich; they are of different qualities; some are rich, some poor, some high, some low, some Masters, some servants, and the like. Now, in this respect, the church may be compared to a commonwealth, for in the church of God some are high, some low, some rich, some poor; some people grow up to a full measure in Christ, others are but novices and children in Christ; some are strong in grace, like Trees, others weak as a broken Reed. As in a commonwealth, so also in the Church of God: there are people of various steps, callings, qualities, and conditions. **1 Corinthians 12:8, 9, 10.** There are...

# A True Account of Man’s
<note>This heading continues from the title of the previous section, likely "A true account of man's miserable state."</note>

...various gifts / for to one is given by the Spirit the word of Wisdom, and to another the word of knowledge, through the same Spirit: and to another faith, and to another the gifts of healing; and to another the working of miracles: and to another Prophecy: and to another the discerning of Spirits: and to another the interpretation of tongues: yet all these things are worked by one and the same Spirit, distributing to each one individually as he wills. Just as it is in a natural body / so it is also in a Spiritual body / that body would be a monstrous body / if the torso were as large as the arm / and the arm as large as the body / and every part as large as the whole; even so it is in the church / it is her Glory / for each to have a different condition.

2. In a **Commonwealth** / although there is a great multitude of People / nevertheless they are all governed by one and the same Laws / and are all subject to one and the same rulers; and so it is in the church of God / although there are many People in it / nevertheless they are all subject to one and the same Laws / and must all walk according to one and the same Rule: and in this respect she may be compared to a **Commonwealth** / for there is but one Rule / the word of God / which belongs to the entire church.

3. In a **Commonwealth** it is the highest crime / to cast away any law / by which the Commonwealth is governed; for if it were not so / the laws of a Civil government would be of no force / if anyone might break / reject, or keep them according to their own pleasure; and therefore a Civil government considers the violation of its laws / as the greatest wrong / and the highest crime that can be committed against it: And so it is in the church / with the word of God / if anyone adds to or takes away from it a jot or tittle / God will blot out his name from the Book of Life, <margin>Revelation Chapter 22. v. 19.</margin>

4. They may be compared with one another in this respect / for one **Commonwealth** differs from another / they do not both have the same Judges; nor the same laws / nor the same customs / but they differ in many things: so also the church of God is distinguished from other parts / and peoples of the World. Civil governments differ from one another in four things. 1. In laws. 2. Clothes / 3. Languages. 4. Government; and so it is also with the church of God.

1. They differ from one another in laws; the law governs a **Commonwealth** / but only the word of God governs in the church.

2. **Commonwealths** differ from one another / in respect of their clothes; and in this the church of God is different from the whole world; she is like a *new man* / while the whole world is draped in old rags and tatters / the church is clothed with a long Robe of Christ's Righteousness / which covers all her nakedness / which the world is without.

3. One **Commonwealth** differs from another in its languages; so the church of God is different in language from the entire World: the church of God speaks the pure language of Canaan <note>original: "tale Kanaans." A biblical metaphor referring to the holy speech and dialect of the godly, derived from Isaiah 19:18.</note>, but all the World outside / speaks a broken and corrupt language.

4. The church of God is different from all

<column-break/>

others / in respect of her government; all kingdoms and commonwealths have men who govern them / but the church of God / has Christ as her Governor.

Thus I have shown you / in what ways the church and a commonwealth are alike; now I come to show you / in what ways they differ.

1. They are different in their laws; a Civil government has laws / Acts / and Ordinances to govern them / but the church has only the word of God to be her Rule.

2. There is a distinction between the extent of these laws: the law of a Civil government applies only to the outward man / and cannot govern the inward. And therefore we commonly say / *our thoughts are free* / God alone can search the heart and test the mind; but the law of the church extends to the innermost Treasury of the Soul and the Spirit / to every thought and imagination of the heart / as the Apostle says: *The Law is spiritual, but I am carnal,* <margin>Romans 7:14.</margin>

3. There is a distinction / in respect of the power and operation of these laws / the law of a **Commonwealth** / binds the outward man / if he does wrong. But the Law of God in the church binds not only in practice / but changes the heart / and all other motivations / and makes you a *new man*.

4. They differ in this respect; a **Commonwealth** may change its laws at will / if they see occasion that some of them might be harmful to the kingdom / they make another / take the first away / and give another in its place / but the church of God cannot do this; the law that the church has now / she must have until the end of the world; God Himself has given the law to His church / and He can give no other / that surpasses the first. Furthermore / the rulers of a commonwealth are but men / and cannot see the most secret things / and therefore they are ignorant / of whether this or that Law is good or not / therefore they change them according to their pleasure / when they see it is necessary; But the Rule of the word of God / is an unchangeable and perfect Rule / which all must follow in practice until the end of the World.

5. They differ in their punishment / the punishment of a Civil government is outward / extending to the Confiscation of goods / banishment / imprisonment / or death; but the punishment of the church extends only to exclusion / and separation from her company and no more: the church of God can exercise no other punishment than excommunication / and therefore / the punishment over her people is not warring <note>meaning "not through physical force or weapons"</note> / but only according to the Rule of God's word; and therefore / those who cry out against church Government / as being Tyrannical / are greatly mistaken / for the punishment of the church of God is not physical / but spiritual. Yet although the church of God may not punish any man / who offends her / she may nevertheless exclude the same from her communion / and keep them under that exclusion as a punishment.

Thus you see then / both / in what the church and a commonwealth are alike / and in what they differ from one another: and if it is so / that the church of God is a Spiritual **Commonwealth** / then I may draw and set these three conclusions from this for you.

# The Miserable State of Man in Nature.

1. See here the necessity of government in the church; have you ever seen a **Commonwealth** stand firm and flourish / without rules / laws, and ordinances? Order is the stay <note>Original: "stai" (support/pillar).</note> of a civil government / if every person might do what he wanted / and what was right in his own eyes / nothing but ruin and dispersion would follow / as the scripture states <margin>Psalm 11:3.</margin> in Psalm 11:3. Surely the foundations are cast down: what has the righteous man done? If the laws and foundations of a civil government are overthrown / nothing follows but dispersion. If the church is a **Spiritual Commonwealth** / then there is an absolute necessity for its government: and therefore those who wish to rob the church of her government / wanting to have nothing / or a wicked government / these strike at the right of the church. Government in a **Commonwealth** is like the hedge around a vineyard: now suppose you had a very precious vineyard / provided with many beautiful and costly flowers / and someone came to you and said; my Lord / I see many beautiful flowers growing in your garden / but your hedge does not grow / therefore pay no mind to it / they shall not grow there for long; you would say to such a person / it matters little whether the hedge grows / it serves only for the protection of the flowers / which grow in the garden / so that they are not harmed by the wild beasts: So also / although government in the church does not make us holy / and a person can come to heaven without government / nevertheless it is very necessary / to preserve the church of God.

2. I may here note regarding the churches / being a **Spiritual Commonwealth** / the necessity of the unity of the church. Civil governments are preserved by concord <note>Original: "Een-dracht" (unity/concord).</note>: you know what the four-year strife has brought upon our Kingdom / it has almost entirely dispersed / the flower of our **Commonwealth**: Unities are the bonds and cords of a civil government; if one is divided / the **Commonwealth** cannot stand; a kingdom that is divided against itself, cannot <margin>Matt. 12:25.</margin> stand, Matthew 12:25. And the church of God / being a **Spiritual Commonwealth** / proves the necessity of the unity of the church / and the great danger of division; the church of God cannot stand without unity. And I say to you (spoken with the sadness of our hearts) there has never been less unity in the church of God / since the first planting by the Apostles / in the primitive times / than in these our days / in which every man is against another; and truly I see this as a coming misfortune / that God wishes to bring upon us through this / the saddest persecutions / that anyone has ever beheld with their eyes. I have read in the **Book of Martyrs** <note>Referring to John Foxe's "Acts and Monuments," a famous history of Christian martyrs.</note> / that before the eighth persecution / there was a great strife and disagreement among the Christians: I wish / Beloved, that it might not be so among us / many of this great multitude cry out against the Ministers of the Gospel / as if they were the causes of strife among you: but I want you to know / that those / who preach against division / are not the causes of schisms / as the Apostle says: see that there be no schism and discord among you. The people who cause divisions / bringing sects and schisms into a land / are the disturbers of the

<column-break/>

people; The Prop of Unity, and the Staff of Salvation <note>An allusion to Zechariah 11:7, where the shepherd takes two staves: "Beauty" and "Bands" (or Unity).</note>, when the one is broken / the other is also broken. I have read a story / of a man who had four children / and lying on his deathbed / he summoned them before him / and gave them a bundle of rods to break; his children did not know what this meant / but they could not break them while they were tied together; but after that he gave the youngest the same rods loosened / who broke them easily; and when he had broken them / he said: now my children / I do this to teach you / that if you unite together / you shall no more be broken than this bundle / no one can damage you or do you any harm / but if you are divided in discord / one against the other / you shall easily be broken: Truly / if the members of the church of God are united together / together sharing in the public ordinances / in hearing / prayer / or in any other duties / being united with one another / we need not fear the power of anyone who might be able to harm us.

3. If the church is a **Spiritual Commonwealth** / then we must necessarily strive to promote the right and the good of that **Commonwealth**. Nature labors to promote the good of the civil government / so we must also strive to stand for the good / of the body of the church / and seek to promote its interests.

<margin>Read.</margin> Thus much of the first Doctrine / we come now 2. to the second / **That it is a great misery, to be strangers to the true church of God.** You can be in the true church / and yet not be of the true church <note>A classic theological distinction between the "Visible Church" (all who profess faith) and the "Invisible Church" (the truly elect).</note>; like evil humors in a person's body / they are in the body / though not part of the body; so you can be in the church / and be of the visible church / and enjoy the outward ordinances / and yet not be members of the invisible church / of the church of the firstborn / and shall not share in the special and spiritual privileges of the church of God. 1. The godless are strangers to the effectual calling of the <margin>1 Pet. 2.</margin> church, 1 Peter 2. You are (says the Apostle) called with a holy calling, which the godless do not have. 2. They are estranged from the comforts / which the people of God enjoy. 3. You are strangers to the Christian communion in the church / a godless person does not know of those spiritual comforts / which the people of God enjoy.

Now / if this is so / that the godless are strangers to the church of God / and its spiritual benefits and privileges / which she has through Christ / then I shall only by way of application set forth these two exhortations.

# A True Account of Man’s Condition

*Christ* and Salvation are as well known in *England* as anywhere else; I do not want you to think that the true church is not in *England* / by no means / she is the church of *Jesus Christ* / but I say only / that you can be born and raised in this church / have a share in all her ordinances / and outward privileges / and yet never come to Heaven: for (as the Apostle says) they are not all *Israel*, who are of *Israel*. <note>Original: "zy en zijn niet alle Israel, die uit Israel zyn."    2. Thus much for the second part / of man’s misery in nature. That at that time you were without *Christ*, alienated from the Commonwealth of *Israel*.

We come now in order to the third part. "And strangers to the covenants of the promise." But before I establish any Teachings from these words / I shall resolve five questions / necessary to be answered here.
   1. What distinction is there between the Covenants and the promises? For many take them both for one and the same thing.
   2. What is understood by the Covenants of the promise.
   3. Why they are called the Covenants of the promise.

<margin>1. Question.</margin>
1. Question, What distinction is there between a Covenant, and a Promise?
<margin>Answer.</margin>
Answer. You may know / that although every covenant is a promise / nevertheless every promise is not a covenant: a covenant contains more than a promise / for in a covenant / many promises are joined together / all the promises of the 

<column-break/>

Gospel <term>Gospel: the "Good News" of salvation through Jesus Christ</term> are tied together in a little bundle / so that you see the distinction here / between a covenant and a promise.
   2. Question, What is understood by a Covenant of the promise?
   Answer. This is that free and gracious promise / which God made with *Adam* after the Fall / with the Patriarchs <term>Patriarchs: the early biblical fathers, specifically Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob</term> *Abraham*, *Isaac*, and *Jacob*, and all the Believers / by which he promised them Salvation / and eternal life through *Christ* / who was to come; this is the covenant of the promise / even that promise which God made to his children before the coming of *Christ* / in which he promises to give them Life and Salvation through *Christ* / who was promised to come.
   3. Why is it said the Covenants of the promise?
   Answer. Because *Christ*, the substance of that covenant, had not yet actually come / but it was only promised that he would come: this is the reason for it.
   4. Question. Why is it named in the plural number / the covenants of the promise / seeing as there was but one covenant of grace / the covenant of works having been made with *Adam* before the fall / and the covenant of grace after the fall?
   Answer. The covenants of the promise / not because there are more covenants / but because there are many administrations of that same covenant; the covenant is the same / now / as it was in the beginning / but it is only differently administered / laid out, and explained; Sometimes it is called a new covenant, that is / new in respect to the delivery and handing over of the same. You have a similar way of speaking regarding love / See, a new commandment I give you, that you love one another. It was called new / because it was newly given to the people.
   The covenant of grace, the content of which is / that we shall live and be saved / through the blood of *Christ*: it is called a covenant / because it was so often renewed in its administration; first / it was made with *Adam* after his fall: The seed of the Woman shall bruise the serpent's head, *Gen. 3. 15.* And it was renewed with *Abraham*, as *Paul* explains in *Heb. 3.* And after him with *Isaac*, and then with *Jacob*, and *David*, and *Solomon*, and all the Believers; yet this covenant was in substance the same / though often renewed / and so it has lasted until this day / and thus you have short answers to these four questions.
   5. Question. What is it to be strangers to the covenants of the promise?
   Answer. If you consider it at its core / you shall find / that it is nothing other / than the ultimate misery of an unconverted person; to be strangers to the covenants of the promise, is to be in such a sad / pitiful, and lamentable state / that none of all the promises of God / of grace / life, and Salvation through *Christ* belong to him: and is this not a miserable and sorrowful condition / that God looks upon man in an unregenerate state / as unfit for any grace / life, or salvation through *Christ*? A covenant (as I have told you /) is a little bundle of promises / containing all the promises of grace / of life / and of salvation: now if you are without the covenant / you must necessarily be excluded from all those promises made through *Christ*.

3. God the Father accepts the obedience and the suffering of *Christ* / as if we had accomplished it in our own person; and herein lies the blessedness of a person under the covenant of grace.

4. The covenant of works was established by God / with Adam, without a mediator: there was no third Person between God and Adam, but the covenant of grace is made by God with us / in the Mediator *Jesus Christus*. You may understand it thus / suppose two people were in strife and difference / one with the other / and a third friend of both / undertakes to settle that dispute: first going to the one / and seeing him reconciled / goes to the other / praying that he be satisfied with the first / until he has united them both: so it is here / *Christ* is a friend / of both God and men / he is the Son of God / and the Father of his church / and being the Mediator of the new covenant / he comes first to his Father / and says: Father I know / that all men have broken that first covenant / made with you / and thereby rightfully lie under your wrath and punishment / because of the breaking of the same / and I know that they displease you; yet I pray you O Father / be satisfied / and reconciled with your people / give them satisfaction while they live here / and give them Heaven and blessedness when they die; then *Christ* comes to the Believers and says to them: people / I have promoted your peace / brought about reconciliation and satisfaction / for your natures here / and Heaven when you die / and therefore lift up your heads in joy: *Christ* went first to his Father / and reconciled him / and then he came to us / and this gives us a great comfort.

5. Adam under the Covenant of works / he had nothing but works by which he could be saved / he had to keep the covenant of works / solely through his own strength, he

<column-break/>

had no strength but his own / to fulfill any duty / he had no ground or foundation but himself / to stand upon; but under the Covenant of grace / we are preserved by the mighty hand of God, through faith unto Salvation. We are in a much better state in the covenant of grace / than Adam was in the state of innocence; for although he was perfectly holy / nevertheless he was not unchangeably holy / but now the foundation of God stands sure / we are preserved by the mighty hand of God unto salvation.

6. The covenant of works / if anyone broke the same / there was no <term>repentance</term> <note>original: "bekeeringe"; turning back to God.</note> for it; even if Adam and Eve had cried their eyes out / or prayed their hearts out / it would have done them no good. Repentance did not go with the covenant of works; just as it is in Civil Law / if a man has committed homicide / that law admits no repentance / or sorrow / because he has done such a thing / it only takes notice of the deed / repentance or not / he must die; but in the covenant of grace it goes in a completely different way / although you have done the deed / and broken God's commands / nevertheless if you repent / and have sorrow over those sins / committed against God / the Lord will pardon and forgive you the same / as if you had never committed them / so that this is a great blessedness / which you enjoy under the covenant of grace.

7. Adam under the covenant of works / was punished by God / upon the first breaking of the covenant / that one sin broke God's covenant and displeased him / but under the covenant of grace your state is not so sorrowful / although you commit many sins; as you can see Romans 5:16. where the Apostle says: *And the gift is not like that which came through the one who sinned; for the judgment which came from one offense resulted in condemnation, but the free gift which came from many offenses resulted in justification.* That is / under the covenant of Works / all people in the World are condemned for one sin / but being under the covenant of grace / through the free gift much Justification has occurred. 8. # Wretched state in nature.

<columns>2</columns>

9. Under the <term>covenant of works</term> <note>The legal agreement where life is earned through perfect obedience.</note> / although God promised life to Adam, upon the completion of the covenant, yet God promised no forgiveness to Adam, upon the breaking of the covenant. God commanded him / do this and you shall live, but God made no promise to him / that if he should have broken his covenant / and sinned against him / he would nevertheless be irresistibly saved / in the covenant of works: there is no forgiveness at all promised / but only life: But under the <term>covenant of grace</term> <note>The theological concept that salvation is a free gift from God through faith in Christ.</note> you have a double promise.

10. Under the covenant of works / God accepted the Person for the sake of the work: but under the covenant of grace / he accepts the work / for the sake of the Person, and herein lies our blessedness; Under the covenant of works / God accepted the Person of Adam / for his work / because it was right and good / he accepted not so much his Person as his work / for as soon as he had broken the covenant / God had a displeasure in him, but under the covenant of grace / God accepts the work for the sake of the Person; just as you see in **Abel**, he was first accepted, and then he sacrificed, first his Person pleased God well / and then the offering / for the Person’s sake: God accepts our praying / reading / hearing / and everything we do / through Christ / with pleasure / for the sake of Christ’s Person / he loves and takes pleasure in all our services because of him.

11. 12. 14. God commands us in Ezekiel 36. You, through your own strength / are as well-equipped to make a world / as to offer a prayer / or to fulfill any holy duty or spiritual work; you could as easily destroy the entire World with your own hands / as bring down a lust through your own strength; but under the covenant of grace / God says / although we cannot keep his Law / he will accept the keeping of it by his Son for us / and he has promised to help and support us / in the fulfillment of all those things / which he commands us.

3. You who are strangers to the covenants of grace / herein lies your Misery / that you have no **Advocate** / to plead for you, nor a **Mediator** to stand between God and you: You have an avenging God who follows you / and a bitter Conscience ready to accuse you / and all other things in the World are against you, you have no friend / neither in Heaven / nor on Earth / to speak for you: Christ is a Mediator only for those who are under the covenant of grace: now / what can you say for yourself O man / why you should not be eternally damned in hell / for your drunkenness / adultery / Sabbath-breaking / swearing / lying / and other ungodly behavior? You can have nothing to plead for yourself / but must necessarily be cast into the unbearable hellish fire: But a Godly person who is under the covenant of grace / he can say / Lord / here is Christ

<column-break/>

my Mediator / who pleads with you for the forgiveness of all my sins / and for the obtaining of Heaven / of blessedness / Glory / for me / through his obedience and merits. But you who are under the <term>covenant of works</term> <note>The state of trying to earn God's favor through perfect adherence to moral laws.</note> / you cannot speak so / as those do / who are under the covenant of grace; for without the covenant of grace there is no Mediator / Christ is only the Mediator of the new covenant: therefore / in what a sorrowful state you are / seeing that you / just as you stand here now / must one day come to stand before the Judgment Seat of God, to give answer / for all things you have done, whether they be good or evil, and then you shall have no Body to plead for you / but must be unmercifully cast into the eternal flame.

4. Being alienated from the Covenant of grace / this is your Misery / that God / will reasonably and strictly carry out his justice / proceed against you on account of your sin / without any compassion or Mercy at all. Beloved, God has no mercy outside of his covenant / but in the Covenant of grace he is a God of mercy, long-suffering and great in kindness and truth, who forgives iniquity and transgression, and sin, Exodus 34:6-7. But he is clothed with Justice and strictness toward those who are without his covenant. Just as it goes in the law in a matter of life and death / the Judge takes no notice / of whether that man be sorrowful or not; the Law is not there to show mercy but to punish the transgressors / the Law does not ask whether a man is penitent and has regret for what he has done but whether he has done the deed or not / if so / he must die for the same / there is no other remedy: Even so it is here / God does not ask under the covenant of works whether you are sorry / for the breaking of his Law / but he asks whether you have broken the same / or not: and if so / he will therefore cast you into the Hellish fire: then shall the poor Soul cry out / O Lord be merciful to me this once / it shall be to my destruction / I will no longer sin or dishonor you / but will henceforth walk more holily / more humbly and more circumspectly before you / but all this you might promise / and it shall not help / for God will hear no one without Christ outside the covenant of grace.

5. A person alienated from the covenant of grace / has no true or particular promise of any blessings from God here in this World / God's blessings go with his Covenant / and therefore it is to be noted / that in that Chapter / where God makes a promise / of the blessing of the covenant of grace, in that same Chapter he promises the blessings of this life, as you may see in Ezekiel 36:25, 26, 27, 28. Where God says / I will sprinkle clean water upon you, and you shall be clean: From all your filthiness, and from all your idols I will cleanse you; and I will give you a new heart, and will put a new Spirit within you, and I will take away the stony heart out of your flesh, and will give you a heart of flesh, and I will put my Spirit within you: and I will cause you to walk in my statutes, and you shall keep my judgments and do them. # The Miserable State in Nature.

<columns>
...the following words of verses 29 and 30, where God says: *I will call for the grain, and will multiply it; and I will lay no hunger upon you; and I will multiply the fruit of the trees and the increase of the field.* And so also in the tenth and eleventh verses of that same chapter: *And I will multiply men upon you... and the cities shall be inhabited, and the waste places shall be built. Yes, I will multiply man and beast upon you, and they shall be increased and be fruitful. And I will cause you to dwell as in your former times, yes, I will make it better for you than at your beginnings; and you shall know that I am the Lord.* Here the Lord adds earthly blessings to the **Covenant of Grace** <note>Theological term for God's promise of salvation through faith.</note>, making it known that all who are under the covenant of grace have a share not only in spiritual, but likewise in temporal blessings. Yet no godless person—being a stranger to the covenant of grace—has any true share in any outward blessings; just as those who are believers are blessed with the faithful **Abraham**, and enjoy outward blessings, the godless may also enjoy some things, but it is like a prison where they are kept until the final day.

6. Your misery (you who are strangers to the covenant of grace) lies here: God will not accept any of your services, even though you do as much as a godly person. Indeed, you may hear more sermons, offer more prayers, and fulfill more duties than a godly person, yet God does not accept them from you as He does from them. As you can see in Genesis 4:4–5, **Cain** and **Abel** both offered sacrifices, one from his breeding and the other from his crops; and the Apostle, speaking of this in Hebrews 11:4, says: *That Abel by faith offered unto God a more excellent sacrifice than Cain.* This was not "more" in terms of the material substance, for to all appearances Cain’s offering was of more value than Abel’s; Abel’s was but a few young lambs, the firstlings of his flock, while Cain’s was from the first fruit of the field. Yet Abel’s offering was accepted and the other rejected because Abel was godly and under the covenant of grace, through which God accepted what he did, even though it was less than Cain's. Proverbs 15:8 says: *The sacrifice of the wicked is an abomination to the Lord: but the prayer of the upright is his delight.* A sacrifice, you know, is much more costly than a prayer, for a prayer costs a person nothing; to provide a sacrifice costs much money, and it is even more costly to offer it to God. Yet God hates the sacrifice of a godless man, while He accepts a small, simple prayer coming from a godly person. So, under the covenant of grace, though your duty be less in substance than that of the godless, yours shall be accepted and theirs rejected.

And thus I have finished the section regarding the "misplacement" <note>Dutch: *verschikkinge*, likely referring to the displaced or wrong state of the soul.</note> and have pointed out a six-fold misery of those who are strangers to the covenant of grace. And because I do not want a poor soul who is under the covenant of grace—and a partaker of all its great privileges—to go away with a sorrowful heart, I shall set down only two or three words of comfort to them. You children of the covenant, who are under the covenant of grace, let not your hearts be troubled by what you have just heard related concerning the misery

<column-break/>

of men who are strangers to this covenant; and lift up your souls, for I shall give you two or three comforting observations.

1. All the outward blessings that you enjoy come to you by way of the covenant; God has given you these blessings as an "appendix" to the covenant, and by the power of the same. The Lord never gives you a common blessing without you seeing therein the love of a Father, of a Husband, of a Friend—yes, the love of God in that blessing. Therefore, as I told you before regarding that same chapter where God promises the blessings of the covenant of grace, He also promises the blessings of this life as a consequence of the covenant. Godless men may have blessings, but not through the power of the promise, nor through the power of the covenant of grace. But should you ask me, "How shall I know if the blessings I enjoy come to me by the power of the covenant of grace?" **Answer:** You may know this by these two things:

1. In the event that you use and apply all the blessings you receive from God to the glory of God. This is what **Abraham** did, as you may see in Genesis 17:1–12. His use of God's blessings for the advancement of God's service was proof that these blessings came down to him from God through the covenant. But for those who are strangers to this covenant, the goods they enjoy are given to them for their harm and ruin.

2. When the blessings are to you a "bond and a cord" to hold you all the more firmly to God, then they come from the covenant. Jeremiah 31:11–12: *For the Lord has redeemed Jacob, and ransomed him from the hand of him that was stronger than he. Therefore they shall come and sing in the height of Zion, and shall flow together to the goodness of the Lord, for wheat, and for wine, and for oil, and for the young of the flock and of the herd: and their soul shall be as a watered garden; and they shall not sorrow any more at all.* That is to say, all the mercies of God shall bring them nearer and nearer and unite them with God. You then, who enjoy your blessings from God, if they join you closer to Him, you may look upon them as a result within you of the covenant of grace.

2. You who are in covenant with God, know this for your comfort: that the Lord accepts the little you do in His service more than the great portion that the godless bring to Him. God would rather accept a few **turtle-doves** from you than ten thousand rams or ten thousand rivers of oil from the godless. He accepts a cup of cold water from the righteous, given in His name to the righteous, whereas He will not accept the most precious sacrifices from the godless. 
O, what a happy state you are in, who are under the covenant of grace! The godless may hear more sermons and perform more services than you, and yet in all their duties they are turned away, while you are accepted.

3. Take this for your comfort: when you have offended God and provoked Him to anger, you have a **Mediator** who stands between God and you. Though you are guilty, yet you have an **Advocate** who pleads your case for you. You who are under the covenant of grace may say to Christ your Mediator as the Israelites said to Mo-

<meta>This page continues the discussion on the Covenant of Grace, moving from the misery of those outside it to the ways a person can determine if they truly belong to this spiritual contract with God. # A True Account of Man's Spiritual State

<columns>
**Moses**, when the people had offended God, went and spoke to God on our behalf. So might you say, when you have nothing but thundering, lightning, and tempests in your soul, and the flames of hell in your conscience, then you may say to **Christ**: "Go now to God and speak for me; ask the Father for the forgiveness of all my sins. I have offended God; oh, pray to God for me. I have committed a great crime; oh, plead with your Father and obtain forgiveness for me." Thus you may speak to Christ when you are under the **Covenant of Grace** <note>A theological term referring to God's promise of eternal life through faith in Christ, contrasted with the "Covenant of Works" (law).</note>.

But here, someone might lie in a state of spiritual complacency and believe they are under the Covenant of Grace when they are actually a stranger to it. Therefore, I shall provide some distinct signs by which you may know whether you are under the Covenant of Grace or not. Before I come to that, I will first set forth four somber conclusions which will pave the way for what follows.

1. Take this conclusion: a person may possess the outward and common privileges of the Covenant of Grace and yet be without its saving and spiritual privileges, such as the forgiveness of sins, having God as your God, and Christ as your Christ, etc. As seen in <margin>Deut. 29:10, 11</margin> Deuteronomy 29:10, 11, 12, where Moses says:
> You stand today, all of you, before the face of the Lord your God: your heads of your tribes, your elders, and your officers, all the men of **Israel**; your little ones, your wives, and your stranger who is in the midst of your camp, from your wood-cutter to your water-carrier, to enter into the Covenant of the Lord your God, and into His oath, which the Lord your God makes with you today.

Now, here you see that they all, rich and poor, were in the Covenant with God; and yet, it is not to be thought that all these people shared in the inward privileges of the Covenant of Grace. They all had **circumcision**, which was the seal of the Covenant regarding its outward privileges, but not all of them shared in that inward and special grace of the Covenant, such as the forgiveness of sin, peace of conscience, joy in the faith of God being their God, and Christ being their Savior. <margin>Rom. 9:4, 5</margin> In Romans 9:4–5, the Apostle says:
> They are Israelites, to whom belong the adoption as children, and the glory, and the Covenants, and the giving of the Law, and the service of God, and the promises; whose are the fathers, and from whom Christ came, as far as the flesh is concerned.

These were great privileges, and yet it says in the 8th verse: *These are not all children of God.* Although they had the outward blessings of the Covenant, they were nonetheless not all children of God. So you see, you can be in the Church of God and have a share in the outward blessings of the Covenant, yet still lack its inward and spiritual blessings.

2. Consider and conclude this within yourself—which is a grievous thing—that most people in the world are without even the common and outward mercies of the Covenant of Grace, such as those in **Judaism**, **Islam**, and **Heathendom** <note>The original text uses "Turkendom," a common 17th-century term for the Islamic world/Ottoman Empire</note>. These are without the outward privileges of the Church and have no hope of salvation. If one divides the world into three parts, and then again into five parts, only one-fifth are Christians; there are nineteen parts of the world that are Jews and Turks,

<column-break/>

and seven parts that are Heathens, so that there are only five parts Christians. The majority of people in the world are without the outward blessings of the Covenant of Grace and therefore cannot obtain salvation through Christ.

3. Take this further conclusion: that most people who *do* have outward and common blessings are nonetheless without the saving privileges of the Covenant of Grace. This is answered in <margin>Matt. 20</margin> Matthew 20: *Many are called, but few are chosen.* There are but few chosen for life and happiness among the many who have the outward blessings of the Covenant of Grace. <margin>Zach. 13:8, 9</margin> Zechariah 13:8–9:
> And it shall come to pass in all the land, speaks the Lord, that two parts therein shall be cut off and die, but the third part shall be left therein. And I will bring that third part into the fire, and I will refine them as silver is refined, and I will test them as gold is tested; they shall call on my name, and I will hear them; I will say, "It is my people," and they shall say, "The Lord is my God."

There was only one part in three that was godly, and as it was then, so it is now; only one part in three can truly say they have a share in the Covenant of Grace. Therefore, Beloved, this may be the lot of some of you: you may have a multitude of outward blessings, having the means of grace and making a profession of Christ, and yet few of you may have any special blessing from Christ. When Christ moved among the multitude, a great crowd followed him, but because power went out from him <note>Original: "kracht van hem was uptgegaan," referring to the healing of the woman with the issue of blood</note>, there are also very few who enjoy the special blessings of the covenant—having forgiveness of sins, bringing their condemnations under control, practicing their duties and services, having God as their God, and Christ as their savior.

4. Likewise, take this conclusion: that it is a natural pride and an imagination of the human heart, because they are under the outward blessings of the covenant, to conclude for themselves that they share in the inward and spiritual blessings of the Covenant of Grace. You will find that the Jews did this in <margin>Joh. 8:33, 39, 41</margin> John 8:33, 39, 41. First saying, "We are **Abraham’s** seed"; thereafter, "We have Abraham as our Father," and from this they conclude in verse 41 that God was their Father. However, Christ explicitly told them they were from their father the **Devil**. The godless are very adept at deceiving themselves; they think they have a share in the spiritual blessings of the Covenant of Grace because they enjoy the **Sacraments** and outward ordinances. But in **Baptism**, your face may be sprinkled with water, and yet you shall not have the sprinkling of the heart by the Blood of Jesus Christ. You can be born in the church and yet not be of the Church of the Firstborn in Heaven. You may have the church here as your mother, and yet God will not be your Father. There is but one means of salvation that the Jews formerly had, from which they are now estranged: the adoption, glory, covenant, promise, and the like. Therefore, God shuts up Heaven and happiness when these things are not present.

</columns>

# The Miserable State in Nature

### Ephesians 2:12

> That at that time you were without Christ, being aliens from the commonwealth of Israel, and strangers from the covenants of promise, having no hope, and without God in the world.

<margin>10th Sermon</margin>
**H**aving previously recounted four conclusions to ensure you do not imagine yourselves to be under the **Covenant of Grace** <note>A theological concept describing God's promise of eternal life through faith in Christ, rather than through following the Law.</note> when you are not, I shall now provide some discoveries by which you may know whether you are persons who rightly have fellowship in the life and salvation of God through Jesus Christ, by the power of His promise. I shall categorize these into three types: 1. You may know if you belong to the Covenant of Grace if you share in the spiritual blessings of the covenant. 2. If you possess those things which inseparably accompany the covenant. 3. If you fulfill the conditions of the Covenant of Grace, which is faith: believe and you shall be saved. If you have these three things, you undoubtedly lie under the Covenant of Grace.

1. If you have the saving and spiritual blessings of the Covenant of Grace, and these are fourfold. First, that God is our God, and we are His people. This is the essence of the Covenant of Grace, according to <term>Jeremiah 31:33</term>: *I will be their God, and they shall be my people.* I shall open this blessing to you a little, for God being "our God" signifies three things: 1. It signifies a special possession in God. 2. All-sufficiency in God for one’s benefit. 3. An absolute power that God has over them.

1. God is our God: It means that God is yours in a special possession, which no one but His children retains. Ungodly men have no part in God as their God; like Pharaoh, when he desired that **Moses** should pray for him, he said: *I have sinned against the Lord your God* <note>original: "uw God"</note>; he could not say, "against the Lord my God." You who can claim God from the Scriptures as your God, as having a special possession in Him, you have a right to the Covenant of Grace.

2. For God to be your God means an all-sufficiency in God to do you good. In <term>Genesis 17:1</term>, God says to **Abraham**: *I am God Almighty; walk before my face and be upright.* You who can look upon God as having a portion and possession in Him, find through experience that He is good to your souls in all things. If you consider every satisfaction in the world individually—as food against hunger, drink against thirst, clothing against nakedness, etc.—your God surpasses them all. He is all satisfactions combined to satisfy your heart. You who can look upon God as an all-sufficient God, as having your portion and part in Him and in no one else; this is an infallible proof that you sit under the Covenant of Grace.

3. For God to be your God signifies God's absolute power over you; for your own good, the Lord wants to rule over you, and subdue the corruptions within you, cast away your pride, and humble your heart, and give you a gentle

<column-break/>

spirit. If you find that God is yours in these three specific ways, you may comfort your heart in an unshakeable portion in the Covenant of Grace; if God is your God and you are His people, having devoted yourselves entirely to the service of God in all things you do.

2. Another special blessing of the Covenant of Grace is that God has promised to sanctify and renew your natures: just as God says in <term>Ezekiel 36:26, 27</term>: *A new heart also will I give you, and a new spirit will I put within you: and I will take away the stony heart out of your flesh, and I will give you a heart of flesh. And I will put my spirit within you: and cause you to walk in my statutes, and ye shall keep my judgments, and do them.* God does not wish to give us life merely for our happiness, but grace for our holiness. He wishes to give us not only **imputed righteousness** <note>Righteousness credited to a believer's account through faith.</note> for our justification, but likewise **inherent righteousness** <note>Righteousness actually present and working within a person's character.</note> for our sanctification. Now, therefore, examine yourselves: have your natures been sanctified and reborn? Have you been washed with pure water, and have you put away the stench of your sins and corruptions? Have you cleansed the inner man and let the Holy Spirit dwell therein? If so, then you have an immediate right to the same—a part in the Covenant of Grace—for no one can have the blessings of the covenant unless he has been within the Covenant of Grace. It is worthy to note that God is not only the one who presents the covenant as a gracious and merciful God, full of compassion, etc.; but He is a Holy God as well as a Merciful God. For this reason, He wishes to work holiness in us and expect holiness from us, just as we expect mercy and happiness from Him. You never have a right to God, nor can you expect life and happiness from Him as a merciful God, until you resolve to become like Him as He is: a holy God.

<margin>Objection</margin>
Yet here some will say, "This is not such a great blessing as you speak of, to be sanctified by the power of the Covenant of Grace: for there are many people who are sanctified by the Covenant of Grace and yet never become saved through it." They base this objection on the passage in <term>Hebrews 10:29</term>: *He has counted the blood of the New Testament an unholy thing, wherewith he was sanctified.*

<margin>Answer</margin>
Answer: The sanctification spoken of here is not true **Sanctification** <note>The process of being made holy.</note>; rather, this consisted only in profession, in the sight of men, and not in the sight of God. This is not sanctification in deed and truth, but only in appearance and in the judgment of men.

3. The forgiveness of sins is a blessing of the Covenant of Grace: <term>Jeremiah 31:34</term>: *They shall all know me, from the least of them unto the greatest of them, saith the Lord: for I will forgive their iniquity, and I will remember their sin no more.* Now Beloved, if you can say that God has forgiven your sins and put away your misdeeds, then you are under the Covenant of Grace.

<margin>Objection</margin>
But here poor souls might say, "Oh, alas! I have been a great sinner and have committed crimes against God, and therefore I fear I have no part in the Covenant of Grace."

# A True Account of Man's State

<margin>Answer</margin> **Answer:** Do not be discouraged, for it is the glory of the **Covenant of Grace** <note>The theological concept that God promises eternal life through faith in Christ rather than through human works.</note> to pardon great sins. This is a significant part of God’s glory: that He forgives great sins and passes over great transgressions. As seen in <term>Amos 5:12</term> <note>The original text cites Amos 4:12, 15, but the quote "I know your manifold transgressions and your mighty sins" is from Amos 5:12.</note>: *I know (says God) that your transgressions are many, and your sins are mighty.* There you see the greatness and multitude of sins; and yet God says: *hate the evil, and love the good, perhaps the Lord will be gracious.* Indeed, the Lord wants to be gracious to you. Although you have many and mighty sins, it is not their greatness or number that damns you, but rather the hardness of your heart and your failure to come to and **rely upon** <note>original: "uystulpinge" — likely meaning to rest one's weight upon or fully embrace.</note> Jesus Christ.

**5.** Through the Covenant of Grace, God writes His Law in your hearts so that we shall never depart from Him, as in <term>Jeremiah 31:33</term>: *I will put my law in their inward parts, and write it in their hearts; and will be their God, and they shall be my people.* That is to say, God wants to give a ready willingness and inclination in your heart to walk in every Commandment of His Law, so that we shall be fit to obey, to take heed of, and to keep the same, and to say that the Law is good; and then God says: *I will never let you go from me.* Examine yourselves: is this work wrought in your hearts by the Spirit of God? Has God written the sermons you have heard not just in your notebooks, but in your hearts? If so, these are good proofs that you have a share in the Covenant of Grace.

**2.** There is yet another sign that you have a share in the Covenant of Grace: that is, if you possess the things that inseparably accompany this covenant, and these are three.

**1.** If you are a person under the covenant of grace, in covenant with God, then you are duty-bound to break that covenant which you have made with your own **lusts** <note>In this context, "lusts" refers to any sinful desires or worldly attachments.</note>. You can be in no covenant with Christ as long as you do not give up your lusts and break off your sins. As the Apostle says in **Acts 3:25, 26**: *You are the children of the prophets, and of the covenant which God made with our fathers, saying unto Abraham: And in thy seed shall all the kindreds of the earth be blessed. God, having raised up his Son Jesus, sent him to bless you, in turning away every one of you from his iniquities.* So, if you are children of the covenant, the Lord wants to show each of you your godless ways; and therefore, you who are not drawn away from your evil course, nor have broken that covenant you made with death and hell, you cannot be under the communication of the Covenant of Grace. In **Psalm 50:16**, God says to the godless: *What hast thou to do to declare my statutes, or that thou shouldest take my covenant in thy mouth? seeing thou hatest instruction, and castest my words behind thee.* You will not forsake your lusts, nor leave your sins, and therefore, what have you to do with the Covenant of Grace? You can have no share in the covenant until you have put to death the "Old Man" <note>A biblical term for the sinful human nature before spiritual rebirth.</note> and brought your sins and corruptions under subjection.

**2.** If you are under the Covenant of Grace, this shall accompany you: you shall be a people entirely devoted and surrendered to the service of God. **Jeremiah 31**: *I will be your God,*

<column-break/>

*and you shall be my people.* The Covenant of Grace is called a **holy covenant** in **Luke 1:72**. This is not so much because it was made by a holy God, as it is because of the holy creatures who are within it, whom He wishes to make holy. Therefore, those who are in the Covenant of Grace with God are called a "holy people"; this they must be. In **1 Corinthians 6:20**, the Apostle says: *You are bought with a price: therefore glorify God in your body, and in your spirit, which are God's.* And **2 Corinthians 7:1**: *Having therefore these promises, dearly beloved, let us cleanse ourselves from all filthiness of the flesh and spirit, perfecting holiness in the fear of God.* Those who are in the covenant with God are a holy people.

**3.** The person who has a share in the blessings of the covenant makes it a matter of **conscience** <note>To "make conscience" means to act out of a sincere moral and religious conviction.</note> to walk in the ways of the covenant. He is not only satisfied with the promise of the covenant, but likewise makes it a matter of conscience to keep the commands of the covenant. For the Covenant of Grace does not only bestow blessings upon you, but also requires certain things that you must do. In **Isaiah 55:3**, God says: *Incline your ear, and come unto me: hear, and your soul shall live; and I will make an everlasting covenant with you, even the sure mercies of David.* The Covenant of Grace is a sure and eternal covenant; but God says, you shall first come to me, and then I will make an eternal covenant with you. God requires that you obey Him if you think you have a portion in the Covenant of Grace. Those who let God command what He will, yet do what pleases themselves, prove that they do not belong to the Covenant of Grace. But if the blessings of the covenant are given by God to you, and this obedience follows, you are in the covenant. Furthermore, faith must be in you as a certain proof of the Covenant of Grace: *Believe, and you shall be saved.* Until you are found in the state of faith, there is not a promise of the Gospel for you; you are hardened and unfit for them. If you have faith, then you may conclude that you belong to the Covenant of Grace. And thus, I have set down these signs by way of examination.

I now have only a word or two for the **application** <note>The "Use" or practical conclusion of the sermon.</note>, regarding how miserable those three types of people are; and a word or two for the comfort of such who cannot assure themselves that they have a share in the blessings of the Covenant of Grace—that God is their God, and they are His people whom God has sanctified and renewed in nature, and whose sins and iniquities He has forgiven and overlooked, writing His law in your hearts so that you do not depart from Him. If you have all these accompanying things, you enjoy glorious blessings and benefits by virtue of the Covenant of Grace.

**1.** You have that which is worth more than a King’s treasure—indeed, more than the world. You have God as your God, who is all in all. This is more than what was promised to Queen Esther by King Ahasuerus: half his kingdom. You have more than the Devil promised Christ when he led Him to the top of the mountain and showed Him all the kingdoms of the earth and the glory of them. You have more than the entire world, for you have God as your God, and you have a share in the Covenant of Grace, which is a bundle of promises, and...

### Ephesians 2:12.

> That ye were at that time without Christ, 
> being aliens from the commonwealth of Israel, and 
> strangers from the covenants of pro-
> mise, having no hope, and without 
> God in the world.

<margin>Second Sermon.</margin>
Now we come to the fourth part of the misery of an uncoverted man, (which you shall think to be a very strange thing) that he is without hope; while these Ephesians were in the state of Heathenism, unconverted to the faith, they were without hope, and the reason for this was because they were without Christ, who is the way, the truth, and the life; there is no other way to Heaven than only through Jesus Christ: and since they were outside the way to Heaven, they must necessarily be without any hope of coming to Heaven; It was the first branch of their misery to be without Christ; this brought them to all the rest, because they were without Christ, therefore they were alienated from the commonwealth of Israel, and therefore they were strangers to the covenants of promise, and without hope, and without God in the world.

<margin>Objection.</margin>
**Objection.** But some are ready to say, how can this be that the Apostle should say they were without hope? For if it were not for hope, the heart would burst, and therefore it is impossible that they should be without hope?

<margin>Answer.</margin>
**Answer.** It is true they had a hope, but it was a vain hope, an unfounded and deceitful hope, and this sort of hope is no better than no hope at all, so that the Apostle may well say they were without hope; that is, no good or well-grounded hope of Heaven; they had only an imaginary hope, which would shame them in the end; they had only a hypocritical hope, which shall perish: and therefore when the Apostle says that these Ephesians during their state of <term>unregeneration</term> <note>original: "onwedergeboorte" — the state of a person who has not yet experienced spiritual rebirth or conversion.</note> were without hope, his meaning is that they were without any well-grounded hope of Heaven; they had no Scripture passages on which to ground their hope that God would bring them into Heaven. This is a very sad point that I am now in, treating of this part of a man's misery, being without hope; the doctrine that I set forth from this is as follows.

<margin>Doctrine.</margin>
**Doctrine.** That all men, during the state of their unregeneration, are without any true or well-grounded hope of Heaven.
