...completely gives himself over / to commit secret sins / and lives as if there were no God in the World. The Reverend <term>Mr. Perkins</term> <note>William Perkins (1558–1602) was an influential English Puritan theologian whose works were widely translated into Dutch.</note> gives us this mark of an Atheist: one who commits that very sin which he would not dare to commit in the presence of a child, yet commits and does it when no human eye sees him. You who do your sins in secret, and think to hide yourself from the all-seeing Eye of God, you are a true Atheist; you who dare to do in the sight of God that which you are afraid to do in the presence of a human being. This shows a significant root of Atheism in the heart. Whenever a wicked man has committed wickedness, he is ready to say, "What does God know of it? Shall He judge through the darkness? The clouds are a covering to Him, so that He does not see." *Job 22:12, 13, 14.* These are the inventions of an Atheist's heart. An Atheist, if he can only keep himself from the punishment and contempt of men, is well satisfied, as long as people do not see it with their eyes and say, "There goes a Drunkard, a Swearer, an Adulterer," or the like; he is never troubled by his sins. Oh, therefore, you who wish to appear chaste where you live, and yet keep such <term>Delilahs</term> <note>A reference to the biblical figure Delilah, used here as a metaphor for a tempting or secret "darling" sin that one cherishes in private.</note> in your lap; and you who do injustice and walk in the ways of sin, seeking only to hide yourself from the eyes of men, know that all of this comes from an Atheistic heart. Whenever the hope of secrecy drives a person to sin, that person is a true Atheist. You who can fear the eye of a mortal man, and yet are not afraid of the All-seeing eye of an immortal God; you who are never troubled by your sins when no one but yourself knows them, yet are distressed when your sins are known to others—O, if it stands thus with you, you are an Atheist. Those who are not troubled that God sees their sin, but only that a man sees it, they are true Atheists, as in *Job 24:13, 15, 17.* *These are those who do not know His ways, nor abide in His paths. The eye of the Adulterer also waits for the twilight, saying, "No eye shall see me," and he puts a veil on his face. For the morning is to them as the shadow of death; if one recognizes them, they are in the terrors of the shadow of death.* Such as these are true Atheists. They were not troubled because God saw their sins, but because man beheld them; this is to them like the snares of the shadow of death. They did not want men to see their sins, yet they were not concerned about committing them in the sight of God. O, all such are true Atheists. A godly person fears to commit a secret sin just as much as a known, great, and public sin. Joseph said in *Genesis 39:9* <note>The original text mistakenly cites Gen. 33:9.</note>, *How then could I do this great evil, and sin against God?* If the realization of God comes to your heart, you will shun secret sins as much as public ones.

2. A person is a practical Atheist who makes no conscience of performing secret duties: he who never prays in private harbors Atheistic thoughts within him, believing that God does not hear him. It is truly worth noting regarding the Scribes and Pharisees in the Scripture that you never read of their secret fasting, nor their secret prayers; yet they had public fasts in great multitude—they fasted twice a week

<column-break/>

and prayed on the street corners, and gave Alms, etc. But you never read of any private or secret duties they performed, which stemmed from the roots of Atheism in their hearts. And so it is a clear proof of an Atheistic heart if you never make it a matter of conscience to go to God in private and pray for grace and mercy from Him. He is the Atheist who lives in the neglect of secret duties. For people who have a realization of the Godhead in their hearts know that no time is so well spent as that which they spend in secret prayers to God. *Song of Solomon 2:14:* *O my dove,* (says Christ) *who art in the clefts of the rock, in the secret places of the steep stairs, let me see thy countenance, let me hear thy voice; for sweet is thy voice, and thy countenance is lovely.* "O you poor soul" (says Christ) "who prays in secret and weeps in the hollows, show me your face and let me hear your voice." A person who has a realization of God before him knows that the Lord takes special notice of the sighing of his heart done in private; and therefore they pray in secret and pour out their souls to God in private, even when they are in public gatherings. It is very remarkable that all four Evangelists note the solitary prayer of *Christ*, when no one was with Him but all had left Him, *Matthew 26:36, Luke 22:39, Mark 14:35, and John 17.* <note>The text cites Luke 22:31, but 22:39 describes the Garden of Gethsemane.</note> While other things mentioned by one are omitted by others, they all mentioned this. Now the reason for this is that *Christ* wants to be an example to us, teaching us to be constant in the performance of these duties; and therefore it is a sign of an Atheistic heart in anyone who makes no conscience of pouring out his heart in secret prayers to God.

3. There is yet another mark: when God's lack of immediate punishment brings one to godlessness. My meaning is this: he who uses the patience and long-suffering of God toward him as an excuse to sin—who, because God does not immediately punish him for his sin, therefore chooses to continue in sin—such a one is a true Atheist. *Psalm 50:21:* *These things you have done,* (says God) *and I kept silent; you thought that I was altogether like you.* Beloved, if any of you harbor such thoughts as these in your hearts—that because God does not punish you presently for your sins, you therefore wish to continue in your sins—let me tell you that this is the practice of an Atheist. Because the drunkard was not taken away by God while he had the wine in his head; and because the swearer was not choked by God while the oath was in his mouth; because the liar is not cut off by God while the lie is on his tongue; therefore they wish to run with delight and willingness into those same sins. All this flows from a root of Atheism which is in their hearts.

A person is an Atheist who carries in his heart a forgetfulness and carelessness regarding the Day of Judgment. *2 Peter 3:3, 4:* *In the last days scoffers shall come, walking after their own lusts, and saying, "Where is the promise of His coming?"* You who harbor in your heart a forgetfulness of the Day of Judgment are a true Atheist; for if you do not believe God to be a Judge, you do not believe Him to be God. And Joshua said to all the people: See, this stone shall be a witness to us, for it has heard all the words of the Lord, which he spoke to us. Yes, it shall be for a witness against you, lest you lie to your God. And therefore the people who do not keep their covenant with God / are true Atheists: and Beloved / in this respect / there are now many more Atheists in England, than there have ever been / since the world began. But the Lord will declare himself to be a righteous God / although the wick-

<column-break/>

-ed break his covenant / and hold that as an unholy thing.

8. The man is a true Atheist / whose Conscience neither troubles him / nor restrains him / in the committing of any sins. The man who swears and drinks day after day / and commits one sin after another / and yet his Conscience never troubles him / that man is an Atheist. He who can live in the world / and commit great sins every day / and if his Conscience never terrifies him for his sins / that man is an Atheist. If you have the fear of God in you / and the thoughts of a God in you / it will preserve you from sins / and make you remember them after 20 Years. Thus did Joseph's Brothers think of their former sins / Gen. 42:21. They said to one another; truly we are guilty concerning our brother, etc. See also Job 13:26. and Psalm 25:7. David prayed / that the Lord would not remember the sins of his youth. Now the man who commits sin upon sin every day / and never feels any trouble in his Conscience over it / he is truly an Atheist; for it is impossible / if we live in the understanding of God / but that the Conscience will do its work.

9. People are true Atheists / who give themselves over to a hateful indifference <note>Original: "hooshepdt," likely a typo for "loosheydt" (emptiness/cunning) or "loofheid" (weariness/lukewarmness).</note> toward Religion: The man who wants to sleep on his side / and do nothing for the advancement of true Religion / is an Atheist. I will give you a powerful passage for this, 1 Kings 18:21. Elijah the Prophet says to the people: *How long will you limp between two thoughts? if the Lord is God, follow him: and if it be Baal, follow him.* But the Text says / the people kept their peace / and answered him not a word. They did not say that they would follow God / nor that they would follow Baal: if God were stronger than Baal they would be for God; but if Baal overcame him / they would follow him; which revealed their Atheism / and that God was not their God. The man who holds God for his God / must follow him through whatever afflictions they may be; if a man is indifferent to Religion / it proves his Atheism. And therefore all people who live according to the times / and who know how to change their Religion according to the times / such are Practical Atheists.

10. People prove themselves to be Atheists / who do not make their practice harmonize with their Profession: of such it says in Titus 1:16. *That they profess with their mouths that they know God, but they deny him with their works.* These who profess themselves to be Christians / and yet live as Heathens; Who profess of themselves to have an inheritance with the saints in light / and yet walk as children of darkness, such people are true Atheists. And thus I have finished 10 discoveries of a Practical Atheist / in all 13 / three from the Scripture / and ten flowing from the Scripture.

<margin>1. Application</margin> <note>Original: "Gebruyk" (Use). In 17th-century sermons, the "Use" section is the practical application of the doctrine.</note>
Now the application that I shall make is for counsel. If this is so / as you have heard / that all unregenerate people are practical Atheists / and live as if there were no God in the world; Oh then / that you would bewail those practical Atheists who are among us; do you please yourself in the doing of secret sins? or do you make no Conscience to fulfill those hidden duties? or all those things which I have previously pointed out to you / if you still...

This shall be to advise you / and to comfort your hearts / you who sit here this day / and hear me / being easily tempted toward atheism / and having committed it; well Beloved / observe this comfort for yourself / in these two things.

1. Are you tempted toward atheism? O, observe that Christ himself was tempted toward atheism and the forsaking of God / when the Devil desired that He should worship him. If you think you are tempted toward atheism / and that you have provoked God's all-seeing eye / or something similar / nonetheless take this for your comfort / that Christ was tempted just as you are / as the Apostle says in Heb. 2:18 <note>Original: "In het gene hy selve verfocht zijnde gheleden heeft, kan hy de geene die verfocht worden, te hulpe komen." This is Hebrews 2:18: "For in that he himself hath suffered being tempted, he is able to succour them that are tempted."</note>. Christ was tempted to serve the Devil / yet the Devil could find no corrupt matter in Christ / to work upon. Christ was like clear water / clear as crystal / that could not be made murky by the Devil / but in us he shall find matter enough to work upon / since our natures are corrupt.

2. Observe / that although you are tempted by the Devil / to the sin of atheism / nevertheless these temptations / if you do not consent to them / nor allow them to dwell in you / shall be cast upon the Devil / as his sins / and not yours. And thus you see that I have briefly gone over this Doctrine / that every man by nature is a practical atheist <note>A "practical atheist" is someone who may believe in God intellectually but lives their life as if God does not exist.</note> / living in the world as if there were no God in the world.

### Ephesians 2 : 12.

> That at that time you were without Christ, being aliens from the commonwealth of Israel, and strangers from the covenants of promise, having no hope, and without God in the world.

<margin>17th Sermon.</margin>
In addition to the Doctrine / which I finished last Sabbath day / there are some others in this Text; Wicked men are without God in the world, that is / they are without any special interest or ownership in God / as their God: the words indicate not only that they live / as if there were no God in the world / but they live without any right / or property in God / though they are not without wisdom / wealth / goods / status / or without honor in the world / yet they are without any part or property in God / as their God / they are without God in the world: From which I wish to note this Doctrine:

<margin>Doctrine.</margin>
That all men by nature, are without any part or property in God / as their God.

Now Beloved / before I come to treat this point / I shall first send ahead three preliminary conclusions <note>Original: "Sluptreden," referring to logical deductions or qualifying points used to clarify a theological argument.</note> / for the enlightenment and explanation of this point / and to show you / what I mean by this Doctrine:

Namely:

1. Take this conclusion / that in some sense / there is no creature in the world / which is without God / although in another respect / men are truly said to be without God; in some sense no one is without God / that is / through creation and preservation: so it may be said of the worst Devil in Hell / that God is his God: and

2. A wicked man has God as his God / through Profession, he professes to know God / and that God is his God; but in another sense / he cannot be said / to have God for his God / that is / in relationship and reconciliation, that God has established His Covenant with him through Jesus Christ.

3. Take this conclusion / that / although a great

<column-break/>

multitude of people may think / God is their God / yet there are but few people in the world / who through the Covenant have God as their God / Zech. 13:8-9. There the Lord looks upon the Jewish Church under a threefold observation: 

> And it shall come to pass in all the land, says the Lord, two parts therein shall be cut off, and give up the ghost, but the third part shall be left therein. And I will bring the third part through the fire, and I will refine them, as silver is refined, and I will try them as gold is tried: they shall call on my name, and I will hear them: I will say, It is my people, and they shall say, The Lord is my God. 

Although you all think you have a part in God / nonetheless only a small portion has a part in Him / who can truly say God is their God / in covenant with Him.

3. <note>The original text repeats the number '3'.</note> Take this conclusion / that the deceitfulness of man's heart is such / that the worst of men are ready to believe and think / that God is their God / when He is not / as you may read in Jer. 3:4-5. There God says / They shall cry unto me, my Father, thou art the guide of my youth. And yet God says / You have done evil things, and have had your way. Likewise Psalm 14:1. The fool says in his heart, there is no God: they are corrupt, they have done abominable works, there is none that does good. These who have no God in their hearts / yet in all their ways / they are quite ready to take God as their God / although they commit detestable works / and do as much evil as they can.

So much for the preliminary conclusions: I come now to treat a practical question / of which it is necessary to speak / before I come to the Doctrine / which is this.

### Question. What are the signs of these people / who are without any part / or property in God as their God / in the manner of the Covenant?

### Answer. This Question I am the more willing to answer / out of consideration of that great complacency / and sinking down that is in the hearts of men / who happen to think God is their God / when He is not / and therefore I shall give you seven distinct marks / of such people / who imagine great things for themselves from God / and yet deceive themselves: these people are without any part or interest in God / as their God.

1. Those who are without any actual knowledge of God as their God.
2. Those who live without making the word of God their Rule.
3. Those who live in the world / without making the ways of God their delight.
4. Those who live in the world / without making the Glory of God their goal.
5. Those who live in the world / without making the Day of the Lord / their delight.
6. Those who live in the world / without making the people of God a primary object of their love.
7. Lastly / those who live in the world / without making sin the primary object of their hate.

Regarding the first / these are without any part / or property in God / who live in the world without any actual knowledge of God; 2 Chron. Chapter 15 v. 3 <note>Original: "Ezron. Capit. 1. v. 3." This appears to be a printer's error for 2 Chronicles (Cron.) 15:3.</note> it says / spoken a long time ago / Israel has now for many days been without the true God, and without a teaching priest, and without the Law. All that time (while they were without Law / and without a teaching priest) they were without God. Those who live without saving knowledge of God / the Scripture views them / as those who have no part or right in God. John 8:54-55. You say (says Christ to the Jews) that he is your God, yet you have not known him. Giving it to be understood / that God was not their God / because they were ignorant of Him. Now beloved / true knowledge of God / does not prove that you have a part in God / until it is:

1. A practical knowledge of Him / John 8:55. There Christ says / I am from God, I know Him / and keep His word. Pointing out / that the man

<meta>This page continues the discussion on the signs of "practical atheism," moving from the definition of the sin to the practical examination of whether an individual truly possesses a "part" or "portion" in God. It addresses the anxiety of those who feel too ignorant to be saved and provides specific tests for the soul.</meta>

# The Miserable State of Nature.

who shall have communion with God / if his God must know him / and this knowledge God shall make sufficient for him / and he shall keep His word; and

2. It must be an experiential knowledge of God / just as David says / Psalm 51:8. "Behold, you desire truth in the inward parts." If you look at your own person in this way / without a practical and experiential knowledge of God / you are without any part in Him / as your God.

<margin>Objection.</margin>
But before I come more to the particulars / I must address an Objection; many a one / who calls themselves a poor and broken soul / says; if it is so / that only those / who know God / have a right to Him / then may the Lord be merciful / for I am poor / ignorant and sinful / since I know nothing of God at all nor do I know Him; and therefore surely / I have no part in God / as my God.

<margin>Answer.</margin>
Answer. Now to such as you are / I shall give these 2 or 3 words / for comfort / by way of answer.

Firstly, take this for an Answer / that in the Scripture the complaint about ignorance / is noted / as a good step toward knowledge. Proverbs 30:2-3. There you read of Agur, an excellent man in virtue and knowledge / in the times of Solomon / and yet you shall not read of a man / who complained more about his ignorance than he: "Surely" (he says) "I am more senseless than any man: and I do not have human understanding: and I have not learned wisdom; nor known the knowledge of the holy ones." <note>original: "Voorwaar (seght hy) ik ben onvernuftiger dan imandt: en ick en hebbe geen menschen verstandt: ende ick en hebbe geene wijsheyt geleert; nochte de wetenschap der heyligen bekent."</note> And yet this man / who so lamented his ignorance / showed such fruits of grace and knowledge in his practice / as much as anyone.

Secondly, by God’s reckoning / he knows the most / who does the most. He does not have the most knowledge / who has a great deal to say / about unnecessary and idle questions; but he is a knowing man in God’s esteem / who walks according to the small measure of knowledge he has. Psalm 111:10. "All who do his commandments have good understanding." God does not measure your knowledge by your questions and disputes / but by your practice and doing. Jeremiah 22:16. "He judged the cause of the miserable and needy; then it went well with him; is that not to know me, says the Lord?"

Thirdly. Your ignorance is no proof / that you have nothing of God / or no part in Him / until your ignorance has these three qualities: such as

1. Suppose you are ignorant of God / yet if you are not <term>satisfied|Dutch "genoegende", being content or complacent</term> in your ignorance / being satisfied in yourself therein / and wish to know everything as you are able / while still praying / and doing like those / of whom it is written / Hosea 8:2. "Then shall they [Israel] cry to me, my God, we Israel know you:" And yet there is no knowledge nor fear of God in the land.

2. If you do not find satisfaction in your ignorance / but labor and strive for more knowledge / for which your state is fit enough. But if you say to God / Job 21:14. "Depart from us, for we have no delight in the knowledge of your ways;" as the wicked did; this is a sad sign / that you have no part at all in God.

3. If you are not stubbornly ignorant / like those spoken of in Psalm 82:5. "They do not know, nor [will] they understand." When people are ignorant / and want to remain ignorant / this is a clear proof that they have no part in God. 2 Peter 3:5. "For this they are willingly ignorant of." Now if your ignorance is accompanied by these three circumstances / the Lord be merciful to you; for these are clear proofs / that you have no part or ownership in God / as your God. But although you are very ignorant / yet if you bewail your ignorance / and labor diligently for more knowledge / and strive for the knowledge of the Lord / not being stubbornly ignorant / but wishing to do more / if you knew more / if it stands so with you / your ignorance does not prevent you / from having part and ownership in God.

2. Another mark of a person without a part in God / is this / he is such a one who lives in the world / without making God’s word his rule. John 4:7. <note>The author likely refers to John 8:47: "He that is of God heareth God's words."</note> "He who is of God hears the words of God: therefore you do not hear, because you are not of God." Those who will not make the Word of God their Rule / and live with practice in obedience to the same / Christ says the reason for this is / because they are not of God. John 4:6. <note>Likely 1 John 4:6</note> "He who knows God hears us: he who is not of God, does not hear us." And therefore / you who walk after the own imaginings of your own hearts / and are governed by your lusts / and do not want to make God's word a <term>bridle|Dutch "breydel", a harness or restraint</term> / to restrain your whims and <term>deafness|Dutch "verdooventheden", a state of being spiritually deaf or numb</term> / but want to do whatever pleases you / let God command what he will. All these are public proofs / that you are not from God.

3. He is without a part in God / who lives in the World / without making the ways of God his delight. 1 John 3:10. "In this the children of God and the children of the Devil are manifest." Everyone who does not practice righteousness, is not of God. Righteousness is not only to be taken here for the Law / or civil justice / but for the whole of Godliness / and the body of Christianity: Everyone who does not practice righteousness, is not of God: this not doing of Righteousness / belongs to the doing of sin, 1 John 3:8. "He who commits sin is of the Devil;" this is not simply to be taken / that he who sins / is of

<column-break/>

the Devil / but he who *commits* the sin. (that is) [doing so with] delight and pleasure / such a person is of the Devil: and so likewise he who does not practice righteousness / is not of God / that is / he who does not work it with pleasure and delight / such a one is not of God. So then beloved / the person is in a sad state / who does sin with more desire and delight / than he performs holy duties.

4. The person is without God / who lives in the World / without making the glory of God his target. It is to be noted / that when the Jews accused Christ / saying / he was a Samaritan, and had the Devil, and was not of God, he was patient / although these slanders were thrown upon him / because he sought not his own honor, but the honor of God, John 8:49-50. Jesus answered / "I do not have the Devil, but I honor my Father, and you dishonor me. Yet I seek not my own honor: there is one who seeks it, and judges."

5. The person is without any part in God / who lives in sin / without keeping the Day of God as his delight / he / who is without God / lives in the [un]holy [violation] of the day of the Lord / but everyone who wants to violate it / that man is without God in the World / John 9:16. The Pharisees said of Christ / "This man is not from God / because he does not keep the Sabbath." This would have been a very good Argument / had it been rightly applied / if Christ had not kept the Sabbath; but they erred grossly / since Christ kept the Sabbath. Truly Beloved / if these Pharisees lived now / they would see you Christians violating the Sabbath day / and spending it in pleasures / in Swearing / drinking and dishonoring of God’s name; never spending an hour therein in praying / reading / hearing / or in the exercise of any holy and religious duties; they would justly conclude / that you are not from God / because you do not keep the Sabbath day.

6. The man is without God / who lives without making the people of God the object of his love; as you may see / 1 John 3:10. "Everyone who does not practice righteousness, is not of God; and he who does not love his brother." And 1 John 4:20. "If someone says, I love God, and hates his Brother; he is a Liar." For he who does not love his Brother whom he has seen, how can he love God whom he has not seen? He who does not love his Brother / the children and the people of God / he cannot love God. You who carry in your hearts a hidden hate against the Godly / who are more holy and religious than you yourself are: acting like the Tigers / hating the images of the Godly / the people of God / and the Ministers of the Gospel / because they are such / hating Godliness as Godliness / these are powerful proofs that the love of God is not in you.

7. The man is without God / who lives in the world / without making sin an object of his hatred; The man has not God / who does not hate sin; although that man could have [it], who [does] righteousness [yet] those who have no part in God [are those] who do not hate sin. And thus I have briefly run over these seven things / by which you can know / whether you truly have communion with God / as your God, yes or no / if you have the true knowledge of God / make His Word your Rule / His way your delight / keep His day / make His Glory your target / the Godly an object of your love / and sin an object of your hate; If these things are found in you / you can know without doubt / that you have part and ownership in God.

<margin>Use</margin>
We come now to the application / which is for unspeakable comfort / to all you who are God’s people / who can assure your good God from the Scripture / of communion with God / as your God.

1. If you have God / you have all things; let me tell you / you who have God for your God / you may challenge all the Kings / Princes and Potentates in the World. Other people may say / they have luxuries and you not / they have Riches / Honors / and Pleasures / and you not / but you may go higher / and challenge them all / because you can say / you have a part in God / and they do not. The wicked cannot lay the communion of God to their hearts; and therefore when they speak to God / they speak to him / as to a God of others / and not of them. First. Genesis 31:29. when Laban spoke to Jacob, (he said) "The God of your father": Likewise Pharaoh, Exodus 8:25, 28. "Go and sacrifice to your God in the Land." And from this the theologians note / that the Scripture does not allow / the wicked to call God by way of Ownership / as their God: But those who are righteous and holy / you have a part in God / "God is not ashamed to be called their God," Hebrews 11:16. You who have a right in God / although you are a poor and despised people / nonetheless are not ashamed before God / as your God / for the Lord is not ashamed / that you should call Him your God. God is not ashamed of us / whose dwellings are in the dust / he wants to honor us: therefore let this encourage you / to go to God as your God / and claim Him as your own / and trust in Him as your God / pray to Him / and name Him as your own God / for He is not ashamed of you. And to speak a little more of this in particular / I want to exhort you to two things.

1. To examine your part in God.

<meta>This page continues the practical application of the previous discussion, moving from the definition of a "portion in God" to the specific methods by which a believer can test and prove that God is indeed theirs. It emphasizes that true faith is found in the "inward man" rather than just outward behavior.</meta>

# A True Account of Man's Miserable State, etc.

2. To prove or to show the same.
1. Labor to demonstrate your portion in God: examine and test yourself whether you can satisfy your hearts on conscientious and scriptural grounds; do not rest or trust on artificial supports <note>original: "gemaakte beenen," literally "made legs," an idiom for false pretenses or unnatural aids</note>, but labor to assure your own souls that God is your God. To help and advance you a little in this examination, I shall here point out those discoveries by which you may know, and be assured without doubt, that God is your God.
1. If you are such a person who seeks to preserve your inward man from secret defilements of sin, as well as your outward part from great transgressions. *2 Corinthians 6:18.* And in the first verse of the following chapter: *And I will be a Father to you, and you shall be my sons and daughters, says the Lord Almighty.* Since we then have these promises, beloved <insert>Beloved</insert> (says the Apostle), *let us cleanse ourselves from all filthiness of the flesh and of the spirit.* And therefore, if you have a care to keep yourself from hidden sins, by which the inward man is defiled, it is a sign that you truly have a portion in God: because God wants to be our God and wants to receive us as His own people. We must not only wash our legs, or our outward man, but our inward part; and if we do so, we may be sufficiently assured that we are reconciled and accepted by God through Jesus Christ. But now, you who make a "conscience" of your ways only so far as people may not see the beam in your eye—if you do not labor to preserve your inward part from defilements as well as your outward man—you have no portion at all in God.
2. Another clear proof of your interest in God is this: if you have an earnest and tireless labor in your spirits to come to the closest likeness and conformity to Jesus Christ, as much as is possible. Do you labor to be holy, as He was holy? And humble and meek, as He was? *2 Corinthians 7:1.* There the Apostle says: *Having therefore these promises, beloved, let us cleanse ourselves from all the filthiness of the flesh and the spirit, perfecting holiness in the fear of God.* If you labor toward the likeness of God in holiness, your portion in God will make you labor toward God's likeness to be perfectly holy, even though you cannot be perfect in holiness. If you have a portion in God, you will labor more and more to be holy as He is holy, and to come to the closest likeness of Him as much as you are able.
3. Another discovery of your portion in God is this: if God has engraved in your soul these saving workings and blessings, which He has placed upon all those who have a part in Him. God has promised that He will be their God, and they His people; that He will give them a new heart, take away from them the heart of stone, and give them a heart of flesh; and that He will sanctify and renew their natures, and write His law in their innermost parts, and work in their hearts a sweet submission to His law, and put His fear in their hearts, so that they shall never depart from Him. These are the blessings of the Covenant of Grace <note>The "Covenant of Grace" is a central theological concept in Reformed tradition, referring to God's promise of eternal life through faith in Christ.</note>. Now, you who find an abundant and certain proof in your own souls that you have found God’s cleansing and purifying of your hearts, and the sanctifying and renewing of your natures, and His law written in your innermost part, and His fear placed in your hearts so that you never depart from Him; if you find these

<column-break/>

things in you, they are indubitable proofs that you have a portion in God.
2. Just as I want you to test your portion in God, I would also have you exhorted likewise to prove your hope in God. If you keep God far from you (if I may say so) and never make use of Him for your spiritual comfort and strengthening, and never go to Him for help in times of danger, you then do not prove your ownership in God.
But here it is that you will ask me: how shall you prove your portion in God?
**Answer.** 1. Prove it thus: in the claiming of your portion in God, there is a great motivation and inward urging to obey God. Thus did David, *Psalm 119:10 <note>The text likely intends Psalm 143:10 based on the quote provided.</note>. Teach me to do your good pleasure,* (he says) *for you are my God;* by this, David wanted to prove his portion in God; and likewise *Psalm 119:115. Depart from me, you evildoers, so that I may keep the commandments of my God.* We shall make our portion in God an urging upon our souls to keep the commandments of God.
2. Then you certainly prove your portion in God when this makes you reckon and weigh all your sins <note>original: "verswaaren," meaning to make heavy or realize the gravity of</note> that you have committed against God. When you have a portion in God, that makes you see sin—how great an evil sin is, and how much you have wronged the Lord your God through your sins. *Jeremiah 3:25. We have sinned against the Lord our God, we and our fathers, from our youth even to this day, and we have not been obedient to the voice of the Lord our God.* Here the children of Israel weigh their sins against God as *their* God. And so Daniel—he makes his portion in God a moving reason for him to weigh his sins, his sins against God. *Daniel 9:5.* There he says: *We have sinned, and have done wrong, and have acted wickedly, and have rebelled, by departing from your commandments and from your judgments,* and then *v. 7. To you, Lord* (he says) *belongs righteousness, but to us the shame of faces, as it is this day.* And again *v. 8. O Lord, to us belongs the shame of faces, to our kings, to our princes, and to our fathers, because we have sinned against you. But with the Lord our God are mercies and forgivenesses, even though we have rebelled against him.* And so he went on, more and more weighing his sins against God, and that up to ten times. It is the consideration of our portion in God that makes us weigh our sins against God, when we consider that we have sinned against our God, against our gracious and merciful Father, who loved us and gives us eternal comforts, and through grace good hope, who is infinite in goodness, overflowing in mercy and truth. Such considerations as these shall bring us to the magnifying of our sins against Him.
3. Prove your portion in God by making the same a ground and a firm foundation to lean upon, and to support your hearts under all the miseries, oppressions, and disturbances that you might encounter here in this world. Thus David encouraged himself in the Lord his God, *Psalm 3:8. Arise, Lord, deliver me, my God.* You then make a right proof of your portion in God when you go to Him, trust, and rely on Him in all times of danger and sorrow; for you have a portion in that God who is both willing and mighty to deliver and help you—a God who has helped you, and yet shall help, and will never leave nor forsake you; and therefore be encouraged to cast all your care upon Him.

# THE ZEALOUS CHRISTIAN.

### Taking Heaven by Holy Violence.

---

->Presented in several<-

## SERMONS,

->Preached by that faithful Servant of Jesus Christ<-

### Mr. CHRISTOPHER LOVE, in his lifetime Preacher at St. Lawrence Jewry, in London.

->Translated from the English by H. V. S.<- <note>H. V. S. likely refers to Hendrick van Schuere, a prolific translator of English Puritan works into Dutch.</note>

### MATTHEW 11 verse 12.

> And from the days of John the Baptist until now, the kingdom of heaven suffereth violence, and the violent take it by force.

<margin>* Sermon in St. Lawrence Jewry within London, April 21, 1649, the contents explained.</margin>

<image-desc>Decorative drop cap 'D' featuring a man sitting on a large initial, with ornate scrollwork backgrounds.</image-desc>

This Text is a part of the great recommendation which Christ gives of the person and ministry of John the Baptist. John was a crier in the wilderness to proclaim the glory of Christ, and Christ was a herald to proclaim the praise of John. And this He does:

<margin>verse 7.</margin>
1. Because of his steadfastness in the doctrine of Religion, verse 7. *What went ye out into the wilderness to see? A reed shaken with the wind?* A light, wavering, and an inconstant Preacher, who like a reed is moved by every wind of doctrine? John was not such a man; not like a reed, which cannot withstand the current or the blowing of the slightest breeze, but like an oak tree or cedar that stands immovable in the midst of the greatest storms.

<margin>verse 8.</margin>
2. Because of his holiness and great measure of Mortification <term>Mortification: the spiritual practice of subduing one's earthly desires and sinful nature</term>, verse 8. *What went ye out for to see? A man clothed in soft raiment?* John was not such a man; he was not at all adorned with the fashion and grandeur of the Court, but he had fine clothing of camel's hair, and a leathern girdle about his loins, *Matthew 3:4.*

<margin>verse 9. verse 11.</margin>
3. He compares him with the preceding Prophets, with those Teachers who went before him, verse 9. *What went ye out for to see? A prophet? Yea, I say unto you, and more than a prophet,* and verse 11. *Verily I say unto you, Among them that are born of women there hath not risen a greater than John the Baptist.*

<column-break/>

He praises him above all his predecessors; not in respect to the dignity of his service, but in respect to the clarity of his teaching. Nevertheless, so that he might not be proud in himself, or others admire him too much, He adds at the end of the 11th verse, specifically: *Notwithstanding he that is least in the kingdom of heaven is greater than he.* These Disciples and Apostles who would live after the resurrection of Christ (from whom the Gospel or the Kingdom of heaven would take its beginning) would be greater than John, in respect to that high knowledge and clear revelation which they would have of Christ.

4. He praises him because of the fruitfulness of his Ministry, and that is presented in the Text: *From the days of John the Baptist the kingdom of heaven suffereth violence, and the violent take it by force.* We shall say a little toward the explanation of this Text.

<margin>The Text explained. [a] The Empyrean Heaven, or Kingdom of Heaven, denotes the preaching of the Gospel and the spreading of the Church. Paraeus. <note>David Paraeus (1548–1622) was a prominent Reformed theologian.</note> [b] The Kingdom of God signifies the state and condition of the Church, which is properly called Christian. Cameron on Matthew 8:11. <note>John Cameron (1579–1625) was a Scottish theologian and scholar.</note></margin>

By the Kingdom of heaven] is not meant the glorious throne of the blessed Angels, but the Evangelical state of the Christian church. [a] It signifies the increase of the Gospel, and the expansion of the church. [b] It signifies the condition of the church which is properly called Christian. The Kingdom of Heaven is interpreted in the Scriptures as an abolition of the observance of the Ceremonial law, and a proclamation of the Gospel by John the Baptist; and so it began when John first preached the Gospel. And so Matthew relates it to us, *Matthew 3:1.* John preached, saying *Repent, for the Kingdom of Heaven is at hand.* Mark calls this *The beginning of the gospel of Jesus Christ, the Son of God, Mark 1:1.* And therefore it is that John is called a Preacher of the Gospel.

Suffereth violence] Violence must not be taken as it is taken in our days of discord and opposition, and has been taken in the days of persecution; as it is taken in our days, in

oppo- <note>This catchword "oppo-" suggests the next page begins with "opposition."</note>

<summary>This page serves as the introduction and title page for a series of sermons by Christopher Love regarding "holy violence," specifically interpreting Christ's praise of John the Baptist and defining the "Kingdom of Heaven" as the era of the Gospel.</summary>
<keywords>Christopher Love, John the Baptist, Kingdom of Heaven, holy violence, St. Lawrence Jewry, Matthew 11:12, Gospel preaching, David Paraeus, John Cameron</keywords>

686 The Zealous Christian.

---

opposition / of equity and justice / and just as it was in the first arrival of the Gospel / when the godless people of the world went out to oppose and oppress the proclamation of the Gospel / but it is a holy violence <note>The author distinguishes between "wicked violence" (persecution) and "holy violence" (spiritual fervor).</note> through which people press forward to obtain the grace of this Kingdom. And so it is generally taken / for a holy violence of the affections or inclinations / or a Godly disposition or state that was implanted in the hearts of many people in the days of John the Baptist.

Violence here is set in contrast to the sluggishness and moderation in God’s service / to that coldness and frozenness that is in the hearts of men under the preaching of the Word. It is called a holy violence / to make a distinction between those who were in fact Christians and other men; to distinguish them from the Scribes and Pharisees who were cold under the ministry of the Gospel. They were so zealous for Christ in the Gospel / that no difficulties or discouragements could draw them away from following after Christ.

<margin>They are so eager that they can be pulled away by no force, but would rather die than be pulled away from the Gospel. Luther. <note>Original Latin: "Adeo avidi sunt ut nulla vi abstrahi possunt, sed potius moriuntur quam abstrahantur ab Euangelio." Martin Luther was the seminal figure of the Protestant Reformation.</note></margin>
They were so greedy for Christ / that no violence could snatch them away / but they would rather die than be pulled away from the Gospel. It is a simile taken from soldiers / who force their way into a City with violence / and take it by force / and divide the spoil. The similar manner of speaking stands *Luke 16:16.* Every man presseth into the Kingdom of God.

As for the period of time / in which this violence happened and was revealed / it was in the fifteenth year of Tiberius, as you read *Luke 3:1.* in the 29th year of Christ.

These teachings could be drawn from these words / but I shall not multiply the Teaching-points. The first and foremost teaching is taken from the time in which this violence was / and the teaching is this:

<margin>Doctrine.</margin>
At the first proclamation of the Gospel, the preaching of the Word was more fruitful / a multitude of people expressed a greater holy violence and intensity of affection toward the service and calling upon God than in any century besides. From the days of John the Baptist until now the Kingdom of heaven suffereth violence.

<margin>They were cold under the ministry of the law of the Scribes & Pharisees, they were fervent under the ministry of John. Musculus. <note>Original Latin: "Frigebant sub ministerio legis Scribarum & Phariseorum, fervebant sub ministerio Ioannis." Wolfgang Musculus (1497–1563) was a Reformer and theologian.</note></margin>
[a] The people were cold under the service of the Scribes and Pharisees / they were hot under the service of John.

In the treatment of this matter two Questions must be answered.

<margin>1. Question? Why was the Gospel so fruitful then.</margin>
1. How did it come to be that the people at that time were so zealous and so inclined toward the Gospel / that the Gospel at that time was so fruitful?
2. How does it come that it is not more fruitful now, or why has that holy violence now decreased?

1. What are the reasons why it was so fruitful in the days of John the Baptist? I answer / that several reasons can be given for that.

<margin>1. Reason. b Human nature is eager for novelty. Mark 1:27. <note>Original Latin: "Natura hominum novitatis avida."</note></margin>
1. Because of the novelty of the Gospel. b. New things are most attracting and pleasing to human nature. This was the basis of the wonder of the people concerning Christ / *Mark 1:27.* They were all amazed, saying, What new doctrine is this? For with power he commands the unclean spirits, and they are [obedient to him].

<column-break/>

[obedient to him]. We are like the Athenians / of whom it is written / *Acts 17:21.* They spent their time in nothing else, but to tell and hear some new thing. While John’s Ministry was new and fresh / they all rejoiced in it / *John 5:35.* You were willing for a short time to rejoice in his light. And so was Paul’s ministry most successful among the Thessalonians in the beginning of it / *1 Thess. 2:1.* You know our entrance to you, that it was not in vain. It is the observation of Melanchthon <note>Philipp Melanchthon (1497–1560), a German reformer and collaborator with Luther.</note>, that people are favorites and followers of the Gospel when it first comes into a place.

Another Reason for the fruitfulness of the Gospel at that time is this: Because the prophecies of the Old Testament had to be fulfilled / both regarding the extension and expansion of the Church with respect to place and persons / and the intensity of the affections /

1. For the expansion of the church regarding place and persons: It was spoken of before in Holy Scripture *Isa. 54:1, 2.* Sing joyfully you barren woman, who has not borne; break forth into joyful singing, and shout, you who have not been in labor, for the children of the desolate are more than the children of the married, says the LORD. Make the place of your tent wide, and let the curtains of your dwellings be stretched out, and do not hinder it: make your cords long, and drive your stakes firmly in, etc. Which passage is applied by Paul to the Gentiles at the first proclamation of the Gospel / *Gal. 4:27.* where he now repeats the words of the first verse.

Another prophecy of the same nature you have in *Isa. 2:2.* It shall come to pass in the last of days, that the mountain of the LORD shall be firmly established on the top of the mountains, and that it shall be exalted above the hills, and to the same all Gentiles shall flow. Which promise is repeated with the same words, *Micah 4:1.* Another promise of the same nature stands in *Isa. 60:3, 4, 5.* And in many other places / which it is not necessary to relate now.

2. There were also promises regarding the intensity or raising up of the affections / *Isa. 40:31.* Those who wait upon the LORD shall renew their strength, they shall mount up with wings, like eagles. The Eagle is a bird of the strongest and highest flight of anything that flies in the air. So *Zech. 12:8.* In that day he who is weak shall be as David, and the House of David shall be as God. So *Psalm 110:3.* it is prophesied of the first introduction of the Gospel / that Your People shall be very willing on the day of your power. And this would happen when God would send forth the Scepter of His strength out of Zion, as it stands in *verse 2.* You know what Hushai said of David *2 Sam. 17:8.* He and his men were heroes, and bitter of spirit like a Bear that is robbed of her cubs in the field. And yet he who is weak shall be as David. Deodatus <note>Giovanni Diodati (1576–1649), an Italian Protestant theologian famous for his Bible translation.</note> brings this promise to the beginning of the Gospel / and likewise Cartwright <note>Thomas Cartwright (c. 1535–1603), an influential English Puritan scholar.</note>. That is the second reason.

3. The Lord did this to bring a greater honor upon the Gospel : and to awaken the worthiness of it in the hearts of the people; for had the Gospel had but a few conversions / and had it had but little fruit upon the first proclamation of the same / the people would not [so...]

4. This happened because of the clarity of the Gospel's teaching, which surpassed that of the Law. The Gospel was now preached more clearly according to the people's capacity than it had been in the time of the Law. Although it is true that the Gospel was preached purely in the time of the Law as far as its substance is concerned, it was nonetheless not as clear as in the times of the Gospel. For the Law is nothing other than an obscure Gospel, and the Gospel nothing other than a clear Law. The Law was hidden and covered under dark shadows and types: but the Gospel was clear and excellent. You have this fully presented in 2 Cor. 3:15.

5. Because of that great and glorious liberty which the Gospel brings to them above the Law; I do not mean a fleshly liberty, but a Christian and holy, an Evangelical liberty. Thus, Baptism was established in place of Circumcision. Our Savior made this presentation: "Come to me, all you who labor and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest," (Matt. 11:28). This passage must not only be understood as laboring under the burden of sin, but also under the burden and yoke of the ceremonial law, under all those costly, difficult, and laborious services laid upon them: which were "a yoke which neither they nor their fathers were able to bear," as Peter speaks of Circumcision in Acts 15:10. And so you have the reasons for the prosperity and fruitfulness of the Gospel in the days of John. And this is sufficient regarding the first question.

<margin>2nd Question. Why is the Gospel now not as fruitful as in former times?</margin>
The second Question is this: How does it happen that the ministry of the Word is not as fruitful now as in the days of its first proclamation? I answer: many reasons can be given. Some regarding the Minister, some regarding the people.

<margin>Reasons, 1. With respect to the Minister. Reason.</margin>
1. With respect to the Minister, and there are five:

<margin>2 Sam. 23:4.</margin>
1. Because the Ministers are not as powerful in preaching, nor as edifying in life and being as John was (John 5:35). He was a burning and a shining light. There was his zeal in preaching; there was the holiness of his conduct (Luke 1:16). "And he shall turn many of the children of Israel to the Lord their God. And he shall go before them in the spirit and power of Elijah, to turn the hearts of the fathers to the children, and the disobedient to the wisdom of the just," etc. Nazianzenus <note>Gregory of Nazianzus, a 4th-century Church Father.</note> said of Basil that he thundered with his teaching and shone with his life.

<margin>3rd Reason. <note>The source text has 3. before 2. in the margin, or misnumbered these points.</note></margin>
<margin>2nd Reason.</margin>
<margin>Mark 1:1, verse 3.</margin>
2. Ministers do not preach the Gospel as purely and perfectly as John did (Mark 1:1). John preached the Gospel of Jesus Christ (verse 3). He preached repentance and the forgiveness of sins. Although John brought in the Evan-

gelium, <note>The Gospel.</note> nevertheless he urged, with all his might, the duties owed; and he did not cast down the duties; he pressed the duties and did not dismiss them; he earnestly urged the duties of the moral law; he preached repentance. In contrast, many Ministers nowadays consider it but a legal and servile work, not fit for Christians under the Gospel to be urged, <note>original: "ghepuyckt," meaning to be singled out or emphasized.</note> not fit for Ministers to preach, or for the people to hear. And this is a major reason why people take such sinful liberty to follow their own ways and lusts, and by which means the Gospel becomes less fruitful. But you see that this was far from John's meaning, constitution, or temperament: for, he says, "Repent, for the Kingdom of Heaven is at hand" (Matt. 3:2). "O you generation of vipers, how shall you escape the damnation of hell?" Such was our Savior’s language in Matt. 23:33, Jer. 23:22.

It weakens and emasculates the power of the Word to have it mixed with falsehood. Much truth is preached in the Church of Rome; nevertheless, conversion is not common among them, because they obscure the truth with many errors.

<margin>Matt. 7:29.</margin>
The Scribes did little good through their preaching because they introduced so many groundless traditions, which they taught without any power or authority (Matt. 7:29). Christ taught as one who had authority, and not as the Scribes.

Many Preachers are like Heraclitus, <note>A Greek philosopher known for his cryptic, paradoxical statements, earning him the nickname "The Obscure."</note> who was called the dark or murky Doctor; they love high observations, obscure expressions, and strange ways of speaking—not making difficult matters clear, but making clear matters difficult.

followed in John’s footsteps, and the Apostles agreed more perfectly with one another and persevered in the teaching of their predecessors. But now in our time, the Ministers are divided; one preaches one thing, and another preaches another; and this greatly disturbs the minds of the people, making them heedless toward the Word, and so the Gospel becomes unfruitful.

2. This comes on account of the people, and that for four reasons:

<margin>
2 With respect to the people.
1st Reason.
</margin>
1. The people now call the Ministry and the Calling of the Ministers into doubt more than they did the Ministry of John. Matthew 21:26, *All men held John to be a Prophet.* The reason why Paul’s Ministry was unfruitful to many of the Corinthians was this: because they disputed his calling. Therefore, he continually labors in the Epistle to vindicate his Apostolic power and to uphold it. This doubt diminishes that fear, that awe and majesty, which ought to be in men alongside the Word. Just as, on the contrary, the reason why Paul’s ministry was so fruitful to the Thessalonians was this: because when they received the Word of God, they received it not as the word of men, but (as it is in truth) as the word of God, which also works in those who believe.

<margin>1 Thess. 2:13.</margin>
1 Thessalonians 2:13. I know that some call the lawfulness of our ministry into doubt on this basis: that miracles do not accompany our preaching as they did at the first proclamation of the Gospel. But this is not a valid reason, and (so that I may remove this hindrance to the fruit of the Gospel) I shall briefly refute it.

<margin>
Matt. 21:25, 26.
John 10:41.
Miracles are not to be multiplied without necessity. <note>original Latin: "Miracula non sunt multiplicanda sine necessitate."</note>
1 Cor. 1:22
1 Cor. 14:22.
</margin>
1. John had his calling from Heaven, Matthew 21:25, 26, and yet John performed no miracle, John 10:41.

2. Miracles are not as necessary now as they were at the first planting of the Gospel. There was then a greater need for miracles so that the people in those days might pay attention to the Ministry. *The Jews requested a sign,* 1 Corinthians 1:22. 1 Corinthians 14:22: *tongues are for a sign, not to those who believe, but to the unbelievers, but prophecy is not for the unbeliever, but for those who believe.*

<margin>2 Cor. 12:12.</margin>
3. Miracles were signs of Apostleship, but not of the regular Ministry of Ministers, 2 Corinthians 12:12. *The signs of an Apostle were shown among you, with signs, and wonders, and powers.* Timothy and Titus could perform no miracles, yet no one doubted their authority. Thus, the lack of miracles does not at all nullify the power of the Ministry. So I have removed the first obstacle to the fruit of the Gospel in our days.

<margin>2nd Reason.</margin>
That is the first reason. The long duration of the Word makes it unfruitful (such is the corruption of men’s hearts). The nature of man tends toward new things, and over a long period of time, the love of men for God’s Word is forgotten; thus, the people gathered at first to the Gospel like doves to the windows, yet afterward they became careless and negligent in God’s Commandments. The Manna was loved at first, but afterward the Israelites became weary of it, and they loathed it. Many people become weary of Christ and the Gospel.

<column-break/>

Another reason is because Discipline, or <term>Church-discipline</term><note>The author uses "Kercke-tucht," referring to the formal system of oversight and correction used by elders to maintain the purity of the church.</note>, is not joined together with the Doctrine. The Church is the Garden of God; the Lord is the flowers of this Garden; Discipline is the hedge or the fence. Neither Christ nor John the Baptist intended by their coming to nullify the government of the Church among the Jews, and when it was cast down, Christ established another in its place. Now see, just as it is in a State—long periods of government generate many "State-heresies," if I may call them that: mutations, riots, and parties among the people, breaking the peace of the Land. So it is in the Church; when the reins of government are long left loose, errors and disorders enter in, and the good seed is smothered by those means.

4. This comes from the misuse of the solemn duties of households. The reason why the Reformation in Germany was so excellent was that the <term>Catechizing</term><note>A systematic method of teaching Christian doctrine through questions and answers, often used for children and new converts.</note> of the people accompanied Luther's preaching. It was laid upon the masters of households as a duty that they must instruct their children, Deuteronomy 6:6, 7. *And these words, which I command you this day, shall be in your heart, and you shall sharpen them upon your children, and speak of them when you sit in your house, &c.*

People do not second their Minister's preaching with this solemn duty of command: that God would sanctify the preached Word to their souls and make it fruitful. It is a noteworthy passage which you find in Mark 4:24: *Take heed what you hear; with what measure you mete, it shall be measured to you, and to you who hear, [more] shall be given.*

Sometimes this manner of speaking is applied to the hasty judging of someone, Matthew 7:2. Sometimes to works of mercy, but here it is used as an argument to rouse the people to prepare their hearts to hear God’s Word with care and conscience. For if it is your care to make yourself fit for the Word, and to fix it in your hearts, and to practice it in your life, God will then measure the same back to you through His blessing of the Word, to the salvation and building up of your souls; whereas the neglect of this solemn duty is a great cause why the Word is not as fruitful now as it was in former times.

### MATTHEW XI. verse 12.

> And from the days of John the Baptist until now, the kingdom of heaven suffers violence, and the violent take it by force.

The doctrinal part being finished, we now come to the application. And this [teaching] may now be profitable to us in several respects. 1. For reproof. 2. For comfort. 3. For instruction. 4. For warning. And 5. for the awakening of our sluggishness.

1. This shall reprove various kinds of persons. I shall draw ten arrows of rebuke from this <term>quiver</term><note>The author uses the Dutch "Pijlkoocker," a standard metaphor in Puritan preaching for a series of sharp, targeted rebukes.</note> that may pierce and wound the hearts of ten different kinds of men.

There are few of whom it can be said, after a long profession of religion, as it was said of Moses <margin>Deut. 34:7.</margin> in Deuteronomy 34:7: *His eye was not dim, nor his natural force abated.* Many are like King Asa; their end is worse than their beginning.

8. This reprimands those who content themselves with moderation in matters of religion; those who reckon a drop of fervor <note>The original Dutch uses "phers," likely a variant of "fervor." This refers to a famous saying by the Puritan Richard Greenham regarding the balance of zeal and wisdom.</note> enough for a talent of discretion, as Mr. Greenham says. Many people are of the opinion that religion is dangerous, and that a "holy violence" in the service of God is accompanied by troubles and perils, and therefore it is best to be moderate in God’s service. There are many such people in our days; otherwise, religion would never have come to such a low ebb as it is now. It was the saying of one man that people might be religious, but then they must not be too zealous: they must not be too intense in the ways of God, for then they are called men of hot and furious spirits. People (as it appears) must not love religion too much. Amama <note>Sixtinus Amama (1593–1629), a Dutch Reformed theologian and Hebraist.</note> notes that Tarnovium <note>Paul Tarnow (1562–1633), a Lutheran theologian.</note> describes a sort of people who introduced a sentiment which he calls a "New Gospel": that if a person performs the outward duties of the service of God—if he goes to church, hears God’s word, prays, etc.—it is enough for salvation. Gallio was of this opinion <margin>Acts 18:17.</margin> in Acts 18:17; Gallio cared for none of these things. A little godliness is enough. Most of the great and "political" men of the world are of this opinion, which God shall one day reckon as a Laodicean lukewarmness <note>A reference to the church in Laodicea (Revelation 3:16), famously rebuked for being neither hot nor cold.</note> or a fearful faint-heartedness. The geographers who write of the situation of England say that it lies between the hot and cold sun, being neither hot nor cold; I wish that our hearts were not like our land.

9. This reprimands those who show more violence outwardly than they have inwardly.

There are many people who will hear sermons on the Lord’s Day and on weekdays, and speak well of the service of God and of the ways and people of God; but if you look upon them in their households and in their private chambers, you shall find them to be of another nature. These people are like pepper: hot in the mouth but cold in the stomach. I may compare such to a pot boiling over the fire: hot at the top, but cold at the bottom. So are some people boiling hot in their speech, but their hearts are cold and frozen. Just as it is with people sick with a fever: the face and hands and the outward parts of the body burn, while the heart shivers and has a chill.

10. This reprimands those who remain dull and sluggish in the service of God all their lives, who, like the horses of wagoners, keep to their common pace; they will not go beyond their set place. They are like dromedaries, swift in the ways of sin, but like the sluggish donkey, lazy in the ways of God. The firstborn of other animals had to be offered to God, but <margin>Exod. 13:13.</margin> not the firstborn of a donkey, Exodus 13:13. *And every firstling of a donkey you shall*

<column-break/>

*redeem with a lamb; and if you will not redeem it, then you shall break its neck;* this is to signify that from sluggish and obstinate hearts, the best services are not acceptable to God. The snail is reckoned among the unclean creatures <margin>Levit. 11:30.</margin> in Leviticus 11:30. Hearts that are of this dull disposition are unclean and hateful in the sight of God. And this much shall serve as a reprimand.

2. This doctrine is useful for **comfort**, namely: 1. To the Minister. 2. To the Hearers.

1. To the Ministers; and for this, there are three reasons.

1. Although there is matter of difficulty here, nevertheless there is no fear of guilt, provided you perform your duty faithfully, even if it is not fruitful. <margin>Ezek. 3:19.</margin> Ezekiel 3:19 says: *If you warn the wicked, and he does not turn from his wickedness, nor from his wicked way, he shall die in his iniquity; but you have delivered your soul.* <margin>Acts 20:26.</margin> In Acts 20:26, when Paul had used his utmost diligence at Ephesus, he vindicates or clears himself thus: *I testify to you this holy day, that I am pure from the blood of all men.* <margin>Acts 18:6.</margin> In Acts 18:6, when Paul preached to the Jews and they would not obey the Gospel, *he shook his clothes, and said to them, Your blood be upon your own heads; I am clean: from now on I will go to the Gentiles.* Even if a Minister ploughed all his life as if upon a rock and sowed in the sand, and spent his strength in vain, nonetheless no guilt shall hang upon a Minister’s conscience: for although it is the Minister’s dutiful obligation to preach the Word, yet it is God’s work to convert the soul.

2. God rewards the Ministers according to their labor, not according to the fruit. <margin>2 Cor. 2:15.</margin> 2 Corinthians 2:15: *For we are unto God a sweet savor of Christ, in those who are saved, and in those who perish.*

The father pays the wet-nurse, even if the child dies. The apothecary’s bill must be paid, even if the patient dies. Likewise, God will reward the Ministers, even if the outcome or success does not answer to their efforts. <margin>Isa. 49:4.</margin> Isaiah 49:4: *But I said, I have labored in vain, I have spent my strength for nothing and in vain; yet surely my right is with the Lord, and my work with my God;* or, the reward of my work.

3. The word creates life in the hearts of the hearers even when the Minister is dead. <margin>John 4:36.</margin> John 4:36: *He who reaps receives wages, and gathers fruit unto life eternal, that both he who sows and he who reaps may rejoice together.* And herein is that saying true: *One sows, and another reaps.* Just as a godless person does harm after his death, so a good man does good. <margin>2 Kings 23:2.</margin> 2 Kings 23:2 <note>Likely referring to the broader narrative of Josiah's reforms.</note>. Jeroboam’s godlessness was a snare to Israel in the days of Josiah, which was 360 years after his death. And David’s example did good to Josiah 430 years later; <margin>2 Kings 22:2.</margin> 2 Kings 22:2: *Josiah did that which was right in the sight of the Lord: and walked in all the way of his father David.*

Although (Luke 8:8) the seed that fell into good soil is said to bear a hundredfold, nevertheless (Matthew 13:23) the types of ground differ, and some brought forth only sixty, and some only thirty.

Christ has lambs in His stable as well as sheep, and young children in His house as well as strong men.

2. It may be that what is lacking in a hasty and short-lived zeal of the spirit is made up for in its condition or firmness. Apple trees <note>The original Dutch *Epele-boomen* is an archaic spelling of *Appelboomen* (apple trees).</note> do not grow as fast as willow trees, but they become firmer.

The true buds of grace are accepted. And how this must comfort weak Christians and encourage them to grow with the increase of God, and to obtain more of this "holy violence" <term>holy violence: a 17th-century term for intense spiritual fervor and persistent effort in faith</term> for heavenly things. (Matthew 12:20): *A bruised reed He shall not break, and a smoking flax He shall not quench, until He brings forth judgment unto victory.* He speaks there of the newly converted holy desires and godly resolutions in a poor soul; even though they only smoke and do not yet burn, nonetheless Jesus Christ will not extinguish them until the time He has brought forth judgment unto victory—by which He means, until they come to be perfect men and women in Christ Jesus.

### MATTHEW 11:12.

<margin>
3rd Sermon at St. Lawrence Jewry <note>A historic Anglican church in the City of London.</note> within London, April 29, 1649.
</margin>
*And from the days of John the Baptist until now, the kingdom of heaven suffereth violence, and the violent take it by force.*

<margin>
3rd Use.
Instruction.
</margin>
For the third time, this doctrine can serve for instruction regarding several things: 1. The nature of this holy violence. 2. The necessity of it. 3. The discovery of it. 4. The differences between a stubborn or headstrong violence and a holy violence.

<margin>
1. What is the nature of this violence?
</margin>
1. Question: If you ask, what is the nature of this holy violence?

I answer: 1. It is a full and strong impulse of a person's desires, affections, and contemplations toward Jesus Christ in the Gospel, so that no difficulties or discouragements, of whatever kind they may be, shall draw him away from following Christ in His commandments.

<margin>
*1 Kings 23:1.* <note>The citation likely refers to a specific verse on zeal, though the numbering may vary by edition.</note>
2. The necessity of it.
</margin>
2. Regarding the necessity of this violence, it appears in five respects: 1. In regard to God. 2. In regard to ourselves. 3. In regard to the Devil. 4. In regard to other men. 5. In regard to Heaven itself.

<margin>
1. In regard to God.
*Rom. 12:11.*
</margin>
1. In regard to God (Ecclesiastes 9:10): *Whatever your hand finds to do, do it with your might.* God demands this from your hands. (Romans 12:11): *Not slothful in business; fervent*

<column-break/>

*in spirit; serving the Lord.* The words mean "boiling in spirit" <note>The author is likely referencing the Greek *zeontes*, which literally means to boil or seethe.</note>.

<margin>
2. In regard to ourselves.
</margin>
2. In regard to ourselves, and for these reasons:

1. We have strong temptations against us; our affections must be equal to our temptations. If our affections are not strong, how can we withstand strong temptation? Shall we not be as diligent and zealous to save our souls as the Devil is to damn them? Satan attacks the soul with cruel and furious assaults.

2. We have been zealous enough in the ways of sin: show as much zeal in the ways of God as you can, and when you have done it all, it will not be comparable to your previous labor and zeal practiced in the ways of sin (Romans 6:19): *For just as you presented your members as slaves to uncleanness, and of iniquity unto iniquity; even so now present your members as slaves to righteousness unto holiness.* There are three "To's" <note>The author notes that in the English translation of Romans 6:19, the word "to" (Dutch: *tot*) appears three times regarding sin: *to* uncleanness, *to* iniquity, and *unto* (to) iniquity. For God's service, it appears only twice: *to* righteousness and *unto* (to) holiness.</note> in the expression of the service of sin: to uncleanness, to iniquity, and unto iniquity; but in the service of God there are only two: to righteousness and unto holiness. This is to make known that we were more inclined to our former sins than we are now to grace; the reason is that then there was nothing but sin in the soul, while now there is <unclear>something</unclear> else besides grace—a stream of corruption to withstand it. We must be as strong in the good as we were in the evil. The same word which means "to persecute" (Acts 26:11) is used to express our earnest devotion toward Heaven (Philippians 3:14) <note>Original: *diōkō*, used for both "persecute" and "press toward the mark."</note>.

<margin>
*Rom. 6:19.*
*Acts 26:11.*
*Phil. 3:14.*
3. In regard to the Devil.
*1 Pet. 5:8.*
</margin>
3. In regard to the Devil. He has strong temptations and promptings (1 Peter 5:8): *Be sober, be vigilant; because your adversary the devil, as a roaring lion, walketh about, seeking whom he may devour.* 1. He is said to be an adversary. Now, an adversary will take all opportunities to your harm and will always watch for them. 2. He is a lion, not a lamb; a lion—a wild, cruel, and furious creature. 3. He is not a sleeping lion, but a roaring lion. 4. Not a stationary lion, satisfied with the prey once he has caught it, but constantly trotting after more: he is not satisfied with what he has caught; although he has been wandering about since Adam's fall, he still goes about constantly to obtain more; he labors to fill hell with souls. 5. He seeks whom he may devour. The Devil watches, and do you sleep? <note>original: "Vigilat Diabolus & tu dormis."</note>

<margin>
*The Devil watches and you sleep.*
4. In regard to other men, and evil men.
</margin>
4. In regard to other men, whether they be evil or good.

1. In regard to evil men.

1. Notice they are violent against the truth; and will you not be as powerful and violent in the confession of the Gospel as their oppositions are against it? As Zeno <note>Likely Zeno of Elea or Zeno of Citium; a common trope in 17th-century sermons regarding steadfastness.</note> said to one of his good acquaintances who was pressured to give false testimony against another and walked in secret because he wanted to avoid the man who sought to bring him to false testimony: "Oh," said Zeno, "shall he not be ashamed of the sin, and will you be ashamed to set yourself against the sin?"

<header>The Zealous Christian.</header>

<margin>

he rushes in like a flooding water <note>original Latin: "irruit more inundanti equæ"</note>
