<meta>This page continues the catechism on the Lord's Prayer, specifically focusing on the Sixth Petition: "And lead us not into temptation." The previous page concluded the Fifth Petition regarding the forgiveness of debts. Here, the author examines why God permits temptation and how a believer should respond to it.</meta>

->### Practical Theology. 811<-
Ppp 4
<meta>catchword: 3. He</meta>

2. That we venture so boldly into the opportunities of sin; when we tempt the devil to tempt us, it is right for God to abandon us in that temptation.

3. When people think that they fight against a temptation through their own power and strength, God desires to let them be defeated by the temptation, so that they may see their own weakness.

4. When God sees that people are proud of their gifts and graces, He commonly punishes that pride with a fall.

5. When the Lord God sees that people judge harshly the Saints who are sometimes overcome by a temptation, God shall—to stop their mouths—let them fall so that they may see that they are surely as incapable as the weakest of resisting temptation if God withdraws His help.

**Question.** From whence do temptations come?
**Answer.** Either from the Devil; or from the evil heart of man, or from the world.

**Question.** How does the Devil tempt us?
**Answer.** 1. By showing us the apparent pleasure of sin, and not the certain sorrow that shall follow it.

2. By presenting to us the profit of sin, just as the Devil did to Christ when he tempted Him; for he said that he would give Him all the glory of the World if He would fall down and worship him. <note>Matthew 4, verse 6. In modern bibles, this specific offer is usually verse 9.</note>

**Question.** How does the heart of man tempt him to sin?
**Answer.** 1. It will make him believe that small sins are no sins; therefore (says the heart) you may freely commit them.

2. It will tell you that great sins are only small sins.

3. It will tell you that the great sin to which you are tempted can coexist with grace; if all these temptations do not prevail over the heart, and the Soul sees that it is no small but a great sin which cannot coexist with grace, then the heart approaches with a fourth temptation, namely:

4. The heart will tell you that you will surely have repentance after the commission of this or that sin; and this temptation often prevails.

**Question.** How shall a man be able to distinguish a temptation that comes from the Devil from another that comes from a man’s own evil heart?

**Answer.** 1. The Devil's temptations are for the most part against nature, such as to stab, drown, or hang oneself, which strives against nature; for nature seeks its own preservation. But those temptations which spring from the heart are commonly more delightful and pleasant to the flesh.

2. The temptations of the Devil are always violent; they come and pass away quickly. But those coming from the corrupt heart remain in the Soul for a long time.

**Question.** What is there in this world that tempts a man to sin?
**Answer.** 1. The advancements to high status in this world. <note>Hebrews 11.</note>
2. The godless people of this world.
3. The pleasures of this world.
4. The profits of this world.

**Question.** What must a man do, when he is tempted to sin, to be able to resist the temptation?

<column-break/>

**Answer.** 1. You must pray that Christ, through His strength, assists you in the struggle.

2. You must resist sin in its first beginnings. <note>James 4:7. Resist the Devil and he shall flee from you.</note> <note>1 Peter 5 verse 9.</note>

3. Avoid all opportunities which might stir up any temptation. <note>Proverbs 3 verse 16. And come not onto the path of the Godless; nor step onto the way of the evil. (Note: This citation matches Proverbs 4:14-15 in most English bibles).</note>

4. Shun all fleshly arguments with Satan.

5. Arm yourself with the whole armor of God, especially with the word of God, the sword of the Spirit, by which you can resist all the fiery arrows of the devil. <note>Ephesians 6.</note>

**Question.** Is a child of God commonly overcome by the temptations of Satan?
**Answer.** Yes.

**Question.** How then shall you distinguish between a Godly and a Godless person, since a graced heart can be overcome by temptations just as well as the Godless?
**Answer.** In these ways:

1. Although a Godly person can be overcome, he nevertheless does not surrender at the first attack; but he has resistance and a struggle against the temptation before he is overcome by it. But a godless person, when he is tempted to sin, runs into the sin like an unbridled horse into battle. <note>Jeremiah 8:6.</note>

2. A Godly person can be overcome by temptations, but he nonetheless has sorrow of heart over yielding to the temptation, and a careful watchfulness to prevent the temptation in the time to come; indeed, he is upset with himself that he has been so base and foolish as to sin against God. But a godless heart seldom conducts itself so.

**Question.** In what danger is a Godly person when he has yielded to a temptation to sin?
**Answer.** 1. He is in danger of being led further and further into the temptation.

2. He is in danger that his clear evidence of going to Heaven shall be darkened, and that he shall lose the assurance of God’s love for his Soul.

3. He is in danger of losing the joy and comfort of the Holy Spirit: sin mists over, darkens, and kills it all.

4. He is in danger that God will give him a great measure of hardness of heart. <note>Hebrews 2:13. Exhort one another every day, as long as it is called Today, so that no one among you becomes hardened through the deception of sin. (Note: This is Hebrews 3:13 in modern bibles).</note>

5. He is in the danger of making the Gospel, which he confesses, into a cause of offense.

6. He is in danger of bringing outward weaknesses upon himself: for sin brings sorrow with it.

**Question.** What must a Godly person do, if he has been overcome by some temptation, to restore himself?

**Answer.** 1. He must pray that Christ, through His power and strength, helps him out of that temptation.

2. He must quickly put to work all the powers and efforts of his soul to stand up, and not remain lying under the temptation.

3. He must keep a more vigilant watch over his ways.
4. He must deeply humble himself because of the remnants of sin that remain in his soul, which give strength to the Devil’s temptation, and because of his own acceptance of the temptation.
**Question.** What do you ask of God in the remainder of the sixth petition, *but deliver us from the evil one*?
**Answer.** That the Lord God would deliver me from that evil one—the Devil—and from those evil works that proceed from him, and even from the evil of punishment, if God deems it good for me. 2 Corinthians 12, verse 9.
**Question.** What is the conclusion of the Lord's Prayer?
**Answer.** These are the words: *For thine is the kingdom and the power and the glory, forever, Amen.*
**Question.** What do you learn from the fact that the conclusion of the Prayer does not appear in Luke as it does in Matthew (as seen by comparing Luke 11:3–4 with Matthew 6:13), and that even the manner of prescribing the prayer is different—for in Matthew it says, *pray thus: Our Father etc.*, and in Luke it says, *say: Our Father etc.*? What do you notice from all this?
**Answer.** I observe from this that the Lord Jesus has not bound me to specific words in praying, but that He leaves me the freedom to express my needs to God in my own words.
**Question.** From where is the conclusion of the Lord’s Prayer taken?
**Answer.** It is taken from 1 Chronicles 29:11.
**Question.** What does this conclusion contain within itself?
**Answer.** 1. A reason why I pray: 1 Chronicles 29:11, 13.
2. A confidence that I shall be heard, for God is a God of power.
3. That the glory of God must be the end <note>The word "end" here means the ultimate goal or purpose.</note> of all my prayers.
**Question.** What do you learn from this, that you ascribe a Kingdom to God?
**Answer.** 1. That God is the supreme Ruler of Heaven and earth. Genesis 14:19.
2. That we are all God's subjects, and that He shall protect us from all our enemies.
3. That He shall bring those who are submissive to His laws to His eternal Kingdom. Hebrews 5:9. *Christ having been made perfect, became the author of eternal salvation to all those who obey Him.*
**Question.** What do you learn from this, that you ascribe power to God?
**Answer.** 1. That God may do whatever He wills, and that all the power I have is from God. 2 Corinthians 3:5. *Not that we are sufficient of ourselves to think anything as of ourselves; but our sufficiency is of God.* Hebrews Chapter 13, Verse 21. *May God make you perfect in every good work to do His will, working in you that which is well-pleasing*

<column-break/>

*in His sight, through Jesus Christ.*
**Question.** What do you learn from this, that you ascribe glory to God?
**Answer.** 1. That after the best prayer I have ever performed, I deserve no praise or glory, but God alone.
2. That I must desire nothing from the Lord God except that which serves His glory and honor; that this must be my objective. Colossians 3:17. *Whatever you do in word or deed, do all in the name of the Lord Jesus, giving thanks to God and the Father through Him.* John 14:23. Jeremiah 33:2.
3. That the glory of the Lord is the true reason and motive why all our prayers are heard.
**Question.** What is understood by this last little word, *Amen*?
**Answer.** 1. Sometimes it is used as a name and title of Christ, to point out His faithfulness and truth in fulfilling the promises. Revelation 3:14. *These things says the Amen, the faithful and true witness, the beginning of the creation of God.* 2 Corinthians 1:20 <note>The original text cites 23, but it refers to 1:20</note>. *For all the promises of God in Him are Yes, and in Him Amen.*
2. At the beginning of a statement, it is used for a stronger confirmation. John 6:26. *Truly, truly <note>Original: "Voorwaer voorwaer"</note> I say to you, you seek Me, not because you saw the signs, but because you ate of the loaves and were filled.*
3. When it is placed at the end of a prayer, it signifies a desire that a matter may happen so, and a confidence that it shall happen. Numbers 5:22. 1 Corinthians 14:16. Or it means: *Let it be so, so be it.*

### Concerning Original Sin

**Question.** How many kinds of sin are there?
**Answer.** Two kinds: <term>original sin</term> <note>Inherited sin from birth</note> and <term>actual sin</term> <note>Sins committed through one's own actions</note>.
**Question.** What is original sin, or the sin of my nature?
**Answer.** It is an inclination toward all evil, and an aversion to all good.
**Question.** Why is this sin of nature called "original sin"?
**Answer.** 1. Because it was in the first man.
2. Because it is in me from my origin <note>Meaning from the very beginning of life/conception</note>.
**Question.** How did you come by original sin?
**Answer.** Through the fall of Adam.
**Question.** Why do you have that sin through Adam’s fall?
**Answer.** 1. Because I was in Adam, and descended from him.
2. Because Adam was established as a <term>representative person</term> <note>Dutch: "alghe-meen persoon," a legal or federal representative for a group</note>, so that all his descendants would stand or fall with him: if Adam had remained standing, I would have been safe and blessed; but now I am rightfully miserable and deformed by his fall.
**Question.** Which is Adam’s sin?
**Answer.** Disobedience to God’s command in eating the fruit of the tree of the knowledge of good and evil.
**Question.** Who tempted Adam?
**Answer.** Eve.
**Question.** Who tempted Eve?
**Answer.** The Devil in the form of a Serpent.
**Question.** What moved the Devil to seduce Eve?

**Answer.** The enmity of his nature against man's happiness, since he was already fallen, he desired that all men, like himself, should become miserable.

**Question.** What is your misery by nature?

**Answer.** I am a child of God's wrath, a child of the Devil, worthy of eternal damnation. Ephesians 2:2.

**Question.** Where is the sin of nature?

**Answer.** In all the powers of my Soul, and in all the parts of my body.

**Question.** In which powers of your Soul is sin spread?

**Answer.** In my understanding, memory, will, heart, Conscience, and affections.

**Question.** What sin is by nature in your understanding?

**Answer.** Ignorance. Ephesians Chapter 4:18. *darkened in the understanding.* 1 Corinthians 2:14. *The natural man <note>In 17th-century theology, the 'natural man' refers to a person in their fallen state, before being changed by God's grace.</note> does not understand the things that are of the Spirit of God: for they are foolishness to him, and he cannot understand them, because they are spiritually discerned.*

**Question.** How do you distinguish the ignorance that is in the understanding of a natural man from that ignorance which is in a converted man?

**Answer.** The ignorance of a godless person is a foolish ignorance, Jeremiah 4:22. *My people are foolish: they do not know me, they are silly children; and they are not wise: they are wise to do evil, but to do good they know not.*

2. It is a willful ignorance; he is ignorant, and he hates knowledge. Proverbs 1:22.

3. It is an unbelieving ignorance; he is blind even when he thinks he sees; he is ignorant even though he boasts of knowledge.

**Question.** What does God do in your understanding when He renews your nature?

**Answer.** He takes away the ignorance of my understanding, and He gives me the knowledge of His blessed will.

**Question.** What sin is by nature in the memory?

**Answer.** A capacity to forget everything good and to remember everything evil.

**Question.** What remedies could be prescribed for the memory?

**Answer.** 1. Fix your meditations firmly on heavenly things; through this, those things will remain fixed in the memory.

2. I must pray for the Spirit of Christ, who has promised that He will bring forgotten things to mind. <note>original: "het vergetene ſal indachtig maecken" - a reference to John 14:26</note>

3. I must listen diligently when I hear God's word taught and give no place to my wandering thoughts.

**Question.** When God works grace in the heart, what does He do in the memory?

**Answer.** He makes it able to remember the things of God and forget all the flickering vanities of this world.

**Question.** What sin is there by nature in the Will?

**Answer.** Resistance, so that it will not do God's will. John 5 verse 40 <note>The text cites verse 43, but the quote "You will not come to me" is from verse 40.</note>. *You will not come to me, that you might have life:* Ezekiel 3:7. *The house of Israel will not listen to you, because they will not listen to me: for the whole house of Israel is stiff-necked and hard-hearted.*

**Question.** When God changes nature, what does He do in the will?

**Answer.** He takes the resistance from the

<column-break/>

will away; He gives me a willing Spirit to obey His blessed will in everything.

**Question.** What sin is by nature in the heart?

**Answer.** Hardness.

**Question.** Can a child of God also have hardness of heart in him?

**Answer.** Yes.

**Question.** How then will you distinguish it from the hardness that is in an unregenerate person?

**Answer.** 1. A godly person is sensitive to the hardness of his heart; he complains about it, he is humbled by it, he prays against it; but a natural man has a hard heart, but he neither sees nor weeps over it, nor is he humbled by it.

2. A godly person exerts all the powers of his soul to be delivered from the hardness of his heart; he cries out with the Church: *Lord, why do you harden our hearts so that we do not fear you?* Isaiah 63:17.

**Question.** What does God do in the heart when He works grace within it?

**Answer.** He takes away the hardness and gives me a sensitive, soft, and inclined heart. Ezekiel 36:26. *I will give you a new heart, and I will put a new spirit within you; and I will take away the stony heart out of your flesh, and I will give you a heart of flesh.*

**Question.** What sin is by nature in the Conscience?

**Answer.** Insensitivity, so that a person cannot sensitively fear the sin committed and the deserved wrath of God. Ephesians 4:18, 19.

**Question.** What does God do in the Conscience when He changes your nature?

**Answer.** He takes away the insensitivity and gives me such a Conscience that is sensitive to sin and does its duty in rebuking me for every sin I commit. Romans 2:15.

**Question.** What sin is there by nature in the <term>affections or inclinations</term><note>The original Dutch 'herts-tochten' refers to the passions or driving forces of the heart.</note>?

**Answer.** Disorderliness.

**Question.** In what does this disorderliness appear?

**Answer.** In loving the sin that I ought to hate, and in hating God whom I ought to love.

**Question.** How many affections are there?

**Answer.** Six: love, hate, joy, sorrow, hope, fear.

**Question.** What does God do to these affections when He changes your nature?

**Answer.** He sets them upon their right object: namely, my love upon God, my hate upon sin, my joy in God, in His ways, in His service and people, my sorrow upon the sin committed and that God is dishonored thereby, my hope upon Heaven and God's favor, my fear upon God and my own heart.

**Question.** What difference is there between the love a godly person has for God and that delusional and apparent love in a hypocrite?

**Answer.** The love that a godly person bears for God makes him do and suffer much for God.

**Question.** What difference is there between the hate of sin in the godly and that apparent hate of sin in a godless person?

**Answer.** 1. The godly hate sin because of the evil that is in it; but the godless hate sin because of the deserved punishment.

<summary>This page presents a detailed catechism on the corruption of the human soul through original sin, systematically examining how each faculty—understanding, memory, will, heart, conscience, and affections—is distorted by nature and restored through divine grace.</summary>

<meta>This page continues the discussion on the transformation of the soul's faculties through grace, transitioning from the renewal of the understanding (from the previous page) to the specific hatred of sin and the joy found in a godly life, before beginning a detailed exposition of the Ten Commandments.</meta>

2. The hatred of sin in a <term>godly person<note>Dutch: *Godtsalighe*. Refers to a person living in a state of grace and devotion.</note></term> is universal against all sin and is irreconcilable; <unclear>never</unclear> does he wish to come into love or agreement with sin again.

**Question.** What difference is there between the joy of a godless person and that of a godly person?

**Answer.** 1. The joy of the godly is a firm, spiritual joy, grounded in the perception of spiritual privileges and of God’s favor in Christ.

2. It is such a joy that it consumes all fleshly and sensory joy.

**Question.** What difference is there between the sorrow in a heart touched by grace and that which can be in a godless person?

**Answer.** 1. True sorrow is more over the sin itself than over the punishment.

2. True sorrow is over small, muffled, and inward evils, but the sorrow of a godless person is only over outward, great evils. So much has been said concerning the sin of your nature; I proceed to speak of <term>actual sin<note>Dutch: *daelijcke* or *daedtlycke sonde*. In theology, this distinguishes specific sinful acts from 'original sin' (the fallen state of human nature).</note></term>.

---

### ->Of actual sin, or of the Ten Commandments in general.<-

**Question.** What is sin?
**Answer.** Sin is a transgression of the law, or a breaking of one of God’s commandments; 1 John 3:4.

**Question.** How many commandments are there?
**Answer.** Ten.

**Question.** To whom were the commandments given?
**Answer.** To Moses.

**Question.** In what place?
**Answer.** On Mount Sinai.

**Question.** In what manner were the commandments given?
**Answer.** With thunder and lightning, storm and tempest; Exodus 19:16, 17, 18.

**Question.** Why in such a manner?
**Answer.** 1. Because He wished to terrify man from the breaking of these commandments.

2. In order that He might show the intensity of His wrath over all those who broke His commandments.

**Question.** By whom were the commandments written?
**Answer.** By the finger of God.

**Question.** Upon what were they written?
**Answer.** Upon two tables of stone.

**Question.** Why on tables of stone?
**Answer.** To signify that they must be eternally enduring.

**Question.** Upon what tables does God now write His laws?
**Answer.** In the hearts of His children. Jeremiah 31:33. *I will put my law in their inward parts, and write it in their hearts; and will be their God, and they shall be my people.* Hebrews 8:10. Proverbs 3:3.

**Question.** In how many tables did God write His law, or the commandments?
**Answer.** In two.

**Question.** How many commandments in the first table?
**Answer.** Four.

**Question.** How many in the second table?
**Answer.** Six.

**Question.** Which words contain the preface to the ten commandments?
**Answer.** God spoke all these words, saying: *I am the Lord your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of bondage.*

**Question.** What does that preface contain?
**Answer.** It contains three reasons why men must keep God’s commandments. Namely:

<column-break/>

1. Because these commandments are given by God Himself, not by Moses; for it says, *God spoke all these words*, and so that no one should say that God only spoke some of these words, it says there that God spoke *all* these words.

2. Because they are not only given by God, but by *our* God: in whom we have right and ownership.

3. Because God had brought about a great deliverance to rescue them from Egyptian slavery; Oh, this ought to bind the heart to break no commandments of God, Exodus 20:2, 4.

**Question.** How does their deliverance from Egypt concern us? We have never been in Egyptian slavery; how then do you set it as a motive to keep God’s commandments?

**Answer.** It concerns us greatly; though we are not Israelites in the letter, we are nonetheless so in the Spirit. Romans 2:29. And their deliverance from Egypt signifies our deliverance in Christ from the power of the devil, of sin, and of death.

**Question.** Which rules must be observed to understand the commandments well?

**Answer.** These: 1. The commandment which forbids a sin commands the directly opposite virtue. Psalm 35:15. *Depart from evil, and do good; seek peace and pursue it.*

2. One must know that the law is spiritual, and that it looks upon the inward as well as the outward man. Romans 7:14.

3. In whichever commandments a sin is forbidden, there also are forbidden the means leading to that sin; and where a virtue or duty is commanded, all the means serving to the promotion of that duty are also commanded.

4. He who breaks one commandment is guilty of all. Colossians 3:10. <note>The citation in the text is Col 3:10, but the quote follows Galatians 3:10 or James 2:10.</note> *Cursed be everyone who does not abide by all things written in the book of the law, to do them.* Deuteronomy 27:26.

5. If two commandments cannot be performed at once, then the lesser must give way to the greater. Hosea 6:6. *I desired mercy, and not sacrifice; and the knowledge of God more than burnt offerings.* Matthew 9:13 <note>The text says Matthew 9:4, but likely refers to 9:13.</note>.

6. The breaking of the commandments of the first table is a greater sin than the breaking of the second table. 1 Samuel 15:23. *Rebellion is as the sin of witchcraft, and stubbornness is as iniquity and idolatry.* Isaiah 7:13. *Is it a small thing for you to weary men, but will you weary my God also?*

7. There is not one sin that is not forbidden in one of these commandments, and not one virtue that is not commanded herein.

8. The commandments concern the female as well as the male gender.

---

### ->Of the First Commandment.<-

**Question.** What is the first commandment?
**Answer.** You shall have no other gods before my face.

**Question.** What is contained in the first commandment?
**Answer.** Four things. Namely: 1. That we must have a God; which condemns the Barbarians <note>In this context, 'Barbarians' refers to those perceived as having no structured religion or knowledge of the true God.</note>.

2. That we must have God for our God.

3. That we must have God alone for our God; which condemns the Samaritans, who served the true God and the idols of the land.

# Practical Theology.

4. That we must have God as our God at all times; which condemns the angels who fell away from the true service of God.
**Question. How does one break this Commandment?**
**Answer.** 1. By not knowing God. **Jeremiah 4:22.** "Surely, my people are foolish, they do not know me; they are sottish children." **Jeremiah 3:34.**
2. By not loving God. **Deuteronomy 32:41.** "I will take vengeance on my adversaries, and will repay those who hate me."
3. By loving <note>The original text "petwes" is likely a typo for "selwes" (selves) or "personen" (persons).</note> oneself above God. **2 Timothy 3:4.** "Lovers of pleasures more than lovers of God." **Philippians 3:19.**
**Question. Which specific sins are forbidden by the power of this Commandment?**
**Answer.** 1. **Atheism** or the denial of God. **Titus 1:16.** "They profess that they know God, but they deny him by their works." **Psalm 41:1.** <note>The author likely refers to Psalm 14:1, "The fool hath said in his heart, There is no God."</note>
2. **Ignorance.** "The Lord has a controversy with the inhabitants of the land, because there is no knowledge of God in the land," says **Hosea 4:1.** See also **Ephesians 2:17** and **Isaiah 1:3.**
3. **Idolatry. Judges 16:23.** "The princes of the Philistines gathered to offer a great sacrifice to their god Dagon," etc.
4. **Unbelief. Jeremiah 17:5.** "Cursed is the man who trusts in man, and makes flesh his arm, and whose heart turns away from the Lord." **Hebrews 10 verse 38.**
5. **Trusting in the creature.** <note>The "creature" here refers to anything created (people, wealth, objects) as opposed to the Creator.</note> **Jeremiah 17:5, 6.**
6. Fearing men more than God. **Revelation 21:8.** "But the fearful, and unbelieving, and the abominable, and murderers, and whoremongers, and sorcerers, and idolaters, and all liars, shall have their part in the lake which burns with fire and sulfur, which is the second death."
7. Placing love or delight in anything above God. **1 Corinthians 16:22.** "If any man does not love the Lord Jesus Christ, let him be anathema, <note>original: "Maranatha." An Aramaic expression meaning "Our Lord comes," used here as a solemn curse.</note> Maranatha." **Mark 10:21, 22.**
**Question. What is commanded by the power of the first Commandment?**
**Answer.** That all the powers and faculties of my soul must be set upon God: Namely,
1. That I must clearly know God with my understanding. **John 17:3.** "This is eternal life, that they might know you, the only true God, and Jesus Christ, whom you have sent." **1 Chronicles 28:9.**
2. That I must heartily love God with my affections. **Deuteronomy 6:5.** "You shall love the Lord your God with all your heart, and with all your soul, and with all your might." **Luke 10; Matthew 5:29, 30.**
3. That I must fear God alone. **Leviticus 19:14.** "You shall fear your God; I am the Lord."
4. That I must trust God in all things. **Psalm 9:10, 11.** "The Lord will be a high tower for the oppressed, and those who know your name will trust in you, for you, Lord, have not forsaken those who seek you." **2 Chronicles 20 verse 20.**

### Of the Second Commandment.

**Question. Which** is the second Commandment?
**Answer.** You shall not make for yourself any graven image, nor any likeness, etc.
**Question. How many things are contained in this Commandment?**

<column-break/>

**Answer.** Two things. 1. That which is forbidden. 2. The reason or motive why it is forbidden, and why we must refrain from it.
**Question. What is forbidden in this Commandment?**
**Answer. First.** In general, all <term>self-willed worship<note>Dutch: *eygenwillige Gods-dienst*. This refers to religious practices invented by human will rather than prescribed by divine scripture.</note></term> which is either invented by others or forged in our own brains, and which is not grounded upon God's word. Some served God under the form of a four-footed beast, like the Egyptians—for Dagon signifies a fish; the Greeks, appearing wiser, served God under the form of a human; but all of this is worthless.
**Answer. Secondly.** The specific sins forbidden by the power of this Commandment are these:
1. The making of images for a religious use. **Leviticus 19:4; Exodus 32:1.** To make an image of God is as if one wished to compare Him to something.
2. To serve God by or before an image. **1 Kings 19:18; 2 Kings 18:4.**
3. To serve God in any way which is not commanded in the Word, even though it may have an appearance of edification and is done with a good intention; nevertheless, if it is not commanded in God's word, it is sinful. **Numbers 15:39, 40; Deuteronomy 12:32; 1 Samuel 15:15; Matthew 23:10; Colossians 2:10.**
4. Consenting to and approving of idolatry through presence, speech, gestures, or silence. **1 Corinthians 10:18; 1 Thessalonians 5:22; Romans 1:31; Deuteronomy 7:25.**
5. Praying with <term>beads<note>Dutch: *koralen*. Literally "corals," referring here to prayer beads or rosaries, which the author considers a superstitious practice.</note></term> or keeping any superstitious customs in order to practice religion. **Isaiah 30:22; Deuteronomy 12:30.**
6. This commandment is broken by binding our presence to a specific time or place. **Numbers 32:28, 29.**
**Question. What difference is there between the first and second Commandment?**
**Answer.** The first commandment concerns God Himself, and the second shows the Way in which this true God must be served.
**Question. How does one break this commandment of God?**
**Answer.** Through all kinds of self-willed worship, such as when I serve God in another way than He has instituted in His word; specifically:
1. When I serve God without knowledge. **1 Corinthians 14:15.** "I will pray with the Spirit, but I will also pray with the understanding."
2. When I serve Him carelessly and out of habit, not out of <term>conscience<note>Dutch: *Conscientie*. Meaning a sincere, inner moral conviction.</note></term>. **Jeremiah 48:10.** "Cursed be he who does the work of the Lord deceitfully."
3. When I serve Him hypocritically without the heart. **Isaiah 29:13.** "This people draws near to me with their mouth, and they honor me with their lips, but they have removed their heart far from me."
4. When I serve Him with <term>superstition<note>Dutch: *over-geloof*. Literally "over-belief," the standard Dutch term for superstition.</note></term> according to the words and traditions of men; as when people bind the service of God to times and places, as if the Church were a holy place and Easter were a holy time.

**Question. Which** is the third commandment?
**Answer.** You shall not use the name of the Lord your God in vain: for the Lord will not hold him guiltless who uses his name in vain.
**Question. How many things are in this commandment?**

# The Marrow of Divinity
<note>original: "Het Mergh van de [Godtheyt]" — a common title for systematic summaries of theology in this period.</note>

<columns>2</columns>

**Answer.** Two things: 1. A command. 2. A punishment.

**Question. What do you understand by the Name of God?**

**Answer.** The name of God is taken to mean God himself, his attributes, his works, and his word.

**Question. How does one use the name of God in vain?**

**Answer.** 1. When one speaks of God without fear and reverence. **Deuteronomy 28:58.** "Fear the glorious and fearful name, the Lord your God"; just as when one says "O God," "O Lord," or "Jesus Christ" in an irreverent manner.

2. When one observes God's works without wonder and gratitude. **Psalm 69:34.** <note>The text cites verse 35, which in some versions corresponds to verse 34's call for praise from heaven and earth.</note>

3. When one hears his word without fruit and growth. **Ezekiel 33:10.**

4. When one curses and swears. **1 Samuel 17:43; Jeremiah 5:2.**

**Question. How many kinds of oaths are there that conflict with this commandment?**

**Answer.** Five kinds, namely: 1. Complimentary and service-offering oaths, such as "by my faith" and "in truth."

2. "Bastard-oaths," <note>Euphemistic or corrupted versions of holy names.</note> such as "by my soul," or "by God," or "Gut" <note>A dialect corruption of "God."</note> which amounts to the same thing.

3. "Country-oaths," such as "by this silver," "by this light," "by this Lord"; these oaths are characteristic of the English Nation.

4. Superstitious oaths, such as saying "by the Mass," "by Saint Anne," or "by our Dear Lady."

5. Blasphemous oaths, such as swearing by the wounds of the Lord, by Christ’s blood, or similar; these are hellish, blasphemous oaths.

**Question. Does this commandment forbid all oaths?**

**Answer.** Yes. "Swear not at all." **Matthew 5:34, 37; James 5:12.** <note>The text cites James 5:20, likely a printer's error for 5:12.</note> All oaths are forbidden, unless one is called to it or there is some other necessity.

**Question. When does one have a lawful calling to swear an oath?**

**Answer.** When people are called before the Authorities to confirm some truth, and when there can be no other way to settle a dispute than through an Oath.

**Question. Which virtues are required by the power of this third commandment?**

**Answer.** 1. That when we speak or make mention of God’s name, we must do so with reverence. **Deuteronomy 28 verse 58; Ecclesiastes 5:1.** <note>The text cites Prediker (Ecclesiastes) 4:17, which is 5:1 in many English Bibles.</note>

2. That we must hear God's word with attention and fruitfulness. **Job 6 verse 27.**

3. That we must walk blamelessly among people in this world. **Philippians 1:27; 1 Peter 3:1, 2.**

4. That we must observe God's work with wonder and gratitude. **Psalm 104:24.**

**Question. What does it mean when it says in the third commandment, "the Lord will not hold him guiltless"?**

**Answer.** I believe that God means to say that He will cast him under the guilt and punishment of the sin; the Lord will not remit it.

**Question. Why does the Lord place a punishment on the breaking of this commandment in particular, and not on the others?**

**Answer.** 1. This shows what special care God has for preserving the glory of his name.

2. Because people have less temptation to this sin of swearing than to any other sins: Now, where the temptation to

<column-break/>

sin is least, there the punishment is greater if the sin be committed.

---

->**Of the Fourth Commandment.**<-

**Question.** **W**hich is the fourth commandment?
**Answer.** Remember the Sabbath day, that you keep it holy, etc.

**Question. Why is this little word, "Remember," placed only before this commandment?**

**Answer.** To show that I am by nature very inclined to forget the duties of the Sabbath.

**Question. How many things are in this commandment?**

**Answer.** 1. A command. 2. A reason why we must obey this command.

**Question. What is the meaning of the word Sabbath?**

**Answer.** It means "rest," to show that I must stop from sin and also from the labor of my lawful calling, which I may well pursue at another time.

**Question. When does the Sabbath begin?**

**Answer.** As soon as the day breaks. **Matthew 28:1.**

**Question. What certainty do you have for keeping this day which you now keep, whereas in the fourth commandment it is commanded to keep the seventh day after creation, which is Saturday?**

**Answer.** The duties of this commandment always retain their power; they require my obedience just as much as that of the people of Israel; but the time has changed, and that by Divine authority, in memory of the great work of mankind's redemption brought about by Jesus Christ. Therefore, I now keep this day; see **John 20:19, 26; Acts 2:1; 1 Corinthians 16 verse 1.**

**Question. Is this fourth commandment not a part of the Ceremonial Law?**

**Answer.** No: for then the law would consist of only nine words <note>The "Ten Words" is a literal translation of the Hebrew name for the Ten Commandments.</note>, whereas it nonetheless consists of ten words. **Deuteronomy 4:13.** <note>The text cites 4:14.</note>

**Question. Is this commandment then Moral, that is, does it still have power and is it not abolished by Christ?**

**Answer.** This commandment is still moral, and it binds all Christians throughout the whole world. **Acts 20:7; 1 Corinthians 16:1, 2; Revelation 1:10.** Moreover, that it is not ceremonial but moral is evident from this: because this law and the other nine were written by the finger of God. **Exodus 31:18.** The law came immediately from God, **Deuteronomy 1:13, 14**, but the ceremonial customs were instituted by Moses.

**Question. It seems that this commandment is done away with, for what else would be the meaning of that passage in Colossians 2:16?**

**Answer.** The Apostle speaks of the Jewish Sabbaths; they observed their Sabbaths of the months and of the years, and their Feast days, calling these "Sabbaths"; and those were indeed abolished by Christ’s coming, but not ours; the Apostle does not speak against the Sabbath in the plural number which the Jews observed.

**Question. What is it to hallow the Sabbath?**

**Answer.** It involves two things:
1. That I must highly honor the Sabbath as the Lord’s day;
2. That I must spend it entirely in the service of God.

**Question. What is the service that God requires on the Sabbath?**

**Answer.** It is threefold: 1. A private service alone. 2. A special service with the family. 3. A general service with the congregation.

# Practical Divinity
<note>original: "Werkige Godtgeleertheyt" — This refers to the application of theological truths to daily Christian living, a hallmark of the "Further Reformation" in the Netherlands.</note>

### Question. What must you do in private to properly sanctify the Sabbath?
**Answer.** 1. I must spend my time in contemplation of the power and greatness of God, who created this world out of nothing, as well as the glorious work of man’s redemption—how voluntary, complete, and unchangeable it is.
2. I must spend it in self-examination: 1. Whether I am fit for the duties of the Sabbath. 2. Whether I have profited from the duties of the Sabbath. 3. If not, that I then search out and consider what those obstacles were, in order to remove them from the path.
3. I must spend it in prayer: 1. That God prepares my heart to hear the Word. 2. That God turns away those intervening wandering thoughts which in any way hinder my advancement through the Word. 3. That God speaks to my heart in particular. 4. That God gives me a hearing ear and an obedient heart to practice what I hear from His Word.

### Question. In what service must households be busy on the Lord’s Day?
**Answer.** The Father of the household must call his family together, and they must practice together, praying, recounting the Word, and singing Psalms.

### Question. What service takes place publicly with the congregation?
**Answer.** Hearing God’s Word preached and joining oneself in spirit with the minister, praying as the Spirit shall give him utterance.

### Question. What are the reasons why one must sanctify a day to the Lord?
**Answer.** 1. Because the Lord has set Himself here as an example.
2. Because the Lord has given us His command concerning this matter; now His will must be a law to us.
3. Because the greatest work was done on this day, such as had not happened since the creation of the world—namely, the redemption of man. <note>The author highlights the shift in focus from the Seventh-day Sabbath of Creation to the Lord's Day (Sunday) focused on Christ's Resurrection.</note>

### Question. How does one break this commandment?
**Answer.** 1. When we let our thoughts out toward worldly vanities.
2. When we keep our hands busy in our usual occupation.
3. When we speak at all of our worldly things, beyond any necessity.

### Question. What may one do on the Lord’s Day without breaking this commandment?
**Answer.** 1. Works of unavoidable necessity, which cannot be done on any other day, may be done on that day.
2. Works of mercy, such as visiting the sick and refreshing the poor.
3. Works of divine service.

### Question. Concerning which people do we read in Scripture that God devised His plagues for the breaking of the Sabbath?
<margin>1. Wood-gatherers, Numbers 15:32, 33, 36.</margin>
<margin>2. Manna-seekers, Exodus 16:27, 28, 29.</margin>
<margin>3. Sellers/Merchants, Nehemiah 13:15, 16.</margin>
**Answer.** Over three kinds of people God has poured out His judgments because of this sin.

# Of the Fifth Commandment.

### Question. What is the brief summary of the last six commandments?
**Answer.** The fifth contains my duty regarding human authority; the sixth regarding human life; the seventh regarding a man’s wife; the eighth regarding a man’s goods; the ninth regarding a man’s name; the tenth regarding whatever 

<column-break/>

belongs to someone.

### Question. What is the fifth commandment?
**Answer.** Honor your Father and your Mother, etc.

### Question. How many things are to be noted in this commandment?
**Answer.** Two things: a command and a promise.

### Question. Who are understood here by "Father and Mother"?
**Answer.** Not only my natural parents, but also all those who are placed over me, such as Magistrates, Ministers, etc.

### Question. Are only the inferiors bound to the superiors, or are the superiors also bound to their inferiors by virtue of this commandment?
**Answer.** Yes: the higher-ranked are as much bound to their subordinates as the subordinates are to their superiors; therefore, we shall show you the duties of both.

### Question. What is the duty of Parents toward the Children?
**Answer.** 1. That they must teach, instruct, and bring them up in the knowledge of the fear of God. **Deuteronomy 6:7; Genesis 14:14; Ephesians 6:4; Proverbs 22:6.**
2. That they must chastise them when they do evil. **Proverbs 23:13, 14.** <note>The original cites verse 5, but the context refers to verses 13-14.</note> But not to strike them in their hot anger, but after the passion has passed; and then not with a club, but with a rod; this is God’s guidance, and by this means one shall save their souls from Hell. **Proverbs 29:17.**
3. They must bring them up in an honorable and lawful occupation. **Genesis 4:2.**
4. They must set aside sufficient goods for their children. **2 Corinthians 12:14.**
5. They must often pray for them. **Genesis 39:28.** <note>Possibly a reference to Genesis 49:28, Jacob's blessing.</note>

### Question. What is the duty of children toward the Parents?
**Answer.** 1. They must show them honor and virtue. **Malachi 1:6; Leviticus 19:3.**
2. They must be obedient to their parents in all lawful commands. **Colossians 3:20.**
3. They must refresh and support their parents, if God should let them suffer want in their old age. **Genesis 47:12; 1 Timothy 5:4.**
4. They must receive both the discipline and the instruction of their parents. **Proverbs 15:5.**

### Question. What is the duty of Masters toward their Servants?
**Answer.** 1. They must see to it that the servants do God’s work as well as their own work—serving God as well as themselves. **Joshua 24:15.** Oh, how few do this.
2. They must command their servants nothing but what is good and lawful. **Genesis 39:9; 1 Samuel 22:18.**
3. They must feed their servants and give them their wages. **Proverbs 31.**

### Question. What is the duty of Servants toward their Masters?
**Answer.** 1. They must be obedient to their masters. **Ephesians 6:5; Colossians 3:22.**
2. They must be as careful over their masters' things in their absence as in their presence. **Colossians 3:22.**
3. They must be faithful to their masters, pilfering nothing at all from them, nor wasting, nor spoiling. **Titus 2:10; Luke 16:1, 2.**

**Question.** What is the duty of Authorities toward their Subjects?
**Answer.** 1. They must ensure the preservation of their people.
2. They must punish their crimes.
3. They must praise and encourage those who do well, and they must be a terror to those who do evil, Rom. 13:3.
**Question.** What is the duty of subjects toward their Authorities?
**Answer.** 1. They must obey only their lawful commands.
2. They must pray for them, that they may occupy their positions with diligence and conscience, to the glory of God and the preservation of the Land, 1 Tim. 2:2.
**Question.** What is the duty of Ministers toward the people?
**Answer.** 1. To instruct the ignorant.
2. To rebuke the godless.
3. To keep watch over the weak.
4. To visit the sick.
5. To give them counsel in their poverty.
**Question.** What is the duty of the people toward their Teachers?
**Answer.** 1. To be willing to hear the word that he speaks.
2. To obey what they hear.
3. To pray for him, so that he may speak with power and usefulness, Eph. 6:18, 19. <note>The OCR reads 9:18, 19, but this is a likely printing error for Ephesians 6.</note>
4. To present their doubts to him, in order to be at rest and peace in their conscience.
5. To give him proper maintenance and reward for the labor he performs in service for the good of their souls.

### Concerning the Sixth Commandment.

**Question.** Which is the Sixth Commandment?
**Answer.** You shall not Kill.
**Question.** How does one break this Commandment?
**Answer.** 1. By being angry with someone without cause, Matt. 5:22.
2. By speaking scornful and spiteful words about someone, Matt. 5:22.
3. By wrongfully taking someone's life.
4. By consenting to the unjust killing of someone.
**Question.** What kind of killing is forbidden by the power of this commandment?
**Answer.** 1. Killing others.
2. Killing ourselves.

### Concerning the Seventh Commandment.

**Question.** Which is the Seventh Commandment?
**Answer.** You shall not commit adultery.
**Question.** How does one break this Commandment?
**Answer.** 1. Through lustful looking, Matt. 5:28.
2. Through filthy and indecent words, Ephes. 5:4.
3. Through wanton gestures and mockery, Rom. 13:13.
4. By the act of impurity itself.
**Question.** What are the primary incitements to impurity?
**Answer.** 1. Filling oneself up with delicacies <note>original: "leckere spijsen" — refers to rich, luxurious food associated with gluttony.</note>.
2. Familiarity with frivolous and wanton people.
3. Letting one's thoughts wander loosely and taking pleasure in wanton folly.

<column-break/>

**Question.** What remedies are there against impurity?
**Answer.** 1. Make a covenant with your eyes, not to look upon a woman with a lustful eye, Job 31:1.
2. Do not let your thoughts wander to the secret parts of nature.
3. Do not enter the company of wanton men or women.
4. Be moderate in eating and drinking; bring your body into subjection through fasting, for that will subject the flesh to the Spirit.
**Question.** What is the difference between Adultery, Fornication, and Incest?
**Answer.** Adultery is between married persons; Fornication is between unmarried persons; and Incest <note>original: "bloetschendingh" — literally "blood-violation".</note> is between those who are very closely related by blood, such as if someone lies with his Sister.

### Concerning the Eighth Commandment.

**Question.** Which is the Eighth Commandment?
**Answer.** You shall not steal.
**Question.** How do people break this Commandment of God?
**Answer.** 1. By not being satisfied with what they have, but desiring more.
2. By living the life of a beggar without a calling.
3. By taking something <unclear>something</unclear> from another, either by force or in secret, without their knowledge or consent.
**Question.** From what does thievery spring?
**Answer.** 1. From dissatisfaction with what one has.
2. From a desire for more.
3. From a lack of trust in God's providence when we suffer want.
**Question.** What does God require of people who are guilty of thievery?
**Answer.** 1. That they earnestly convert and have repentance.
2. That they restore what was stolen and give full satisfaction to those they have wronged.

### Concerning the Ninth Commandment.

**Question.** Which is the Ninth Commandment?
**Answer.** You shall not bear false witness against your neighbor.
**Question.** What is understood by the word Neighbor?
**Answer.** Not only he who is located nearest to me in terms of place, but also every person, man or woman, in the world.
**Question.** How do people break this Commandment by speaking false witness?
**Answer.** In two ways: either in court, or outside of court in ordinary conversation.
**Question.** How do people speak false witness outside of court, in their usual conversation?
**Answer.** 1. By speaking any untruth against someone, Lev. 19:11.
2. By gossiping and tale-bearing, Prov. 20:19, Lev. 19:16.
3. By speaking any evil of someone which might bring them reproach, whether to their face or behind their back.
4. By lightly accepting bad rumors about others.
**Question.** What is required of you by the power of this commandment?
**Answer.** 1. That I, whenever I [stand] before the...

### Concerning the Tenth Commandment.

**Question.** Which is the Tenth Commandment?
**Answer.** You shall not covet your neighbor’s house; you shall not covet your neighbor’s wife, etc.
**Question.** What does this commandment contain within itself?
**Answer.** Five things. 1. A prohibition against allowing oneself to lust after anything of the neighbor's house. 2. Nor his wife. 3. Nor his servants. 4. Nor his cattle. 5. Nor anything that belongs to him.
**Question.** Is this only one Commandment, or must it be divided into two?
**Answer.** It is true that the Roman Catholics <note>original: "Paepsche," a term used by Protestants in this period to refer to Catholics</note> divide this commandment into two because they omit the second commandment—which is against the worship of images—and therefore, to make ten out of them, they divide this one into two. But this must not happen, for in Deuteronomy 5, there are only "ten words" that God gave to Moses, from which not one tittle must be added.
**Question.** Why does God place "house" before "wife"?
**Answer.** To teach us that we must first provide ourselves with a house before we look for a wife.
**Question.** Why is "wife" placed before the "servants"?
**Answer.** To show that one must not make a slave or a handmaid out of his wife, but must hold her in higher regard than a servant.
**Question.** Why are "servants" placed before "ox and donkey"?
**Answer.** To show that even the lowliest servants must be valued above irrational animals <note>original: "onredelijcke dienaers," literally "unreasoning servants"</note>; this condemns those who value their horses, pigs, and dogs more than their servants.
**Question.** Why did the Lord God, after He had forbidden all this, still add: "Nor anything that is your neighbor’s"?
**Answer.** To take away all excuses and objections that a person might raise, such as: "Though they may not covet another's wife, they might still covet her social standing." So that no one might think such a thing, everything that belongs to another is forbidden for us to covet.
**Question.** What distinction is there between the seventh and the tenth commandment, since they both forbid the coveting of another man’s wife?
**Answer.** The seventh commandment forbids the *act* of adultery and impurity, but the tenth reaches further and forbids every *inclination* <note>original: "bewegingh," literally "movement" or "stirring" of the soul</note> toward lewdness, even if it never comes to the act or to consent—indeed, even if there were an immediate internal resistance against it.
**Question.** How do people break this commandment?
**Answer.** Through any covetous lust for another’s wife, or through any covetous hankering after the status or condition of another, even if one never consents to the inclination.

### Concerning the Knowledge of God.

**Question.** What must a person know if he wishes to be saved?
**Answer.** 1. He must clearly know God in His attributes.
2. He must know Jesus Christ through experience <note>original: "met ervarenthept," suggesting a personal, lived faith</note> in His glory.
3. He must know the Holy Spirit for his salvation in His sanctifying office.
4. He must know himself distinctly in his extremity and misery.
**Question.** What is God?
**Answer.** A pure Spirit, whom no one can see, and yet who sees all; everywhere present, Almighty, pure, and righteous in all His ways; all-wise, all-holy, eternal, infinite.
**Question.** From where do you prove that God is a Spirit?
**Answer.** From John 4:24: *God is a Spirit, and those who worship Him must worship Him in spirit and truth.*
**Question.** What do you learn from this, that God is a Spirit?
**Answer.** 1. That God is invisible, unable to be seen, and yet He sees everything.
2. That all the religious services I perform must be spiritual, just as God is; I must do them with my spirit (John 4:24).
**Question.** Why do you say that God is a Spirit?
**Answer.** To distinguish Him from physical bodies.
**Question.** Why do you say that God is a *pure* Spirit?
**Answer.** To distinguish God from the fallen angels, who are spirits but evil spirits.
**Question.** Why do you say that God is invisible, and yet sees everything?
**Answer.** To distinguish God from the good spirits in glory (angels), who do not see everything and cannot search the hearts of men.
**Question.** What are the attributes of God?
**Answer.** 1. His *incommunicable attributes* <note>attributes belonging to God alone</note> are His Omnipotence, by which He is powerful to do all things; His Omniscience, by which He knows all things; His Omnipresence, by which He is everywhere; and His Eternity, by which He is without beginning or end.
2. The *communicable attributes* <note>qualities God shares in a finite way with humans</note> are His power, justice and mercy, love, truth, goodness, holiness, and wisdom.
**Question.** What is the justice of God?
**Answer.** It is an attribute of God by which He deals impartially with men without respect of persons, repaying each according to his deeds: punishment to the godless, and grace to His children.
**Question.** What do you learn from this, that there is justice in God?
**Answer.** 1. That I must fear to sin against God, for He is so righteous that He will not see or suffer any sin in anyone, not even in His own people.
2. That there is no hope of swaying God through gifts or flattery; there is nothing other than righteousness in God.
3. That He will, at some time, avenge all the wrongs...

# The Marrow of the W[ord]

**Question.** What is the Mercy of God?
**Answer.** It is an attribute of God through which He, out of His own free grace and good pleasure, does good and gives to the creatures He has made.
**Question.** What do you learn from the fact that there is mercy in God?
**Answer.** 1. That I must not provoke such a merciful God to anger.
2. That I must fear the Lord God. Hosea 3:5. And the Psalmist says, "there is forgiveness with You, that You may be feared." <note>original: Psalm 130:4</note>
3. That I must not sin because of God’s grace. Romans 6:14, 15.
4. That although we have nothing in ourselves to deserve anything from God, there is nevertheless mercy in God, which is the motivation for everything.
**Question.** What is the Power of God?
**Answer.** It is an attribute of God through which He is powerful enough to do everything that pleases Him by His own self.
**Question.** What do you learn from the fact that there is such power in God?
**Answer.** 1. That the hardest things that churches or individuals must face are not too hard for God.
2. That enemies, no matter how strong they may be, are still weaker than God.
**Question.** What is the Holiness of God?
**Answer.** It is an attribute of God through which He, because of the purity of His nature, hates and punishes all sinners for their sins.
**Question.** What do you learn from the fact that God is holy?
**Answer.** 1. That I must be holy. 1 Peter 1:16. "Be holy, for I am holy."
2. That all creatures must be holy. Habakkuk 1:13. "You are of purer eyes than to behold evil."
3. That we, as converted sinners living and dying in unholiness, shall hereafter live eternally and holily with God.
**Question.** What is the Wisdom of God?
**Answer.** It is an attribute of God through which He possesses depths of counsel and knowledge to contemplate and arrange everything in Heaven and on earth.
**Question.** What do you learn from the fact that there is wisdom in God?
**Answer.** 1. That God will catch all enemies in their wisest counsel and most hidden plots, and that He will mock them.
2. That God has wisdom in Himself to provide ways and means for the deliverance of His church, which far exceeds all fleshly wisdom.
**Question.** What powerful effects will the knowledge of God have on the hearts of people who clearly know God?
**Answer.** 1. Those who clearly know God will boldly trust in Him. Psalm 9:10. "Those who know Your name will put their trust in You; for You, Lord, have not forsaken those who seek You."
2. The knowledge of God will make a person know himself.
3. It will instill a fear in the person, so that he will fear to sin against God, provided he knows Him.

<column-break/>

->Of the Knowledge of Christ.<-

**Question.** **W**hat is the second thing that someone must know to be saved?
**Answer.** Jesus Christ in His Glory.
**Question.** What must one necessarily know about Christ?
**Answer.** 1. His <term>Natures</term> <note>referring to His existence as both God and human</note> /
2. His Names /
3. His <term>Offices</term> <note>His roles as Prophet, Priest, and King</note> /
4. His Glories /
5. His Graces.
**Question.** How many natures are in Christ?
**Answer.** **Two** / 1. A Divine nature, insofar as He is God; and a human nature, insofar as He is man.
**Question.** Why must Christ be God?
**Answer.** To support His human nature and to satisfy God’s wrath, which was deserved by man’s sin; which He could not have done being only man.
**Question.** Why did Christ have to be man?
**Answer.** Because He could not die in His Divinity, therefore He had to be man; and because man had sinned, therefore Christ had to be man in order to die.
**Question.** What are the names of Christ?
**Answer.** 1. He is called Emmanuel. Matthew 1:23. That is, "God with us."
2. Jesus. Matthew 1:21. That is, a "Savior," because He shall save His people from their sins.
3. Christ, because He was anointed—that is, ordained by God the Father—to be fit as a Savior of His people.
4. The other names of Christ are in Isaiah 9:6 <note>OCR says 6:5, but the text describes the famous "Prince of Peace" passage</note>: Wonderful, Counselor, Mighty God, Everlasting Father, Prince of Peace.
**Question.** In what does the glory of Christ appear?
**Answer.** 1. In that He is personally united with the Godhead.
2. That He is the express image of the Father’s glory. Hebrews 1:3.
3. That He had no stain, weakness, or sin in body or in Soul.
**Question.** Which graces shine in an outstanding way in Christ?
**Answer.** 1. The voluntariness of His love. Romans 5:8. "God demonstrates His love toward us, in that while we were still sinners, Christ died for us."
2. His meekness and patience. Matthew 11:29. "Learn from Me, for I am meek and lowly in heart." Isaiah 53:7. "He opened not His mouth; He was led as a lamb to the slaughter, and as a sheep before its shearers is silent." Hebrews 12:3.
3. His humility. Philippians 2:5-7. <note>OCR says 1:5-7</note> "Let this mind be in you which was also in Christ Jesus, who, being in the form of God, did not consider it robbery to be equal with God, but emptied Himself, taking the form of a bondservant," etc.
4. His mercy and compassion for the miserable. Luke 19:41, 42. "As He drew near and saw the city, He wept over it, saying, 'If you had known, even you, especially in this your day, the things that make for your peace!'"
5. His zeal. Psalm 69:10. "Zeal for Your house has consumed me."
**Question.** Which are the offices of Christ?
**Answer.** He is a Prophet, a Priest, and a King.

<meta>This page continues the catechism-style instruction from page 820. # Practical Theology

**Question.** Has anyone except Christ ever held these three offices?
**Answer.** No; some were certainly **Prophets** and **Kings**, like David; others were **Prophets** and **Priests**, like Abraham, and one was even **King** and **Priest**, namely Melchizedek, but never has anyone besides Christ been **King**, **Priest**, and **Prophet** all at once.
**Question.** Why is Christ a **Priest**?
**Answer.** To offer sacrifices and prayers for His people.
**Question.** What sacrifice did Christ offer?
**Answer.** Himself, that is, His human nature.
**Question.** Every sacrifice had to be offered by a Priest; who then was the Priest?
**Answer.** Christ Himself.
**Question.** Every sacrifice was offered on the Altar; what then was the Altar on which this sacrifice took place?
**Answer.** Christ, in regard to His Divinity, bore His humanity as the Altar; the Divine nature supported the human nature to be a sacrifice for man's sin; so that you see from this that Christ is the Altar, the Priest, and the sacrifice all at once.
**Question.** What do you learn from the **Priestly office** of Christ?
**Answer.** 1. That although there is no worthiness in my religious practices, Christ nevertheless offers them up to His Father, and so I hope to be acceptable through His worthiness.
2. That I must never come to God in my own name or worthiness.
3. That Christ is suitably moved <note>original: "aengedaen" — here meaning to be touched by or "clothed in" the feelings of others</note> by all the weaknesses of His children. *Hebrews 4:15*. "For we do not have a High Priest who cannot sympathize with our weaknesses, but was in all points tempted as we are, yet without sin."
4. That Christ makes reconciliation between God and my soul. *Hebrews 4:17*. <note>The printed text cites Heb. 4:17, but the quotation provided is actually Hebrews 2:17</note> "Therefore, in all things He had to be made like His brethren, that He might be a merciful and faithful High Priest in things pertaining to God, to make propitiation for the sins of the people."
**Question.** Why did Christ have to be a **Prophet**?
**Answer.** So that He might teach His people.
**Question.** Christ is indeed in Heaven, and His children are on earth; how then does He teach them?
**Answer.** Christ teaches His children: 1. Through His Spirit. 2. Through His word.
**Question.** How does the Spirit teach us?
**Answer.** 1. By enlightening our understanding to His knowledge.
2. By inclining our hearts to His love.
3. By bending our will to His obedience.
**Question.** What do you learn from the fact that Christ is a **Prophet**?
**Answer.** 1. That I must go to Christ to obtain knowledge, for He is the great **Prophet**.
2. That those who die in ignorance have no right to Christ, for He teaches all His children from the least to the greatest.
**Question.** What is Christ's **Kingly office**?
**Answer.** It is that supremacy which Jesus has over all creatures, through which He governs His Church by laws according to His own will, and subdues His enemies who do not want Him to rule over them.

<column-break/>

**Question.** What do you learn from Christ having this **Kingly office**?
**Answer.** 1. That I must be taught by all the laws which Christ our King gives us. *Isaiah 33:22*.
2. That Christ is willing and powerful to protect His entire Church.
3. That Christ shall tread all His enemies under His feet. *Revelation 19:15, 16*.
**Question.** What must move people to seek the knowledge of Christ?
**Answer.** 1. Because the knowledge of Christ is a most glorious knowledge. *Philippians 3:7, 8*. "But what things were gain to me, these I have counted loss for Christ... yet indeed I also count all things loss for the excellence of the knowledge of Christ Jesus my Lord, for whom I have suffered the loss of all things, and count them as rubbish, that I may gain Christ."
2. Because eternal glory is joined to the knowledge of Jesus Christ. *John 17:3*. "And this is eternal life, that they may know You, the only true God, and Jesus Christ whom You have sent."

-> Of the knowledge of the Holy Spirit. <-

**Question.** What is the **Holy Spirit**?
**Answer.** The third person of the blessed Trinity, from all eternity proceeding from the Father and the Son.
**Question.** Why is the Spirit of God given this name?
**Answer.** Because it is His proper work to **sanctify** <term>sanctify: to make holy or set apart for God's use</term> people.
**Question.** From what do you prove that the Holy Spirit is God?
**Answer.** From *Acts 5:3, 4*. "Why has Satan filled your heart to lie to the Holy Spirit... You have not lied to men but to God." And *1 John 5:7*. "For there are three that bear witness in heaven: the Father, the Word, and the Holy Spirit; and these three are one."
**Question.** What is the **sin against the Holy Spirit**, as mentioned in *Matthew 12:31, 32*?
**Answer.** It is an abominable evil committed by someone who, being a **professor** <term>professor: in this context, a "believer" or "confessor" who openly declares their faith</term> of the Gospel, falls away from the confessed truth and, against his conscience, persecutes the truth and its professors with very great malice and rage.
**Question.** Is this sin unpardonable?
**Answer.** It is not unpardonable in the sense that God does not have enough power, nor Christ enough merit, to forgive this sin; but it is such because the heart of everyone who commits this sin is so highly hardened that he cannot have repentance for his sins, and consequently, he can receive no forgiveness.
**Question.** Why is this sin called the sin against the **Holy Spirit**, since every sin is against God?
**Answer.** Not to exclude God the Father or the Lord Jesus, as if it did not also happen against them, but because it is primarily against the work and office of the **Holy Spirit**, which is to enlighten the understandings of men and to sanctify their hearts.
**Question.** What is required in someone before he can commit this sin against the **Holy Spirit**?
**Answer.** 1. He must be a **professor** of the Religion; thus, no godless heathen can commit this sin.

### Practical Theology

**Question.** Has anyone besides Christ ever held these three offices?
**Answer.** No; some were indeed Prophets and Kings, like David; others were Prophets and Priests, like Abraham; indeed, one was even King and Priest, namely Melchizedek, but never has anyone besides Christ been King, Priest, and Prophet all at once.
**Question.** Why is Christ a Priest?
**Answer.** To offer sacrifices and prayers for His people.
**Question.** Which Sacrifice did Christ offer?
**Answer.** Himself; that is, His human nature.
**Question.** Every Sacrifice had to be offered by a Priest; who then was the Priest?
**Answer.** Christ Himself.
**Question.** Every Sacrifice was offered upon an Altar; what then was the Altar upon which this Sacrifice took place?
**Answer.** Christ, in respect to His Divinity, carried His humanity as the Altar; the Divine nature supported the human nature to be a sacrifice for the sins of man; so that you see from this that Christ is the Altar, the Priest, and the sacrifice all at once.
**Question.** What do you learn from the Priestly office of Christ?
**Answer.** 1. That although there is no worthiness in my practice of God's service, nevertheless Christ offers the same to His Father, and so I hope to be acceptable through His worthiness.
2. That I must never come to God in my own name or worthiness.
3. That Christ is deeply moved by all the weaknesses of His children. <note>original: "gevoeliglijk wort aengedaen" — literally "feelingly affected"</note> Hebrews 4:15: *For we do not have a High Priest who cannot sympathize with our weaknesses, but was in all points tempted as we are, yet without sin.*
4. That Christ makes reconciliation between God and my soul. Hebrews 4:17. <note>The text cites Heb. 4:17, but the verse quoted is actually Hebrews 2:17</note> *Therefore, He had to be made like His brethren in all things, that He might be a merciful and faithful High Priest in things pertaining to God, to make propitiation for the sins of the people.*
**Question.** Why did Christ have to be a Prophet?
**Answer.** So that He might teach His people.
**Question.** Since Christ is in Heaven and His children are on earth, how does He teach them?
**Answer.** Christ teaches His children: 1. By His Spirit. 2. By His word.
**Question.** How does the Spirit teach us?
**Answer.** 1. By enlightening our understanding to know Him.
2. By inclining our hearts to His love.
3. By bending our will to His obedience.
**Question.** What do you learn from this, that Christ is a Prophet?
**Answer.** 1. That I must go to Christ to obtain knowledge, for He is the great Prophet.
2. That those who die in ignorance have no right to Christ, for He teaches all His children from the least to the greatest.
**Question.** What is Christ’s Kingly office?
**Answer.** It is that supremacy which Jesus has over all creatures, by which He governs His Church by laws according to His own will, and subdues His enemies who do not want Him to rule over them.

<column-break/>

**Question.** What do you learn from this, that Christ has this Kingly office?
**Answer.** 1. That I must be taught by all those laws which Christ our King gives us. Isaiah 33:22. <note>The Dutch text mistakenly cites Isaiah 23:22</note>
2. That Christ is willing and powerful to protect His entire Church.
3. That Christ shall tread all His enemies under His feet. Revelation 19:15, 16.
**Question.** What should move people to seek the knowledge of Christ?
**Answer.** 1. Because the knowledge of Christ is a most glorious knowledge. Philippians 3:7, 8. *But what things were gain to me, these I have counted loss for Christ. Yet indeed I also count all things loss for the excellence of the knowledge of Christ Jesus my Lord, for whom I have suffered the loss of all things, and count them as rubbish, that I may gain Christ.*
2. Because eternal glory is linked to the knowledge of Jesus Christ. John 17:3. *And this is eternal life, that they may know You, the only true God, and Jesus Christ whom You have sent.*

->On the knowledge of the Holy Spirit.<-

**Question.** What is the Holy Spirit?
**Answer.** The third person of the blessed Trinity, proceeding from all eternity from the Father and the Son.
**Question.** Why is the Spirit of God given this name?
**Answer.** Because it is His own work to sanctify mankind. <note>The name "Holy" Spirit refers to His role in making believers holy (sanctification).</note>
**Question.** How do you prove that the Holy Spirit is God?
**Answer.** From Acts 5:3, 4. *Why has Satan filled your heart to lie to the Holy Spirit... you have not lied to men but to God.* And 1 John 5:7. <note>The text cites "Joh. 5. 7" referring to the first epistle</note> *For there are three that bear witness in heaven: the Father, the Word, and the Holy Spirit; and these three are one.*
**Question.** What is the sin against the Holy Spirit, mentioned in Matthew 12:31, 32?
**Answer.** It is a terrible evil committed by someone who, being a professor of the Gospel, falls away from the confessed truth and, against his conscience, persecutes the truth and its professors with great malice and rage.
**Question.** Is this sin unpardonable?
**Answer.** It is not unpardonable in the sense that God lacks enough power or Christ lacks enough merit to forgive this sin; but it is such because the heart of everyone who commits this sin is so exceedingly hardened that he cannot repent of his sins, and consequently he cannot receive forgiveness.
**Question.** Why is this sin called the sin against the Holy Spirit, since every sin is against God?
**Answer.** Not to exclude God the Father or the Lord Jesus, as if it were not also against them, but because it is primarily against the work and office of the Holy Spirit, which is to enlighten the minds of men and to sanctify their hearts.
**Question.** What is required in someone before they can commit this sin against the Holy Spirit?
**Answer.** 1. He must be a professor of the religion; thus, no godless heathen can commit this sin.

# The Marrow of the W. <note>likely "Woord" or Word</note> Of the knowledge of Christ.

...just as / which happened against him and his people.
**Question.** What is the Mercy of God?
**Answer.** It is an attribute of God / whereby He, out of His own free grace / and good pleasure, does good / and gives to the creatures / which He has made.
**Question.** What do you learn from this, that there is mercy in God?
**Answer.** 1. That I must not provoke such a merciful God to anger.
2. That I must fear God the Lord, *Hos. 3:5*. and as the Psalmist says / there is grace with You that You may be feared.
3. That I must not sin upon God's grace / *Rom. 6:14, 15*.
4. That although we have nothing in us / to deserve anything from God / that nevertheless mercy is in God / which is the motive <note>original: "beweegreden" — the driving reason or impulse</note> for everything.
**Question.** What is the power of God?
**Answer.** It is an attribute of God / whereby He is mighty of Himself to do everything that pleases Him.
**Question.** What do you learn from this, that there is such power in God?
**Answer.** 1. That the hardest things / which remain to be done for churches and persons / are not too hard for God.
2. That the enemies / though they be ever so strong / are nonetheless weaker than God.
**Question.** What is the holiness of God?
**Answer.** It is an attribute of God / whereby He, on account of the purity of His nature / hates and punishes all sinners for their sins' sake.
**Question.** What do you learn from this, that God is holy?
**Answer.** 1. That I must be holy, *1 Pet. 1:16*. Be holy, for I am holy.
2. That all Creatures must be holy, *Hab. 1:13*. You are of purer eyes, than that You should behold evil.
3. That we, having been converted Sinners [once] living and dying in unholiness / shall hereafter live holily with God eternally.
**Question.** What is the wisdom of God?
**Answer.** It is an attribute of God / whereby He has depths of counsel and knowledge / to conceive and ordain everything in Heaven and on earth.
**Question.** What do you learn from this, that there is wisdom in God?
**Answer.** 1. That God shall catch all enemies in their wisest counsel / and highest designs / and that He shall mock them.
2. That God has wisdom in Himself / to provide ways and means for the deliverance of His church / which far exceeds all fleshly <note>or carnal</note> wisdom.
**Question.** What powerful effects will the knowledge of God have on the hearts of men who clearly know God?
**Answer.** 1. Those who clearly know God shall trust in Him confidently, *Psalm 9:10*. Those who know Your name shall trust in You, because You, Lord, have not forsaken those who seek You.
2. The knowledge of God shall make a man know himself.
3. It shall instill a fear in man / so that he shall fear to sin against God / if he knows Him.

->Of the knowledge of Christ.<-

**Question.** What is the second thing which one must know to be saved?
**Answer.** Jesus Christ in His Glory.
**Question.** What must one necessarily know of Christ?
**Answer.** 1. His Natures /
2. His Names /
3. His Offices /
4. His Glories /
5. His Graces.
**Question.** How many natures are in Christ?
**Answer.** Two / 1. A Divine [nature] / insofar as He is God / and a human [nature] insofar as He is man.
**Question.** Why must Christ be God?
**Answer.** To support His human nature / to satisfy God's wrath / deserved by man's sin / which He could not have done being only man.
**Question.** Why did Christ have to be man?
**Answer.** Because in His Divinity He could not die / therefore He had to be man; because man had sinned / therefore Christ had to be man in order to die.
**Question.** Which are the names of Christ?
**Answer.** 1. He is called Immanuel, *Matt. 1:23*. that is, God with us.
2. Jesus, *Matt. 1:21*. that is, a Savior / because He shall save His people from their sins.
3. Christ, because He was anointed / that is, ordained by God the Father / to be fit as a Savior of His people.
4. The other names of Christ stand in *Isa. 9:5*. Wonderful, Counselor, Mighty God, Father of Eternity, Prince of Peace.
**Question.** In what does the glory of Christ appear?
**Answer.** 1. In that He is personally united with the Divinity.
2. That He is the express image of the Father's glory, *Heb. 1:3*.
3. That He had no blemish / weakness, or sin in body or in Soul.
**Question.** Which graces shine in an outstanding way in Christ?
**Answer.** 1. The mercy of His love, *Rom. 5:8*. God confirms His love toward us, that Christ died for us while we were yet sinners.
2. His meekness and patience / *Matt. 11:29*. Learn from Me that I am meek and lowly of heart, *Isa. 53:7*. He did not open His mouth; as a lamb He was led to the slaughter, and as a Sheep that is dumb before the face of its Shearers, *Heb. 12:3*.
3. His humility / *Philipp. 2:5, 6, 7*. Let this mind be in you, which was also in Christ Jesus, who, being in the form of God, did not consider it robbery <note>original: "geenen roof geacht" — a traditional translation of "something to be grasped" or "usurped"</note> to be equal with God, but emptied Himself, having taken the form of a servant, etc.
4. His compassion and pity for the miserable / *Luke 19:41, 42*. When He now saw the City, He wept over it, saying; Oh, if you also knew in this your day, the things which still serve for your peace.
5. His zeal / *Psalm 69:10*. The zeal for Your house has consumed me.
**Question.** Which are the offices of Christ?
**Answer.** He is a Prophet / a Priest and King.
